A review committee could view key details of applications with different statuses, then review summary details of those with an accepted status to make a final determination.

docs.title: A Housing Support case
docs.text:
In this Housing Support example, the Open Case activity is marked as Completed when the case opens. Three more activities are scheduled automatically: a medical evaluation for the following day (reference offset 1), securing temporary housing (reference offset 2), and a follow-up three days later.

The case has three roles. The Homeless Service Coordinator creates and manages the case. A Health Services Coordinator role and a Benefits Specialist role are also created when it opens.

docs.title: Relationship Type status warnings in CiviCase
docs.text: Use this page to identify unusual Relationship Type situations that may produce CiviCase status warnings. It also records the remedies described for duplicate types and labels.

docs.title: Before changing a Relationship Type
docs.text: If you have not created any relationships between contacts, you can delete the relationship type and recreate it. If you have created only a small number, you may consider deleting those relationships, deleting and recreating the relationship type, then recreating the relationships between contacts.

docs.title: Internal name duplicates
docs.text: This can happen when setting up A/B directions. For example, you create Candy maker is (A to B) / Candy maker for (B to A), then create a second type with Candy maker for (A to B) / Candy maker is (B to A), thinking both types are needed to show both directions. If you then rename the second type to Gum maker is / Gum maker for, assigning Gum maker roles will cause problems.

docs.title: Display label duplicates
docs.text: Two different relationship types may have the same display label. The simplest solution is to change one label or delete the duplicate. If the types describe the same relationship, keeping both is a bad idea.

docs.title: Cross-duplication
docs.text: A particular order of changes to relationship types can cause confusion. For example, you create Candy maker, Gum maker and Sweets maker. Later you delete Gum, rename Sweets to Gum, then rename Candy to Sweets. At that point, the system will get confused about which type means what.

docs.title: Ambiguous direction
docs.text: If you create a bidirectional Relationship Type such as Spouse of, then edit it so that direction matters, the system will still function, but some relationships of that type may appear backwards. The reverse change—from unidirectional to bidirectional—is also possible.

docs.title: Missing roles
docs.text: A missing role can occur when an external XML file contains a typo, so its relationship type does not match an existing type. It can also occur when a relationship type is deleted but the file still refers to it.

docs.title: How CiviCase structures a case
docs.text: This page explains the concepts and assumptions behind CiviCase, including what your organisation can customise when planning its case management work.

docs.title: Activities and cases
docs.text:
CiviCRM tracks most interactions as activities. An activity is useful for a single task or interaction: for example, a constituent calls for information and a staff person directs them to a website. Activities have a start date and time, duration, status, priority, creator and subject or target. They can also be assigned to someone for action.

A case brings together interactions that are more complex than one activity. Multiple activities can form a case story. CiviCase can organise them with a Timeline or a Sequence and can optionally restrict which activities are available for tracking interactions.

CiviCase also records the people involved and their roles. Case Coordinator is a predefined role, and you can add others. The Case Dashboard shows users the cases they are involved in, while cases provide an extra layer of access control.

Together, these features can describe a workflow with specific steps: a client fills out an intake form, meets with a staff person, then receives a certificate from the organisation for meeting certain goals.

docs.title: Case types and activity types
docs.text:
A Case Type describes a group of related tasks, interactions or processes. For example, the Physician Health Program supports physicians experiencing problems related to emotional health, inappropriate use of alcohol and/or drugs, or coping with physical illness. Its case types include In-patient Treatment and Referral to Counsellor. A community services organisation might use Housing Assistance, Job Training or Prenatal Counseling.

Within a case, activities track specific tasks and interactions. You can schedule them in advance or create them ad-hoc. They may involve the case client (also called the constituent), a third party such as a family member or assisting professional, and other case workers. Your organisation decides how much detail to record; many organisations record every phone call, meeting and internal discussion as part of the case story.

CiviCRM comes with activity types including Phone Calls, Meetings, Emails Sent, Interviews and Follow-ups. You can add types for other tasks. For example, a community services organisation might add Client Intake, Skills Evaluation, Review and Consultant Referral. Specific types can make an activity list easier to read than using Follow-up for every task.

Some activities are created during the life of a case:

  • Open Case: Created when the case is created.
  • Follow up: Available when a more specific type is unnecessary.
  • Change Case Type: Created whenever the case type is modified.
  • Change Case Status: Created whenever the case status is updated.

docs.title: Information recorded on an activity
docs.text:
The standard activity information includes who recorded and reported it; when and where it will or did occur; a free-form subject and detailed description; and time spent on it. This may be enough for some activities.

For others, structured information may help. An Open Case (intake) activity, for example, might need specific questions about the client and their situation. You can use Custom Fields to associate additional data with each activity.

docs.title: Timelines and sequences
docs.text:
A timeline defines an expected set of activities for a case type and when they should occur. A simple timeline might contain Open Case and a Follow up scheduled two days later. A more complex timeline provides a case plan: it lists expected activities and the time frame for completing them.

Activity dates are calculated when you add a timeline to a case; they do not update automatically. You must change dates manually if the schedule changes.

Every case type must have a standard timeline. It is created automatically when a new case is opened and can consist of only the completed Open Case activity. You can add more activities, defining the expected number of days from the beginning of the case to each one.

You can also define multiple non-standard timelines and add them to a case when appropriate. These can use any activity as the reference for later activities. For example, if the standard timeline includes a medical evaluation, you could define two or more treatment schedules and add one based on the evaluation’s outcome. Those timelines would typically use medical evaluation as their reference activity.

A non-standard timeline can instead work backwards from a case end date. If a case must finish by the start of the school year, for example, you can define activities with negative offsets: each is scheduled a number of days before that date. You would open the case, add the final activity with its scheduled end date, then add the timeline. The resulting dates show the latest each activity could be completed for the case to finish on time.

A sequence defines activities that follow one another without time offsets. The first activity is created when the case opens; each subsequent activity is created as soon as the previous one is completed. Its scheduled date is always its creation date.

A sequence may suit work where the timing of completion is outside your control. Because its activities appear progressively, however, it does not give the same at-a-glance view as a timeline. A case can use a sequence instead of, or alongside, timelines.

Note

If you use a timeline and a sequence in the same case, their activity types must not overlap. Including an activity type such as Meeting in both will create problems.

docs.title: People connected to a case
docs.text:
CiviCase provides three ways to connect people to cases and clients:

  • Case Roles identify people directly involved in a particular case, such as an Intake Specialist, Case Coordinator, Addiction Counselor or Employment Counselor. You can identify one role as the case manager for a case type.
  • Other Relationships connect people to the client beyond a particular case, such as a Spouse, Sibling or Family Doctor. Generally, use a relationship if someone should appear on all cases for that client; otherwise, use a case role.
  • Case Resources are people and organisations involved with many or all cases in your case management setting. Examples include regulatory agency contacts, service providers and frequent referral contacts.

CiviCRM provides relationship type definitions for many standard relationships, such as Spouse and Child. You will probably need additional relationship types for case roles, such as Case Coordinator, Addiction Specialist and Job Counsellor.

docs.title: Planning your case management work
docs.text:
CiviCase assumes that activities are single tasks or interactions with a client or constituent, or between people in your organisation. A case is a succession of those activities; their record forms its story, and almost all case information should be stored as an activity.

Consider these questions before configuring CiviCase:

  • Which case types do you need? List regular, multi-step processes. Work that spans days or weeks, includes several activities and involves multiple people may be a good candidate for case management. Defining case types lets you describe workflows and evaluate results.
  • Which activities and activity types belong in each case type? Decide what your organisation needs to record and whether the existing types describe the work clearly.
  • Who should activities be assigned to? A Case Coordinator might initially receive everything and reassign work according to capacity, or particular activities might need a specific person.
  • What should the standard timeline contain? Decide whether activities should be scheduled from the start of the case, from one another or from an end date. An expected schedule can help case workers manage work and measure progress.
  • Who takes part in each case type? List the expected roles, identify which is normally the case manager, and decide whether existing relationships are adequate or case-specific ones are needed. Clear roles help people communicate about case activities. Also consider people and outside organisations your team contacts in most or all cases as case resources.

docs.title: Find and merge duplicate contacts
docs.text:
Use a dedupe rule to find possible duplicates, review each pair and decide what to do. You can use the default rules without configuring new ones.

An alternate interface is available in the deduper extension.

docs.title: Scan for duplicates
docs.text:
1. Go to Contacts > Find and Merge Duplicate Contacts.
  2. Click Use Rule for the rule you want to use.
  3. Choose whether to search All Contacts or limit the search to a group.
  4. Click Continue.

If you select a group, CiviCRM looks for pairs in which at least one contact belongs to that group. It scans contacts of the type assigned to the rule and lists pairs whose match meets or exceeds the rule's threshold.

The list of possible duplicates has show/hide tickboxes for Street Address, Post Code, Conflicts and Threshold.

docs.title: Review and merge a pair
docs.text:
1. Click Merge for a pair to compare its records. CiviCRM places the duplicate record on the left and the original record, into which selected data will be merged, on the right.
  2. If the information should move in the opposite direction, choose Flip between original and duplicate contacts at the top of the page.
  1. Review the colour-coded rows and choose what to keep:
  2. Green: The information is the same on both contacts. You can hide these rows with Show/Hide rows with the same data on each contact record.
  3. Red: The information differs. For each field, leave the middle-column checkbox unticked to keep the original value on the right, or tick it to use the duplicate's value. For email addresses or phone numbers, you can keep both values by ticking the middle-column checkbox and “add new” in the right column.
  4. Yellow: The middle-column checkbox is ticked by default, so the duplicate's data will be added to the original's data. This includes tags, groups and activity data, such as event attendance and contributions. If you untick the checkbox, the duplicate's data will be lost.
  5. Click Merge... to complete the merge. If the contacts are not the same person or organisation, click Mark this pair as not a duplicate instead.

Contacts marked “not a duplicate” are excluded from all dedupe results listings. To review them, click View the Dedupe Exceptions on the main Find and Merge Duplicate Contacts screen.

docs.title: Check for duplicates in stages
docs.text:
One rule may leave some duplicates in your system. For individuals, you can check first with the stricter Unsupervised rule, then use a Supervised or General rule to look for contacts it missed. If your Individual Unsupervised rule is strict enough, you may be able to batch merge duplicates in the first stage; otherwise, review pairs manually.

  1. Click Use Rule for Individual unsupervised: contact type Individual, usage unsupervised.
  2. Select All Contacts or a particular group.
  3. Click Continue.
  4. If duplicates are found, merge or delete the duplicate contacts.
  5. Click Use Rule for Individual supervised: contact type Individual, usage supervised. You can also use a General rule to look for contacts missed by the stricter rule.
  6. Select All Contacts or a particular group.
  7. Click Continue.
  8. If duplicates are found, merge them or mark them as “not a duplicate”.

docs.title: Merge contacts from search results
docs.text:
If you notice duplicates while working with search results, you can merge them without starting a separate scan.

  1. Tick the checkbox to the left of each duplicate contact in the search results.
  2. Select Merge Contacts from the Actions menu.
  3. Review and merge the contacts as described above.

docs.title: Batch merge duplicate contacts
docs.text:
Use batch merging to process multiple pairs from a list of possible duplicates. You can also run a batch merge from the command line.

Before you begin: Batch dedupe is intended for large data sets with strictly managed field structures. If your database is small and has only a few duplicates, merge them manually using your own judgement. Back up your data before a batch merge: merged duplicate records are deleted and are not recoverable unless database logging is enabled. Links from the duplicate to records elsewhere in the system—including event participant records, groups, tags, contributions, activities, cases and memberships—transfer to the original contact. You cannot reverse this change.

docs.title: Merge from the possible duplicates screen
docs.text:
The possible duplicates screen can display up to 100 rows.

Before merging, check which record will be kept: Contact 1 is kept; contact 2 is merged into it and then deleted. Use Flip Selected Duplicates beneath the list if you need to switch the order of selected records.

Choose one of the options beneath the list:

  • Batch Merge All Duplicates merges all duplicates found, not only those displayed on your screen.
  • Batch Merge Selected Duplicates merges the pairs whose left-hand checkboxes you have ticked.

The batch merge processes all contacts under the given rule or all selected contacts, provided there are no data conflicts. For example, two contacts named “Michael Blake” might match on first and last name, with neither having an email address. They can be merged if their other information is identical, or if one has a work phone number and the other has a mobile number. If they have different home telephone numbers, the pair is skipped instead.

After the batch merge, CiviCRM returns you to the original list. If records were skipped because of conflicts, a message is displayed. Click Refresh Duplicates to see the updated list; the page does not refresh automatically because searching a very large database could cause a significant delay. You can then assess and merge the remaining pairs manually.

The deduper extension offers additional ways to resolve pairs in batch, including treating conflicts on certain fields as non-blocking and handling diacritic names.

docs.title: Merge from the command line
docs.text:
Batch merging can also be done from the command line. For example:

 echo '{"search_limit": 10000, "criteria":{"contact" : {"id" : {">" : 200}}}}'
   | drush --in=json cvapi Job.process_batch_merge

This finds contacts matching any of the first 10,000 contacts found with an ID greater than 200 and attempts to merge them using the defaults: “safe” mode, which skips conflicts, and the default rules for individuals.

docs.title: Dedupe rules and duplicate contacts
docs.text: Use this page to look up how CiviCRM identifies possible duplicate contacts and how its dedupe rules work.

docs.title: Where duplicates come from
docs.text:
Duplicate contacts can enter your database when:

  • Someone creates a contact through the admin interface without realising the contact already exists.
  • Someone signs up or enters their details online using a different name or email address from the one already recorded.
  • Imported contacts include records that were not identified as duplicates.

CiviCRM has features that try to prevent duplicates from being created and features that help you find and merge duplicates already in the database. You can scan contacts with a selected dedupe rule, select two contacts from search results to merge, or receive suggestions when adding or editing a contact through the user interface. CiviCRM can also merge a person's details into an existing contact during online sign-up for Events, Membership, Contributions and Profile pages, or when importing contacts.

docs.title: Rule types
docs.text:
A dedupe rule specifies when CiviCRM should consider two contacts duplicates. For example, a rule could require both email address and first name to match.

Rules are configured separately for individuals, organizations and households. Each contact type has a default supervised rule and a default unsupervised rule. CiviCRM uses default rules for automatic checking.

Rule type How CiviCRM uses it Unsupervised CiviCRM automatically uses this rule when contacts are created through online registrations, including Events, Membership, Contributions and Profile pages. It is also selected by default when you Import contacts. Unsupervised rules generally use a narrow definition of a duplicate to avoid accidentally merging a false match. Supervised CiviCRM automatically checks this rule when someone adds or edits a contact through the user interface. If a new contact matches, the user interface alerts the person, who can edit the existing contact or continue creating a new one. A broader definition is suitable because the person can decide what to do. General Additional rules provide other criteria for scanning for possible duplicates. You can configure any number of General rules.

You can configure only one Unsupervised rule and one Supervised rule for each contact type.

docs.title: How a rule determines a match
docs.text:
A rule checks up to five fields that you specify. For each field, you can set a length and a numeric weight.

  • Length sets how many characters CiviCRM compares. With a length of 2 on First Name, “Mike” matches “Michael” because their first two characters match. With a length of 3, they do not match. If length is blank, CiviCRM compares the entire field value.
  • Weight sets the relative importance of a match on that field. When a field matches, CiviCRM adds its weight to the rule's total.

After checking the fields, CiviCRM flags the contacts as suspected duplicates if the total weight meets or exceeds the rule's numerical threshold.

You can see the available rules at Contacts > Find and Merge Duplicate Contacts.

docs.title: Export contacts
docs.text: Export contact information from CiviCRM to a CSV file that you can use in a spreadsheet, another database application, or a word processing mail merge.

docs.title: Where you can export
docs.text: Export is available in any of the search tools and when viewing contacts in a group. It is also available in component-based search results. Those exports can include component-specific data rather than only core contact data. For example, a Contributions > Find Contributions search can export donors’ contact information and total amounts donated for a thank-you letter.

docs.title: Export contact information
docs.text:
1. Search for the contacts you want to export. You can use Quick search, Find Contacts, Advanced search, Search Builder, or a custom search. For help, see Searching.
  2. Select all records, or use the checkboxes beside individual records to select them.
  3. Choose Export Contacts from the - actions - dropdown menu. This opens the export wizard.
  1. Under Export all or selected fields, choose whether to export primary fields, select your own fields, or use a previously saved export mapping, if you have one.

A primary fields export contains 80 fields: core contact fields with primary email, phone, and address data. Selecting your own fields lets you include non-primary email, phone, and address data, custom contact fields, and data from related contacts.

  1. Set any other export options you need:

  2. For mailing labels, choose one record per household or one per address. If you choose one per address, you can specify the Addressee and postal greeting formats.

  3. Exclude contacts with “do not mail” privacy, no street address, or who are deceased.

  4. Add contacts from an additional group.

  5. Click Continue. If you chose primary fields, the export happens immediately. If you chose your own fields or a saved mapping, the Select Fields to Export page opens.

  6. If the Select Fields to Export page opens, choose the fields for your export.

  • For a saved export mapping, its fields are displayed. You can use them as they are or modify them. If you modify the mapping, you can update it or save your changes as a new field mapping.

  • For a new mapping, choose Save this field mapping if you want to use it again.

  • If you selected fields, click Export when the fields and other options are correct.

The file is exported in .CSV format. By default, CiviCRM uses a comma as the field separator for import and export. If you need a different separator, go to Administer > Localization > Languages, Currency, Locations and select the appropriate Import/Export Field Separator.

docs.title: Import contacts
docs.text: Use the four steps of the import wizard to choose your data, match its fields, preview the results and check the imported contacts. Prepare and test your data before importing a large batch.

docs.title: Fields to include
docs.text:
The contact import interface marks these fields red and with a star:

  • Email (Match to Contact)
  • External Identifier
  • First Name
  • Last Name

The source says selecting one of these fields is enough if you have less data. It also says a field identified as (Match to Contact) is required for deduplication. External Identifier is useful when you want to update existing contacts.

docs.title: Import contacts
docs.text:
1. Choose the data source

Choose a CSV file or an SQL query against a database on your server. If the first row of a file contains column headings, select the check-box for that option.

Imports use the default unsupervised Dedupe Rule to identify duplicates unless you select another Dedupe Rule at this step. The Deduping and Merging chapter in this section explains duplicate matching rules. Choose what the import should do when it encounters a duplicate:

Option Result Skip Leaves the existing contact unchanged and skips the duplicate. Update Updates the existing contact with fields present in the import data. Fields absent from the import data remain unchanged. Fill Adds imported data where the existing contact has missing or blank fields. Fields that already have values remain unchanged. No Duplicate Checking Inserts all valid records without comparing them with existing contacts for possible duplicates.

You can match imported data directly to existing Contact IDs only in Update, Fill or No Duplicate Checking mode.

An import mapping tells CiviCRM which fields in your source correspond to its fields. If you have saved a mapping for a file with the same structure, select it from Load Saved Field Mapping on the Choose Data Source screen.

docs.title: Import contacts
docs.text:
1. Match the fields

If your file has column headings, they appear in the first column of the Field Map. The next two columns show two rows of source data, and the fourth is Matching CiviCRM Field. A mapping loaded in step 1 appears here; change any choices that do not fit this import.

Select the matching CiviCRM field for each column you want to import. The choices include standard contact fields, such as First Name and Last Name, and any custom data fields configured for contacts on your site. For example, match a source column headed Surname to Last Name. Select - do not import - for a column you want to leave out.

To reuse this mapping later, select Save this field mapping at the bottom of the Match Fields screen and enter a name and description.

If you add columns to a spreadsheet that already has a saved mapping, put them after the previously mapped columns. You can then load the mapping, match the new fields and select Update this field mapping if you want to save those additions. Otherwise, leave the saved mapping unchanged. If you insert new columns before the previously mapped ones, you cannot use the saved mapping and must map all the fields again.

docs.title: Import contacts
docs.text:
1. Preview the import

Check the number of rows to be imported and the field matches shown in the preview. If rows do not meet CiviCRM's field requirements, the screen reports how many are invalid. Select Download Errors and review the downloaded file so you can fix those rows before importing.

At the bottom of the form, you can add contacts to an existing group, import them to a new group, create a new tag or tag imported records. A separate group for the import is strongly recommended: it helps you find the contacts quickly and, if necessary, delete and reimport them. Remember that all contacts in a single import receive the same selected groups and tags.

docs.title: Import contacts
docs.text:
1. Check the summary and records

The final screen reports successful imports, Duplicate Contacts and Errors. If you added all imported contacts to a Group or Tag, you can follow the link to their records.

Search for the contacts you imported. Examine their fields and custom data to check that the import worked as expected.

docs.title: Import contact relationships
docs.text:
Use separate contact imports to link related contacts, such as a child and their parents. Other related data, including organisational addresses with employees, activities and contributions, also requires a separate CSV file for each type of data you import. CiviCRM has specific import tools for related contact data, contributions, memberships and event participation; see the chapters for those tools for their details.

For example, to import a child, father and mother, run three contact imports:

  1. Import the child with an external identifier that you can use to match them to their parents.
  2. Import the father as a related contact, linking him to the child with the child's external identifier.
  3. Import the mother as a related contact, linking her to the child in the same way.

The father and mother information in the example below is in one CSV file, used twice during the imports. The father is linked to the child by external identifier using the Child of relationship type.

After an import, search for the parent and examine the relationship tab. It should show a relationship linking the parent to the child. You can repeat the process for other relationships as needed.

docs.title: Requirements for other data imports
docs.text: Use this reference to check the minimum CSV fields for each type of import and the conditions that affect matching or updating records.

docs.title: Activities
docs.text:
Import action Minimum CSV fields Insert new activities Activity Date; Activity Type ID; Target Contact ID (Match to Contact); Subject Update existing activities Activity ID; Activity Date; Activity Type ID; Target Contact ID (Match to Contact); Subject

Target Contact ID attaches an activity to the contact it is done on. Import contacts before activities; these are separate import jobs.

docs.title: Contributions
docs.text:
You can insert new contributions or update existing ones. On a recent version of CiviCRM, enabling the Civi-Import extension also lets you create or update the contact and any soft credit contacts in the same import.

Import action Minimum CSV fields Insert new contributions Fields to match or create the contact; Financial Type; Total Amount Update existing contributions Transaction ID or Invoice ID or Payment ID, to match an existing contribution; Financial Type; Total Amount

Without Civi-Import, the contact fields needed to insert a contribution are Contact ID, External Identifier, or all fields used in your Unsupervised Duplicate Matching rule to match an existing contact. With Civi-Import enabled, those matching options still apply, but you can specify which Dedupe rule to use.

Update existing contributions can also add or change data in other core or custom contribution fields. Include an ID that matches an existing contribution, Financial Type and Total Amount in the CSV even if the latter two values are unchanged.

See Importing contributions in the Contributions chapter.

docs.title: Memberships
docs.text:
You can insert new memberships or update existing ones.

Import action Minimum CSV fields Insert new memberships Contact Id or External Identifier or all fields used in your Unsupervised Duplicate Matching rule, to match an existing contact; Membership Type; Membership Start Date Update existing memberships Membership Id, to match an existing membership; Membership Type; Membership Start Date

Update existing memberships can also add or change data in other core or custom membership fields. Include Membership ID, Membership Type and Membership Start Date in the CSV even if the latter two values are unchanged.

See Importing memberships in the Memberships chapter.

docs.title: Participants
docs.text:
Each import session can insert new registrations or update existing participant records.

Import action On duplicate entries setting Minimum CSV fields Insert new registrations, allowing only one registration per person for each event Skip Contact Id or External Identifier or all fields used in your Unsupervised Duplicate Matching rule, to match an existing contact; Event ID; Participant Status Insert new registrations, allowing duplicate registrations for the same contact and event No Duplicate Checking Contact Id or External Identifier or all fields used in your Unsupervised Duplicate Matching rule, to match an existing contact; Event ID; Participant Status Update existing registrations Update Participant ID, to match an existing registration; Event ID or Event Title; Participant Status

Update existing registrations can also add or change data in custom participant fields. Include Participant ID, Event ID or Event Title, and Participant Status in the CSV even if the latter values are unchanged.

docs.title: Tags
docs.text:
There is currently no inbuilt way to import tags or tag sets. An advanced extension can be used for this.

To assign individual tags during a contact import, either:

  • Split the CSV file by individual tags and import each subset separately.
  • Import tag information as standard data into temporary custom fields. After importing, use advanced searches to find contacts with particular values and mass tag them. You can remove the temporary custom fields when finished.

docs.title: Prepare contact data for import
docs.text: Use this guide to organise your source data, choose an import format and check details that could affect the results.

docs.title: Plan your data
docs.text:
CiviCRM can import data from sources such as older databases, spreadsheets and email address books. You can import core and custom contact data, as well as event attendance, activities, memberships and contributions. The steps on this page focus on preparing contacts; the processes for other types of data are similar.

Before preparing a file, read Organizing your data, especially Mapping your data into CiviCRM. You need to understand how your existing data relates to CiviCRM fields before you import it. The sections of this manual about each type of data can help you plan that mapping.

You can import from:

  • A CSV file. Most database and spreadsheet applications, including OpenOffice.org Calc, Google Spreadsheets and Microsoft Excel, can create or work with CSV files. A CSV file can make it easier to inspect and clean data than working in your old database.
  • An SQL query against another SQL or MySQL database stored on the same server. This option is for advanced users who understand server and database administration.

docs.title: Set up your CSV columns
docs.text:
Give each distinct piece of information its own column. For example, CiviCRM stores First Name and Last Name separately, as it does city and postal code/zip code. Most spreadsheet programs have tools for splitting text across columns.

Plan your column headings around the data you are collecting. You may need more than one CSV file and more than one import.

Check these details before importing:

  • Use country names as they appear in CiviCRM: for example, United States rather than United States of America, and United Kingdom rather than Britain.
  • Use an accepted date format in your data source. Select the same date format on the import wizard's Choose Data Source screen.
  • Set up any name prefixes and suffixes you use under Administer > Option Lists in the navigation menu.
  • If your CSV fields are separated by semicolons (;) rather than commas, change Import/Export Field Separator in the CiviCRM Localization settings. In the navigation menu, choose Administer > Configure > Global Settings > Localization.

docs.title: Check fields that need particular care
docs.text:
Multiple-choice fields. For a custom field with choices, such as check-boxes or radio buttons, your source data can use either the label shown to users or the value stored in the database. For a multiple-choice core data field, use the value, not the label. Separate multiple choices with a comma: for example, 1, 2, 3 or fred, red, yellow.

Updating multiple choices. New values replace the entire field. If a contact's Colors field is blue and you update it to orange, the result is orange, not both orange and blue.

Multiple locations. The first imported location becomes the primary location address. Arrange your columns so the intended location comes first. You may need separate imports if different records need different types of primary location. If you choose the location type Primary for an address field, it updates an existing contact's primary address if one exists. For a new contact, or one without an existing address, the location type becomes your site's default.

Master Address Belongs To. This special import field works only with CiviCRM_Address.id. The information needed to use it is available directly from the MySQL database tables, not from CiviCRM data screens, link URLs, profiles or exports. See the Wiki information on using this field.

docs.title: Plan for later imports
docs.text:
If you will import related data, such as contributions, event participation or memberships, give contacts unique IDs that also appear in that related data. In the initial contact import, map those IDs to CiviCRM's External ID field. You can then use the original IDs to match related data to contacts in later imports.

Alternatively, when preparing related data for a specific contact, the contact record should have First Name, Last Name and Email so that you can link the data during later imports.

Each import can add all its contacts to new or existing groups or tags, but every contact in that import receives the same groups and tags. Assign only groups and tags that apply to the whole batch. If assignments differ by contact, you can:

  • Import smaller batches whose contacts share the same groups and tags.
  • Import the intended assignments into searchable custom data fields. Afterward, search those fields and use the Add Contacts to Group or Tag Contacts batch actions on the results.

A group or tag can also identify which batch contacts came from. This helps you find when they were imported and undo an entire import if necessary.

docs.title: Check a small import first
docs.text:
Test with a small subset of records. After importing it, visit the records in CiviCRM and check that the data was imported and works as expected. A test contact containing every attribute in your existing data set can help you check how CiviCRM represents each one.

If an import times out or takes too long, try smaller batches. If you have the appropriate permissions on your web server, you can also increase memory_limit and max_execution_time in php.ini.

docs.title: Consider address standardisation
docs.text: Consistent addresses can make address searches more accurate. In the US, standardisation means following the United States Postal Service's Standards for Addresses. CiviCRM can parse addresses based on USPS standards if you choose to use that option. See the Installation chapter of the Configuration section of this manual for more about Address Parsing. When adding or editing contacts, enter elements such as street number, street name and Apt/Unit/Suite number according to those standards.

docs.title: Create a print/merge document
docs.text:
Use Print/merge document to create letters for selected contacts directly in CiviCRM. You can insert database-field tokens, save the letter as a template and choose its output format.

Generating a large number of letters can be resource intensive, particularly with PDF output. If this happens, consider the wkhtmltopdf alternate PDF generation tool, which scales to higher volumes better than the default tool. See Administer > Misc > Path to wkhtmltopdf executable for implementation details.

  1. Find the recipients using Search > Find Contacts > Advanced Search or a Custom Search. For members of a Group, go to Contacts > Manage Groups and click “Contacts” next to that Group.
  2. Enter your search criteria and click Search. Skip this step if you used a Group.
  3. Select the contacts who will receive the letter.
  4. Choose Print/merge document from the Actions dropdown menu.
  5. Optionally select a template as the basis for your letter.
  6. Optionally associate the letter with a Campaign.
  7. Review Page Format and adjust the paper size, margins or page orientation as needed.
  8. Enter your letter in the WYSIWYG editor and make any formatting adjustments. You can also insert an image, such as your organisation’s logo or a signature: click where it should appear in the letter, then click the Image icon.
  9. To personalise the letter, click where a token should appear, then choose it from the Insert Tokens dropdown above the letter at the top right. Tokens are placeholders replaced by field values for each selected contact; Postal Greeting is a commonly used example.

  1. If you will reuse the letter, save it as a new template. If you started from a template, you can instead update that template.
  2. Select an output format: PDF, HTML, MS Word (.docx) or Open Document (.odt). Some formats may handle complex layouts and designs better than others.
  3. Click Download Document to generate the letters. Depending on your browser configuration, a pop-up may ask where to save the file, or you may be prompted to open it immediately.
  4. Review the downloaded file to check its formatting. The window remains open so you can adjust the letter and generate it again.

You can also use Print/merge document for other documents, such as attendance certificates for a workshop. The action is available from the Actions dropdown in a contact record. For contributions, use the Thank you letters search result action after using Find Contributions.

docs.title: Generate mailing labels
docs.text:
Use CiviCRM to prepare address labels for a postal mailing to selected contacts.

The option to exclude people with “do not mail” checked in their privacy options is selected by default and is recommended. Check this option before generating labels.

  1. Search for the contacts you want to target.
  2. Choose Mailing Labels from the Actions dropdown menu and click Go.
  3. Select the mailing label style.
  4. Decide whether to exclude people with “do not mail” checked.
  5. Decide whether to merge records with the same mailing address into one label.

Merging records at the same address can prevent duplicate mailings to households or organisations. Each name at that address appears on a separate line of the label.

Your system administrator can configure which fields appear on mailing labels. See the information about configuring address settings in the Contacts chapter for the available options.

docs.title: Plan postal mail communications
docs.text: CiviCRM supports several ways to prepare postal mail. Your choice depends on whom you are mailing and whether each item needs personalised content.

docs.title: Questions to consider
docs.text:
Before preparing a mailing, decide:

  • What types of mailing does your organisation send?
  • Will the mailing go to everyone in the database or to a selected group of contacts?
  • How should you greet recipients—for example, “Dear Jane” or “Dear Jane Doe”?

A strong understanding of CiviCRM searches, custom fields, activities and profiles, as well as mail merges in word processing software, will help with these workflows.

docs.title: Choose a method
docs.text:
• Generate mailing labels when the content does not need to be personalised, such as when sending a printed brochure.
  • Export contacts for a mail merge in a tool such as OpenOffice or Microsoft Word. See Exporting for detailed export instructions.
  • Use Print/merge document to merge letters directly in CiviCRM.

If your organisation needs to sort recipients by zip code for bulk mailing in the USA, create the labels in a word processor where you can control the sort order, rather than in CiviCRM. You can reuse the same spreadsheet for the mail merge.

docs.title: Postal greetings
docs.text:
You can set a postal greeting format for each contact, from “Dear John” to the more formal “Dear Mr. John Doe”. You can also enter a customized greeting, such as “Your royal highness”. Edit postal greetings in the Communications Preferences section of the contact edit form.

To set or reset postal greetings for many contacts, see Scheduled Jobs and the documentation on updating greetings and address data.

docs.title: Tokens and mail merge
docs.text: Use this page to look up how CiviCRM tokens insert database values into emails and printed materials, and to find token examples and link formats.

docs.title: How tokens work
docs.text: Tokens represent fields in your CiviCRM database. You can use them to mail merge emails and printed materials, such as letters and mailing labels. For example, a Postal Greeting token can add a customised greeting to each recipient’s PDF letter. Most contact fields, including custom fields created for your site, are available as mail merge tokens.

docs.title: Contact data tokens
docs.text:
To address each email recipient by first name, type Dear in the HTML Format field, then use Insert Tokens at the top right to find and select “First name”. After you click Close, the message reads Dear {firstname}. CiviCRM inserts the appropriate first name when each email is sent.

Browse the Insert Tokens pop-up for the available contact data tokens, including custom fields created for your site.

docs.title: Organisation tokens
docs.text: You can insert standard organisation information. For example, “Domain (organizational) address” displays the address defined at Administer > Communications > Organization Address and Contact Info.

docs.title: Tokens in emails
docs.text:
Emails can use additional tokens, including action tokens for links that let recipients opt out or unsubscribe. Some tokens, such as one that links to a message stored online, are available only for mass mailings.

Note: In the HTML format editing area, put tokens that generate URLs in the URL field of the Link creation screen. Otherwise, the recipient’s email client displays the URL as text rather than a clickable link.

docs.title: Action tokens
docs.text: Action tokens can insert links for actions such as opting out and unsubscribing. To display these links properly in HTML messages, add the appropriate link tags using the editor’s Source icon.

docs.title: Required tokens for CiviMail mailings
docs.text:
Every CiviMail mailing must include either the opt-out token, {action.optOutUrl} or the unsubscribe token, {action.unsubscribeUrl}, and the organisational address token, {domain.address}. Put them in the mailing body, header or footer. If your organisation uses a standard mailing footer, including the tokens there means people do not have to add them to each new mailing.

Clickable unsubscribe and opt-out links are generally friendlier for recipients than the reply-to email method. You can provide both options. See the entries for the opt-out token, unsubscribe token and organisational address token below.

docs.title: Checksum links
docs.text:
A checksum lets you send someone a link to a contribution form, profile, petition or event registration form pre-filled with information already in their contact record. This can save them from entering the same information again. You can also ask people to review and update their contact information.

Warning: Checksum links last for seven days from the time the email is sent. You can change this duration at Administer > System Settings > Misc (Undelete, PDFs, Limits, Logging, etc.), but use caution: anyone with a link that remains valid can access that user’s account. In some cases, this could give them full account access for a long period.

In a CiviMail message, a link containing {contact.checksum} lets CiviCRM identify the recipient and pre-fill available information on the contribution form or profile. The token {contact.checksum} supplies the full cs=checksum value, so do not add cs= to the URL yourself. {contact.checksum_value} supplies only the checksum.

For tokens used with Form Builder, see the secret links section in creating new forms.

docs.title: Contribution pages
docs.text:
In these paths, IDNUMBER is the ID of the contribution page:

  • Drupal: http://example.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • Joomla!: http://example.org/index.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/contribute/transact&reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (with Clean URLs): http://example.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (without Clean URLs): http://example.org/?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/contribute/transact&reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}

docs.title: Membership renewal contribution pages
docs.text:
In these paths, IDNUMBER is the ID of the contribution page. These links are typically used in Scheduled Reminders for membership renewals, where membership.id is evaluated to the membership being renewed:

  • Backdrop/Drupal: http://example.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}&mid={membership.id}
  • Joomla!: http://example.org/index.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/contribute/transact&reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}&mid={membership.id}
  • WordPress (with Clean URLs): http://example.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}&mid={membership.id}
  • WordPress (without Clean URLs): http://example.org/?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/contribute/transact&reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}&mid={membership.id}

docs.title: Standard Profiles
docs.text:
In these paths, IDNUMBER is the ID of the Profile:

  • Drupal: http://example.org/civicrm/profile/edit?reset=1&gid=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&id={contact.contact_id}
  • Joomla!: http://example.org/index.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/profile/edit&reset=1&gid=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&id={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (with Clean URLs): http://example.org/civicrm/profile/edit?reset=1&gid=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&id={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (without Clean URLs): http://example.org/?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/profile/edit&reset=1&gid=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&id={contact.contact_id}

docs.title: Event registration pages
docs.text:
In these paths, IDNUMBER is the ID of the event:

  • Drupal: http://example.org/civicrm/event/register?reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • Joomla!: http://example.org/index.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/event/register&reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (with Clean URLs): http://example.org/civicrm/event/register?reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (without Clean URLS): http://example.org/?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/event/register&reset=1&id=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}

docs.title: Petition signature pages
docs.text:
In these paths, IDNUMBER is the ID of the petition:

  • Drupal: http://example.org/civicrm/petition/sign?reset=1&sid=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • Joomla!: http://example.org/index.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/petition/sign&reset=1&sid=IDNUMBER&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (with Clean URLs): http://example.org/civicrm/petition/sign?sid=IDNUMBER&reset=1&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (without Clean URLS): http://example.org/?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/petition/sign&sid=IDNUMBER&reset=1&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}

docs.title: CiviMail view-in-browser links
docs.text:
These CiviMail links let contacts view an email in their browser, including content personalised with tokens:

  • Drupal: http://example.org/civicrm/mailing/view?reset=1&id={mailing.key}&cid={contact.contact_id}&{contact.checksum}
  • Joomla!: http://example.org/index.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/mailing/view&id={mailing.key}&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (with Clean URLs): http://example.org/civicrm/mailing/view?id={mailing.key}&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}
  • WordPress (without Clean URLS): http://example.org/?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/mailing/view&id={mailing.key}&{contact.checksum}&cid={contact.contact_id}

docs.title: Site tokens
docs.text:
Starting in CiviCRM 5.76, Site Tokens let site administrators define pre-set snippets for content that uses CiviCRM’s standard token-handling features. Site Tokens marked “reserved” are also inserted automatically in specific places, such as Message Templates.

For example, {site.message_header} is inserted automatically at the top of every Message Template. Its default value is empty. An administrator can give it content such as an organisation logo or other branding without editing each Message Template directly. Administrators can also create any number of additional Site Tokens.

Site Tokens appear in the Insert Tokens utility under “Site”. For example, a Site Token labelled “Lorem Ipsum” becomes available when creating an email:

Users with the “edit system workflow message templates” permission can manage Site Tokens at Administer > Communications > Site Tokens. See Available tokens for the Site Token listed in this page.

docs.title: Custom tokens
docs.text: Developers can create custom tokens—for example, to display a contact’s total contributions. See the Developer Guide on custom tokens.

docs.title: Date tokens
docs.text:
Dates and times can use full words, abbreviations, numbers and different regional formats, such as MM/DD/YYYY and DD/MM/YYYY. An administrator may configure date preferences during system setup. Tokens such as {event.start_date}, {domain.now} and {contact.created_date} are formatted automatically according to those preferences.

From CiviCRM v5.43+, the |crmDate filter lets you format an individual date token. The examples below use {domain.now}.

docs.title: Configured formats
docs.text:
CiviCRM includes approximately seven configurable formats. On new deployments, the initial configuration follows English (US) conventions; organisations often adjust it for their language and locale.

Format name Example token Example value (US English) “Complete Date and Time” (default) {domain.now|crmDate:"Datetime"} September 18th, 2022 11:58 PM “Complete Date” (default) {domain.now|crmDate:"Full"} September 19th, 2022 “Short Date” {domain.now|crmDate:"shortdate"} 09/18/2022 “Month and Year” {domain.now|crmDate:"Partial"} September, 2022 “Time Only” {domain.now|crmDate:"Time"} 1:34 PM “Year Only” {domain.now|crmDate:"Year"} 2022 “Financial Batch” {domain.now|crmDate:"FinancialBatch"} 09/19/2022

docs.title: Ad hoc formats
docs.text:
Ad hoc formatting codes can specify details such as the month, day, year, day of the week, day of the year, week of the year and time zone.

Example token Example value {domain.now|crmDate:"%B %Y"} September 2022 {domain.now|crmDate:"%m/%Y"} 09/2022 {domain.now|crmDate:"%l:%M %P"} 1:34 PM

For the full list of formatting codes, see the PHP Manual: strftime().

docs.title: Smarty in mail templates
docs.text:
Mail templates use Smarty to include variables, tokens and functions. See the Smarty manual for a tutorial, including if/then logic.

Warning — system administrator required: For Smarty to work, a system administrator must add or modify the following line in civicrm.settings.php. The file is under sites/default/ for Drupal and administrator/components/com_civicrm for Joomla.

phpdefine('CIVICRM_MAIL_SMARTY', 1);

You can use CiviCRM tokens within Smarty. To check whether a field has a value before using it, use the |boolean modifier:

{if {contact.email_primary.email|boolean}}
  Email: {contact.email_primary.email|boolean}
{/if}

docs.title: Token modifiers
docs.text:
Add a modifier after a pipe in a CiviCRM token. For example, {contribution.total_amount} is a token to which a modifier could be added.

Modifier Effect upper Uppercase lower Lowercase capitalize Title case, with each word capitalised boolean Returns 0 or 1 crmDate Formats a date; see Date Tokens default Returns the value if it exists and is not falsy in PHP; otherwise returns the value you provide. For example, {contact.first_name|default:"friend"} returns friend when the contact has no first name.

docs.title: CiviMail click tracking for tokenised links
docs.text:
Up to CiviCRM version 5.34, CiviMail did not track clicks on links containing tokens. From version 5.35, the FlexMailer extension shipped with CiviCRM can track links with tokens in URL query parameters.

For example, a personalised Contribution Page link can pre-fill fields for its recipient:

<a href="https://example.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=1&cid={contact.contact_id}&{contact.checksum}">Donate now</a>

Here, cid uses {contact.contact_id}, and {contact.checksum} generates code such as cs=aaaaaaaaaaaaa.... The mailing report counts clicks on Donate now and lists the tracked link without the tokens: https://example.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=1.

The following rules describe tracking and the safety of links containing tokens:

  • Token location: Tokens in the query part of a URL can be tracked. Tokens in the domain, path or entire URL cannot.
  • Tracked: https://example.org/somepage?magic={some.token}
  • Not tracked—token in domain: https://{some.token}.org/
  • Not tracked—token in path: https://example.org/{some.token}
  • Not tracked—token is the whole URL: {some.token}
  • Mixed query parameters: Query parameters with and without tokens can appear in any of these orders:
  • https://example.org/somepage?magic={some.token}&x=1&y=two
  • https://example.org/somepage?x=1&y=two&magic={some.token}
  • https://example.org/somepage?x=1&magic={some.token}&y=two
  • Fragments: Tokens can appear in a URL fragment, but the fragment is not included in the tracked part of the URL:
  • https://example.org/spa#{some.token}
  • https://example.org/spa?cid={contact.id}#{some.token}
  • URL safety: A token’s expanded value must be URL-safe. This does not determine whether a link is tracked, but an unsafe value can break a link or pose a security risk.
  • URL-safe: https://example.org/somepage?cid={contact.id} — a Contact ID is a number.
  • Not reliably URL-safe: https://example.org/somepage?cid={contact.first_name} — a first name could contain other characters.
  • Depends on the custom token: https://example.org/somepage?mycustom={mycustom.token} — its code would need to output URL-safe data, such as a numeric ID, a hex hash or a rawurlencoded value.
  • CMS safety: The expanded value must also be safe for the CMS:
  • https://drupal.example.org/?q={some.token} — Drupal uses q for its own purposes. This could be valid in special cases where the token is a valid Drupal path.
  • https://wordpress.example.org/?action={some.token} — WordPress has many reserved terms that are not allowed.

docs.title: Available tokens
docs.text: The entries below give each token’s listed purpose, where it can be used and an example. Where the source does not confirm every possible location, that uncertainty is retained.

docs.title: {action.optOutUrl}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides an opt-out link for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: You can also <a href="{action.optOutUrl}" >opt-out of all future mailings from us</a>.

docs.title: {action.optOut}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides an opt-out email address for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: To opt-out of all mailings from us, send mail to {action.optOut}.

docs.title: {action.reply}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides a reply-to email address for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: To reply to this mailing, send mail to {action.reply}.

docs.title: {action.resubscribeUrl}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides a re-subscribe link for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: You may <a href="{action.resubscribeUrl}" >resubscribe to this mailing</a> at any time.

docs.title: {action.resubscribe}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides a re-subscribe email address for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: To resubscribe to this mailing, send mail to {action.resubscribe}.

docs.title: {action.subscribe.gid}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides an email address to subscribe to a specific group.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer.
  • Example: To subscribe to our Monthly Newsletter, send mail to {action.subscribe}.

docs.title: {action.subscribeUrl.gid}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides a link to subscribe to a specific group; gid is that group’s CiviCRM ID.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer.
  • Example: You can <a href="{action.subscribeUrl.2}" >subscribe to our Monthly Newsletter</a>.

docs.title: {action.subscribeUrl}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides a link to view and subscribe to any public mailing lists.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer.
  • Example: If you’re interested, <a href="{action.subscribeUrl}" >view all our mailing lists and sign up!</a>.

docs.title: {action.unsubscribeUrl}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides an unsubscribe link for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: You can <a href="{action.unsubscribeUrl}" >unsubscribe from this mailing</a> at any time.

docs.title: {action.unsubscribe}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Provides an unsubscribe email address for each recipient.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Unsubscribe, Resubscribe.
  • Example: To unsubscribe from this mailing, send mail to {action.unsubscribe}.

docs.title: {contact.custom_nn}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the content of custom contact field nn.
  • Used in: Mailing Body and Subject; use elsewhere is uncertain.
  • Example: Thanks for indicating your interest in {contact.custom_1}. We will keep you updated on that topic.

docs.title: {contribution.custom_nn}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the content of custom field nn for the contribution.
  • Used in: Mailing Body and Subject; use elsewhere is uncertain.
  • Example: Thanks for indicating that if your first choice for where we should use your contribution is {contribution.custom_42}.|

docs.title: {domain.address}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the postal address for your domain.
  • Used in: Mailing Body or any message templates.
  • Example: Mailing Address: {domain.address}

docs.title: {domain.email}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays your domain’s email address.
  • Used in: Mailing Body or any message templates.
  • Example: Or send a mail to {domain.email}.

docs.title: {domain.name}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays your domain name.
  • Used in: Mailing Body or any message templates.
  • Example: This mailing is from {domain.name}.

docs.title: {domain.phone}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays your domain’s phone number.
  • Used in: Mailing Body or any message templates.
  • Example: To contact us call {domain.phone}.

docs.title: {mailing.group}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Lists the names of the groups to which a mailing has been sent.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Resubscribe, Unsubscribe or Optout.
  • Example: This mailing has been sent to the members of {mailing.group}.

docs.title: {mailing.name}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the mailing name.
  • Used in: Mailing Body, Header, Footer, Resubscribe, Unsubscribe or Optout.
  • Example: Name of this mailing is {mailing.name}.

docs.title: {mailing.viewUrl}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Creates a “View in Browser” URL.
  • Used in: Mailing Body.
  • Example: Can’t see this email? <a href="{mailing.viewUrl}"><strong>View in Browser</strong></a>

docs.title: {resubscribe.group}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the group name in re-subscribe messages.
  • Used in: Resubscribe Message.
  • Example: As requested, you have been resubscribed to {resubscribe.group}.

docs.title: {site.message_header}
docs.text:
• Listed purpose: Displays the newly joined group name in a welcome message. The source also describes this token as the automatically inserted header for Message Templates; see Site tokens.
  • Used in: Default Message Templates automatically; anywhere tokens are provided.
  • Default value: Empty.
  • Example customised value: <h4>CiviCRM<\h4><img src="https://drupal.example.org/sites/all/modules/civicrm/i/logo_lg.png">

docs.title: {subscribe.group}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the group name in subscription confirmation requests.
  • Used in: Subscription confirmation request.
  • Example: You requested to be subscribed to the {subscribe.group}.

docs.title: {unsubscribe.group}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the group name in unsubscribe confirmation messages.
  • Used in: Unsubscribe Message.
  • Example: You have been unsubscribed from {unsubscribe.group}.

docs.title: {welcome.group}
docs.text:
• Purpose: Displays the newly joined group name in a welcome message.
  • Used in: Welcome Message.
  • Example: Welcome to {welcome.group}.

docs.title: Accounting batch screens and statuses
docs.text: Use this page to check what an accounting batch screen shows, how to find batches or their transactions, and which actions are available for each status.

docs.title: Transaction assignment screen
docs.text:
The top of the transaction assignment screen displays these batch details:

  • CREATED BY
  • STATUS: Open, Closed, or Exported
  • DESCRIPTION entered when the batch was created
  • Specified PAYMENT METHOD
  • Number of ENTERED TRANSACTIONS
  • Number of ASSIGNED TRANSACTIONS
  • ENTERED TOTAL amount of the transactions
  • ASSIGNED TOTAL amount, which updates as transactions are assigned
  • Date the batch was OPENED

Below these details is the Assigned Transactions list. It is empty until transactions are assigned. Its action drop-down is unavailable until then. Edit Search Criteria opens the search pane, and search results appear at the bottom of the page.

docs.title: Find batches
docs.text:
Go to Contributions > Accounting Batches and select Open Batches to reach the Accounting Batch main page. You can filter the displayed batches by Status (Open, Closed, or Exported), Batch Name, the User who created the batch, Payment Instrument, entered number of transactions, or entered total amount.

Status Available actions Open Select Transactions to assign or remove transactions, or Edit to change batch parameters. Under more, you can close, export, or delete the batch. Closed Select Transactions to view assigned transactions, or Export to export them to a CSV or IFF export file. Under more, you can re-open or delete the batch. Exported Select Transactions to view assigned transactions, Download to export the CSV or IIF file of assigned transactions, or Delete to delete the batch. An Exported batch cannot be re-opened.

To act on more than one batch from the search results page, select the batches and choose Re-open, Close, Export, or Delete from the action drop-down menu.

docs.title: Find transactions by batch
docs.text: In the Advanced Search Contribution pane or Find Contributions, search by Batch Name. Select a batch to return all transactions stored in it.

docs.title: Create and export an accounting batch
docs.text: Use an accounting batch to export the double-entry financial transactions for a group of contributions so you can import them into your accounting software. You can create a batch from existing transactions or use one created through Batch Data Entry.

docs.title: Use a batch from Batch Data Entry
docs.text: If you entered transactions through Batch Data Entry, follow Manual Entry of Contributions to validate and close the batch. It will then appear in the accounting batch listing with a status of Closed, ready for export.

docs.title: Create a batch from existing transactions
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Accounting Batches.
  2. Select New Batch. The batch creation screen opens.
  1. Enter the required Batch Name. CiviCRM supplies a default of "Batch N" plus the open date, which you can edit.
  2. If needed, enter a Description of the Batch.
  3. If the batch should contain only transactions paid by one Payment Instrument, select it from the drop-down list. The options include Credit Card, Debit Card, Check, Cash, EFT, and any custom Payment Instruments your organisation has set up.
  4. If you know how many transactions the batch will contain, enter the Number of Transactions.
  5. If you know their total in advance, enter the Total Amount.
  6. Select Save. The transaction assignment screen opens.

You can edit these batch parameters later while the batch remains Open. When you close the batch, CiviCRM checks any entered Number of Transactions and Total Amount against the assigned transactions; you can override a mismatch warning.

docs.title: Assign transactions
docs.text:
You can use the transaction assignment screen after creating a batch or opening an existing one.

  1. Open Edit Search Criteria.
  2. Specify the criteria for the contributions you want to add. If you selected a Payment Instrument when creating the batch, it is selected by default.
  3. Assign transactions from the search results:
  4. For one transaction, select Assign at the end of its row.
  5. For multiple transactions, select them and choose Assign to Batch from the action menu above the results.

Assigned transactions appear in the Assigned Transactions list and disappear from the search results. The assigned transaction count and total at the top of the screen update.

If you need to remove a transaction, select Remove at the end of its row in the Assigned Transactions list. To remove several, select them and choose Remove from Batch from the action menu above that list.

You can leave the batch and return to it later from the Accounting Batch main page. Its status remains Open.

docs.title: Close or export the batch
docs.text:
Before closing: If the assigned transaction count or total differs from an entered Number of Transactions or Total Amount, CiviCRM displays a "Mismatch" error. You can dismiss it and correct the batch, or select OK to override it. Overriding updates the entered count and total to match the assigned count and total, then closes the batch.

Once you have finished assigning transactions, choose whether to Close the batch or Close and Export it.

  • Close changes its status to Closed without exporting. You can re-open it before exporting, or export the transactions later.
  • Close and Export lets you choose CSV or IIF. CSV produces a spreadsheet of comma-separated values. IIF produces a file in Intuit Interchange Format, used by Intuit products such as Quickbooks to import transactions. After export, the status changes to Exported, and you cannot re-open the batch.

docs.title: Create a contribution form with FormBuilder
docs.text:
Use FormBuilder to create a form for contributions to your organisation. You can start with a simple donation form or create a checkout experience that includes donations, paid memberships and/or event registrations.

New functionality

Creating Contribution Forms using FormBuilder is a new alternative to Contribution Pages. You can help with development by raising issues or feature requests on the CiviCRM Issue Tracker.

docs.title: Before you begin
docs.text:
• FormBuilder Contributions is available in CiviCRM 6.14. Upgrade to at least this version before you start.
  • Install a Payment Processor extension that supports FormBuilder Contributions. At the time of writing, the main supported integrations are Paypal Complete Payments and Stripe; more may become available. Check the available Checkout Options.
  • Configure a Payment Processor connection for your chosen processor. The steps vary: you may need to log in on a connection page or copy an API key from your account with the Payment Processor.
  • If you have not already enabled the FormBuilder extension, enable it to edit forms through the UI.

Familiarity with using FormBuilder will help, especially if your form includes multiple entities such as Memberships or Event Registrations.

docs.title: Set up the starter donation form
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > CiviContribute > CiviContribute Component Settings and enable FormBuilder Contributions functionality for your site.
  2. Open the starter donation form at https://my.example.site/civicrm/donate. A simple donation form should now be available.

The starter form uses the Pay Later Checkout Option by default. To offer another way to pay, either set your preferred Checkout Option, such as Stripe Embedded Checkout, or add Checkout Option as a field so users can choose.

You can add fields to the Individual entity, or add Contribution fields such as Contribution Source. You can also rearrange inputs and add Rich Content elements to change the form’s appearance. When the form is ready, test it.

docs.title: Use Test Mode
docs.text: To use Test Mode for Contributions created through the form, add testMode=1 to its URL, for example: https://my.example.site/civicrm/donate?testMode=1. This uses the Test connection configured for the selected Checkout Option / Payment Processor.

docs.title: Offer recurring contributions
docs.text: To let users set up a Recurring Contribution, use the Recur Period field on the Contribution entity. Set a fixed value on the left-hand side, or add it as a field input so users can choose an option.

docs.title: Add a thank you message or page
docs.text: Use the Confirmation Type setting on the Form Settings tab to show a confirmation message or redirect to another URL for a thank you page. You can include tokens from the form submission to personalise the message or redirect URL, for example Thank you {Individual1.0.first_name}! or https://my.example.site/thank-you?contribution_id={Contribution1.0.id}.

docs.title: Create a new form
docs.text:
You may find it helpful to clone the civicrm/donate form: it should already meet the minimum requirements. For a form that takes payments, check all of the following:

  • Include a Contribution entity.
  • Include the Checkout Option field on the Contribution, either with a fixed value on the left-hand side or as a user input on the right-hand side.
  • Include the Checkout Details field on the Contribution. Always include it as a user input on the right-hand side.
  • Set Allowed Actions for the Contribution to either Create for a new Contribution or Update to take payment for a previously created contribution. Do not select both.
  • Include at least one Price Field, either as a fixed value on the left-hand side or as a form input on the right-hand side. It can be on the Contribution or a linked Membership or Participant entity. The starter form uses the simplest option, the Contribution Amount field.

docs.title: Available Checkout Options
docs.text: Option Extension Status Notes Stripe Embedded Checkout Stripe Working Requires version 6.16+ Stripe Hosted Checkout Stripe Working Requires version 6.16+ Paypal Complete Payments Paypal Working New extension HelloAsso HelloAsso Working Requires version 2.1.1+ Authnet AcceptJS Authnet Working in sandbox https://lab.civicrm.org/extensions/authnet/-/merge_requests/45 Authnet Credit Card Authnet Working in sandbox Renders form fields from Quickform metadata https://lab.civicrm.org/extensions/authnet/-/merge_requests/45

docs.title: Contribution Page settings
docs.text: Use this reference to find the settings available when you create or configure a Contribution Page. CiviContribute also offers optional features such as recurring Contributions, Pledges and Personal Campaign Pages.

docs.title: Title and Settings
docs.text:
Go to Contribution > New Contribution Page. Contribution > Manage Contribution Pages > Add Contribution Page opens the same screen.

Setting What it controls Page Title and Financial Type These are the only compulsory fields. CiviCRM comes with four standard Financial Types; you can create more for your organisation’s accounting needs. Campaign Optionally link the Contribution Page to a Campaign. Introductory Message and Footer Message Optional messages on the page. Goal Amount An optional goal for the page. Start Date and End Date These dates apply to a Contribution Widget and Personal Campaign Pages. You must still enable or disable the Contribution Page manually. Honoree soft crediting Choose whether to accept Honoree soft crediting. Confirmation page Choose whether visitors check their details on a confirmation page or payment is processed as soon as they submit the Contribution form. Social media links Choose whether to display links on online pages and in the automatically emailed receipt, if one is sent. Active Choose whether to make the Contribution Page active now.

Click Continue to save a new Contribution Page for the first time. You can return to the Title (and Settings) tab to change it later. The Amounts tab and the other feature tabs are then visible.

docs.title: Amounts tab
docs.text:
Setting What it controls Execute real-time monetary transactions Checked by default. Uncheck it for free membership signup, in-kind (non-monetary) donations, or a page where all users submit payments offline. Currency The currency for the page. Payment Processors Select one or more previously configured Payment Processors. You can offer a choice by configuring multiple processors and checking their boxes here. Pay Later Lets users submit payment offline, for example by mailing a cheque, calling in a credit card or depositing money into a bank account. If enabled, choose a checkbox label and instructions for delayed payments. Contribution Amounts Section Enabled If unchecked, the remaining fields on this tab disappear. You can then accept only fixed-amount membership fees or, with a membership Price Set, fixed-amount membership fees and other Contributions specified in that Price Set, all charged in a single transaction. Price Set or fixed amounts Select a predefined Price Set for more complex payment options, or enter up to 10 fixed Contribution amounts in the table at the bottom of the page. Recurring Contributions Available if your payment processor and its CiviCRM integration support recurring billing. Membership fees have restrictions on recurring payments. When enabled, further settings appear: you can set one frequency, such as monthly donations, or let users choose their interval and/or number of installments, such as once every three months for 12 installments. Pledges Lets users pledge future payments. Contribution amount label The label for the Contribution amount area on the page. Allow other amounts Lets users pay an amount they choose. You can set a minimum and maximum for “Other Amount” Contributions.

Click Save and Done when you have finished on this tab.

docs.title: Memberships tab
docs.text: See Memberships for details.

docs.title: Automatic Contribution recording
docs.text:
CiviCRM automatically records donations made through a Contribution Page. It adds a Contribution to an existing donor’s contact record or creates a new record if the donor does not already exist.

A Contribution can be credited to the wrong contact when people have multiple email addresses or share an email address. Adjusting CiviCRM’s default duplicate matching rules can reduce this risk; see Deduping and Merging.

docs.title: Add a Profile to a Contribution Page
docs.text: Use a CiviCRM Profile to collect information such as age, interests or skills at the beginning or end of a Contribution Page. You can select an existing Profile or create a new one.

docs.title: Check the Profile’s fields
docs.text:
