A Profile used on a Contribution Page can contain only fields belonging to Contact or Contribution records. Profiles containing fields from other record types are not available for this purpose.

A Contribution Page always has a required email address field. If none of its Profiles contains an email address field, CiviCRM adds one near the top of the form.

Each Profile appears as a fieldset. Its legend uses the Profile Public Title if one is set; otherwise, it uses the Profile Name. Names that identify Profiles in a list and Public Titles that work as form-section headers serve these different purposes.

docs.title: Include the Profile
docs.text:
Warning

Editing an existing Profile while configuring a Contribution Page changes that Profile everywhere it is used. Unless it exactly meets your needs, copy it, then rename and edit the copy.

  1. Go to Manage Contribution Pages and, for the page you want to configure, click Configure > Include Profiles.
  2. Select a CiviCRM Profile from the dropdown menu for the top and/or bottom of the Contribution Page.

  3. Preview your selection if needed. You can also edit or copy an existing Profile, or create a new one. The Profile drag-and-drop interface lets you click the pencil icon to edit its name, public Title, and pre- and post-form help text.

  4. Click Save, Save and Done or Save and Next.

docs.title: Address fields and billing address
docs.text:
Most payment processors add address fields alongside payment details and use them to save a billing address. If you put a Profile with address fields at the top of the Contribution Page, CiviCRM can add a checkbox indicating that the Billing Address is the same as the address entered in the Profile. When set up correctly, the checkbox is checked by default; unchecking it reveals billing name and address fields.

For the checkbox to hide and reveal the billing address fields:

  • Include the Profile at the top, not the bottom, of the page. The Include Profiles configuration page has a dropdown menu for each position.
  • Include the same fields as the Billing Address Profile: First Name, Last Name, Street Address, City, State, Postal Code and Country. Mark all these fields as required.

If the correct fields are present but are not marked required, the checkbox still appears, but the javascript does not work and the billing name and address fields remain visible.

docs.title: Advanced Profile settings
docs.text:
Some Advanced Settings take effect when a Profile is included in a Contribution Page. To change them, use the main Profile settings form; they cannot be edited from within the Contribution Page settings.

  • Adding contacts to a group: Bear in mind that many donors do not want to join a mailing list merely because they donated.
  • CMS User account registration options: A donor can be offered, or required, to log in or create a user account while making a Contribution.
  • Including ReCAPTCHA: A CAPTCHA can make it more difficult for bots and donors to submit the form.

Other advanced settings, such as what to do upon duplicate match, are ignored on Contribution Pages. For more information, see Profiles.

docs.title: Create and publish a Contribution Page
docs.text:
Set up a page where visitors can make Contributions to your organisation, then make it available on your website. You can start with a simple page and configure more features later.

Alternative: use Contribution Forms

Contribution Forms provide another way to take Contributions from visitors to your site. They are built with FormBuilder, which gives site admins more flexibility to tailor forms and provides more modern clientside payment integrations. At the time of writing, only a few Payment Processors are supported.

docs.title: Create a simple page
docs.text:
Make sure you have a payment processor configured before you begin.

  1. Go to Contributions > New Contribution Page.
  2. Enter the Title for your website page.
  3. Select the appropriate Financial Type.
  4. Click Continue. Your Contribution Page is saved, and you move to the next page.
  5. Leave the other settings as they are, except for ticking Allow Other Amounts. Set minimum and/or maximum amounts if you want to.

Choose how receipts will be sent:

  • Receipt from the payment processor only: Click Save and Done.
  • Receipt from your organisation as well: Click Save, then select the Receipt tab. Enter the Title for your Thank-you page, tick Email Receipt to Contributor, enter the FROM email address in Receipt From Email, and click Save and Done.

You can then display the page on your website.

docs.title: Customise thank-you and receipt emails
docs.text:
To edit an existing Contribution Page’s thank-you and receipt emails:

  1. Go to Administer > CiviContribute > Manage Contribution Pages.
  2. Use the Configure link to the right of the page in the list.
  3. Click Thank-you and Receipting and enter the information you want in the thank-you email.
  4. Click Save and Done.

Donors usually expect a receipt as soon as their transaction is complete, so enabling the automatic Email Receipt is recommended.

docs.title: Send staff email alerts
docs.text:
You can enter one or more staff email addresses in CC Receipt To or BCC Receipt To to receive real-time updates when someone processes a Contribution. Separate multiple addresses with commas.

Warning

Make sure addresses in CC Receipt To and BCC Receipt To are correct and do not bounce or return an error email. CiviCRM interprets a returned email as a bounce for the CiviCRM Contact who received the receipt, not for the CC/BCC address. The contact’s email address could be put On Hold, preventing future emails from being sent. See the issue report for details.

docs.title: Publicizing your Contribution Page
docs.text: Make the page easy to find on your website, for example through a donate button or menu item. The way you display it depends on your website’s CMS.

docs.title: Menu item in Joomla!
docs.text:
You can expose a Contribution Page or membership signup/renewal page through a menu item.

  1. Navigate to a menu and create a new CiviCRM item.
  2. Choose Contributions from the menu options.
  3. In the basic parameters section, select the contribution page from the dropdown menu.
  4. Save the menu item.
  5. View the website to confirm that the page works.

docs.title: Menu item in Drupal
docs.text: In the Contribution Page listing, select Live Page to view the finished page. Copy its URL into a content page or assign it to a menu item.

docs.title: Page or Post in WordPress
docs.text:
You can embed a Contribution Page in a Post or Page on your WordPress front-end site.

  1. Log in to your WordPress administration dashboard.
  2. Click Pages or Posts > Add New.
  3. Click the CiviCRM icon next to Upload / Insert.
  4. Select Contribution Page as your Frontend Element.
  5. Select the desired Contribution Page.
  6. Save the Page or Post. The Contribution Page is embedded within your site’s theme on that Page.

docs.title: Use a memorable URL
docs.text:
A CiviContribute Contribution Page URL can be difficult to remember, for example:

www.myorganization.org/civicrm/contribute/transact?reset=1&id=1

A URL redirect can give visitors a shorter address, such as:

www.myorganization.org/donate

For Drupal, the Path Redirect module lets you create redirects through its user interface without web server configuration. For Joomla!, if Search Engine Friendly URLs are enabled in Global Settings, you can create a menu link to the Contribution page and define the shorter URL using the alias field.

docs.title: Share the page by personalised email
docs.text: CiviMail lets you send targeted emails to groups of contacts and track how many people click a link to your Contribution form. You can also use checksum tokens to send each contact a personalised link that fills in their contact information on the form. This saves them from entering it again and can increase the chance that they donate.

docs.title: Find contributions
docs.text:
Use Find Contributions when you need results for individual contribution records rather than one result per contact.

CiviCRM distinguishes contributions from the people who made them. Before searching, consider which records your task needs. For example, if you are sending gifts to people who contributed in the last year, a contribution-based result could include two entries for someone who made two contributions. Whether that means sending two gifts depends on your approach.

docs.title: Search contribution records
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Find Contributions.

  1. Enter the criteria you need, such as Date Range, Contribution Amount or Contribution Status. You can use a relative Date Range such as "Last Month" or "Last Year".

  2. Run the search. Each returned contribution must match all the criteria you specified. For example, a search for the Financial Type "donation" and the Date Range "January 1st to May 31st" returns contributions that meet both criteria. Adding criteria narrows the results.

The results screen shows the matching records, Total Amount, Number of Contributions, Average Contribution Mean and Mode.

docs.title: Work with search results
docs.text:
Select all or a subset of the results, then choose an option from Actions:

  • Update multiple contributions: Update many contributions at once, such as setting their thank-you date. You must create the profile you want to use before searching and making the batch update.
  • Delete contributions: Removes contributions entirely, as if they had never been entered. Editing a contribution and changing its status to canceled provides a better audit trail. Deletion may be appropriate for a contribution entered on the wrong contact's record.
  • Export contributions: Exports one row per contribution, including when multiple contributions belong to the same contact. For a search that returns one result per contact, use the contact advanced search.
  • Receipts - Print or Email Contribution: Creates a PDF file of all receipts in the search or emails receipts to the associated donors. See "Sending thank you letters" for more information.
  • Email - send now: Sends an email to all or selected contacts found in the search.
  • Thank-you letters - print or email: Creates a custom PDF letter for each selected contribution, with the option to update its receipt or thank you date.
  • Record payments for contributions: Records payment details for all or selected online "Pay Later" contributions. This action works only for contributions with the status Pending (Pay Later).

docs.title: Search with additional criteria
docs.text: Advanced search returns contacts by default. To return contribution records instead, choose Contributions in Display Results As. Expand the Contribution pane for the standard contribution search criteria; you can also apply additional filters. For example, you could look for donations to a tax appeal made by members of your organisation, or contacts who contributed more than $100 last year AND live in California.

docs.title: CiviContribute dashboard
docs.text:
Use the CiviContribute dashboard to browse recorded contributions and compare contribution totals.

The CiviContribute main page, or dashboard, summarises contributions received in the current Month-To-Date, Year-To-Date and cumulatively since inception. The cumulative total includes all contribution records in your CiviCRM installation, whether recorded automatically or added manually. The dashboard also has buttons to manage and add contribution pages.

docs.title: Dashboard layouts
docs.text:
• Table Layout shows contribution summaries. The following screenshot shows the most recent contribution to a campaign using this tab:
  • Chart Layout shows bar or pie charts comparing contribution totals across months of a given year and across years:

You can also add any number of contribution Report Dashlets to your personal CiviCRM Dashboard. Examples include a bar chart of Year-To-Date contributions by Financial Type or month, and a list of the top 10 donors.

docs.title: Import contributions using Civi Import
docs.text:
Use Civi Import to bring contributions from a prepared data file into CiviCRM.

You need the Civi Import extension, which is shipped with CiviCRM, and a file containing the contributions you want to import. The file may come from a third party or be created within your organisation. For help installing extensions, see the Extensions section.

docs.title: Choose your file and import options
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions>Import Contributions.

  1. Under Choose Data Source, select your file format. This example uses Comma-Separated Values (CSV). You can also import from a spreadsheet (.odt or .xlsx files) or a SQL Query.

  2. Use the button next to Import Data File to select a file from your computer or network.

Note: If your CSV file contains special characters, it needs to be UTF8 encoded. See the Wikipedia definition for background.

Caution: Check how your file represents decimal amounts before choosing a field separator. If your file uses a comma (,) for decimal values, using a comma as the field separator can damage the amounts. You may want to use a semicolon (;) as the field separator instead.

  1. Specify the field separator used in your file.

  2. Select the contact type for the contributions. This example uses Individual because the contributions were made by individual people.

  3. Choose whether to create new contributions or update existing contributions. For this example, select insert new contributions.

  4. Select the date format used in your file. This example uses mm/dd/yy.

  5. If you have a saved field mapping, select it from saved field mapping. Leave it blank if you do not have one, as in this example.

  1. Select Continue to open the Match fields page.

docs.title: Match the fields
docs.text:
The Import to settings at the top of the Match fields page control how contributions and contacts are handled.

  1. Review the Contribution setting. Because this example inserts new contributions, it is set to Create and cannot be changed.

  2. Choose how to handle Contribution Contact. This example uses update or create contacts. You can instead match existing contacts or update existing contacts.

  3. Check the contact type. You selected Individual on the first screen, but you can change it here.

  4. Specify the dedupe rule for the import. For background, see Deduplication.

  5. Decide whether to import soft credits. This example does not import them. For background, see Soft credits.

  6. Match each imported Column Names field to its Matching CiviCRM Field so the data goes to the right place. Select do not import for any data you do not want to import.

  1. If a field needs a value when the input file has none, specify a Default value. In this example, Financial Type uses a default because the file has no data for it. The field must still exist in the import file, though it can be empty.

  2. If you want to reuse this mapping for files with the same data layout, tick Save this field mapping.

  3. When the mapping is ready, select Continue to see the preview.

docs.title: Import and review the results
docs.text:
1. Review the preview to see what will happen.
  1. If you are satisfied, select Import now.

The results show how many rows were imported successfully or how many had errors.

  1. Select See rows to view detailed results or errors.

  1. To review a specific contribution and its imported data, select its hyperlinked contribution ID number.

docs.title: Customize an invoice
docs.text: Use your organisation’s contact information and the invoice message template to change what appears on an Invoice.

docs.title: Change organisation details
docs.text: The out-of-the-box template code takes the Company Name, Address and Website Information shown at the top right of Invoices from Organization Address and Contact Info. Edit those details at Administer Console > Configuration Checklist > Organization Address and Contact Info.

docs.title: Change the appearance and image
docs.text:
Edit the look of the Invoice and its image at Administer > Communications > Message Templates > System Workflow Messages > Contributions-Invoice.

To change the image, modify the template code by replacing the image source (img src):

<td><img src = "{$resourceBase}/i/civi99.png" height = "34px" width
= "99px"></td>

For more advanced configuration with accounting software packages such as QuickBooks, involve your organisation’s bookkeeper or accountant when setting up Financial Types and Financial Accounts. See Accounting Integration and the Wiki Page for more information.

docs.title: Create an invoice
docs.text: Enable invoicing, then print or email an invoice from a contact’s contribution record.

docs.title: Enable invoicing
docs.text:
Invoicing works for all Financial Types and for Completed and Pending Contribution Statuses, but you must enable it first.

  1. Go to Administer > CiviContribute > CiviContribute Component Settings.
  2. Check Enable Tax and Invoicing.

On the same screen, you can also set:

  • A prefix for Invoices and Credit Notes
  • The interval of days, weeks, or years until the Due Date
  • Customized Notes or Standard Terms to appear on the Invoice

docs.title: Print or email an invoice
docs.text:
1. Go to the contact’s Contribution tab.
  2. View the Complete or Pending Contribution you want to invoice.

Note

You cannot add CC / BCC when you send an Invoice by email. If you need explicit CC / BCC fields, the invoicehelper extension provides them.

  1. Choose Print Invoice to download a PDF, or Email Invoice to open an options screen.

Before sending an Invoice by email, you can choose the From Email Address and type an additional message.

Here is an example of a printed Invoice. Invoices can be customized.

docs.title: Set up contribution tracking
docs.text:
Use your organisation’s income categories and data needs to decide which CiviContribute settings to use. If you plan to take payments online, you can also connect a payment processor.

  1. List the types of contributions your organisation receives, or wants to receive, and identify which you want to track in CiviCRM.

  2. Write down the information you need about contributions, including the reports you want to produce.

  3. Compare that list with CiviCRM’s predefined contribution fields by looking at the screen for adding a new contribution. Core fields already provide useful functionality, so avoid duplicating them with custom fields.

docs.title: Financial types and accounts
docs.text:
Consult your organisation’s bookkeeper or accountant before creating or changing financial types or financial accounts.

  1. To add a financial type, go to Administer > CiviContribute > Financial Types and select Add Financial Type.

CiviCRM creates a revenue account with the same name and links it, along with the default asset, expense and cost-of-sales accounts, to the new financial type.

  1. If you need different accounts for a financial type, select Accounts beside it at Administer > CiviContribute > Financial Types.

The preconfigured financial accounts suit many organisations, but you can change or add accounts if needed. Changing a financial account name also changes the financial type name. Keep that effect in mind before editing an account.

  1. To edit a financial account, go to Administer > CiviContribute > Financial Accounts.

Name and Financial Account Type are the only required fields. CiviCRM sets them for a revenue account when you create its financial type. The other fields depend on your workflow. If you will export financial transactions for your accounting software, enter the accounting code without extra or missing spaces. If you use Quickbooks, you also need the account type code.

You can control access to contribution data through CiviCRM’s role-based Financial Type permissions.

docs.title: Payments
docs.text:
To take online payments for fundraising campaigns, membership dues or event attendance, configure a payment processor. It connects your website to the credit card and banking infrastructure that processes payments.

  1. To change the payment methods available for contributions, go to Administer > CiviContribute > Payment Methods. You can edit an existing option or select Add Payment Methods. Credit card, cash, check, debit card and EFT are installed by default. Ask your accountant or bookkeeper to confirm that each payment method is linked to the correct Asset account.

If billing information is collected on the payment processor’s website, configure accepted credit cards and payment methods on that site.

  1. To change acceptable credit cards in CiviCRM, go to Administer > CiviContribute > Accepted Credit Cards. You can edit an existing option or select Add Accepted Credit Card.

docs.title: Additional contribution data
docs.text: If the predefined fields do not cover information your organisation needs to track, you can use custom data fields to further categorise contributions or record additional information. See Creating Custom Fields.

docs.title: Contribution statuses
docs.text:
Use these descriptions to interpret a contribution’s status in CiviCRM. Every contribution has one status.

Status Meaning Pending (Pay Later) The contribution has been entered, but payment has not been received. This is usually for payment by paper or electronic check. Pending (Incomplete) The contribution was entered in CiviCRM and sent for online processing, but payment was not completed at the processor or CiviCRM has not yet received its response. If a contribution remains in this status even though processing was completed, the communication between CiviCRM and the processor warrants investigation. Failed The contribution was entered in CiviCRM and forwarded for processing, but processing was declined, rejected or resulted in an error reported back to CiviCRM. Completed The contribution was entered in CiviCRM, payment was processed and a successful response was received.

Other statuses, such as In Progress, Overdue and Partially Paid, are used by optional features for partial payments and automatic recurring payments.

You can change Contribution Status labels at Administer > System Settings > Option Groups. Adding statuses is not recommended because it may interfere with CiviCRM’s accounting validation.

docs.title: Financial types and financial accounts
docs.text:
Learn how CiviCRM records contribution income and connects it to your organisation’s accounts.

Organisations need different levels of financial reporting. Some need only the total donation or membership income recorded in CiviCRM. Others need to export double-entry financial transactions for their accounting software. Financial types let you classify income without working directly with debits and credits, while CiviCRM still records those transactions.

Each contribution must have a financial type. A financial type is linked to financial accounts that can track income, assets, fees and premiums, where applicable. The following image shows the links for the four default financial types.

Financial accounts should be based on your organisation’s Chart of Accounts. When you save a contribution, CiviCRM automatically records the appropriate debits and credits in the accounts linked to its financial type. If you use price sets, each option can have a different financial type; CiviCRM records the appropriate transactions for all the linked accounts.

The standard financial types are event fee, member dues, donation and campaign contribution. You can change the existing setup or add financial types to suit your organisation.

Generally, you need one financial type for each kind of income you track separately in your accounts. For example, if you report tax appeal donations, festive appeal donations and recurring donations separately, a single “Donation” financial type will not be enough. You would need “Tax Appeal”, “Festive Appeal” and “Recurring Donations” financial types.

When you create a financial type, CiviCRM creates a revenue (income) account with the same name. It links that account and the default accounts for assets, expenses and cost of sales to the new financial type. This simplifies a setup with one Deposit Bank Account, one Accounts Receivable account and one Accounts Payable account, while allowing different accounts where needed.

docs.title: Enter payments in a batch
docs.text:
Use Batch Data Entry to record multiple offline Contribution, Membership or Pledge Payments. Its grid has ‘autocopy’ icons at the top of each column to help fill in field values, and you can check the batch’s item count and total amount against your deposit slip(s).

Each batch contains one payment type: Contribution Payments, Membership Payments or Pledge Payments. You can create contacts while entering a batch and save an unfinished batch to continue later.

docs.title: Create the batch
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Batch Data Entry or Membership > Batch Data Entry.
  1. Enter or edit the required Batch Name. CiviCRM supplies a default of “Batch N” plus the open date.
  2. Select the Type: Contribution, Membership or Pledge Payment. This selects the corresponding reserved profile for the Batch Entry Grid Screen: Contribution Batch Entry, Membership Batch Entry or Pledge Payment Batch Entry.
  3. Enter the required Number of items and Total amount for the payments in the batch. Status defaults to “Open”.

You can later return to the Bulk Data Entry screen and click Edit or Delete beside a batch. With the appropriate permissions, you can also edit the total amount and item count in its definition.

docs.title: Enter the payments
docs.text:
1. Enter a payment on each line of the batch entry grid.
  1. In Contact, start entering an existing contact’s name and select it from the potential matches. To create a contact instead, use the “-create new contact-“ drop-down to select New Individual, New Organization or New Household, then enter the contact’s information.
  2. Complete the payment fields for each line. When entering Membership Payments, you can add a new membership or renew an existing one. For Pledge Payments, you can assign a payment to any pending pledge for that contact. With the appropriate permissions, you can click adjust payment amount beside Amount to change the pledge payment’s amount or schedule.

docs.title: Save or process the batch
docs.text:
You can enter every transaction in one session or return later. Once a batch has a “closed status”, it is no longer editable. Check your entries before processing it.

  • To pause, click Save & Continue Later. To resume, go to Contributions > Batch Data Entry or Membership > Batch Data Entry, then click Enter Records beside the batch and continue entering payments.
  • When you have finished, click Validate & Process the Batch. A processed batch has the status “Closed” and is available for searches and reporting.

If the payment count or total does not match the values entered when the batch was created, CiviCRM alerts you when you try to close it. You can then either:

  • Continue entering or editing payments, then click Validate & Process the Batch again.
  • Click Ignore Mismatch & Process the Batch? to update the batch values to match its transactions and set its status to “Closed”.

docs.title: Batch entry fields
docs.text: Use this reference to check which fields appear when entering Contribution, Membership or Pledge Payments in a batch. The batch’s Type determines which reserved profile supplies the grid.

docs.title: Fields in every batch
docs.text:
Eight fields appear for all batch types:

Field Description Contact Select an existing contact from potential matches as you enter their name, or use “-create new contact-“ to create a New Individual, New Organization or New Household. If the grid profile includes details such as phone number or email address, those values are populated for an existing contact and can be updated. Financial Type Financial type of the payment. Amount Payment amount. (Payment) Status Payment status. Received – Date and Time When the payment was received. Send Receipt Check the box to send a receipt by email. Soft Credit Soft credit for the payment. Soft Credit Type Type of soft credit.

docs.title: Contribution Payment fields
docs.text:
The standard profile adds:

Field Description Source Text describing the source of the payment. Paid by Payment vehicle, such as cash, check or EFT. Check Number Check number, if paid by check. Invoice ID Invoice ID.

docs.title: Membership Payment fields
docs.text:
You can add a new membership or renew an existing one. The standard profile adds:

Field Description Type For a new membership, select the organisation and membership type. For a renewal, you can change the membership type. Member Since: Populated with the current date when you open the batch entry form. If you renew a membership, it changes to that membership’s start date. You can edit it. Start Date(reserved) Blank initially. Fill it in only if you want a start date other than the default. End Date(reserved) If left empty, CiviCRM uses the membership rules to set the date. Source Text describing the source of the payment. Paid by Payment vehicle, such as cash, check or EFT. Check Number Check number, if paid by check. Invoice ID Invoice ID.

docs.title: Pledge Payment fields
docs.text:
A payment can be assigned to any pending pledge for its contact. With the appropriate permissions, you can change the pledge payment’s amount or schedule using adjust payment amount beside Amount. The standard profile also adds:

Field Description Source Text describing the source of the payment. Paid by Payment vehicle, such as cash, check or EFT. Check Number Check number, if paid by check. Invoice ID Invoice ID.

docs.title: Find payments in processed batches
docs.text:
Use one of these routes to find Contribution, Membership or Pledge Payments in verified and processed batches:

  • Go to Searches > Find Contributions, enter contribution criteria, and select the batch under Batch Name.
  • Go to Searches > Advanced Search, enter contact criteria, then open the Contributions area, enter any contribution criteria, and select the batch under Batch Name.
  • Go to Contributions > Batches and select Closed in Status.
  • Go to Memberships > Batches and select Closed in Status.
  • Go to Pledge Payments > Batches and select Closed in Status.
  • Go to Reports > Create Reports from Templates, click Contribution Report Detail, and enter your report criteria. Under Set Filters, select “is one of” or “is not one of” beside Batch Name, then select the batch name or names.

docs.title: Configure profiles for batch entry
docs.text: Change the relevant reserved profile to adjust which fields appear when you create a contact or record a payment in the Batch Entry Input Grid. See Profiles for more about profiles.

docs.title: Change fields for new contacts
docs.text:
The reserved New Individual, New Household and New Organization profiles control the fields used when you create those contacts during batch entry.

Changes to these profiles also appear on other CiviCRM screens where you can create a contact inline.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles.
  2. Open the Reserved Profiles tab.
  3. Click Fields beside New Individual, New Household or New Organization.
  4. Add, edit or rearrange the fields you want in the Batch Entry Input Grid.

The image shows CiviCRM’s default New Individual profile, used when creating an individual during batch entry of Contributions or Membership Payments.

docs.title: Change payment fields
docs.text:
To change the fields collected for Contributions or Membership Payments, update the reserved Contribution Batch Entry or Membership Batch Entry profile.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles.
  2. Open the Reserved Profiles tab.
  3. Click Fields beside Contribution Batch Entry or Membership Batch Entry.
  4. Add, edit or rearrange fields for the Batch Entry Input Grid. For example, you can include custom contribution fields you want to display and collect.

See Profiles for more about changing profiles.

The image shows CiviCRM’s default Contribution Batch Entry profile, used to record information about a contact’s Contribution or Pledge Payment.

The image shows CiviCRM’s default Membership Batch Entry profile, used to record information about a contact’s Membership Payment.

docs.title: Contribution import requirements
docs.text: Use this reference to prepare a contribution CSV file and check how imported contributions can be matched to contacts. If you have not imported data before, read Importing data into CiviCRM.

docs.title: Required fields
docs.text:
Include these fields in the CSV file:

Required field Value Financial Type The full text of the Financial Type Name, not the Financial Type ID. Total Amount The contribution’s total amount. Contact match At least one of Contact ID (Match to Contact), Email (Match to Contact) or External Identifier (Match to Contact).

docs.title: Matching contacts
docs.text:
Contributors must already exist as contacts in the database before you import their contributions. If they do not, import the contacts first, preferably with a unique external identifier, often an ID from the database or application supplying the records.

The source describes these ways to match contributions to existing contacts:

  • Include the contact’s external ID in a CSV column. If you have external IDs on record but did not import them with the contacts, you can run a second contact import to update that field before importing contributions.
  • Match using your contact de-dupe rules. For example, include the donor’s first name, last name and email address with each contribution. If a contact matches those three fields, the contribution is assigned to that contact.

docs.title: File size
docs.text: CSV files must be less than 2MB. If a file exceeds that size, split its data between multiple CSV files.

docs.title: Record a contribution manually
docs.text:
Use this guide to add a contribution received by cash, cheque, EFT or another offline method to a contact’s record. Payments made through CiviCRM, such as an online membership or event fee, are recorded automatically; recording offline payments helps keep reports accurate.

If the donor is not yet in the database, create their record first. See Contacts.

  1. Find the contact using a search tool, such as Search > Find Contacts.
  2. Open the contact’s Contributions tab.
  3. Click Record Contribution (Check, Cash, EFT...).

If you have set up a payment processor that allows credit card transactions directly on your site, you can instead select Submit Credit Card Contribution to process the payment immediately.

  1. Complete the New Contribution Form. The image shows the offline contribution form; the credit card form is almost identical apart from its payment-related fields.

  1. Enter the Financial Type, Amount, Received Date, Receipt Date and Status. The Received Date defaults to the current day, the Receipt Date appears on the receipt generated by the system, and the Status defaults to Completed. Any custom contribution fields also appear on this form.
  2. If relevant, use Soft Credit To to assign a soft credit to the owner of a Personal Campaign Page (PCP) when you enter a donation for the contributor. For more about PCPs and campaign fundraising pages, see the Set-up chapter of the CiviContribute section.
  3. If relevant, use Additional Details to add a note or enter the date a thank-you letter was sent.
  4. If relevant, complete Honoree Information when the contribution is in someone else’s honour, or Premium Information when it has an associated premium.
  5. Click Save, or Save and New if you are entering another contribution.

If you have more than a few contributions to enter at once, consider Batch Data Entry instead.

docs.title: Create thank-you letters for contributions
docs.text:
Use Thank-you letters - print or email to create letters for selected contributions. For example, your organisation can thank donors to a campaign and tell them the total amount raised, or send each contact one end-of-fiscal-year receipt covering their tax-deductible donations.

This action is available from search results displaying Contributions, rather than contacts.

  1. Use Find Contributions, or use Advanced Search with Display Results As set to Contributions.
  2. Select the contributions for which you want letters or combined receipts.
  3. Choose Thank-you letters - print or email.

  1. Choose Update thank-you dates for these contributions or Update receipt dates for these contributions, as required. The current date will be entered in the appropriate field.
  2. Choose one of the Print and Email Options:
    • Generate PDFs for printing (only)
    • Send emails where possible. Generate printable PDFs for contacts who cannot receive emails
    • Send emails where possible. Generate printable PDFs for all contacts.
  3. Set Group contributions by. Choose -no grouping- to make one letter for each contribution. To show multiple contributions from the same contact together in a letter, choose a grouping option. There are five grouping options.
  4. If you chose a grouping option, choose a Separator (grouped contributions).
  5. Check the Page Format settings.
  6. Use an existing template, create a new letter for one-off use, or create a new letter and save it as a template. See Tokens and mail merge and Postal mail communications for more about creating letter templates.
  7. Click Make Thank-you Letters. The letters are generated, and a "Print/Merge Document" activity is created for each letter with the Activity Subject you specified.

docs.title: Grouped contribution thank-you letters
docs.text:
Grouping contributions lets you produce an end-of-fiscal-year giving statement or tax receipt for a contact. In Group contributions by, choose an option other than -no grouping- to place details of multiple contributions from the same contact in one letter.

In a standard CiviCRM installation, grouped letters are fairly rudimentary. Separator (grouped contributions) applies only when you choose a grouping option.

docs.title: Separator formats
docs.text:
• Comma places contribution amounts and dates one after another, separated by commas. For example, “Thank you for your generous donations of {contribution.total_amount} received on {contribution.receive_date} respectively.” becomes “Thank you for your generous donations of $100.00, $150.00, $325.00 received on 1 January 2015, 5 March 2015, 16 May 2015 respectively.”
  • Table Cell places each contribution in its own table column. For example, this letter template:

produces this result:

This format works well for a few contributions, but monthly, fortnightly or weekly donations can make the table wider than the page.

Neither format can include the total yearly contribution amount in the letter.

docs.title: Yearly totals with Smarty
docs.text:
To include the total yearly contribution amount and make a letter better suited to several contributions from one person, you or your implementer/developer need to enable Smarty functionality for emails. Once enabled, the token {$contribution_aggregate} can include the total yearly contribution amount.

For example, this HTML source for a letter:

<p>Dear {contact.first_name}</p>
<p>Thank you for donating ${$contribution_aggregate} to help the arts during the 2014 financial year</p>
<p>Your donation is tax deductible and the details are given below.</p>
<p>with appreciation for your generosity,</p>
<p>the CEO</p>
  <table class="table" style="width: 500px;" border="1" cellspacing="0" cellpadding="2" align="left">
    <tbody>
      <tr>
        <th>Date</th>
        <th>Amount</th>
        <th>Receipt Number</th></tr>
    <!--
    {foreach from=$contributions item=contribution} {assign
    var="date" value=$contribution.receive_date|date_format:"%d %B
    %Y"}
  -->
      <tr>
        <td>{$date}</td>
        <td>{$contribution.total_amount}</td>
        <td>{$contribution.id}</td>
      </tr>
   <!--
    {/foreach}

 --></tbody>
  </table>

produces a letter like this:

docs.title: Send contribution receipts
docs.text:
Use a contribution record to send or resend a receipt to one contributor, or use a contribution search to send receipts to several contributors.

Donors who contribute through an online form automatically receive an email receipt if that option was selected when the contribution page was configured.

docs.title: Send a receipt for one contribution
docs.text:
1. Edit the contribution record against the contact.
  2. Tick Send Receipt?.
  3. Click Save. The off-line contribution receipt is sent.

docs.title: Send receipts for multiple contributions
docs.text:
By default, emailing receipts or creating PDF receipts updates each contribution’s receipt date. You can choose to keep the existing dates. You can also choose to disregard Do not email/Do not mail settings so that all selected contributors are sent a receipt.

  1. Open Find Contributions.
  2. Select the contacts you want to send receipts to.
  3. Choose Receipts - print or email from the actions drop-down menu.

  1. Choose whether to email the receipts or make PDF receipts to send to contributors.

  1. Choose whether to update or keep the existing receipt dates, and whether to disregard Do not email/Do not mail settings.

The standard off-line contribution receipt displays limited information. Customising it requires knowledge of Smarty. For receipts you plan to send later, you may find the thank-you letters workflow easier to use.

docs.title: Prepare an offline postal appeal
docs.text: Use CiviCRM to select recipients for a postal appeal and prepare the information you need to mail them. After the appeal, enter any contributions collected offline so your reporting is accurate.

docs.title: Create your recipient list
docs.text:
1. Go to Search > Find Contacts and search for the people who should receive your appeal. Your list could include your entire database.

  2. If you want to track who receives the appeal or how successful it is, select all the search results using the check box. Then choose **Group

  3. add contacts** or **Group

  4. create smart group** from the Action dropdown menu.

Later, you can mark everyone in that group as a recipient of the appeal using Add Activity under the Actions dropdown menu.

docs.title: Prepare letters
docs.text:
You can create letters with CiviCRM’s PDF letters - print feature. Alternatively, export your recipient list as a CSV file and use mail merge in a word processor, such as OpenOffice, to insert fields into your letters.

To export the list:

  1. Select all records or a subset using the checkboxes, then choose Export Contacts from the Actions dropdown menu.
  2. Choose Export PRIMARY fields or Select fields for Export, then click Continue. If you choose primary fields, CiviCRM generates the CSV file immediately. If you choose to select fields, a list of dropdown options appears.
  3. If you chose to select fields, select the fields you need. To keep that selection for future exports, check Save this field mapping, then click Export to generate the CSV file.
  4. Click Done when you have finished to return to the contact list.

docs.title: Print mailing labels
docs.text:
Repeat the search you used for your recipient list. The option to exclude people whose privacy settings say “do not mail” is checked by default and is recommended.

  1. Choose Mailing labels - print from the Actions dropdown menu.
  2. Select the mailing label number. Decide whether to exclude people with “do not mail” checked and whether to combine records with the same mailing address into one label. Combining them can help avoid duplicate mailings to a household or organization; each name at that address appears on its own line.
  3. Click Make Mailing Labels to create a printable PDF.

CiviCRM prints labels in the order shown on the research results page, in a column-by-column pattern.

docs.title: Record contributions
docs.text: After collecting donations through the appeal, an event or another offline method, manually enter the Contributions in CiviCRM to keep your final reporting accurate.

docs.title: Set up a Payment Processor
docs.text: Configure one or more Payment Processors in CiviCRM, then assign an active processor to each paid Event and Online Contribution Page.

docs.title: Configure the processor
docs.text:
The Financial Account you select records where money is deposited, not the type of revenue received. Contribution, Membership and Event payments are also recorded in different revenue Financial Accounts according to the configuration of your contribution pages and events. You may want a separate Financial Account for each Payment Processor; ask your bookkeeper or accountant for advice. For a partial explanation, see Double Entry Accounting in Wikipedia.

  1. Go to Administer > System Settings > Payment Process and select New Payment Processor.
  2. Choose the Payment Processor Type from the dropdown list.
  3. Enter a descriptive name for the processor configuration. This name appears when you select a Payment Processor for a Contribution Page or Event.
  4. If useful, enter a description. This can help distinguish multiple merchant accounts for different chapters or sub-organisations that use the same Payment Processor type.
  5. Select a Financial Account.
  6. Make the processor active. An active processor is available for paid Events and Online Contribution Pages. If it collects credit card details on your website, staff can also use it to submit credit card Contributions and payments for Memberships and Events.
  7. If you have multiple Payment Processors, set a default if needed. It will be selected when you create a Contribution or Event Page or process a credit card payment in the admin area, but you can override the selection.
  8. Enter the live payment and test payment details for your processor. The fields vary by Payment Processor type.

You also need to complete setup on the payment gateway itself. That setup is beyond the scope of this book and should be documented by your gateway. Once setup is complete, the processor is available for paid Events and Contribution pages; assign an active processor to each page or event where you want to take payments.

docs.title: Test payment details
docs.text:
You can configure dummy Payment Processors for testing. If you use a dummy Payment Processor or a payment page in test mode, these card details should work:

Detail Test value Card type Visa Card number 4111 1111 1111 1111 CVV Any three digits Expiry Any date in the future

docs.title: Manage a Recurring Contribution
docs.text: Where you make changes to a Recurring Contribution depends on its Payment Processor. Check which processor handles the payment before editing it.

docs.title: Where changes are made
docs.text:
With PayPal and Authorize.net, people can set up a Recurring Contribution, but you must log into the Payment Processor’s site to change its amount, frequency or other payment details. Each time a payment is made, the processor creates a contribution record in CiviCRM.

Other processors, including IATS, eway, Payment Express, SagePay and Paypal Commerce/Checkout, expect you to manage Recurring Contributions in CiviCRM. CiviCRM triggers the payment by sending a request to the processor and receives a completed contribution record if the payment succeeds.

If your configured Payment Processor includes Recurring Payments as a feature, you can enable Recurring Contributions in your Contribution Page settings. For page-specific configuration, see Online Contributions.

docs.title: Manage a contribution in CiviCRM
docs.text:
1. Open the contact record’s Contributions tab.
  2. Find the separate Recurring Contributions section.

From that section, you can View, Edit or Cancel a Recurring Contribution. When editing, you can change its Amount, Number of Installments, Next Scheduled Contribution Date, Financial Type, Status, Start Date and whether the donor receives an email notification for each payment instalment. You cannot change the donation frequency, such as weekly or monthly, from within CiviCRM.

If you View the Recurring Contribution, you can also View, Edit or Process the card on file. Viewing or editing brings up the customer and card information.

To recharge a card, processors often store a payment token. It can be used to charge the card only to put money into your account, not anyone else’s. Rules for using tokens vary, and most processors use them only for regular Recurring Payments.

docs.title: View recent iATS transactions
docs.text: For iATS users, an administrative page shows recent iATS transactions. Go to Contributions > iATS Payments Administration to see the report.

docs.title: Choosing a Payment Processor
docs.text:
The right Payment Processor depends on where your organisation operates, how you want people to pay, and what it will cost you.

CiviCRM includes support for approximately 15 Payment Processors. You can download other community-contributed processors from the Extensions Directory, and additional processors may be available from third-party sites. For a comparison, see the Payment Processors comparison in the System Administrator Guide.

You can configure more than one Payment Processor and let constituents choose which one they prefer. If possible, ask similar organisations near you about their experiences.

docs.title: Onsite and offsite payments
docs.text:
With an onsite processor, people enter credit card details on your website. This provides a more seamless experience and lets staff process card payments for Contributions, Membership Fees and Event Payments from CiviCRM admin pages.

With an offsite processor, people go to another site to pay and then return to yours. You may be able to add your organisation’s name, logo and colours to that site, but the change of site can interrupt the workflow. Some people may not complete their payment.

Before choosing an onsite processor, account for the security setup. You need an SSL certificate to protect card details as they travel over the internet. Certificates typically have an annual cost and can be difficult to set up; your hosting provider or system administrator can help. You may also want to read Security in the Initial set up chapter of this book. CiviCRM never stores credit card details on your server: it only transmits them to the Payment Processor.

docs.title: Regional availability
docs.text: Check whether a processor supports the currencies you need. For many countries, no available CiviCRM Payment Processor supports the local currency. If the provider you want to use has no suitable CiviCRM processor, you can write an integration or ask—or pay—a third party to write one.

docs.title: Merchant accounts and costs
docs.text:
Many organisations that accept credit cards have a merchant account through a bank. These accounts usually have monthly charges, which may not suit smaller organisations, though their percentage charges are generally lower. You may pay both a merchant-account fee and a Payment Processor fee; the two may be bundled. World Pay and Paypal are examples that do not require a separate merchant account.

Compare costs using the number and average size of your transactions. Commission percentages, per-transaction charges, fixed monthly charges and set-up costs vary. If you process many transactions, a monthly fee with a lower commission may suit you. If payments are infrequent, avoiding a monthly fee may be cheaper even with a higher commission.

docs.title: Recurring payments and usability
docs.text:
Not every Payment Processor available for CiviCRM supports Recurring Contributions and auto-renewing memberships. Some have incomplete support, including Moneris. How you manage Recurring Contributions also varies by processor.

For an offsite processor, consider how easy its payment workflow is to use. Paypal Standard can confuse people who are unsure whether they need a PayPal account, which can reduce completed contributions.

docs.title: Support
docs.text: CiviCRM supports processors incorporated into its core codebase to the extent of ensuring that upgrades do not break them. CiviCRM does not support community-contributed processors; their support and enhancements are generally expected to come from the community. They may be just as reliable as built-in processors, but make sure you have adequate technical support in-house, from the processor’s author or from a trusted third party.

docs.title: Enable and share Personal Campaign Pages
docs.text: Enable PCPs on an existing online contribution page or event, then choose how to invite constituents to create their own pages.

docs.title: Enable PCPs
docs.text:
1. Create an online contribution page through Contributions > New Contribution Page, or an event through Events > New Event.
  2. While editing the contribution page or event settings, open the Personal Campaigns tab.
  3. Click enable personal campaign pages.
  4. Configure the options that apply to your campaign:
Option What it controls Approval Required Requires an administrator to approve each new PCP before it becomes active. After approval, the page owner is notified by email and can promote the page. Use Notification Email so an administrator knows when a page is awaiting review. Notification Email Sends an email when a new PCP is created. Enter the administrators' email addresses, separated by commas. Supporter Profile Selects a profile of fields. The source describes these as fields collected from PCP supporters and, in its setup instructions, from the person creating the PCP. Owner Email Notification Controls emails to a PCP owner when someone donates through their page. You can always send them, never send them, or let each owner choose during setup. This setting applies to PCPs under the particular event or contribution page. Allow 'tell a friend' functionality Lets a PCP owner email contacts to encourage them to visit and contribute. Campaign Type For an event, can offer a registrant the choice of creating a fundraising event of their own or a contribution page—for example, to raise money in support of their attendance.

You can also customise the text on the button used to create a PCP.

docs.title: Invite people to create a PCP
docs.text:
Once PCP creation is enabled, people have two ways to start:

  • Someone who donates through the contribution page or registers for the event can use the button on the 'thank you' page.

  • You can give constituents a direct link without requiring them to donate or register first. You can email the link, embed it in a page or add it as a menu item.

http://<EXAMPLE.ORG>/civicrm/contribute/campaign?action=add&reset=1&pageId=<CONTRIBUTION_OR_EVENT_ID>&component=<EVENT_OR_CONTRIBUTE>

For the direct link, replace:

  • <EXAMPLE.ORG> with your domain address. The source's replacement notes call this YOUR-SITE.ORG.
  • <CONTRIBUTION_OR_EVENT_ID> with the event or contribution page ID. Find the ID alongside the item in Manage Events or Manage Contribution Pages.
  • <EVENT_OR_CONTRIBUTE> with contribute for a contribution page or event for an event. The resulting parameter is component=contribute or component=event.

docs.title: Notification message customisation
docs.text: Automated emails, or system workflow messages, go to the PCP administrator and page owner at various stages of a campaign. Modifying these messages requires a working knowledge of Smarty 2 (http://www.smarty.net/). The default notification to a PCP owner when a donation is received is shown below.

docs.title: Review and manage Personal Campaign Pages
docs.text: Use Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages to review PCPs that need approval and manage pages after they have been created.

docs.title: What the page owner can set
docs.text:
After using the creation button or a direct link, a constituent fills in a form. They can provide a title, descriptive message, monetary goal and text for the donate button. They can also upload one photo, show a progress bar in the style of a thermometer, and choose whether to display an honor roll of donors who have not chosen to be anonymous.

The owner can choose whether the campaign is active, including activating it later. They can create a username or log in with an existing username so they can edit their PCP later.

docs.title: Review a page awaiting approval
docs.text:
If Approval Required is enabled, a new PCP cannot be used until an administrator approves it in the CiviCRM back-end. To make sure administrators hear about pages awaiting review, enter an address in Notification Email in the contribution page settings.

  1. Go to Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages.
  2. Find the PCP in the list.
  3. At the end of its row, click Approve, Reject or Delete, as appropriate.

After approval, the owner receives a confirmation email. They also receive an email explaining how to promote and edit the page, provided they have been given user access.

docs.title: Manage an existing page
docs.text:
From Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages, the user or an administrator can use Edit, Delete or Disable/Enable to manage a PCP. Administrators can edit PCP content, disable a page or deny it. The More link can also be used later to enable or disable a PCP.

Administrators can view the amount collected by each PCP, run summary reports of PCP fundraising using CiviReport, and enter 'offline' contributions such as checks while crediting the money to a PCP.

docs.title: Understanding Personal Campaign Pages
docs.text:
Personal Campaign Pages (PCPs) let your constituents create fundraising pages of their own and ask others to support their cause.

A constituent can use a PCP to explain their personal reasons for supporting a fundraiser, event or organisation. They can share the page with friends, who can then contribute. Examples include “Sponsor My 5k Walk”, “Help Fund Our Trip” and “Let's Raise Money to Build A School”.

docs.title: Limits to consider
docs.text:
• Team fundraising: CiviCRM's PCP functionality does not support a leader recruiting team members, managing membership and tracking how much each member raises.
  • Images: A fundraiser can upload one image to a PCP. CiviCRM does not automatically resize it.
  • Page appearance: The thermometer and honor roll can be modified, but changes apply to all PCPs. These customisations require a coder.

docs.title: Configure premiums for contribution pages
docs.text:
Set up a Premium, such as a T-shirt or subscription, to offer on your contribution pages.

  1. Navigate to Administer > CiviContribute > Premiums (Thank-You Gifts).
  2. Click Add Premium, or click Edit for an existing Premium.
  3. Enter the Premium’s Name, Description, Minimum Contribution Amount and Market Value. You can also enter an SKU (an optional product code), Premium Image (an optional image of the item), Actual Cost, Financial Type and Options, such as colors and sizes.

If you’re offering a Subscription or Service, click Subscription or Service Settings to define additional information, such as Period Type (Fixed or Rolling), Fixed Period Start Day, Duration and Frequency.

docs.title: Contribution reports and analysis
docs.text: Use this page to look up CiviCRM’s standard Contribution Reports and other ways to analyse contributions. You can also use CiviCRM’s search features for reporting and analysis.

docs.title: Standard Contribution Reports
docs.text:
CiviCRM includes thirteen Contribution Reports out of the box.

Report What it shows Contribution Summary Report Groups contributions by criteria including contact, time period, type and location, and shows summary statistics. You can use it to compare income from fundraising campaigns, events or memberships. Contribution Detail Report Shows a detailed report for a subset of contributions. It opens automatically when you click a row in the Contribution Summary Report, or you can open it on its own. Repeat Contribution Report Compares contacts’ total contributions across two time periods and shows the percentage increase or decrease. It can help you find contacts who are giving more or less than before. SYBUNT report Helps you find donors who gave in some years but not this year. LYBUNT report Helps you find donors who gave last year but not this year. Contribution by Household Report Aggregates contributions by household, including donations attached to the household record. For example, you can see contributions made by a particularly active family. Contribution by Organization report Aggregates contributions by organization, including donations attached to the organization record. For example, you can see employees’ contributions alongside a donation made by their organization after a collective office fundraising event. Top Donors Report Lists the top donors for a time period you define. You can choose how many to show, such as the top
  1. If you leave Show no. of Top Donors empty, the report includes all contacts included by the other filters. | | Personal Campaign Page Report | Shows the status of Personal Campaign Pages. You can filter by contribution page to see pages for a single campaign, or use other appropriate criteria. | | Soft Credit Report | Shows soft credits and contacts who are at least partially responsible for other people’s donations. | | Contribution Aggregate by Relationship Report | Lists a contact’s donation history by year, alongside contributions attributed to the contact’s related contacts. | | Recurring Contributions Report | Shows the status of recurring contributions. | | Bookkeeping Transactions Report | Shows transaction details for all payments, including financial type and accounts, transaction number, invoice ID, payment instrument and check number. |

The household and organization reports are useful if your organisation uses those contact types. For example, you can use the organization report to see employees’ contributions and thank them as a group.

docs.title: Other ways to get the information you need
docs.text: Standard reports are configured to display particular information and may not meet every need. You can download and install extensions to access additional reports. If you still cannot extract the information you need, consider commissioning a new report or custom search and contributing it back to the community.

docs.title: Set up Sales Tax or VAT
docs.text: If your organisation charges Sales Tax or VAT, you can enable the feature and assign a tax account to the Financial Type it applies to.

docs.title: Enable Sales Tax or VAT
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > CiviContribute > CiviContribute Component Settings.
  2. Check Enable Tax and Invoicing.
  3. Enter a Tax Term for what your organisation calls the relevant Sales Tax or VAT.
  4. Choose a Tax Display Settings option:
  5. No breakdown, total only
  6. Shows as inclusive price — $120 (includes $20 tax)
  7. Shows as exclusive price — $100 + $20 tax

docs.title: Create a Financial Account for tax
docs.text:
Once Sales Tax or VAT is enabled, create one or more Financial Accounts for it. For more advanced configuration with accounting software packages like QuickBooks, involve your organisation's bookkeeper or accountant in setting up Financial Types and Financial Accounts.

  1. Go to Administer > CiviContribute > Financial Account.
  2. Scroll to the bottom of the page and click Add Financial Account.
  3. Set Financial Account Type to Liability.
  4. Select Enabled.
  5. Select Is Tax.
  6. Specify the Tax Rate.
  7. If you use Quick Books, set Account Type Code to SALESTAX.
  8. Set Accounting Code based on your organisation's specific Accounting Codes.
  9. Create the Financial Account.

docs.title: Assign the account to a Financial Type
docs.text:
1. Go to Adminster > CiviContribute > Financial Types.
  2. Find the Financial Type that the Sales Tax applies to and click Accounts.
  3. Click Assign Account.
  1. For Financial Account Relationship, choose Sales Tax Account is.
  2. In Financial Account, select your Sales Tax account.
  3. Click Save.

The Sales Tax Financial Account appears with the other Financial Accounts for that Financial Type.

docs.title: Enable Honoree information on a contribution page
docs.text:
You can let people making online contributions provide Honoree information and have the Honoree receive a Soft Credit.

When creating a contribution page:

  1. Select the Honoree Section Enabled checkbox. Additional fields appear.
  2. Specify the Honor Types and Profile to include in the Honoree section.

People using the contribution page can then enter Honoree information.

CiviCRM checks whether the Honoree already exists using your site’s default duplicate checking rules. If it finds no duplicate, it creates a new contact record. A Soft Credit is added to the Honoree’s contact record.

docs.title: How Soft Credits work
docs.text:
Soft Credits let you recognise people who helped bring in a contribution, even when they are not the donor.

A Soft Credit assigns credit for a donation to one or more people other than the donor. It helps your organisation understand where contributions came from without counting the same contribution twice. You can also credit parts of one donation to multiple people.

docs.title: Soft Credit Types
docs.text:
A Soft Credit Type describes why someone receives credit. CiviCRM provides these reserved Soft Credit Types:

  • In Honor of
  • In Memory of
  • Solicited
  • Personal Campaign Page
  • Gift

Administrators can use reserved or custom Soft Credit Types to attribute contributions received through charitable contribution arrangements such as Donor Advised Funds, Scholarships and Family Bequests, whether solicited (P2P) or not.

docs.title: Examples of attribution
docs.text:
If an active member encourages 10 other people to contribute, Soft Credits let you recognise that member while keeping each person who gave as the donor. In this example, Magan Cooper’s $1,500.00 contribution has been soft credited to three people, with $500 credited to each.

Soft Credit Types can distinguish different roles in a more complex contribution. Suppose Joe solicits a contribution from Jane on behalf of a community foundation, and your organisation receives a check from the foundation:

  • The community foundation is the donor.
  • Joe receives the Solicited Soft Credit.
  • Jane receives the donor advised Soft Credit.

This attributes credit without duplicating the contribution.

docs.title: Reporting and Personal Campaign Pages
docs.text:
The contribution detail report has optional columns for Soft Credit details. When selected, these show four extra columns in CiviReport for viewing soft credit information.

Soft Credits are also connected to Personal Campaign Pages. When someone donates through a Personal Campaign Page, the donation is soft credited to the page’s owner.

docs.title: What is CiviContribute?
docs.text: CiviContribute records financial and in-kind contributions to your organisation. Understanding what CiviCRM means by a contribution helps you see how donations, event fees and membership payments fit together.

docs.title: What counts as a contribution?
docs.text:
Throughout CiviCRM, a contribution is a financial transaction or payment, such as a donation, event fee payment or membership fee payment. The term also includes in-kind contributions.

CiviContribute lets your organisation:

  • Accept donations and other financial or in-kind contributions.
  • Process membership signups and renewals.
  • Accept and manage event fees.
  • Run specific fundraising campaigns.
  • Let supporters fundraise through personalised campaign pages.
  • Enter contribution and membership payments quickly using “batches”.
  • Export batches of financial transactions for import into accounting software.
  • Report on and evaluate fundraising results and trends.

docs.title: How contributions fit into a workshop
docs.text:
Arts in Action, a community arts group, runs leadership workshops for young people under

  1. It uses CiviEvent and CiviContribute to help plan and administer them. The workshops have three sources of funding: participant fees, local arts funding and donations.

Most donations come from former workshop participants who remain Arts in Action constituents. Twice a year, the group uses CiviMail to send a call for donations with a link to a donations page. Some donors give regularly; others make one-off donations. When a payment is successfully processed, each donor automatically receives a thank-you email and receipt. Donations are tagged for the workshops, so staff can report on total workshop donations and see who has donated in individual contact records.

Participants register through an online form and pay a flat registration fee, with additional fees based on their choices of optional workshops, food and lodging. They can pay by credit card. If a participant is not already a contact, registration creates a contact record. The payment is recorded in that contact’s contribution record and linked to the workshop event.

Participants can also choose to pay later. Many do not have a credit card and pay cash at the workshop instead. CiviContribute distinguishes an actual payment from a commitment to pay. That distinction appears in the registrants report printed for checking attendance and payment on the day. At the registration desk, staff use a computer to enter cash and cheque payments manually in participants’ contribution records.

Arts in Action considers word of mouth and participants bringing friends its most effective workshop publicity. The “tell-a-friend” mechanism lets participants forward the registration link after completing the form, by email or through social networking platforms, to friends and colleagues who may want to attend.

After each workshop, the accountant uses a report template to show total income from participant fees, local arts funding and donations. Staff also track donation trends and keep the Board informed about larger donors. Key statistics appear as graphs on staff members’ CiviCRM dashboards.

docs.title: Create and embed a contribution widget
docs.text: Create an automatically updated visual representation of your fundraising campaign that you and your supporters can use to promote it on a website.

docs.title: Create the widget
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages.
  2. Click Configure for your Contribution Page.
  3. Select the Widgets tab.
  4. Click Enable Widget.
  5. Enter a Title. It can be the same as your Contribution Page name, but it does not have to be.
  6. If you want to show a logo, enter its web address in URL to Logo Image. The image must already be uploaded to your web server; you may need your system administrator’s help to get its URL.
  7. Enter a Button Title for the button that takes potential donors to your donate page. In the example above, the title is Contribute.
  8. Enter About text in the editor. You can enter as much as you want, but consider where you plan to display the widget.
  9. Click Save and Preview to preview the widget and update its embed code.

The code for embedding the widget on a web page appears on the right.

docs.title: Adjust the colours
docs.text:
1. Expand Edit Widget Colors at the bottom of the configuration page.

  2. Enter hexadecimal (hex) colour codes for the areas you want to change. W3schools has a colour picker that provides hex values. If your website has colour standards, check them with your designer.

  3. Click Save and Preview to see your changes and update the embed code.

docs.title: Add the widget to a website
docs.text:
1. Click Select Code to select all the code needed for the widget.
  2. Copy the selected code.
  3. Paste it where you want the widget to appear on your website. You may need help from your system administrator or the person who administers your website.

If you use WordPress, the CiviCRM Contribution Page Widget plugin lets you embed a CiviCRM widget anywhere a WordPress widget can go.

docs.title: Create and evaluate a CiviMail A/B test
docs.text:
Send two test emails to random samples of your recipients, then use the available results to choose which mailing to send to the remaining recipients.

Before you begin, put your recipients in a Mailing List. For more about configuring Mailing Lists, see the chapters on Groups and Tags.

docs.title: Set up the test
docs.text:
1. Go to Mailings > New A/B Test.
  2. On the Setup screen, define the campaign that corresponds with the mailing.
  3. Select one type of test:
  4. Different Subject lines
  5. Different From lines
  6. Entirely different emails

docs.title: Choose recipients and distribution
docs.text:
1. On the Target screen, define your recipients.
  2. Drag the blue percentage bar to set the percentage of recipients who will receive test mailings. This also controls the percentage who will receive the final mailing. Together, the test mailings and final mailing add up to 100%.

docs.title: Compose and test the mailings
docs.text:
1. On the Compose screen, enter the fields for your chosen test type. The screen changes depending on the type:

  2. For different From lines, enter From (A) and From(B).

  3. For different Subject lines, enter Subject(A) and Subject(B).

  4. For entirely different emails, enter a From and Subject for each mailing.

  5. Choose an email template you have previously composed.

Before scheduling or sending the final mailing, send a test email.

docs.title: Review results and choose the final mailing
docs.text:
1. After the test mailings are complete, go to Mailings > Manage A/B Tests.
  2. Select Results. On the A/B Test Results screen, you can monitor the test results.
  3. Use the available metrics to select which mailing should be submitted as the final mailing to the remaining recipients.

docs.title: Send a quick email to fewer than 50 contacts
docs.text:
Use a search to email several contacts at once when you do not need email tracking or an opt-out option.

Do not use this method for a mass mailing. It is limited to 50 contacts, provides no email-tracking options and does not give contacts the option to opt out. For mass mailings, use Mass mailings using CiviMail.

  1. Click Search > Find Contacts or Advanced Search, choose your criteria and click Search. You can also use another search to find the contacts you want to email.
  2. Select some or all of the contacts in the search results.
  3. Click Actions > Email -send now (to 50 or less).
  4. Compose the message as you would when sending an email to one contact. You can add CC or BCC recipients, choose and edit a template if one is defined, or enter your own content.

Before you send, note that each recipient will see only their own email address in the To field. If it matters who the message is for, you may want to say so in its text—for example, “TO: Members of the board, staff”.

  1. Click Send.

The email is recorded as an Activity for each recipient and for the sender. The activity record also lists the other message recipients. Unlike mass mailings, emails sent with the Send Email function have no single place where they are all listed.

docs.title: Insert an image into an email
docs.text:
Use the email editor to select an image already on your server or upload one from your computer.

  1. Click the image button in the WYSIWYG editor.

  1. In the Image Properties window, click Browse Server.

  1. In the directory in the left sidebar, find the image you want. If it is not already on the server, click Upload to choose a file from your computer.

  1. If you clicked Upload, find the file in your computer’s file-browsing window, select it and click Open. You can repeat this to upload multiple files at once.
  2. Double-click the image you want to insert. You will return to the Image Properties window.
  3. If needed, adjust the image’s size, alignment and border.
  4. Fill in the Alternative Text field. This text appears when the image is unavailable—for example, when a reader does not load images in their email client or uses a screen reader. Include alternative text so the image’s information remains accessible.
  5. Click OK to insert the image.

docs.title: Send an email to one contact
docs.text:
Use CiviCRM to email a person when you want others at your organisation to see the message or you want to use a pre-defined template.

  1. Find the contact using either method:
  2. In the Quick Search box at the top left, type part of the person’s name or email address, then choose them from the suggestions.
  3. Go to Search > Find Contact, enter part of the person’s name or email address, click Search, then click their name in the results.
  4. On the contact summary page, click Actions > Send an email. Alternatively, open the Activities tab and choose Send an Email from the dropdown menu.
  5. If needed, add other recipients in the CC and BCC fields.
  6. If templates are defined and you want to use one, choose it from the Use Template dropdown menu. This fills the text content and HTML content fields with the template’s message, which you can edit.
  7. Enter your message. To send only a Plain Text version, ignore the HTML Format section, click the Plain Text Format section and enter your message in the box.
  8. Click Send.

To see the recorded email activity, open the contact’s Activities tab.

docs.title: Resolve email addresses on hold
docs.text: Use Advanced Search to release holds, or use Mail Bounce Report to find addresses you can correct or update.

docs.title: Release a hold
docs.text:
1. Go to Advanced Search.

  2. In Basic Search Criteria, select Emails On Hold.

  3. Select the contacts with held email addresses from the results.

  4. Choose Unhold Emails from the action dropdown list.
  5. Click Go.

docs.title: Correct or update held addresses
docs.text:
You need a group for bad emails and a profile containing just Primary Email to use Batch Update via Profile.

  1. Create a group for bad emails.
  2. In the top menu, go to Reports.
  3. Select Mail Bounce Report. The report shows contacts whose emails have bounced.
  4. If you need to limit the results to a specific bounce type, open Report Criteria at the top of the mailing.
  5. Add the contacts in the results to the group you created.
  6. Find that group using Advanced Search. Selecting Email on Hold is also recommended so you do not include records that bounced previously but may already have been updated.
  7. Select Batch Update via Profile for the results whose email addresses you can correct or update.
  8. Select the profile containing just Primary Email.
  9. Click Update.

docs.title: Bounced emails and email preferences
docs.text:
Learn what happens when an email bounces and how a held address differs from an unsubscribe, an opt-out or Do not email.

Keeping bounce and unsubscribe rates low helps you maintain healthy email lists. High bounce rates can raise concerns about blacklisting or a response from your SMTP provider. High bounce and unsubscribe rates can also point to deeper issues in your organisation.

docs.title: Why emails bounce
docs.text:
When you send a bulk email through CiviMail, some messages may bounce. A bounced message has not reached its recipient. Reasons include:

  • An email address was entered incorrectly.
  • An email address is no longer in use.
