  • An inbox is full and temporarily cannot accept messages.
  • A recipient has an automatic away reply while on vacation or out of the office.

CiviCRM handles bounce types differently. A temporary bounce does not affect the contact record, and CiviCRM will try to send future mailings to the address. A permanent bounce may put the contact’s email address on Hold. No future emails will be sent to an address on Hold unless someone fixes the address and removes the hold.

For each bounce type and the number of bounces allowed before an address is put on hold, see the System Administrator Guide’s Inbound email chapter.

docs.title: Holds, unsubscribes and opt-outs
docs.text:
A held address is different from an unsubscribe. A recipient unsubscribes by clicking an “unsubscribe from this mailing” link created by the tokens {action.unsubscribe} or {action.unsubscribeUrl}. If they unsubscribe from a single mailing list, CiviCRM removes them from the group used as that mailing list.

A recipient can instead opt out of all bulk emails by clicking a link in a mass email. You can create that link with the tokens {action.optOut} or {action.optOutUrl}, placed in the mailing body or a footer message.

A contact who has opted out can still receive individual or small-volume emails sent with Send Email from their contact record or after a search. They will also still receive scheduled reminders. Be careful about what you send to someone who has opted out if you do not want your messages to be considered spam.

docs.title: Do not email
docs.text:
If Do not email is selected for a contact, they cannot receive individual or small-volume emails through Send Email, whether you access that action from their contact record or after a search. They will not receive bulk emails through CiviMail either.

They will still receive scheduled reminders unless you specifically exclude them. If you set Do not email manually after someone contacts you in person, consider excluding them from scheduled reminders. The Schedule Reminders chapter explains how to do that.

docs.title: Ensuring a contact receives no email
docs.text: Settings can be changed incorrectly, and an email address can be used manually. The only way to fully guarantee that a contact receives no emails is to remove all email addresses from their contact record. If you do this, the contact will not be able to log in to your website.

docs.title: CiviMail mailing setup fields and options
docs.text: Use this reference to check what a setting does while defining a mailing. Step 1: Define Mailing contains the Mailing tab and optional tabs for attachments, headers and footers, publication, responses and tracking.

docs.title: Mailing tab
docs.text:
• Mailing Name: An internal name that recipients do not see. Choose one that identifies the mailing’s purpose. Starting it with a date, such as “2015/04/25 - Monthly Newsletter”, can make it easier to include or exclude its recipients in later mailings. The email’s Subject is entered separately.
  • Campaign: Associates the email with a particular campaign.
  • Template: Populates HTML Format and Plain-Text Format with content from an existing message template. You can edit that content for this mailing, but cannot update the template or create one from this form. CiviCRM ships with three sample newsletter templates. Users with the Administer CiviCRM permission can customise them with your organisation’s details or create templates at Administer > CiviMail > Message Templates.
  • From: Initially contains the default sender email address; you can choose another from the dropdown. Users with the Administer CiviCRM permission can add addresses at Administer > CiviMail > From Email addresses.
  • Recipients: Select Groups to include, shown in green, or exclude, shown in red with a strike-through. Only Groups of the “Mailing List” type appear in the dropdown. For a search-based mailing, you can further refine or add to the recipients. The estimated final count appears to the right, highlighted in yellow.

You can also include or exclude recipients of previous mailings. For example, to avoid emailing Group members who received an earlier message, choose that mailing under Exclude Past Recipients From. The message will then go only to members who did not receive the original mailing. - Unsubscribe Group: Required for search-based mailings only. Choose it carefully: it records who has unsubscribed and excludes those contacts from mailings sent to that Group, but does not itself supply recipients to the search-based mailing. - Subject: The subject recipients see. It can contain tokens. CiviCRM uses the Subject, not Mailing Name, when creating an activity or mailing record for each contact. - HTML: An expandable section for composing the message. You can use tokens to personalise it. For a plain-text-only email, leave it aside and open Plain Text to enter the message. - Preview: A panel at the bottom of Define Mailing, displayed whichever tab is selected. It previews HTML or Plain Text without attachments, sends a test to one email address, or sends a test to an existing CiviCRM Group. The HTML preview shows formatting and tokens converted with your data, but cannot guarantee the appearance in every email client. A test mailing fills in tokens and includes planned attachments. Sending a test to an address not already in CiviCRM creates a contact record.

docs.title: Recipient edit options
docs.text:
The wrench between Recipients and the estimated recipient count opens Edit Options.

  • Dedupe by email: CiviCRM always deduplicates by contact record: a contact in three included Groups receives one copy. If multiple contacts share an email address, an unticked box sends one copy per contact; a ticked box sends one copy to that address. Set the default at Administer > CiviMail > CiviMail Component Settings with “CiviMail dedupes e-mail addresses by default”. You can override it for an individual mailing.
  • Location Type: By default, CiviMail sends to email address locations set for “Bulk Mailings”, or, if no location type has that setting, to the location marked “Is Primary”. In Edit Options, you can change Location Type and Selection Method. You can filter to send only to email addresses with a specified location type or exclude addresses with that type.

docs.title: Attachments tab
docs.text: Upload files to include as email attachments.

docs.title: Header and Footer tab
docs.text: New mailings include the default Header and Footer defined at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages. Use this tab to select a different header or footer. Additional Headers and Footers are defined at the same menu location; see Set-Up for details.

docs.title: Publication tab
docs.text:
Mailing Visibility controls who can view the email as a web page:

  • Public Pages: Anyone with the “View public CiviMail content” permission can view it.
  • User and User Admin Only: Only recipients of the mailing and administrators can view it. Recipients must log in.

To link to the web version, include the Mailing permalink token in the message. It generates a URL where the message can be viewed. To display that link properly in HTML messages, add the appropriate link tags using the editor’s Source icon.

docs.title: Responses tab
docs.text:
• Track Replies: Sends recipients’ replies to a CiviMail-specific address instead of the sender’s address so they can be stored in CiviCRM. Selecting it reveals:
  • Forward Replies: Select this if the From address should also receive recipients’ replies.
  • Auto-respond to Replies: Sends a specified automatic reply to anyone who replies. Set up an autoresponder beforehand at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.
  • Opt-Out Message: Sent to someone who opts out of all mailing lists.
  • Resubscribe Message: Sent to someone who resubscribes to a mailing list.
  • Unsubscribe Message: Sent to someone who unsubscribes from a mailing list.

Edit the Opt-Out, Resubscribe and Unsubscribe messages at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.

docs.title: Tracking tab
docs.text:
• Track Click-Throughs: Records how many users, and which users, click links in the message. It redirects links through your server, replacing them with custom links containing your domain name.
  • Track Opens: Tracks how many people open the email, but an open is not recorded if the recipient blocks remote images, even if they read it. Blocking remote content is common.

You can set the defaults for click-through and open tracking at Administer > CiviMail > CiviMail Component Settings.

HTML link caution: Some phishing filters may treat a link as unsafe if its displayed text differs from its destination. Rather than <a href="http://example.com">http://Example.com</a>, use <a href="http://example.com">click here to go to Example</a>.

Plain-text link caution: With click-through tracking, short URLs are replaced by long links containing your site name and a code, such as http://example.com/sites/all/modules/civicrm/extern/url.php?u=529&qid=29011.

docs.title: Review results for a sent mass mailing
docs.text:
Use a mailing’s Report to see tracked results, then open a statistic when you need to see the contacts behind it.

  1. Go to Mailings > Scheduled and Sent Mailings.

  2. Find the mailing in the list, or use the filters above it.

  3. Click Report in its “action” column. The report shows basic information about tracked actions, including opens, link click-throughs and the percentage of bounces; see Managing bounces for more about bounces.

  4. Click a statistic’s name to see the contacts it applies to and further details, such as the time an email was opened for tracked opens. You can also find the mailing’s “Bulk Email” record in the Activities tab of a contact’s profile when that contact was sent the mailing.

  5. To narrow the contacts behind a statistic, click Advanced Search beside it. The search opens with the relevant email attributes filled in, ready for more criteria. For example, clicking beside Tracked Opens starts a search for contacts who opened the email; you could then narrow it to people aged 21 to 30 or registered for a given event. See Searching for more about advanced searches.

docs.title: Where to find and manage mass mailings
docs.text: Use the Mailings menu to find a mailing according to its stage and check the actions available there.

docs.title: Draft and Unscheduled Mailings
docs.text: A message appears here after you name it in Step 1 and click Next. If you click Save & Continue Later or leave a message after completing some steps, use Continue beside it to resume work. You can also Delete drafts here.

docs.title: Scheduled and Sent Mailings
docs.text:
A mailing appears here when you send or schedule it and remains until it is archived or deleted.

  • Report shows delivery results.
  • Copy starts another mailing based on the existing one.
  • Archive and Delete are under more. A mailing that is scheduled but not yet sent has Cancel instead of Archive.
  • Pause and Resume are also under more. Pausing is gradual, not instantaneous. You can use it when you want another scheduled or pending mailing to send first.

docs.title: Archived Mailings
docs.text: This area lists mailings archived from Scheduled and Sent Mailings. Archived mailings cannot be included in or excluded from a recipient list. The same actions otherwise remain available as in Scheduled and Sent Mailings, including viewing Reports and using Copy.

docs.title: Create and send a mass mailing with CiviMail
docs.text: Use this guide to choose recipients, prepare your message, check it and submit it for sending. CiviMail also supports tracking responses, processing bounces and letting people unsubscribe.

docs.title: Choose recipients
docs.text:
You can start with existing Groups or with search results. Most of the mailing process is the same, but a search-based mailing requires an Unsubscribe Group.

Every mass mailing needs a way to track unsubscribe requests. A simple unsubscribe process is required by law in many countries and may help prevent your mailings from being treated as spam. When you mail a Group, people who unsubscribe are excluded the next time you mail that Group. Search results do not provide that built-in tracking, so you must designate a Group for it.

For a search-based mailing, a contact who has already unsubscribed from the designated Unsubscribe Group will not receive the mailing. If they use the mailing’s unsubscribe link, they will be unsubscribed from that Group and will not receive future emails sent to it, whether or not they were originally a member.

The Unsubscribe Group records unsubscribes; it does not add its members to the mailing. A member who does not match your search will not receive the message unless you also include the relevant Group.

For example, suppose your organisation wants to announce an event to contacts added in the last week. You could find them through Search > Custom Search > Date Added to CiviCRM and use those results for the mailing. If your event email list is a Group called Event Alerts, you would probably choose Event Alerts as the Unsubscribe Group. If no suitable Group exists, you may want to create one called “Miscellaneous Mail Unsubscribes” and add it to future mailings to exclude people who have unsubscribed.

docs.title: Know when recipients are fixed
docs.text:
When you submit a mailing, its recipient list is set from the mailing’s Groups at that moment—even if you schedule it for a month later. It does not update when the mailing is sent. Contacts who are opted out, marked do not email, deceased or deleted, or whose email is on hold at sending time will not receive it.

For a smart group, the recipient list reflects its criteria when you submit the mailing, not when it is sent. From search results, selecting All NNN records and then using the Actions dropdown to send a mailing creates a hidden smart group. Its members are updated against the search criteria when you submit the mailing. To use a group that will not update against those criteria, select all records using the checkbox at the top of each page, then choose NNN Selected records only. This creates a non-smart group containing those contacts.

docs.title: Define the mailing
docs.text:
1. Start from one of these places:
  2. For an existing Group, go to Mailings > New Mailing.
  3. For search results, run your search—for example, at Search > Advanced Search—then choose **Email
  4. Schedule/Send via CiviMail** from Actions.

Both routes open similar Define Mailing screens. For search results, “Search Results” is included in Recipients and cannot be removed, and you must choose an Unsubscribe Group. The HTML pane is open by default on the search-based screen; it was closed in the image to show the bottom buttons.

  1. Enter a Mailing Name that you and others in your organisation will recognise. This is an internal name, not the subject recipients will see.

  2. Check Recipients and, if this mailing is based on search results, choose the Unsubscribe Group. The estimated final number of recipients appears to the right of Recipients, highlighted in yellow.

  3. Enter the email Subject. You can use tokens in it.

  4. Compose the message in HTML, or open Plain Text and enter a plain-text message. You can personalise the message with tokens. If you only want to send plain text, you can ignore HTML.

The Mailing tab contains all compulsory fields. Use the other tabs if you need attachments or different header, footer, publication, response or tracking settings. You can click Save Draft at any stage.

docs.title: Preview and test
docs.text:
Before sending a test to an email address that is not already in CiviCRM: doing so creates a new contact record.

Use Preview at the bottom of the Define Mailing screen to check the HTML or Plain Text version. The HTML preview shows formatting and tokens converted using your data, but not attachments. Email clients may display it differently, so the preview is useful for checking basic layout, font consistency and colour, not for guaranteeing the final appearance.

You can send a test to one email address or an existing CiviCRM Group. The test fills in all tokens and includes planned attachments. Send one to yourself and view it in your email client; for a complex layout, use a test Group to check different email clients. It is preferable to ask more than one person for feedback. See Testing templates in the Set-up section for more tips.

docs.title: Review and submit
docs.text:
1. Click Next > at the lower left to open Step 2: Review and Schedule.

  2. Check the Review panel. Click ~XX recipients to see the names and email addresses on the recipient list. Click HTML or Plain Text to see the message with any header or footer, and click an envelope to see the named message. Ticks and struck-through crosses show which tracking and response choices are on or off.

  3. Choose to send immediately or set a date and time in Schedule.

  4. Click Submit Mailing.

By default, CiviMail checks for mailings ready to send every 15 minutes, so sending may start up to 15 minutes later. Mailings to large recipient lists are sent in batches of about 400 to reduce the likelihood of spam filtering; delivery can take several hours, depending on your server configuration.

docs.title: Message template HTML and editor behaviour
docs.text: Use these details when preparing HTML for a message template or choosing an editor.

docs.title: Full HTML documents
docs.text:
HTML pasted into a User-Driven template may be a full document, such as one copied from an email design tool or an older CiviCRM sample template. Unlike content intended only for the body of an email, a full document has its own <!DOCTYPE>, <html>, <head> and <body> tags.

Switching a full document to the rich text (WYSIWYG) editor keeps only the content inside <body>. It discards the <!DOCTYPE>, <html> and <head> wrapper and anything in it. CiviCRM warns you before this happens.

Usually, losing the wrapper is harmless for a CiviMail User-Driven message: CiviMail combines a separate Header, the message and a separate Footer into one email. It is not harmless if the document’s <head> contains styling needed for display, commonly a <style> block that makes a layout responsive across screen sizes, with a <meta name="viewport"> tag and media queries, for example. Switching to the rich text editor then silently removes that styling. If you are unsure, keep editing in Raw HTML mode or check with whoever built the template.

docs.title: HTML email design
docs.text:
HTML allowed in email is more restricted than HTML used for web pages. Email templates need tables for layout and inline CSS, and must not include background images.

Element Consideration Table borders An HTML <table> element can have a border attribute. Its default is 0, so a border does not appear unless you set one. Setting it to 1, for example <table border="1">, shows table edges and can help you find layout problems. Email templates often have multiple or nested tables. Make one change at a time and switch to HTML view to see the result. Put spaces between a table’s parameters. Table spacing Adjust cellpadding and cellspacing in different tables to improve readability. Width Keep an email no wider than 600 pixels for maximum compatibility across email clients. The outermost table, tables within it and the total width of each image should not exceed 600 pixels. An image’s horizontal padding can add to its width. Images Images must be online and accessible. Set each image’s width and height to suit the template, then save it with as small a file size as possible. Free online resources can help you resize an image if you do not have, or do not know how to use, image-editing software.

docs.title: Editors
docs.text: CiviCRM includes two WYSIWYG editors, CKEditor and TinyMCE, and a plain text editor, Textarea. If your Drupal, Joomla or WordPress installation has another editor configured, you can choose it instead at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences by selecting a different WYSIWYG Editor.

docs.title: Modify system workflow message templates
docs.text:
You can change the text or branding of a pre-configured message, such as a contribution receipt or event registration confirmation. These templates include program logic that displays constituent information such as contribution amounts, payment methods and event fees.

Before editing: CiviCRM sometimes updates system workflow templates during version upgrades. Once you customise a template, CiviCRM stops applying updates to it. This preserves your changes, but you may miss important updates as functionality changes. The System Administrator Guide has instructions for merging conflicting edits when both your organisation and an upgrade change the same template; that process is not easy. Avoid editing these templates unless you need to.

As of CiviCRM 5.76, you do not need to edit a Message Template to add your organisation’s logo or other branding. You can use the {site.message_header} Site Token instead.

  1. Go to Administer > Communication > Message Templates.
  2. Open the System Workflow Message tab to see the templates you can modify.
  3. Choose the message to change. Both HTML and Text formats are provided.

Before changing the content: Do not modify the program logic in a workflow template. In most cases, you can restrict changes to the top row of the HTML layout.

  1. Make the text or layout changes you need, such as adding wording or a logo to the HTML version.
  2. Test the workflow and review the emails it sends for errors or missing information.

If your changes cause problems, you can return to the system default for that workflow. After a template has been customised, a Revert to Default link appears next to it; select that link to revert to CiviCRM’s version.

docs.title: Variables and tokens in workflow message templates
docs.text:
Use this reference to distinguish tokens from Smarty variables and check the variables described for contribution workflow messages.

A token has no dollar sign, for example {contribution.tax_amount}. Smarty variables have a dollar sign: {$taxAmount} and {$contribution.tax_amount} are examples. Tokens are generally consistent across multiple screens. Available Smarty variables depend on what has been coded and vary considerably. CiviCRM is moving towards tokens in workflow templates where possible, but some variables are specific to a template or more complex. Work to standardise and document the available Smarty variables is ongoing.

As of CiviCRM 5.53, all contribution workflow message templates should support all contact and contribution tokens, as well as the following Smarty variables:

Variable Meaning Detail Example $isShowLineItems Whether the contribution uses a price set TRUE or FALSE {if $isShowLineItems}...{/if} $isShowTax Whether sales tax is enabled for the site TRUE or FALSE {if $isShowTax}...{/if} $taxRateBreakDown An array of the amount charged at each tax rate [] for no tax or {foreach from=$taxRateBreakdown item=taxDetail key=taxRate}{$taxDetail.percentage}%{/if}{/foreach}

$lineItem is an array of line items. The source gives this example using $lineItems:

  {if $isShowLineItems}
    <tr>
    <td colspan="2" {$valueStyle}>
      <table>
      <tr>
        <th>{ts}Item{/ts}</th>
        <th>{ts}Qty{/ts}</th>
        <th>{ts}Each{/ts}</th>
        {if $isShowTax && '{contribution.tax_amount|raw}' !== '0.00'}
          <th>{ts}Subtotal{/ts}</th>
          <th>{ts}Tax Rate{/ts}</th>
          <th>{ts}Tax Amount{/ts}</th>
        {/if}
        <th>{ts}Total{/ts}</th>
      </tr>
      {foreach from=$lineItems item=line}
        <tr>
        <td>
          {$line.title}
        </td>
        <td>
          {$line.qty}
        </td>
        <td>
          {$line.unit_price|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
        </td>
        {if $isShowTax && '{contribution.tax_amount|raw}' !== '0.00'}
          <td>
            {$line.unit_price*$line.qty|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
          </td>
          {if $line.tax_rate || $line.tax_amount != ""}
            <td>
              {$line.tax_rate|string_format:"%.2f"}%
            </td>
            <td>
              {$line.tax_amount|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
            </td>
          {else}
            <td></td>
            <td></td>
          {/if}
        {/if}
        <td>
          {$line.line_total+$line.tax_amount|crmMoney:'{contribution.currency}'}
        </td>
        </tr>
      {/foreach}
      </table>
    </td>
    </tr>

  {/if}

docs.title: Create and manage user-driven message templates
docs.text:
Create a template when your organisation wants to reuse an email, or part of one, in a mass mailing or a Send Email activity.

User-driven messages are created by staff to communicate with constituents. Thank-you letters and meeting announcements are examples. Message templates remain available when CiviMail is disabled.

docs.title: Save a message as a template
docs.text: When composing a Send Email activity or a mass mailing, select Save as New Template on the message creation screen.

docs.title: Create a template from scratch
docs.text:
You can open message templates through Mailings > Message Templates or Administer > Communications > Message Templates. You can also start at the Administer CiviCRM page and choose Message Templates in the Communications section.

  1. Open the message template list. If no templates exist, it displays: “There are no Message Templates entered. You can add one.”
  2. Select Add Message Template, >>New Message Template, or add one, according to the option shown. This opens the New Message Template page.
  3. Enter a Message Title. It organises your messages and does not appear in the email.
  4. Enter a Message Subject. You can use tokens to personalise it.
  5. Create your message in HTML Message or the HTML Format section. You can use tokens in the message to personalise details such as names, dates and gift amounts.
  6. Leave Text Message blank unless you have a strong reason to write and maintain a separate text version. A fully empty text version is generated from the HTML version when the message is sent.
  7. Select Enabled? to make the template available for use.
  8. Select Save to save the template, or Cancel to cancel.

After a successful save, you may see a confirmation such as: “The Message Template "Membership Renewal Initial Message" has been saved.”

docs.title: Enter HTML directly
docs.text:
The WYSIWYG editor toolbar has a Source icon. Its appearance and label depend on whether you use Drupal, Joomla or WordPress. Select it to view the HTML code if you want to paste HTML from an external template, write HTML directly or change HTML made with the editor. You can also find sample email templates online; resources about creating HTML email templates need not be specific to CiviCRM.

Before switching a full HTML document back to the rich text editor: If it contains a <!DOCTYPE>, <html>, <head> and <body>, the editor keeps only the content inside <body>. CiviCRM warns you before discarding the wrapper and anything in <head>. This can remove a <style> block needed for responsive layout, including styling associated with a <meta name="viewport"> tag and media queries. If you are unsure whether the document needs that content, keep editing in Raw HTML mode or check with the person who built the template.

docs.title: Maintain a separate plain text version
docs.text:
Messages can be sent in plain text or HTML. Sending a plain text version as well as HTML helps ensure recipients can read the message. The recommended option is to leave the text version fully blank so it is generated from HTML when sent.

If you enter a separate text version, you must keep it up to date yourself. Otherwise, people using plain text-only email clients may receive an incorrect or incomplete message. This may include visually impaired people whose email reading software prefers the text version.

To create a separate plain text version from HTML:

  1. Copy the text from the WYSIWYG view of the HTML Format field into the Plain Text Format field. Do not copy from Source view: you need the text, not the code. Pasting from the WYSIWYG view strips formatting and other elements that do not work in plain text.
  2. Copy each link’s URL to the appropriate place in the Plain Text Format field.
  3. If the HTML contains tables, adjust the text layout so it remains readable.

docs.title: Manage an existing template
docs.text:
The template list provides links to Edit, Preview, Disable and Delete existing templates.

  • Edit: Change the template’s options on the Edit Template page. You can also check or uncheck Enabled? at the bottom of the page. Select Save to keep your changes. A successful save may display: “The Message Template "Membership Renewal Initial Message" has been saved.”
  • Disable: Select Disable to temporarily disable a template. At “Are you sure you want to disable this Message Template?”, select OK to continue or Cancel to keep it enabled. Select Enable to re-enable it.
  • Delete: Select Delete. At “Do you want to delete this message template?”, select Delete to continue or Cancel to keep it.

docs.title: Review bounced emails
docs.text:
Use the Bounces report to find delivery problems, correct email addresses and make corrected addresses available for future mailings.

If your server is set up to process bounces, a contact is marked On Hold when their email bounces. Further messages to that address are suppressed until you remove its On Hold status.

  1. Open the mailing report from Mailings > Scheduled and Sent Mailings.
  2. Select Bounces in the Delivery Summary to review the bounced addresses.
  3. Check the reason for each bounce. An incorrect address, such as contact@gooogle.com, may be the cause.
  4. Correct any email addresses you can verify.
  5. Remove the corrected addresses’ On Hold status.
  6. To re-use the mailing, add it to the EXCLUDE Recipients of These Mailing(s) list on the Select Recipients screen of the re-used mailing setup.

You can also find emails that are On Hold with Search > Advanced search. In its Mailings area, you can search by bounce type.

docs.title: Mailing report statistics
docs.text:
Use this page to understand the delivery and click-through figures in an individual mailing report, and the reporting options in CiviReport.

You can view an individual mailing report from Mailings > Scheduled and Sent Mailings. The report uses live data, so you can refresh the page to see updated figures. Some figures are available only if you enabled the relevant tracking when you set up the mailing.

docs.title: Delivery summary
docs.text:
The Delivery Summary shows high-level statistics. Select a link in the summary to see the contacts who took that action.

Statistic What it shows Intended Recipients The number of people the mailing was intended for. Unique Opens The number of people or bots CiviCRM thinks opened the email, if you enabled Open tracking. Total Opens The total number of times CiviCRM thinks people or bots opened the email, if you enabled Open tracking. Click-throughs The total number of times people clicked links in the email, if you enabled click tracking. Forwards The number of times people forwarded the email using a forward link included as a token in the mailing. Replies The number of times people replied to the email, if you enabled reply tracking. Bounces The number of email addresses that could not be delivered to, if you enabled bounce processing. Unsubscribe requests The number of people who clicked an unsubscribe link included in the email.

docs.title: How open tracking works
docs.text:
There is no completely reliable way to know whether someone opened an email. Like other mass mailers, CiviCRM embeds a small image with a unique name in each email. When an email client downloads that image, CiviCRM records an open.

To protect privacy, most email clients ask people whether they want to download images. The reported figure therefore reflects image downloads, not every person who read the email; the actual number of readers is higher than the number reported. Treat tracked opens as indicative rather than exact. In the experience described here, a reported opening rate of 30% can be considered good, though this varies by organisation and audience.

Rather than focusing on absolute figures, you can compare mailings to see how different layouts, writing styles and lengths work for your constituents.

docs.title: Click-through summary
docs.text:
This section shows two statistics for each link:

  • Clicks: The number of times the link was clicked.
  • Unique clicks: The number of people who clicked the link.

docs.title: Reports in CiviReport
docs.text:
CiviReport offers four reports with similar functionality: Mail Bounce Report, Mail Summary Report, Mail Clickthrough Report and Mail Opened Report. Available from the Reports menu, they let you report on multiple mailings and use other CiviReport features, including adding reports to dashboards and having reports emailed.

See Reporting for more information.

docs.title: Scheduled reminder options and behaviour
docs.text:
Use this page to check what scheduled reminders can target and how their timing affects delivery.

Scheduled reminders send email or SMS messages automatically when contacts meet the selected criteria. For example, you can remind participants about a training course the day before it starts, or send membership renewal emails as the end date approaches.

docs.title: Supported entities
docs.text:
You can create reminders for these CiviCRM components (Entities) at Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders:

Entity Available criteria and examples Contacts Use Birth Date, Created Date, Modified Date, or a custom contact date field, such as a marriage date or qualification expiry date. A reminder can be sent every year on the same date for an anniversary, or once in relation to the actual date for a non-repeating event such as an expiring qualification. By default, a reminder created from this screen applies to all contacts with a date set in the selected field; limit recipients if, for example, only children should receive birthday greetings. Activities Use any combination of core and custom activity types, with any combination of statuses such as scheduled, completed or cancelled. Recipients can be Activity Assignees, Activity Targets or Activity Sources for the selected types and statuses. For example, reminders could tell staff about assigned interviews, notify the person who scheduled an activity when it is completed, or thank someone who met with you. You could also log major-donor calls as Phone Call activities and email the Activity Details to your executive director. Contributions Email contributors based on the contribution page they used or the contribution/financial type of their donation. You can select contribution pages or financial types alongside any combination of contribution statuses. Memberships Select by characteristics including membership type and status. For example, you could email current members one month before their membership end date, send a “sorry you are leaving” email one week after it, or send an engagement letter two weeks after the membership start date to remind members of their benefits. Membership-related activities, such as Membership Signup, can also be used as the basis for a reminder. Events Select specific events or all events of selected types, such as conferences or meetings. You can target all participants or selected participant statuses, such as registered, attended, cancelled or no-show, and all or selected participant roles, such as volunteer or host.

Event reminders can also be created on an event's Schedule Reminders screen: use the Schedule Reminders tab while setting up an Event, or Configure > Schedule Reminders beside the event on the Manage Events screen. The configuration steps are the same as on the administration screen. A reminder created from the event configuration screen applies only to that event; use the administration screen for reminders covering all events of a selected type, such as evaluation forms after workshops.

Event reminders can serve different purposes: emailing volunteers before an annual fundraising dinner with their arrival time, fundraising to training-course attendees the day after a course, requesting attendee feedback, thanking speakers and hosts, or asking registered people who did not attend why they could not come.

docs.title: Tokens
docs.text:
Alongside the standard CiviMail tokens, scheduled reminders can use tokens for the event, activity, contribution or membership they concern. This lets one template work across different events, membership types, contribution types or activity types.

For example, an event location token supplies the specific event's location, while a membership message can use an individual's expiry date. Membership and event ID tokens can be used to create links to specific pages, such as a membership renewal page. The checksum token can authenticate people to specific pages without a login and show forms with details already filled in.

docs.title: When event reminders are sent
docs.text: Timing selected Delivery behaviour A specific date The reminder is sent only on that date. Contacts registered earlier receive it when the Send Scheduled Reminders cron job first runs that day, likely shortly after midnight. Contacts who register that day receive it shortly after registration. Those who register later do not receive it. Before the event start or end Registrants who register before the event ends receive it, including those who register after the selected reminder time. After the event start or end Any registrant receives it, regardless of when they register. Before the registration start or end Contacts who register up to the registration end receive it. After the registration start or end The reminder is not sent at all.

docs.title: Check a scheduled reminder that was not received
docs.text:
Use the activity record first to distinguish a reminder that was sent from one that did not run for the contact.

  1. Open Find Activities.
  2. Search with Activity Type set to Reminder Sent, or Membership Renewal Reminder for a membership renewal.

If matching activities appear for the contacts, the reminder may have been sent but not received, for example because of an email delivery issue.

If no matching Reminder Sent or Membership Renewal Reminder activities appear, check these conditions:

  • The contact is deleted or deceased.
  • The contact has Do not email enabled, or their email address is On hold. Opting out of bulk emails alone does not prevent scheduled reminders.
  • For a Membership Renewal Reminder, Status Override? is enabled on the Membership. The selected status then remains in force, and no Membership Renewal Reminder is sent.
  • The Send Scheduled Reminders scheduled job is not enabled or is not configured to run Always. It must execute when the reminder's criteria are met; delays can cause those criteria to be skipped.
  • The scheduled reminder is disabled.
  • Limit or Add Recipients is set to Limit To, but the target contact is not included.
  • No scheduled reminder matches the contact's criteria.
  • The reminder's When (trigger date) has passed or otherwise has not been met.

docs.title: Create and manage scheduled reminders
docs.text:
Set up an email or SMS message to be sent automatically when contacts meet criteria you choose.

Your system administrator needs to ensure that the Send Scheduled Reminders scheduled job is enabled and runs at least once a day. See Scheduled Jobs for configuration details.

docs.title: Create a reminder
docs.text:
You can create a reminder at Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders, or while creating an event. To create one from the administration page:

  1. Go to Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders and click Add Reminder.
  2. Give the reminder a name that you and others will recognise.
  3. Select an Entity. The options available in the adjacent window depend on your selection.
  4. Select the options that the reminder should cover. The middle field allows multiple selections; depending on those selections, a third set of options appears in the right-hand box, which is usually also a multi-select field.
  5. Choose when to send the reminder: on a set date, or a period before or after the start or end of the selected entity.
  6. Check Repeat if the same group should receive the reminder more than once. Choose the repeat interval and when repetition should end.
  7. Check Record activity for automated email if you want a record of the contacts who received the reminder.
  8. Fill in From Name and/or From Email if you do not want to use your site's default name and email address.
  9. Choose recipients using the options described below.
  10. Choose email, SMS, or either method according to each contact's preferred method(s) of communication.
  11. Compose the message using a Message Template or by writing it from scratch.
  12. Click Save.

The SMS option is available only if you have set up an SMS Gateway.

You can edit, disable or delete reminders at Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders.

docs.title: Choose recipients
docs.text:
The Entity options determine the initial audience. For example, you can choose an event type and participant status, a membership type and auto-renew option, an activity type and status, or an entry in a contact date field.

For activity reminders, use Recipient to choose Activity Assignees (contacts in Assigned To), Activity Source (the logged-in user who added the Activity), or Activity Targets (contacts in With Contact). You can instead choose a predefined group with Select a group, or specify contacts with Choose recipient(s). A selected group or contact receives the reminder only if they also meet its other criteria.

For Event, Contact and Membership reminders, set Limit or Add Recipients to Limit to to restrict the audience. Then choose Select a group, Choose recipient(s) or, for Event reminders only, Participant Role. You could, for example, limit birthday greetings to members under

  1. Selected groups, contacts and roles must still meet the reminder's other criteria.

To send the reminder to contacts who do not meet its general criteria, set Limit or Add Recipients to Also include. You can then select a group or an individual. For example, you could also send a reminder scheduled for event registrants two days before an event to Bob Adams, your office manager, so he remembers to check the room setup and equipment.

docs.title: Configure membership reminder examples
docs.text:
Renewal reminder: To email members five days before their membership expires, set Entity Type to Membership and select one or more Membership Types. If those types allow auto-renewal, you may want to include only memberships that do not renew automatically. Set When to five days before Membership End Date, do not select Repeat, then check Send Email and choose a Template or create and save one. If a member renews, they will receive their next reminder five days before their new Membership End Date. Information to include in the email is discussed in Renewals in the CiviMember section.

Pending membership payment: To contact people whose membership is pending because payment has not been received, create a smart group of contacts with a pending membership status. Set the reminder's Entity Type to Activity, with Membership Signup and Completed selected—not the Membership entity. Set Restrict Recipients to the membership pending smart group. Without that restriction, members who have already paid will also receive the message.

docs.title: Exclude contacts who opted out of bulk email
docs.text:
Scheduled reminders are still sent to contacts who have opted out of bulk emails. That may be appropriate for an upcoming event or membership renewal, but not for every reminder. Scheduled reminders are not sent to contacts with Do not email selected or an email address On hold.

To exclude contacts who opted out of bulk email from a particular reminder:

  1. At Search > Search Builder, find contacts who have not selected Do not email or NO BULK EMAIL, using the criteria shown below.
  2. Create a smart group from the search results.
  3. Select that smart group as the reminder's Recipients.

docs.title: Allow people to sign up for mailing lists online
docs.text: Make a mailing list group public, then offer either a subscribe link or a form for people to join it.

docs.title: Make the group available
docs.text:
1. Go to Contacts > Manage Groups.
  2. Click Settings for the group that holds your mailing list recipients.
  3. Check Mailing List under Group Type if you did not select it when creating the Group.
  4. Change Visibility to Public Pages.

For people without a CiviCRM login to sign up on Drupal, anonymous users must have the Access CiviMail subscribe/unsubscribe pages permission.

docs.title: Share the subscribe link
docs.text:
Direct people to the subscribe page for your site:

Platform Example address Drupal example.org/civicrm/mailing/subscribe Backdrop example.org/civicrm/mailing/subscribe WordPress with clean URLs example.org/civicrm/mailing/subscribe?reset=1 WordPress without clean URLs, the default for CiviCRM instances installed before version 5.13 example.org/civicrm?page=CiviCRM&q=civicrm/mailing/subscribe&reset=1 Joomla example.org/administrator/index2.php?option=com_civicrm&task=civicrm/mailing/subscribe&reset=1

You and anyone who accesses the link can subscribe to available mailing list groups.

docs.title: Use a profile to collect more information
docs.text:
A profile can collect information beyond a mailing list subscription. For example, create a profile called Newsletter Sign-up and add the fields you want website visitors to complete. Set every field’s Visibility to Public Pages.

You can make individual fields required or optional, but the profile must include a required email field. CiviCRM uses that address to send a confirmation request. Until the person confirms, their mailing list group subscription has a status of Pending.

Choose how to display the profile:

  • Share a public link: At Administer > Custom Data and Screens > Profiles, click More beside the profile, then Use Profile-Create Mode. Your browser opens the public page; publish its link.
  • Embed a form: At Administer > Custom Data and Screens > Profiles, click More beside the profile, then HTML Form Snippet. Copy the HTML code from the window that opens and paste it into a page on your website.
  • Use a WordPress shortcode: On a WordPress Page, click CiviCRM above the editor. Set Page Type to Profile, select your profile from the next drop-down, and select the Edit radio button so users can add information such as their email address and name to your database. Click Insert Form to add the shortcode to the editor.

To add people who complete the profile to a mailing list group, choose one of these options:

  • Let people choose groups: In the profile’s fields, click Add Field. For Field Name, select Contacts, then select Group(s) in the second field. Leave Field Label as “Group(s)” or change it to something clearer for visitors, such as “Newsletter Sign-up.” Set the field’s Visibility to Public Pages. The public form then shows checkboxes for all Mailing List Groups whose Visibility is set to Public Pages, allowing people to choose the groups they want.
  • Add people to one group automatically: In the profile’s Advanced Settings, select the desired Mailing List Group for Add new contacts to a Group? People who complete the form will be added to that group.

docs.title: Use a Drupal Webform
docs.text: Drupal site administrators may prefer a Webform to a profile for newsletter sign-up because it offers features such as advanced spam control and flexible theming. See Webform CiviCRM Integration.

docs.title: Check the confirmation workflow
docs.text:
Before people sign up, check the desired Enable Double Opt-in options at Administer > Administration Console > CiviMail Component Settings.

After someone subscribes through the subscribe link or a profile, CiviCRM sends an email asking them to confirm. Their group subscription remains Pending until they click the confirmation link. CiviCRM then changes the status to Added and sends a welcome message. If someone subscribes to multiple groups at once, CiviCRM sends a separate confirmation email for each group.

docs.title: CiviMail messages, headers and footers
docs.text: Use this reference to identify CiviMail’s automated messages and the parts of a mailing that you can prepare for reuse.

docs.title: Automated Messages
docs.text:
CiviCRM sends Automated Messages in these circumstances:

Action Message Someone signs up for a mailing list A confirmation email containing a link they must click. Someone confirms their subscription A welcome email. Someone unsubscribes, opts out of all emails from your domain, or resubscribes to a list they previously left A confirmation email that requires no action. Someone replies to a CiviMail message An autoresponse, if you set one up.

You can edit Automated Messages and add new ones at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages. For more about unsubscribes, bounces and email holds, see Maintaining healthy email lists.

docs.title: Headers and footers
docs.text:
Headers and footers are available only for CiviMail mass mailings and only when CiviMail is enabled. Manage them at Mailings > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.

  • A header appears above the main email content. It can contain elements such as your organisation’s logo and a newsletter title.
  • A footer is the last part of the email. It is a place for the compulsory unsubscribe tokens.

You can create different headers and footers for different campaigns or programs, with different images and titles. Styling them similarly helps give your messages a consistent identity. Once configured, they are available for staff to select when preparing a new mailing, helping them produce standardised messages that readers can recognise and navigate.

Like Message Templates, headers and footers have both text and HTML versions. Unlike Message Templates, their creation pages do not have a WYSIWYG editor: you must write the HTML directly or use another HTML editor to produce it.

docs.title: Testing templates
docs.text:
Test templates in different email clients, such as Mozilla Thunderbird, MS Outlook, Mac Mail, Gmail, Yahoo and Hotmail. One approach is to create a group with a test contact for each destination and use it for every new mailing.

Email clients can display the same HTML differently. Keep HTML as simple as possible, use only inline CSS or tables for formatting, and include as much of the layout as possible in tested templates. This reduces the review needed for each new mailing.

docs.title: How email auto-filing works
docs.text:
Email auto-filing can record conversations from your regular email client as activities in CiviCRM.

An email is filed when it includes a designated auto-filing address in its To, Cc or Bcc field. Bcc is recommended because the recipient cannot see it. CiviCRM files the email as an activity for contacts whose addresses match the other addresses in the From, To and Cc fields. If an address is not already in CiviCRM, a new contact record is created.

This can also work for inbound email, but it depends on the sender including the auto-filing address in To, Cc or Bcc. An administrator must have configured IMAP or other mail accounts and set them up in CiviMail. See Email System Configuration, particularly Adding an incoming email account for handling bounces or auto filing to CiviMail, in Initial Set-Up.

docs.title: Editing filed email activities
docs.text:
Users cannot normally edit activities created through email-to-activity processing because the Inbound Email activity type restricts editing. An administrator can grant either of these permissions to roles that need to edit them:

Permission What users can edit CiviCRM: edit inbound email basic information Every activity field except the original message stored in the activity’s details. CiviCRM: edit inbound email basic information and content Every activity field, including the original message’s content.

docs.title: Prepare CiviMail for mass mailings
docs.text:
Set up your organisation’s contact details and mailing groups, then check the jobs that send mailings and process bounces.

Your server must already be configured to send and process email. See CiviMail Setup in the System Administrator Guide for server setup, including From email addresses.

docs.title: Add your organisation’s contact information
docs.text:
CiviMail requires your organisation’s name, a short description, an email address and a postal address. Mass mailings must include the sender’s postal address and unsubscribe/opt-out links to comply with privacy laws in many countries. This information is available through tokens and must be included in mail sent with CiviMail.

Go to Administer > Communications > Organization Address and Contact Info to enter the information.

docs.title: Create a mailing list group
docs.text:
CiviMail uses Groups to organise recipients of mass mailings.

  1. Go to Contacts > New Group.
  2. Create the Group and check Mailing List under Group Type so it is available as a Mailing List in CiviMail.
  3. Search for contacts and add them to the Group.

docs.title: Create a Smart Group instead
docs.text:
A Smart Group updates its membership when contacts match its search criteria. For example, a Smart Group based on Advanced Search can include contacts with active memberships or contacts in a given city. As people become members or move to that city, they are automatically added, so you do not have to update the group before mailing it.

  1. Go to Advanced Search or Find Contact and run a search using the criteria for your group.
  2. On the results page, select the radio button for all records.
  3. From Actions, select Group - create smart group.
  4. Review the criteria, give the Smart Group a name and, optionally, a description, and make it a Mailing List.
  5. Click Save Smart Group.

Info

You can create a Smart Group from a Participant search, but its save page will not offer the Mailing List option. To make it available to CiviMail, change its settings at Contacts > Manage Groups. The same applies if you use Advanced Search and choose Event Participants under Display results as.

You cannot create Smart Groups from Membership, Contributions or Pledge searches. You also cannot create one from Advanced Search results when Display results as is set to anything other than Contacts, except for the Event Participants case described above.

docs.title: Check scheduled jobs
docs.text:
Warning: Without Send Scheduled Mailings and Fetch Bounces, CiviMail will not send mailings or process bounced messages.

  1. Go to Administer > System Settings > Scheduled Jobs.
  2. Enable Send Scheduled Mailings, Fetch Bounces and any other jobs you want to run regularly.

Scheduled jobs cannot trigger themselves. Something on your server must trigger them; the most common option is a cron job, which can trigger one, several or all scheduled jobs. See Managing Scheduled Jobs for details and examples.

docs.title: What is CiviMail?
docs.text:
CiviMail helps your organisation send mass email campaigns and understand their results. The examples below show how it can work alongside other CiviCRM components.

CiviMail can reliably deliver a high volume of email and provide detailed reports on the results and effectiveness of those emails. For example, you might email non-members to encourage them to become members, or contact people who have not yet registered for an event.

docs.title: Mail server setup
docs.text:
CiviMail, like all of CiviCRM's mail features, interacts with your mail server. Configuring the mail server and setting up CiviMail properly are system administrator tasks, and you may need professional assistance. You also need to check that your web hosting provider meets the configuration requirements and ask about any limits on how many emails you can send per day.

A misconfigured mail server can put your organisation on a spam blacklist. Getting off one is much harder than getting on one. For more information, see the Email system configuration chapter in the Initial set up section.

docs.title: Managing email lists
docs.text:
St Ethelburga's Centre for Peace and Reconciliation uses CiviEvent to run a yearly programme of events on different themes. People sign up on a mailing list page to hear about events that interest them, and St Ethelburga's uses CiviMail to email them about those events.

When someone unsubscribes from an event theme mailing list, CiviCRM records their choice. St Ethelburga's also automatically subscribes people who have attended an event on a particular theme to emails about that theme. CiviCRM remembers who has unsubscribed and does not re-subscribe them.

From time to time, the centre director sends personal messages highlighting particular issues to a mailing list containing nearly all contacts in the database. To test which message format is more effective, St Ethelburga's often sends two similar versions to different groups. They send one version to half the contacts in a group, then send the other version while excluding contacts who received the first.

docs.title: Mobilising with email
docs.text:
The Townsville Organisation For Tenants (TOFT) held a survey and petition to gather data and support for its Demand Affordable Public Housing campaign. Volunteers visited selected constituents at home to conduct the survey. The petition was widely promoted to the public, who could sign it and answer questions online.

Early in the campaign, the TOFT volunteer coordinator searched for contacts in the group Volunteers and used the Send Email action to ask for help with the survey. A small group of those who said they were available were trained to make home visits and record survey responses.

After creating the online petition with tools in CiviCampaign, the TOFT communications officer prepared an email with text, images and links encouraging people to visit the site and complete it. TOFT sent the email to its entire database using CiviMail. It included a forwarding link so recipients could share the email through their own networks.

CiviMail let TOFT track responses to the mass email. Reports showed that 89% of recipients clicked through to sign the petition and 75% forwarded the email to others. TOFT compared these results with previous offline petition and survey efforts to demonstrate the campaign's increased reach through CiviCRM.

docs.title: Design an email and reusable template
docs.text:
Use these design choices when preparing an email or template for your organisation. Layout and content both affect how well your message works for people reading on phones, tablets, laptops, desktops, browsers and email applications.

  • Start with a reusable base template. Encourage or enforce its use to keep your organisation’s emails consistent. It might be a single-column table layout with a header image and text footer, or a choice of progressively more structured layouts.
  • Keep the layout simple. Complex layouts are more likely to display poorly on some devices. If you use one, test it thoroughly or use an email testing service.
  • Consider an existing responsive template. Responsive email design is challenging because email applications and reading environments vary and do not share universally accepted rendering standards. A well-tested free template may be a better starting point than building one from scratch.
  • Use tables for layout. Unlike websites, where div tags are more appropriate for layout, tables render more consistently across email clients.
  • Use inline CSS. Many commonly used email clients do not support CSS from external files or style blocks. Put styles inline with element tags to improve the chance that they are recognised.
  • Investigate display differences. Tags and CSS styles can render differently between email applications; research why a style is ignored in a particular environment.
  • Give content and presentation equal attention. A strong layout cannot make up for neglected content, and good content can suffer from poor presentation.

docs.title: Plan your use of CiviCRM email
docs.text: Learn how CiviCRM handles different kinds of email and what to consider when planning your organisation’s messages. Read this before you start sending email to contacts; the Everyday Tasks section covers how to carry out the activities described here.

docs.title: How email fits into CiviCRM
docs.text:
CiviCRM sends email in three broad situations:

  • To individuals and small groups through the Send Email action.
  • To larger groups as mass mailings through CiviMail.
  • To individuals as part of workflows in other components, such as an event registration confirmation email.

Unlike email sent through your email client or a bulk email tool other than CiviMail, every message sent through Send Email or CiviMail is stored as an activity in each recipient’s activity history. You can see, for example, that John Doe donated three days after receiving your April newsletter, or that your volunteer coordinator emailed Jane Smith about staffing an information table.

docs.title: Choose between Send Email and CiviMail
docs.text:
Send Email is suited to individuals and small groups. It is available even when the CiviMail component is disabled, and is quicker and easier when you are contacting fewer than 50 recipients and do not need to track opens or link clicks. You can attach files, CC and BCC contacts, and use message templates. Reporting is limited to an activity record for each recipient.

CiviMail is suited to mass mailings and scheduled emails to small groups. It provides bounce processing, reporting, subscription management and, if configured, automatic reply tracking. You can use it to measure opens and link clicks. It takes more work to configure and more steps to send a mailing; you must set up CiviMail before sending mass emails. For more about mailing results, see the Reports and analysis chapter.

The source describes Send Email as limited to a maximum of 50 email addresses, but also says you must use CiviMail for 50 or more contacts at once. For a mailing to 50 contacts, these statements conflict; for fewer than 50, use the other differences above to choose.

docs.title: Replies and longer exchanges
docs.text:
CiviCRM records messages you send with Send Email, but replies arrive at your email address and are not recorded in the database. Do not rely on Send Email to record an extended exchange. To record one, you could create an activity called Email Exchange and paste the conversation into its body, as you would record a telephone call.

CiviMail can file emails that recipients send in reply to a mailing and send an autoresponse to those replies.

docs.title: Choose recipients and manage subscriptions
docs.text:
With Send Email, you can select recipients from a contact record or from search results. With CiviMail, you can use search results or Groups marked as Mailing Lists. Create those Groups before setting up the mailing.

Every CiviMail message must have an unsubscribe link. When a recipient belongs to a Group, an unsubscribe request removes them from that Group’s mailing list. If a recipient selected from search results is not in a Group, CiviCRM must add them to one when they unsubscribe so it can record the request.

CiviCRM also lets you publish a website sign-up page or form, called a profile, for a mailing list. Recipients must be able both to unsubscribe from a mailing list and to opt out of ever receiving email from you. CiviCRM keeps track of those requests. See the Set-Up chapter for more information.

docs.title: Personalise and reuse messages
docs.text:
Both Send Email and CiviMail support tokens: placeholders that CiviCRM replaces with a value, such as a recipient’s name, when it sends each message. Some CiviMail tokens are not available in the Send Email activity.

You can send regular or mass email from your personal address, a general address for your organisation, or another person’s address. For example, an assistant can send an official message under their manager’s name.

Templates let you reuse whole emails or parts of them. You can create a template beforehand or while sending an email, and edit it at any time. For mass mailings, you can also include customised headers and footers. Configure them under Administer > CiviMail > Headers, Footers, and Automated Messages.

docs.title: Record email sent outside CiviCRM
docs.text: CiviCRM can automatically record email sent through your email client. This requires a special email address in the message’s BCC field. CiviCRM reads the message, converts it into an activity and files it against the contact whose email address matches. If that address does not exist in the database, CiviCRM creates a new contact record. See the Email System Configuration chapter in Intial set up for details.

docs.title: Questions to settle before sending
docs.text:
For your organisation’s overall email setup, consider:

  • Which emails do you send repeatedly and want to turn into templates?
  • What content, if any, should appear in every mailing’s header or footer?
  • Do you want a web page where people can sign up?
  • Which kinds of email matter enough to store in recipients’ contact records?

For a particular message, consider:

  • How many people will receive it?
  • Do you need to know who opens it or clicks its links?
  • Have you created a Group or Smart Group to send it to?
  • Should recipients be able to view the mailing in a browser if they have trouble viewing it in their email browser?
  • Who should appear as the sender: a general organisation address or a named person?

Other CiviCRM components use email and CiviMail for messages such as confirmations, thank-yous and receipts. Read the sections for those components alongside this section to understand how to customise their messages.

docs.title: Privacy and delivery risks
docs.text:
Email privacy laws differ by country, including rules about opt-out and unsubscribe options. Consider whether CiviMail’s tracking is appropriate for a particular message: for example, you may not want to track who clicks a link titled “how to deal with drug issues” in a mailing.

Mass email can be marked as spam, affecting delivery of both the current mailing and future email from your server. Managing deliverability is complex and outside the scope of this guide. If your organisation does not have a system administrator, consultant or email hosting service knowledgeable about these issues, consider seeking expert advice.

docs.title: Set up discounts by sign-up date
docs.text:
Use Discounts by sign up date to offer early bird rates when your event uses a simple fee structure. During the dates you specify, these discounts override the regular event fees.

  1. In the fees section of your event configuration, check Discounts by sign up date beneath the regular fees. A new fee table appears towards the bottom of the page, duplicating the original fee table.
  2. Create a discount set and add it to the fee table.
  3. Edit the labels and fees in the new table to match the discounts for each original fee option.

You can create multiple date-based discount sets for an event. For example, a series of early bird dates can progressively increase the registration cost as the event gets closer.

Discount sets and discounts through price sets are built-in CiviCRM options for discounts based on sign-up dates. For other types of discounts, the CiviDiscount extension offers options such as discount codes and discounts based on membership status.

docs.title: Create complex event fees with a price set
docs.text:
Use a price set when the regular fees layout, which lets a registrant select one fee option, does not meet your event’s needs. A price set breaks fees into pieces so you can charge for optional items, such as a post-conference dinner or a book.

This example shows registration fees for a conference with optional pre-conference training, meals and lodging:

docs.title: Create the price set
docs.text:
It helps to plan your registration fees and build the price set before creating the event. If you have already started creating the event, you can finish that process, create the price set, and return to the event configuration page to assign it.

  1. Navigate to CiviEvent > New Price Sets.
  2. Enter a name in the Price Set form.
  3. Check Used For > Event.
  4. Select the financial type to be used, such as Event Fee.
  5. If helpful, add pre or post form help text for the registrant.
  6. Check Is this price set active.
  7. Press Save. A form appears for the first field in your price set.

docs.title: Add price fields
docs.text:
1. Enter a name for the event item in Field Label.
  2. Choose an Input Field Type:
Input Field Type What the registrant can do Text/Numeric Quantity Enter a quantity in a text box. CiviEvent multiplies that quantity by the unit value to calculate the fee. Select Choose one option from a dropdown list. Radio Choose one fee option from a list. Checkbox Select or unselect any number of options in a list.

You can combine these field types to build your fee structure. This example shows a price field for pre-conference training with two options:

  1. If each unit should count towards the event’s maximum number of participants, enter a number in Participant Count. For example, set it to 8 for a fundraiser table that seats eight people.
  2. For Text/Numeric Quantity, enter a unit amount in Price. For Select, Radio and Checkbox, enter a price for each option in the options table.
  3. Check Display Amount? if you want the price to appear next to the event item.
  4. Set Field Help, whether the item is required, Visibility and whether it is Active as needed. Visibility determines whether the item is public or visible only to the administrator. These fields are described in the Custom fields chapter of Organising your data.
  5. If needed, choose the dates when the price field is active. You can use different fields for very early discounted rates, standard rates until two weeks before the event, and premium rates during the final two weeks.
  6. Press Save to finish this field, or Save and New to create another field in the price set.

docs.title: Assign the price set to an event
docs.text:
On the event’s Fees tab, select the price set’s name in the Price Set field.

You can reuse a price set across multiple events, such as events in a regional training seminar programme.

docs.title: Manage an existing price set
docs.text: To manage CiviEvent price sets, navigate to Manage Price Sets and choose Events, or navigate to CiviEvent > Manage Price Sets and choose Administer.

docs.title: Event information and settings
docs.text:
Use this page to check the options on the first event creation screen. Click a blue question mark for field help. A pencil opens a screen for editing available options; if your permissions do not allow that, you will not see the pencil.

Option What it controls From template Creates the event from a template instead of from scratch. See the Event templates chapter in this section. Event type Categorises the event. Campaign If CiviCampaign is enabled, you can select a campaign for the event. See the Campaign section. Roles Distinguish participants such as attendees, speakers and staff. The role selected here is assigned by default when people register online or when you import registrations, unless your CSV import file includes Participant Role with other values. Attendee is the most common value. Participant Listings Enable a list of participants and determine how much information it reveals. Listings can demonstrate support and help generate interest, but enabling one does not display it on your website: you must create a menu item or link to it. After you create the event, its participant listing link appears on the event configuration page. See participant listings and other ways to promote your events in Event management. Event Title Appears on event information pages, registration pages, event listings and the Manage Events administrative page. Choose a meaningful title. Event Summary and Complete Description Both appear on event information pages. The description has a rich-text editor for photos, images and formatted text. Start date/time and End date/time Appear on the event information page and in event listings. Maximum number of participants Sets a participant limit. You can also define the message displayed when the limit is reached. Location map Can show the event location using Google Maps or Open Street Maps. Configure the mapping solution under Administer > System Settings > Mapping and Geocoding. Public Event Includes the event in promotional listings such as RSS feeds, iCal files or feeds, and event listing pages. Allow sharing through social media Adds sharing links to the Event Info page, Thank-you page, Tell-a-Friend page (if enabled), and event confirmation emails. Active or inactive An inactive event is not inadvertently listed on event listing feeds while you finish configuring it. You can activate it when you are ready to publicise it. Show Calendar Links Adds links to the information page and registration emails for downloading a calendar meeting invitation. Test thoroughly if you enable this: calendar invitations do not work well when participants are in different time zones from the server.

docs.title: Set up an event reminder
docs.text:
Create a scheduled reminder to email event registrants at a chosen time before or after an event. For example, you could point them to a conference schedule a week before the event, request feedback a day afterward, or warn someone with a Pending from Pay Later registration two days before payment is due that their registration will be cancelled unless they provide payment details within 48 hours.

  1. Open the event’s scheduled reminders tab. It shows any existing reminders for that event.
  2. Click Add Reminder.

  1. Set the timing and recipients. You can limit recipients by status, such as registered or attended, and by role, such as speaker, attendee or volunteer.
  2. Choose a template or compose a message in the HTML format box. For example, you could email all registered speakers three days before the event start date.

You can also set up reminders for specific event types or add them to specific event templates through Administer > Communications > Scheduled reminders.

docs.title: Edit event confirmation and receipt emails
docs.text:
Change the message templates used for automated confirmation and receipt emails. These emails can go to participants who register online or are registered by staff or volunteers.

Before editing: The templates contain both the text people see and necessary program logic. Take care not to change the program logic.

  1. Go to Administer > Communications > Message Templates.
  2. Open the System Workflow Message tab.
  3. Click Edit next to the “Events - Registration Confirmation and Receipt” rows.
  4. Modify or add text in the provided HTML and Text formats. You can also add branding, such as a logo, to the HTML versions.
  5. Test the workflow and review the emails sent after your changes. If changes cause problems, errors or missing information, you can revert to the system default for that workflow.

To set the from email address for confirmations and receipts, see Set-Up in the Email section.

docs.title: Create an event
docs.text:
Use the event configuration screens to create an event and choose how people can register for it.

If you plan to accept credit card payments through online registration, configure a payment processor before creating the event. See Payment Processors in the Contributions section.

  1. Choose Events > New Event. If you cannot see the Events menu, check that the Events component is enabled under Administer > System Settings > Components.
  2. Complete Event Information and Settings. You can use From template to create the event from a template rather than from scratch; see the Event templates chapter in this section. Click Continue >> to create the event and move to the next screen.
  3. Complete the event location and contact details. You can list phone numbers and email addresses on the event information page so registrants can contact event organisers. For an event away from your organisation’s primary location, you may also want to provide contact information for the meeting location.
  4. Choose whether the location appears on the registration and event information screens.

Before editing a reused location: Changes to an existing location affect every event that uses it. To reuse a location, click Use existing location and select it from the dropdown list.

docs.title: Set event fees
docs.text:
If the event is free, set Paid Event to No, click Save, and skip to Online Registration.

For a paid event:

  1. Set Paid Event to Yes to show the fee options.
  2. Choose the Contribution Type (financial type) assigned to paid registrations. Event Fee is a common value, but you can define multiple Financial Types and assign them to different events. See Set-Up in the Contributions section.
  3. If registrants may pay by mailed check, on-site cash or credit card, or another arrangement, enable the Pay Later option and enter a label and payment instructions. If you leave it unchecked, registrants must pay by credit card.
  4. If you use Regular Fees, add labelled price levels and, if needed, set a default. Registrants select one level—for example, an individual registration for $50 or a family registration for $100.

This example shows fees for members, non-member students and regular non-members:

For more options or add-ons, see the Complex event fees chapter in this section for price sets and discounts.

docs.title: Choose registration and sharing options
docs.text:
If you do not need self-service registration on your website, leave Allow Online Registration unchecked. Otherwise, see Online event registration. For registrations handled by staff or volunteers, see Manual event registration.

On the final event creation page, you can enable Tell-A-Friend and define the text and links shown on its page and in the email sent from the tool.

Each time a participant uses Tell-A-Friend to email friends, a “Tell a friend” activity is added to that participant’s Activities tab. This lets you identify active supporters. People emailed through the feature are also automatically added to CiviCRM as contacts.

You can stop on any subsequent configuration page by clicking Save and Done. To continue later, go to Events > Manage Events and click Configure for the saved event.

docs.title: Where to store custom data for events
docs.text: You can collect extra information about events and their participants with custom data. Where you store each field determines whether it describes a contact, a person's participation, or the event itself. If you are new to custom data, read Custom fields in Organising Your Data first.

docs.title: Choose the right record
docs.text:
