• Contact record: Store information about a person that is unlikely to change between events, such as dietary preference.
  • Participant record: Store information that matters in the context of a particular event, such as session preference.
  • Event record: Store information about the event itself, not its participants.

Choosing the wrong record can make the data harder to use later. In particular, avoid putting information about participants on the event record.

docs.title: Custom data for events
docs.text:
For example, an organisation that holds training workshops throughout the year could use a checkbox-style custom field to track six common workshop topics. If the field is added as custom data for events of the type workshop, it will be available when creating an event of type Workshop.

You do not have to select a specific event type. Leaving the dropdown set to Any makes the field available to all events, regardless of type.

docs.title: Custom data for participants
docs.text:
The participant option you choose controls where a group of custom fields is available:

  • Participants: Available on all participant records. Use this for information that applies to all participants.
  • Participants (Event Name): Available for a specific event. This works like Participants, but lets you collect complex registration data for one event without adding those fields to all events.
  • Participants (Role): Available only for particular types of participants. For example, you could record speakers' biographical profile details with their event registrations.

docs.title: Adding custom data
docs.text:
Adding custom data requires the administrator permission. To add custom data for participants, add new custom fields through Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Custom Data. To create custom fields for events, first add the custom field set on the appropriate record, then add the fields.

You can also create custom fields during event creation; see Creating an event.

docs.title: Planning and managing an event
docs.text: The choices you make before, during and after an event affect how you set it up in CiviEvent and what information you can use afterward.

docs.title: Plan the registration experience
docs.text:
If you are new to CiviEvent, think about the structure of your event and what registration should be like for participants before you configure it. Consider:

  • What types of events does your organisation hold, and what type is this event?
  • What roles will participants have?
  • What information do you need from participants, such as food or lodging preferences?
  • Will people be able to register online?
  • Is there a limit on attendance? If so, will you use a waitlist when registrations exceed it?
  • Will registrations need approval, or can anyone register?
  • Can one person register multiple people?
  • Will registrants receive confirmation?
  • Will the participant listing be public?
  • Does this event repeat regularly with roughly the same details?

For a paid event, also consider its Financial Type and fee structure. Decide whether you need separate fees for sessions or meals, discounts, or early registration.

Think about both the information you need to run the event and what would be useful to collect during it and from participants. If you run similar events repeatedly, event templates or the event copy features may make setup easier.

docs.title: Promote the event
docs.text:
Who you want to attend and where they get information will shape how you promote the event. Consider which channels to use, whether to list it on your website with online registration, and whether email is a good way to reach your constituents. If the event is by invitation only, decide whom to invite. Plan when to send the initial announcement and event reminders.

Listing the event prominently on your organisation’s website and public calendar is one way to promote it. You can also let other people and organisations know about it and encourage participants to spread the word. For website information, see “Integrating events with your website” in the Online event registration chapter.

If another website or organisation’s calendar publicises your event, make the registration method clear. For example, Facebook events and other organisations may have their own registration systems. Wherever someone finds your event, they should be able to tell how you expect them to register.

docs.title: Follow up afterward
docs.text:
Updating each participant’s status during or soon after the event helps keep the information you use to evaluate it accurate.

You may want to email attendees to thank them and share links to online documentation, and send a different message to people who registered but did not attend. Follow-up can also be an opportunity to promote another event, suggest membership of your organisation, or ask for donations to a specific campaign. See Scheduled Reminders in the Email section for more about sending follow-up messages.

docs.title: Create and use an event template
docs.text: Use an event template when you need to set up several events with similar configurations. You can save shared settings, then use the template when creating each event.

docs.title: Create the template
docs.text:
The template form has no starting or ending dates. Set those dates for each actual event.

  1. Go to Events > Event Templates.
  2. Click Add Event Template.
  3. Enter a descriptive template title, such as “Monthly community meetup with online registration”.
  4. Select the event type.
  5. Select a campaign if all events created from this template should be associated with a Campaign.
  6. Continue the normal event set-up process, choosing settings that will stay the same across events. These might include location, event fees, online registration settings and tell-a-friend settings.

docs.title: Use the template
docs.text: When you start to create a new event, select the template from the From template listbox. The new event will be pre-filled with the saved configuration properties.

docs.title: Integrate events with your website
docs.text: You can promote your events on your website or another organisation’s website by sharing event pages or an RSS feed. Depending on your website, you can also display a registration form or a list of upcoming events.

docs.title: Link to an event page
docs.text:
1. Go to Events > Manage Events.
  2. Click Event Links for the event.

The menu includes links to the event info page and the event registration page. The info page also links to the registration page. Copy the URL for the page you want to share, then add that link anywhere on your website.

docs.title: Add an event to a Joomla! menu
docs.text:
1. Go to the Joomla! control panel.
  2. Choose Menu Manager > Your menu name.
  3. Click New.
  4. Expand CiviCRM > CiviCRM Events and click Event Info.
  5. Choose the event from the Select an Event list on the right side of the page.
  6. Click Save.

docs.title: Show a registration form in WordPress
docs.text: Use the CiviCRM icon ‘shortcode’ to insert an event registration form into a Page or Post.

docs.title: List upcoming events in Drupal
docs.text: The Drupal views module offers options for displaying lists of content, including an automatically updating list of upcoming events. For more details, see Integrating with Drupal in the Website integration chapter.

docs.title: Share an RSS feed of upcoming events
docs.text:
Visitors can subscribe to all your events in the RSS feed reader of their choice. Many website management systems can also subscribe to an RSS feed and show its information within the website’s layout.

  1. Go to Events > Manage Events.
  2. Click the orange and white square icon at the top right of the page.
  3. Copy the URL to share or embed in your website.

docs.title: Find event participants and individual fees
docs.text: Use the Dashboard for an upcoming event’s participant list, Find Participants for a search with more criteria, or Event Aggregate to list individual fees.

docs.title: View participants for an upcoming event
docs.text:
1. Go to Events > Dashboard.
  2. Click the Counted: link for the event to see its contacts.

If a count is zero, its text is not a link. Some participant roles, such as someone on clean-up duty, may not count towards the event total.

docs.title: Search for participants
docs.text:
1. Go to Events > Find Participants.
  2. Start typing in the event name field, then select the event from the list.
  3. Set any additional search choices for the fields you want to see.
  4. Click Search.

The results let you select all participants or a subset for an action. This search is for existing participants; to add someone, see the Manual event registration chapter.

docs.title: List individual fees
docs.text:
1. Go to Search > Custom Searches.
  2. Click Event Aggregate.
  3. Choose your search criteria.
  4. Click Search.

docs.title: Change an existing participant’s event selections
docs.text:
Edit an event registration when a participant needs different selections, a different fee option or a different role.

For example, back-office staff might change an online registration from attendee to volunteer and choose a zero-fee option in an admin-only price field. A participant might withdraw from a conference dinner and request a refund, or add a pre-conference workshop and provide credit card details for the extra charge. A child in a holiday programme might switch from pottery to archery without a fee change, so staff know which session the child should attend.

  1. Open the participant’s event registration. One way is through Events > Find Participants.
  2. Select View or Edit at the right of the event record.

  1. Click Change Selections.
  2. Make the required adjustments.

The event fee adjusts accordingly. Based on the difference between the new event fee and contributions already processed, the event status becomes partially paid, registered or pending refund.

If an additional payment is needed, enter it using the record payment link associated with the event registration record; the payment may be by credit card or an offline method. Use that link for a refund by an offline method only. The section on partial payments describes recording these payments and refunds.

docs.title: Create and print event name badges
docs.text: Create a badge layout for your event, then use it to generate a PDF of name badges for the participants you select.

docs.title: Create a badge layout
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > CiviEvent > Event Badge Layout > New Badge Layout.
  1. Choose the layout settings you need:
Setting Available choices and use Label format Avery 5395 - 2-1/3" x 3-3/8"; A6 Badge Portrait 150x106; Fattorini Name Badge 100x65; or Hanging Badge 3-3/4''x4-3/4''. Image (top left) and Image (top right) Select an existing image or upload a new one. The two positions can hold, for example, your organisation’s logo and a major sponsor’s logo. Elements - Rows Select most standard or custom contact, event and participant fields for up to 6 rows, or select spacer to adjust the layout. Examples include display name, current employer, country and participant role. With appropriate custom fields, you could also show registered sessions or a selected meal option. Barcode? Add a linear barcode or QR code at the bottom of the badge. Enabled? Tick this for people to use the layout. You can untick it when a special layout, such as one for an annual conference, should not be used. Reserved? Select this to help prevent admin users from accidentally deleting the layout.

You cannot preview the badge layout unless at least one event has been created and at least one participant has been registered.

docs.title: Print the badges
docs.text:
Once your participant list is finalised:

  1. Go to Events > Find Participants.
  2. Select the relevant participants.
  3. Choose Print Event Name Badges from the actions drop-down list, then click Go.
  4. Select the name badge layout for the event.
  5. Click Make Name Badges.

CiviCRM creates a PDF that you can print on the appropriate-sized labels.

docs.title: Event administration screens and participant actions
docs.text: Use this page to identify where CiviEvent shows event information and what you can do with existing participants.

docs.title: CiviEvent Dashboard
docs.text:
The CiviEvent Dashboard is at Events > Dashboard. It brings event and participant information together in an Event Summary table showing up to ten scheduled and recent events.

  • Click an Event name to view the event as site visitors will see it.
  • Click a Participants count to see a list of participants.
  • Click Find more event participants at the end of the page to search by Participant Name, Event, Date Range and Status.
  • Click Manage Events to find and manage specific events, or New Event to create a new event page.
  • Use the RSS feed and calendar icons to use event data in external applications.

docs.title: Manage Events
docs.text:
Events > Manage Events lists all CiviEvents that have been created. Filters at the top of the page let you search by event name, event type or date.

The source describes four links at the right of each event, but names only these three:

Link What it provides Configure Settings for Information and Settings, Location, Fees, Online Registration, Schedule Reminders and Tell a Friend. Participants Lists of participants who are registered or attending, and participants who are not attending. Event Links Links to Register Participant and the live event information and online registration pages.

docs.title: Actions for selected participants
docs.text:
After a participant search, you can select all results or a subset and choose an Action. These actions apply to existing participants. To add participants, see the Manual event registration chapter.

Warning: Delete participants from event cannot be undone. It does not delete contact records, but it deletes all transactions and activities associated with the selected participants for this event.

Action What it does Cancel registration Cancels registration for the selected participants. Delete participants from event Deletes the selected participants from the event, with the consequences described above. Email - send now Sends an email to the search result list. For example, you could tell participants about parking options or a change to the programme. Export participants Exports to CSV using a predefined set of fields (an export mapping) or a mapping you create and save for reuse. The CSV can be opened in standard spreadsheet software or used for mail merges. Group - add contacts Adds contacts to an existing group or a group you create during the action. Group - create smart group Saves search results based on defined criteria. CiviCRM reruns the search each time you open the smart group, which is useful for complex criteria you need regularly. Name badges - print Lets you select a badge type and generates a printable PDF with the selected participants’ names. PDF letter - print for participants Prints a PDF letter for participants. Participant status - change (emails sent) Sends emails when a status changes from the pending class, such as Pending (pay later) or Pending from approval, to Registered or Attended in the positive class. Emails are also sent if the status changes to Expired or Cancelled. Print selected rows Prints the on-screen information for the rows you selected. Update multiple participants Lets you edit multiple fields for multiple participants in a table grid. You must create the profile set you want to use before choosing this action. If Profiles are unfamiliar, see Profiles in Organising your Data.

docs.title: Record partial payments for an event registration
docs.text: You can register a participant with a payment smaller than the event fee, then record one or more additional payments later.

docs.title: Record the first payment
docs.text:
During manual registration, enter the amount being paid now in the Amount field of the Payment Information section. Set Participant Status to Partially paid.

A Partially paid registration is included in the participant total, as a Pending from pay later registration is. The expectation is that further payments will be made until the full event fee is paid.

docs.title: Add another payment
docs.text:
1. Go to the registrant’s contact record.
  2. Open the Events tab.
  3. Click more at the far right of the partially paid event record.
  4. Select Record Payment or Submit Credit Card payment.

You can add more than one payment. When the fee is paid in full, Participant status automatically changes to Registered, unless you choose a different status when making the last payment. The linked contribution’s status automatically changes to Completed.

When the registration is created, the event fee is added to accounts receivable. Each partial payment is then added as a separate line item until the fee is paid in full.

docs.title: Check payments and the amount owed
docs.text:
The event registration and linked contribution always display the full event fee, rather than just the amount paid. To see how much is owed, choose View on the event registration. Select ›› view payments under Total Paid to see a summary of each payment.

You can also see the payments by clicking the arrow next to the Contribution record at the bottom.

docs.title: Register multiple contacts for an event
docs.text:
Use mass registration to add several contacts to an event at once. The registration choices you make will apply to every contact you select.

You cannot mass register participants for a past event. You also cannot apply contribution information, such as a pay later contribution or a credit card transaction, in a batch action. Mass registration is therefore best for free events or contacts who do not need to pay a fee at this point; you can add payment details for individual contacts later.

  1. Search for the contacts you want to register. For example, Arts in Action could go to Search > Find Participants to find people who attended a previous youth leadership workshop.
  2. On the search results page, choose All x records or check each contact you want to register.

  1. From the actions list above the results, choose Register participants for event, then click Go.
  2. Choose the event.
  3. Complete the registration form with the choices you want to apply to everyone selected, such as setting Participant Status to Pending.
  4. Click Save.

If different contacts need different choices, register them in separate groups. For example, Arts in Action could set previous workshop participants it plans to call or email to Pending, then register event leaders known to be attending as Registered. If a pending contact confirms they will attend, the event organiser can change that person’s status from Pending to Registered.

docs.title: Import event registrations
docs.text: Import participant registrations from a comma-separated values (CSV) file when you need to add multiple registrations to an event. If most of the contacts are already in CiviCRM, mass registration may be faster.

docs.title: Prepare contacts and the CSV file
docs.text:
The individuals in the CSV file must already exist as contacts in CiviCRM; participants cannot be imported before their contacts exist. If necessary, import the contacts first, preferably with a unique external identifier, often an ID assigned by the database or application you are importing from.

You can match a participant to an existing contact in either of these ways:

  • Include the contact’s external ID in a CSV column. If the contacts were imported without external IDs but you have those IDs, you can run a second contact import to update the field before importing participants.
  • Use your contact de-dupe rules. For example, include each individual’s first name, last name and email address in the file; if a contact matches those three fields, the event participation is assigned to that contact.

Include Event ID, Participant Status and one—not all—of these fields marked (Match to Contact) in your CSV file:

  • Contact ID (Match to Contact)
  • Email (Match to Contact)
  • External Identifier (Match to Contact)

docs.title: Import the registrations
docs.text:
1. Go to Events > Import Participants.
  2. Browse to the data file on your local computer.
  3. Select the appropriate contact type, date format and other options, then click Continue.
  4. Match the CSV fields to the CiviCRM fields.
  5. If you may repeat the import, check the Save this field mapping box.
  6. Preview and Save.

docs.title: Register a contact for an event
docs.text:
Use the contact’s record to register someone who calls or writes to your organisation, or someone you are registering on their behalf.

  1. Enter the person’s name in the Quick search box.
  2. Select the contact from the results.
  3. Open the Events tab on the contact record.

The Events tab lists the contact’s current and past event bookings and provides links to register them for another event.

  1. Choose the registration option that matches how the person will pay:
  2. Add Event Registration is for someone who will pay later, such as by sending a check or paying when they arrive.
  3. Submit Credit Card Event Registration is for someone paying immediately by credit card. This option is available only if a payment processor is configured to allow direct payments through your web site. If you are taking a registration by phone, you can ask for the person’s credit card information and enter it manually.
  4. Select the event and participant role on the registration form.

The two registration options use similar forms, except for fields that record payment details. Sections of the form change as you make selections. For example, selecting an event and participant role automatically loads any predefined custom data fields that apply to them.

For a paid event, the form displays the event fees defined in the event configuration and an option to Record Payment. An event registration records a contact’s participation; a financial transaction records its monetary value. The records are separate but can be linked. This lets you register someone, such as a V.I.P., a speaker or a person participating in a limited way, without necessarily creating a financial transaction.

  1. If you are recording a payment, select Record Payment and enter the details in the Payment Information section.

With Record Payment selected, the registration and the contact’s contribution record are linked. The registration appears under Events, and the financial record appears under Contributions. After recording the registration, you can see the related contribution at the bottom of the event registration record. If you do not select Record Payment, only a registration record is created.

docs.title: Set up an event waitlist
docs.text:
You will enable a waitlist for an event with limited spaces and set the time available to complete registration when a space opens.

CiviEvent can limit the number of people allowed to register—for example, 25 people for a training workshop or 200 for a fund-raising dinner. Once the limit is reached, further visitors cannot register and instead see an automatic message: “The event is currently full.” You can customise that message and offer a first-come-first-served waitlist.

  1. At Administer > CiviEvent > Participant statuses, enable On waitlist and Pending from waitlist.

  2. On the event's Info and settings tab, check Offer Waitlist.

  3. Set the message to display on the event information page when the event is full.

  1. On the Online registration tab, set Pending participant expiration (hours) to control how long someone has to complete registration after a space becomes available. Set it to 0 if you do not want a time limit.

  2. Make sure the Update Participant Statuses scheduled job is running at Administer > System Setting > Scheduled jobs. It is needed for the status processing described below.

When a space becomes available—for example, because someone cancels—an On waitlist participant moves to Pending from waitlist. They receive an email with a link to complete registration, including payment of any event fees. If they do not complete registration within the configured time, their status moves to expired and another person on the waitlist gets the opportunity to register.

docs.title: Require participant approval for an event
docs.text:
You will set up approval so you can review registrations before invited people complete them.

This is useful when an event is intended for a particular group, such as an appreciation dinner for volunteers who have donated 100 or more hours. Someone might forward the invitation; approval lets you check who registered.

  1. At Administer > CiviEvent > Participant Statuses, enable Awaiting approval, Pending from approval, and Rejected.

  2. On the event's Online Registration tab, check Require participant approval?.

  3. Set the approval message. When someone registers, the reply says: “Your registration has been submitted. Once your registration has been reviewed, you will receive an email with a link to a web page where you can complete the registration process.” You can customise this reply for your organisation.

  4. If you want to limit the time available to finish registration after approval, enter the number of hours in Pending participant expiration. For example, enter 72 to allow three days.

  5. Make sure the Update Participant Statuses scheduled job is running at Administer > System Setting > Scheduled jobs. It is needed for status processing.

New registrations receive Awaiting Approval status. To review them, go to Find Participants and select the Change Participant Status task. Approved participants move to Pending from approval and receive an email link to complete registration, including payment of any event fees.

docs.title: Contact matching and duplicate management
docs.text:
This page explains how CiviEvent uses duplicate rules during online registration and what its matching warnings mean.

Allowing people to register from outside your database can create duplicate contacts. One way to reduce that risk is to require people to log in: remove the register for events permission from anonymous users and give it to logged-in users or a specific role. That restriction may discourage registrations for an event such as a conference or AGM where you want as many people as possible to register.

If people can register without logging in, CiviCRM needs to decide whether a registrant already has a contact record. For example, “James Martin” might already be in the database—and there could be one James Martin in London and another in Paris. Duplicate rules determine how contacts are matched. The Deduping and merging chapter covers duplicates and merging more generally.

By default, CiviEvent matches using the Unsupervised rule. You can select a different Duplicate matching rule for a particular event's online registration. That rule applies to both the primary participant and any additional participants.

The Online Registration tab checks whether the included profiles have field combinations that could satisfy the event's matching rule:

  • Duplicate Matching Impossible appears when the profiles do not contain a combination of fields that could match contacts using that rule.
  • Duplicate Contacts Possible appears when the profiles contain enough matching fields, but not all of those fields are required.

docs.title: Set event registration permissions
docs.text:
You will review who can see event information and use online registration forms on a Drupal site.

After enabling online registration, go to Administer > Users > Permissions to review Drupal user permissions. Most organisations allow anonymous users—people who have not logged in—to view and register for events. To allow that, assign the following CiviCRM module permissions to the anonymous user role:

Permission When it is needed access all custom data When you collect information in custom fields from registrants. profile create When an online registration form includes any profiles. register for events To allow event registration. view event info To allow visitors to see event information. view event participants When you want to display a list of registered participants.

If anonymous visitors should not view or register online for events, assign these permissions to an authenticated user role instead.

CiviCRM also has Access Control Lists (ACLs) for controlling access to CiviCRM data. A CiviCRM ACL Role is not related to a Drupal Role; see the Permissions and access control chapter for more information. If you need to limit access to specific events, use Manage Access Control to assign access to specific groups of contacts.

docs.title: Test online event registration
docs.text:
You will complete a test registration, find its participant record, and check the form before showing the event to the public.

  1. Go to Events > Manage Events.

  2. Under Event Links, select Test-drive. If your payment processor has sandbox options, Test-drive uses them. It creates a registrant record marked as a test so you can review and easily remove it.

  3. Fill out the registration form and complete the registration process.

  4. Go to Events > Find Participants.

  5. In the search criteria, check Find Test Participants to find the new test participant record.

  6. If you need to change the event, return to Events > Manage Events and select Configure for that event. Configure returns you to the event setting pages so you can edit the elements you need to adjust.

  7. If anonymous users can register for your events, test again while logged out. Check the event permissions if you need to review access.

Once the event information and registration form work as intended, you can display the event on your website.

docs.title: Set up online event registration
docs.text:
You will enable registration, choose what information to collect, and set up the pages and emails people see when they register.

Online registration lets people register at a time and place convenient for them, while reducing administration for your organisation. The usual registration flow is event information, event registration, confirmation, and thank you. The event information page shows the date, location, map link, contact information, description, and a link to register. The registration form collects information such as profile fields, event fees, and credit card or pay later details. The confirmation page shows the registrant's selections and information before a credit card transaction; the thank-you page tells them to expect an email receipt.

docs.title: Enable registration
docs.text:
Warning: When a logged-in user opens the registration form, CiviCRM pre-fills it with their own contact details. If they replace those details with someone else's, CiviCRM saves the changes to the logged-in user's own contact, not a new contact. On sites where CMS user accounts are kept in sync with contact records, this can also overwrite the user's CMS account email. If you expect logged-in users to register other people, give them a registration link ending in cid=0, for example:

https://example.org/civicrm/event/register?reset=1&id=123&cid=0

With cid=0 in the URL, CiviCRM skips pre-fill, shows a blank “you are completing this form on behalf of someone else” form, and does not save the contact to the logged-in user.

  1. In the Online Registration step of event creation, check Allow Online Registration.

  1. Enter the link text that will take visitors from the event information page to the registration form. “Register Now” is a common choice.

  2. Set the registration start and end dates. These control when website visitors can register. You can close registration before the event starts, for example, to prepare name tags.

  3. If one person should be able to register and pay for several people in a single transaction, enable Register multiple participants. This can be useful when an organisation sends several people to a conference or someone registers with their partner. By default, each person registered must have a different name and email address.

  4. If registrants should be able to share an email address, check Allow same email and multiple registrations? This setting also allows a contact to register more than once for the same event—for example, to buy another concert ticket later. CiviCRM uses a separate contact record for each individual registered: an existing record if the contact is already in the system, or a new one otherwise.

You can select a Duplicate matching rule for this event. For the matching behaviour and warnings shown on the Online Registration tab, see Contact matching and duplicate management.

docs.title: Set time limits and self-service options
docs.text:
Pending participant expiration (hours) sets how long participants with a status classed as Pending have to confirm or finish registration. It works with the Update Participant Statuses scheduled job at Administer > System Setting > Scheduled jobs. If both are set, a registration that is not finalised within that time is cancelled, and the would-be registrant is notified by email. This can help manage Pending from pay later registrations when used with scheduled reminders.

Select Allow self-service cancellation or transfer if participants should receive a self-service link in their confirmation email. They can use it to transfer and/or cancel their registration. Set Cancellation or transfer time limit (hours) to disable those actions the selected number of hours before the event starts.

docs.title: Set up the registration form
docs.text:
Enter the introductory text shown at the top of the registration page and the footer text shown at the bottom. Between them, the page displays some or all of these elements, in this order: profile, fee selection, credit card details, and additional profile(s).

Profiles collect information from registrants. You can place one profile immediately after the introductory text and one or more after any fees and payment details. If the built-in Profiles do not provide the flexibility you need, FormBuilder offers another way to build the booking form.

Warning: Changes to an existing profile made while configuring online registration apply everywhere that profile is used. Unless a profile exactly matches your needs, copy it, then rename and edit the copy.

By default, the top profile is Your Registration Info, with first name, last name, and email address fields. CiviCRM requires either first name and last name or email address for each contact, so you can modify this profile or create one with fewer fields. If you do not collect email addresses, uncheck “Send confirmation email?” at the bottom of the configuration page.

If you need a new profile, you can create it without leaving the Online Registration configuration page. The drag-and-drop profile interface also lets you create custom fields. Custom fields can apply to all events or participants, or only to particular Event Types or Participant Roles. See Custom data on events for more about where to store custom data.

Each profile appears on the form as a fieldset. Its heading is its Public Title, if set; otherwise, it is its Profile Name. For example, a copy of Your Registration Info with workshop-specific fields could have the Profile Name “Workshop Registration” and the Public Title “Your Registration Info”. This distinguishes it in profile lists while keeping a familiar heading on the form.

Some profile Advanced Settings take effect in online event registration. To change them, use the main profile settings form; they cannot be edited in the profile interface within online registration settings:

  • Adding contacts to a group: Bear in mind that many registrants do not expect to join a mailing list because they signed up for an event.
  • CMS User account registration options: A participant can be offered or required to log in or create a user account while registering.
  • Including ReCAPTCHA: A CAPTCHA can make it harder for bots and people to register.

Other advanced settings, such as what to do upon duplicate match, are ignored on contribution pages. For more information, see Profiles.

docs.title: Set up confirmation pages and email
docs.text:
Enter the text for the Confirmation page, Thank-you page, and emailed confirmations or receipts, if enabled. Free events skip the Confirmation step. For paid events, payment is processed between the Confirmation and Thank-you pages, and the confirmation email also acts as a receipt.

For most events, enable Send Confirmation Email. Enter a valid email account on your mail server as the Confirm From Email address. The contents of the Text field appear in both TEXT and HTML versions of receipt emails, so do not include HTML tags or formatting there.

To receive real-time registration updates, enter one or more staff email addresses in CC Confirmation To or BCC Confirmation To, separated by commas.

Warning: Make sure addresses in CC Receipt To and BCC Receipt To are correct and do not bounce. CiviCRM interprets a returned email as a bounce for the CiviCRM contact who received the receipt, not for the CC or BCC address. This can put the contact's email address On Hold and prevent future emails from being sent. See the issue report for details.

If you enable Personal Campaign Pages (PCPs), people who have completed registration can create and customise a page to promote either the event they registered for or an online contribution page. See Contributions > Personal Campaign Pages in this book for more information.

Click Save and Done when you have finished creating the event.

docs.title: Set up a repeating Event
docs.text:
Set an Event to repeat on a certain day and time, specify when it ends, and exclude dates when it should not repeat.

If you want Scheduled Reminders to repeat, set them up on the Event you are repeating. You can edit them later. It is recommended that you send reminders two weeks or a few days before the Event rather than set them to repeat on specific days.

  1. Go to Manage Events.

  2. Under Configure, select Repeat from the dropdown.

  3. On the Repeat Event Screen, specify the Repeating intervals in hours, days, weeks, months, or years.

  4. Specify the Event end date.
  5. Specify the occurrence end date.
  6. Specify the Repetition Start Date. This is recommended.

  7. Specify any Excluded Dates. This is recommended if there are dates you do not want to repeat.

  8. Click Save.

  9. In the popup window, choose to Continue with your selection.

docs.title: Display an event report on your home dashboard
docs.text:
Make an existing event report available for the dashboard, then add it to your Home dashboard so you can see its information there.

If you have not created an Event Report, see Reports and Analysis for instructions. For details on creating an event report from a template, see Reporting Set-up.

docs.title: Make the report available
docs.text:
1. From the navigation menu, click Reports and select the report you want to display.
  2. In the Report Settings area, check Available for Dashboard?.
  3. Click Update Report.

The report is now available to add to your dashboard.

docs.title: Add the report to your dashboard
docs.text:
1. Navigate to Home.
  2. Click Configure Your Dashboard.
  3. Drag the report from the Available Dashlets area into the Left Column or Right Column of the dashboard area.
  4. Click Done.

You should now see the report on your home dashboard. To view the latest updated information for the report and any other items on your dashboard, click Refresh Dashboard Data.

docs.title: Ways to analyse events
docs.text: You can use the event dashboard, searches and CiviReport for different kinds of event analysis. The right choice depends on whether you need an overview, a list of contacts or participants, or a more detailed report.

docs.title: Start with the event dashboard
docs.text:
The event dashboard gives a quick overview of upcoming events. For each event, it shows the number of registrations and their statuses, including how many are registered, counted or pending for different reasons.

It is limited to 12 events scheduled to start on dates closest to today, so it may not be sufficient if your organisation has many scheduled events.

docs.title: Decide whether you need contacts or participants
docs.text:
CiviCRM distinguishes between contacts and event participants. A contact-based question might be “Which contacts came to events in 2011?” A participant-based question might be “How many training sessions did we deliver as part of our sexual health education programme this year?” Keep this distinction in mind when searching for event attendees.

Find participants searches participant data and returns participants. Advanced search can combine most participant information with other contact information and return contacts. In Advanced search, you can also choose Participant from the Display Results As column to show participants rather than contacts.

These searches provide simple totals. You can also export the results as CSV for further analysis in spreadsheet software.

docs.title: Use reports for more detailed analysis
docs.text:
Searches cannot aggregate data from multiple events at once or limit the date of registration very flexibly. Repeating the same searches can take time; saving them as Smart Groups can lead to a proliferation of groups. Instead, you can set up reports for an event or a collection of events.

CiviCRM includes four event reports:

Report What it shows Event Participants List Participant data, individual data and all custom data. These can also be used as filters. Attendee List A list of event attendees that you can filter to one event. You can add a blank column on the left and one, two or three columns on the right to make an event sign-up sheet. Event Income Detail Details of revenue from events. Event Income Summary Total income for a series of events, such as all your conferences in
  1. Clicking an event gives more detail about its income breakdown by role and status. The report can also be displayed as a Pie Chart or Bar Chart. |

Event Income Detail and Event Income Summary work together to show event revenue. Reports can be automatically assigned to a designated submenu, such as Events > Reports, or made available as dashlets on the main dashboard.

If a built-in report or search does not meet your needs, consider commissioning a new report or custom search. See the CiviReport section for more information. If you are interested in the financial aspects of events, the Reports and analysis chapter in Contributions may also be useful.

docs.title: What is CiviEvent?
docs.text: CiviEvent helps your organisation run events, from registration and promotion to attendance tracking and reporting. This page explains its main features and how they fit together.

docs.title: What CiviEvent can do
docs.text:
CiviEvent supports simple and complex registration processes. You can use it to:

  • Let participants register themselves and pay online by credit card.
  • Track sign-ups, cancellations and attendance.
  • Promote events on your website.
  • Reuse event templates or copy an event to make similar, recurring events easier to set up.
  • Check in participants on-site from any computer with an internet connection.

docs.title: How an organisation might use it
docs.text:
Arts in Action, a community arts group, runs leadership workshops for people under age 25 throughout the year. It wants to attract new attendees and encourage past attendees to volunteer and teach. Youth from local schools and theater groups attend alongside youth speakers, volunteers and other workshop speakers.

For each workshop, staff create an event page with an online registration form. An event template fills in much of the information needed during set-up. Attendees select a registration with a flat fee and any optional workshops with additional fees, then pay online. The form uses a CiviCRM profile to collect food and lodging preferences.

Staff use existing contacts to create a targeted list of youth and groups. They send personalised invitations through CiviMail, using a mail template they can reuse for later events. Each invitation links directly to the event page. Staff also announce the workshop on the Arts in Action website and enable Tell-a-friend so people can share it through their networks.

A designated staff member checks that payments are being made, manages the wait list if sign-ups exceed the maximum number, and answers questions. On the day, organisers check in attendees to track attendance and no-shows in real time. They can ask participants with outstanding fees to pay; the database updates immediately to record payments and free up spaces for people on the wait list.

After the workshop, staff use CiviEvent to report on the number of attendees, total event fees paid and the amount still due. They can update the event and mail templates and save them for the next workshop.

docs.title: Events, contacts and participants
docs.text: You can create one or more events in CiviCRM. A contact who takes part in an event is a participant.

docs.title: Event Types
docs.text:
Event Types let you categorise events according to your organisation’s needs, such as Conferences, Meetings and Fundraisers. They can also support different requirements: for example, custom fields can store and display additional event data according to Event Type. See Custom data on events.

Event Types also help you find and segment events and attendees. For example, you could find contacts who attended a Workshop or a Fundraising event.

docs.title: Participant Default Roles
docs.text:
Every contact who participates in an event is assigned a Participant Default Role. Attendee is a common role; Volunteer, Host and Speaker are other examples. You can customise participant roles to match your events.

Roles help you group people by how they took part. For example, you could email Volunteers only or list past table captains for fundraisers. You can also create custom fields for specific roles, such as a field collecting availability from Volunteers only.

docs.title: Participant statuses
docs.text:
Participant statuses track a contact’s stage in the event process. Examples include Registered, No-show, Attended and Cancelled. You can customise statuses to match how your organisation handles registration.

Statuses help you group participants by what has happened so far. You can use those groups to generate sign-in sheets, estimate how many people are likely to attend and tailor emails to registrants.

docs.title: How CiviEvent works with other parts of CiviCRM
docs.text:
You can use CiviMail to promote an event to a targeted list and email participants before and after it. For more information, see the Email section’s Set-up and Scheduled Reminders chapters.

CiviContribute lets you accept event payments online. To do this, you must enable CiviContribute and set up a payment processor. See Contributions for more information.

docs.title: Manage grants and recipient reports
docs.text: Use CiviGrant to find grant records, record recipients and update their grants when reports arrive.

docs.title: Find a grant
docs.text:
Go to Other > Grants > Dashboard to open the CiviGrant Dashboard. It shows a summary of grants in your CiviCRM database, including the status of all grants grouped by grant type. It also shows an overview of recent grants and a table of recent grant recipients.

To view one contact’s grants, open their contact record and select the Grants tab.

docs.title: Add a grant recipient
docs.text:
After Wookie Hole Community Action selected recipients for the Cave Festival, its grant administrator looked up each successful applicant’s contact record and entered a new grant record for each one.

  1. Go to Other > Grants > New Grant.
  2. Select an existing contact or create a new contact to receive the grant.
  3. Complete as many grant details as possible, including any custom data that has been set up. You can edit and update these details later.
  4. Click Save.

docs.title: Update a grant
docs.text: You can edit a grant at any time using the edit link in its grant record.

docs.title: Record a received report
docs.text:
When a recipient’s report arrives, you can update the grant information from either the CiviGrant Dashboard or the contact’s record.

  1. Open the grant for editing.
  2. Check Grant Report Received? in the form.
  3. Add any appropriate notes.

docs.title: Grant reporting and analysis options
docs.text: Use this page to choose a search or report based on whether you need results about grants or contacts.

docs.title: Choose what you want to count
docs.text:
CiviCRM distinguishes between contacts and grants. Before searching, decide whether your question is about contacts, such as which contacts were successful grant applicants in 2011, or about grants, such as how many Community Chest grant applications your organisation received this year.

Option What it provides Grant dashboard A quick overview of your grant types. Find Grants search form Searches grant data and returns grants. Grants tab in Advanced search Searches most grant data, can combine it with other contact information, and returns contacts. Grant report Shows grant details, for example, all grants of a particular type. At the bottom, it includes aggregated statistics for amounts requested and granted.

Searching grant data also gives you simple totals and the option to export results as a .CSV file for further analysis.

If a built-in report or search does not meet your needs, consider commissioning a new report or custom search. See CiviReport for more information.

docs.title: Set up CiviGrant
docs.text: Enable CiviGrant, then configure the grant types, statuses and custom fields your organisation needs.

docs.title: Enable CiviGrant
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > System Settings > Extensions.
  2. Enable the CiviGrant extension.

docs.title: Set up grant types
docs.text:
You cannot add custom data to grant types, but you can add it to grants.

  1. Go to Administer > CiviGrant > Grant types.
  2. Set a title and description for each grant type you need.

docs.title: Set up grant statuses
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > System Settings > Option Groups.
  2. Select Options on the right of the Grant status line to view existing statuses.
  3. Create any new statuses needed to match your grant-giving workflow.

docs.title: Add custom data to grants
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Custom Fields.
  2. Click Add Set of Custom Fields.
  3. Set Used For to Grant.

Consider adding custom fields to upload the original application form. You could convert the form to a PDF before uploading it to make it read-only and reasonably future compatible.

For more information, see Creating Custom Fields.

docs.title: What is CiviGrant?
docs.text:
CiviGrant helps your organisation manage money it distributes to others. This page explains how it differs from CiviContribute and shows how a grant giver might use it.

CiviContribute tracks money coming into your organisation; CiviGrant tracks money going out. CiviGrant supports the grant application process, including recording the amount applied for, the amount received and reports needed during the process. Foundations and other grant givers are examples of organisations that may use it.

As of CiviCRM version 5.46, CiviGrant ships as an extension that can be enabled from the extensions screen. If your grant application process has multiple pathways, you may wish to use CiviGrant with CiviCase.

docs.title: Example: Wookie Hole Community Festival
docs.text:
Wookie Hole Community Action is a small umbrella organisation that distributes funds for the annual Wookie Hole Community Festival in Wookie Hole Cave. Each year, it makes a £40,000 grant pool available to local organisations participating in the festival. The money comes from local businesses and other grant-giving organisations.

Each applicant completes an eligibility questionnaire, which is entered into the applicant's contact record. They also submit an application explaining how they will spend the money. The organisation attaches the application to the grant, fills in fields for the grant and attaches a read-only PDF of the original application form for future reference.

Ineligible applications are rejected. Eligible applications are scored against pre-defined criteria. If the total amount requested exceeds £40,000, the grant committee reviews the eligible projects again to decide which to fund fully or partially. CiviGrant has fields the organisation can use to store and search this information.

After awarding funds, the organisation uses CiviGrant with CiviMail to request feedback and reports from funded organisations. It marks a grant as "feedback received" when the feedback arrives. Because it often needs to send several reminders, it uses an email template and searches for contacts who received a grant but have not yet sent feedback.

Once all reports are in, a staff member compiles a report and thank-you email for every organisation that contributed to the festival fund. The report explains how their funds benefited the local community. Wookie Hole Community Action also prints a certificate directly from CiviCRM for each local business and funder to display on their premises.

docs.title: Understanding CiviGrant
docs.text: Learn how CiviGrant records a grant’s progress and how grant types, statuses and custom data relate to your organisation’s process.

docs.title: How the grant process is recorded
docs.text:
CiviGrant helps grant-giving organisations manage their grants. It is one of the simpler CiviCRM components, so you may find it straightforward if you already use other components.

The standard workflow begins with details of the grant a contact is applying for, including the amount applied for and when the application was received. You can then record when the grant decision was made, how much was granted, when money was transferred, when the grant report was due and whether it has been received.

docs.title: Grant types and statuses
docs.text:
Grant types describe the different types of grant your organisation distributes. You can set up as many as you like and search for grants by type.

Grant statuses show where a grant is in your workflow. CiviGrant includes three default statuses: Pending, Granted and Rejected. You can add statuses to match your organisation’s process.

docs.title: Application forms and eligibility criteria
docs.text: You can use CiviCRM’s custom data fields to create application processing forms and eligibility criteria in CiviGrant. When planning these fields, consider which information belongs to the contact applying for the grant and which belongs to the grant.

docs.title: Questions to consider before you begin
docs.text:
• What grant types does your organisation offer?
  • What is your grant application workflow, and how can you map it to CiviGrant statuses?
  • Do you have an application form? If so, how can you model it using custom data?
  • What kinds of reports do you want to generate from the grant process?

docs.title: Configure USPS address standardization
docs.text:
Follow this process to obtain a USPS Web Tools ID, send test requests from CiviCRM, and set up the production server. Address standardization is currently available only through the United States Postal Service API.

USPS restricts use of the Address Information APIs to USPS shipping services. The API must be used when someone enters an address on a website, not for batch processing or database cleansing. USPS must approve access to its production server.

docs.title: Register for a Web Tools ID
docs.text:
1. Open the USPS Web Tools registration page.
  2. For Will use:, select Exclusively on my website.
  3. Submit the registration.

You will receive a confirmation email. Keep the Web Tools ID for the next steps. If you are developing a website for a client, you need a separate Web Tools ID for each client. You may have the client complete the forms. A unique email address owned by the client can help keep the registration compliant; during development, you can forward its messages to yourself or send them to both yourself and the client.

Do not share a User ID outside your organisation or use the same User ID for more than one website. The USPS terms state that a User ID cannot be packaged, distributed, or sold, and that use from more than one website can cause users to lose production-server access. A problem that appears technical may instead result from a terms-of-service violation.

docs.title: Request access to the Address Information API
docs.text:
1. Open the USPS Address Information API page.
  2. Enter the URL of your CiviCRM website.
  3. Select U.S. Postal Service® package shipments and U.S. Postal Service letters. Do not select other choices: the source states that other uses are not provided or permitted for this API.
  4. Explain that you will use USPS-provided information only to ship letters or packages through USPS, and that an address will be updated only when a user changes their postal information.

The source describes the website URL as “the address of the site of the owner of the” and suggests that there may be one Web Tools ID per company or individual and a unique USPS-provided Server User ID per website. It marks that detail as needing confirmation.

The USPS Internet Customer Care Center (ICCC) may email you for more information. Its example request asks for a detailed description of how you will use the API and the URL of your development or production site. It also says the API output must be used solely with USPS shipping services:

Dear USPS Customer,

Address Information APIs are accessible with special permission. The APIs can only be used in conjunction with USPS SHIPPING SERVICES ONLY.

We must first understand how you'll be using the API. We need a commitment that the API will be used on a transactional basis (not batch processing or cleansing of a database, but as a customer enters the information into a form on a website). Also, you must state that you will use the output from this API solely in association with USPS SHIPPING SERVICES ONLY.

Please provide a detailed description how you plan to use the APIs, include the URL of the site (development or production). We will review the material received to see if you meet our requirements.

docs.title: Send test requests
docs.text:
USPS needs requests containing your Web Tools ID before it can grant production access. The source suggests that you might be able to skip this step by contacting USPS and explaining that you use a fully developed open-source project, but says sending requests may make approval easier.

Do not leave CiviCRM using the test server long term. It does not work for all addresses, and prolonged use could cause your access rights to be halted. Only preset addresses validate on the test service. For other addresses, USPS returns an API error that CiviCRM reports as an address that could not be validated. See the USPS Address Information API documentation.

  1. In CiviCRM, go to Administer → Localization → Address Settings [Address Standardization].
  2. Select USPS as the standardization provider.
  3. Enter your Web Tools ID.
  4. Enter this test server URL:
http://testing.shippingapis.com/shippingapitest.dll
  1. Create a contact and enter 6406 Ivy Lane, Greenbelt, MD as an address.
  2. Save the contact. CiviCRM should display a complete, standardized address or an error saying that USPS could not validate it.
  3. Repeat the test with 8 Wildwood Drive, Old Lyme, CT 06371.

Either result indicates that a request was sent to the API. If you think the test did not work, check your settings. If USPS does not appear in the provider dropdown, see CRM-11337.

docs.title: Request production access
docs.text:
After USPS approves your use of the Address Standardization API, ask for production-server access by email or phone, using the contact details USPS provided. Tell USPS that you use CiviCRM, a fully developed open-source project, rather than developing the integration yourself.

The ICCC may ask further questions by email or phone and may want to see how your production website uses the service. A URL for the forms where users enter postal addresses may help. If those forms require registration, a temporary account for USPS may help them review the forms.

docs.title: Set up the production server
docs.text:
After your testing is complete and USPS grants production access, its email may identify http://production.shippingapis.com as the Production Server URL and https://secure.shippingapis.com as the URL for APIs calling the secure server. It may also tell you to remove test from shippingapitest.dll.

Before you use address standardization during contact imports, note that CiviCRM also invokes the API for imports. The source advises turning off standardization during imports or limiting imports to “only a addresses”; that second option is unclear in the source. USPS prohibits using the API for batch processing or database cleansing.

  1. In CiviCRM, go to Administer → Localization → Address Settings [Address Standardization].
  2. Enter this production server URL:
http://production.shippingapis.com/shippingapi.dll

The source includes this sample production setup under Administer → Localization → Address settings:

docs.title: USPS contact and related resources
docs.text:
The USPS Internet Customer Care Center (ICCC) is staffed from 7:00 AM to 11:00 PM Eastern Time.

  • Email: icustomercare@usps.com
  • Telephone: 1-800-344-7779

The source also lists these discussions and resources:

  • USPS Address Standardization Returns BLANKS
  • Is anyone using the United States Postal Services (USPS) Address Standardization web service plugin?
  • OSDir.com > USPS Address Standardization web service: msg
  • USPS Address Information API documentation

docs.title: Address settings
docs.text: Use this page to check what each address setting controls and which tokens you can use in address formats.

docs.title: Mailing labels
docs.text:
Individual Name Format sets the order and fields used for an Individual Contact’s name when that name appears on a mailing label. The default is:

{individual_prefix}{ }{first_name}{ }{middle_name}{ }{last_name}

Mailing Label Format uses tokens to format addresses on mailing labels. Include {contact_name} if you want the contact’s name to appear on the label. Use {state_province} for the state or province abbreviation, or {state_province_name} for the full name.

The standard format is:

{contact_name}
{street_address}
{supplemental_address_1}
{supplemental_address_2}
{city}{, }{state_province}{ }{postal_code}
{country}

docs.title: Displayed addresses
docs.text:
Address Formatting uses tokens to format addresses for display. Use {state_province} for the state or province abbreviation, or {state_province_name} for the full name.

The standard format is:

{street_address}
{supplemental_address_1}
{supplemental_address_2}
{city}{, }{state_province}{ }{postal_code}
{country}

docs.title: Contact address fields
docs.text:
• Maximum Locations sets the maximum number of different locations or addresses allowed for a contact.
  • Include County? controls whether contact address input forms include a County field.

docs.title: Address standardization
docs.text:
CiviCRM includes an optional plugin for the United States Postal Service (USPS) Address Standardization web service. USPS is currently the only supported provider. You must register to use USPS Web Tools; if approved, USPS provides a User ID and service URL. See the how-to guide on integrating with USPS for address standardization.

Setting Meaning Provider – Address Standardization Provider Select USPS, the only supported provider. User ID The USPS-provided User ID. Web Service URL The USPS-provided web service URL.

Select Save to save your changes or Cancel to cancel them.

docs.title: Understanding change logging
docs.text: Learn how CiviCRM records changes, what detailed logging adds, and what to consider before turning it on.

docs.title: Default change logging
docs.text: CiviCRM’s light-weight logging is on by default. Each contact has a change log tab, populated when the contact is added or edited. It shows who changed the record and when, but not what changed. Many organisations find this level of detail sufficient.

docs.title: What detailed logging adds
docs.text:
When enabled, detailed logging tracks changes to almost all CiviCRM data, including contacts, memberships and events. It also covers configuration data such as Activity Types, Case types and Contribution Types. For each update, it records:

  • the value before the change;
  • the value after the change;
  • when the change was made;
  • who made the change.

In the change log, clicking update on the left shows the details of a change.

Detailed logging can help you revert unwanted changes, whether administrative staff or contacts using your website made them, accidentally or maliciously. Recording all these changes can collect a large amount of data and has a small performance impact on your database. Detailed logging is off by default, so consider whether the existing records described below meet your needs before turning it on.

docs.title: Other ways to see changes over time
docs.text:
Activities happen at specific points in time, so a contact’s activity tab can provide a record of changes over time. You do not need to create an activity for every contact edit. In some cases, the existing activity record, supplemented by a few manually recorded activities, provides enough history.

Memberships also build a historical record over time, including contributions toward the membership, renewals and up-sells. This built-in record may meet your needs without detailed logging.

docs.title: Reverting changes
docs.text:
With detailed logging enabled, you can revert changes to your data. For many contact fields, a revert button appears at the bottom of the screen showing the change details.

That screen is not available for every contact change, although detailed logging still records the data. If you need to revert a change that cannot be reverted through the user interface, contact your system administrator or someone familiar with CiviCRM’s detailed logging functionality.

docs.title: Customize the navigation menu
docs.text:
You can add, delete, rename and move items in the CiviCRM navigation bar to suit your organisation’s work.

You might remove unused items, add links to data entry Profiles or non-CiviCRM web pages and apps, rename items using familiar terms, or move them to support a workflow.

docs.title: Open the menu editor
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Navigation Menu.
  2. Click the small triangles beside folder names to expand the menu tree. Each menu item is represented by a folder icon.

docs.title: Change an existing item
docs.text:
Choose the action you need:

  • To delete an item, right-click it and select Delete.
  • To rename an item, right-click it and select Rename.
  • To move an item, drag and drop it to the desired place in the tree.

docs.title: Add a menu item
docs.text:
1. Click Add Menu Item.
  2. Enter the text to display in the Title field.
  3. Enter the item’s link in the Url field.
  4. Choose its location from the Parent dropdown. You can place an item at any navigation level; leave Parent unselected to place it at the top level.
  5. If you want a line below the new item to separate it from the next item, check Separator.

docs.title: Create a contact data entry form
docs.text: Create a Profile containing only the fields that staff or volunteers need when manually entering batches of similar contacts. This can make data entry faster.

docs.title: Create the Profile
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles.
  2. Click Add Profile.
  3. Give the Profile a name that describes its purpose, such as Name and Address Data Entry Form.
  4. Check the Standalone Form or Directory box in Used For.
  5. If needed, enter text for data entry users in Pre-form Help and Post-form Help.
  6. Click Save. The Add Fields screen opens.

docs.title: Add fields
docs.text:
Choose only Contact, Individual, Organization, Household or a custom contact subtype when selecting a record type. Other record types in the Field Name menu do not work with data entry forms. Fields that apply to more than one contact type, such as Phone and Email, appear under Contact.

  1. In Field Name, choose the contact record type containing the field you need.
  2. In the dropdown that appears, choose the field.
  3. If needed, edit Field Label to change the text shown on the form.
  4. Check Required? if every record entered through the form must contain a value for this field.
  5. If needed, add text for data entry users in Field Pre Help or Field Post Help.
  6. If needed, set Order to position the field. Lower numbers appear before higher numbers.
  7. Click Save and New to add another field, or Save when you have finished.

The next screen lists the fields and their settings.

docs.title: Preview and use the form
docs.text:
1. Click Preview (all fields) to check how the form looks.
  2. Click Use (create mode) to open the page containing the form.
  3. Copy the link to that page. You can use it to create a navigation menu item; see Customizing the navigation menu.

docs.title: Customizing the navigation menu
docs.text: Use the copied form link as the Url when you add a navigation menu item for the form.

docs.title: Customize a search view
docs.text:
Set up a Profile for Search Views, then select it when you conduct an advanced search.

  1. Create or open a Profile.
  2. Mark it as used for Search Views. In CiviCRM 4.1 and earlier, this was called Search Results.
  3. For each field you add to the Profile, set Visibility to Public Pages.
  4. For each field you want in the results, check Results Column.
  5. When conducting an advanced search, select your Profile from the Search Views dropdown at the top right of the page.

docs.title: Change terminology with Word Replacements
docs.text:
Use Word Replacements to change existing CiviCRM text to terms your organisation uses. For example, an organisation that calls monetary transactions “donations” rather than “contributions” can define a replacement throughout its CiviCRM instance.

If you use CiviCRM in a language other than English, enter the English words as the originals to replace. Word Replacements do not work when the original terms are entered in the language you are using. Also consider alternate word forms and the different ways a term may appear in CiviCRM.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Word Replacements.
  2. Enter the existing text in the Original column on the left.
  3. Enter your preferred text in the Replacement column on the right.
  4. Check Exact Match if you want to replace only an exact match. Without it, replacing “Contribution” with “Donation” also replaces “Contributions” with “Donations”; with it, that plural replacement does not happen.
  5. Check Enabled on the left to enable the replacement.
  6. If you need more replacements, click Add row and enter them.
  7. Click Save when you have finished.

docs.title: User interface settings
docs.text: Use this page to find settings that affect what your users see in CiviCRM and how they search and enter dates. Changes to the data your organisation collects and tracks are covered in Organising Your Data and in the What you need to know and Set-up chapters for individual CiviCRM components, such as event types in Events.

docs.title: Contact form dropdown options
docs.text:
At Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Dropdown Options, you can add, rename, disable or remove options in these contact entry and editing fields:

Field Examples or limitations Gender Individual prefixes and suffixes Ms., Mr.; Jr., Sr. Phone types Phone, Mobile, Pager Mobile phone providers Sprint, Verizon, Cingular Instant messenger services Yahoo, MSN, AIM, GTalk, Jabber, Skype Website types Work, Facebook, Twitter Location types Home, Work, Billing, Main. Billing is assigned to Billing Addresses entered when constituents contribute or pay event and membership fees online. Location type names cannot contain spaces: use SummerHome, not Summer Home.

You can change the Preferred Communication Methods choices on contact entry and editing forms, such as Phone, Email, Postal Mail and SMS, at Administer > Communications > Preferred Communications Methods.

Dropdown options that define data, such as Activity Type, Relationship Type and Contribution Status, are outside the scope of these interface settings. See Organising Your Data and the sections for the relevant CiviCRM components.

docs.title: Display preferences
docs.text: Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences to control which parts of the interface appear.

docs.title: Viewing contacts
docs.text:
The checkboxes under Viewing Contacts control which tabs appear when you view a contact record.

For example, if your organisation does not use Cases or Grants, you can uncheck those boxes to hide the tabs. Hiding a tab does not remove its information from the database. If you check the box again, the stored information appears as it did before.

docs.title: Editing contacts
docs.text:
The checkboxes under Editing Contacts control which blocks appear when you edit a contact.

For example, you can hide Demographics or Communication Preferences if your organisation does not collect that information. Information already entered in hidden fields remains in the database and appears again if you recheck the boxes.

docs.title: Popup forms
docs.text:
CiviCRM uses popup dialog boxes for quick viewing and editing. Deselect Enable Popup Forms to use traditional browsing instead.

Disabling popup forms makes CiviCRM slower: every form then requires a complete browser page load.

docs.title: Activity assignee notifications
docs.text: By default, CiviCRM notifies all activity assignees when an activity is created. Deselect Notify Activity Assignees to disable this feature. You can also select activity types in the field below to disable email notifications for those types.

docs.title: Contact search fields
docs.text: The Contact Search checkboxes control which types of fields appear on Search > Find Contacts and Search > Advanced Search. Uncheck a box to remove the corresponding fields from those search screens.

docs.title: Search preferences
docs.text:
Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences to change CiviCRM’s default search behaviour.

Setting Behaviour Automatic Wildcard Choose Yes to add wildcards to both ends of a Name search term. A search for ada can then find Adams, Janet and Nadal, Jorge. Choose No to add a wildcard only to the end: ada can find a last name beginning with those letters, such as Adams, Janet, but not Nadal, Jorge. Disabling this option may speed up searches on a large database. Include Email Choose Yes to include email addresses automatically in Name searches. Disabling this option may speed up searches on a large database. Include Nickname Choose Yes to include the contents of the Nickname field automatically in Name searches. Include Alphabetical Pager Choose Yes to show an alphabet bar above search results. Clicking A, for example, displays only contacts that begin with A. Disabling this option may speed up searches on a large database. Include Order By Clause Choose No if you do not want search results to be ordered. Smart group cache timeout Controls how often the smart group cache is refreshed. A value of 0 turns off caching. The suitable value can vary by site; see the admin guide for more information. Autocomplete Contact Search Check basic contact fields, such as name, email or phone, to include them in the autocomplete results from the Quick Search bar at the top left of all screens. Contact Reference Options Check basic contact fields, such as name, email or phone, to include them in autocomplete results for Contact Reference custom fields. Autocomplete Results Sets the maximum number of results displayed while typing in an autocomplete field.

If your database is large and searches are slow, consider disabling some search options to improve speed.

docs.title: Date preferences
docs.text:
The default date display preference is set at Administer > Localization > Date Formats. At Administer > Customise Data and Screens > Date Preferences, you can override the default and define the range of allowed dates for specific field types.

CiviCRM provides default input ranges for certain date fields. For example, the default Activity Dates range runs from 20 years before the current year to 10 years after it. To log an activity from 25 years ago, you would need to extend that range.

docs.title: Date settings
docs.text: Use this page to look up CiviCRM’s date format, calendar and date range settings.

docs.title: Date localization
docs.text: Go to Administer > Localization > Date Formats to configure date and time conventions for your locale. The page contains settings for date display, date input fields and the calendar.

docs.title: Date display
docs.text:
CiviCRM uses about seven date and time formats in different contexts. You can adjust each format to suit local preferences. For example, an accounting report may use a short date such as 09/19/22 to save space in a table of 1,000 donations, while an event registration form may use a longer date such as September 19th, 2022 for clarity.

A typical United States configuration might look like this:

Format name Example configuration Example value Complete Date and Time %B %E%f, %Y %l:%M %P September 18th, 2022 11:58 PM Complete Date %B %E%f, %Y September 19th, 2022 Short Date %m/%d/%Y 09/18/2022 Month and Year %B %Y September 2022 Time Only %l:%M %P 1:34 PM Year Only %Y 2022 Financial Batch %m/%d/%Y 09/19/2022

For a full list of formatting codes, see the PHP Manual: strftime().

docs.title: Date input fields
docs.text: Date Input Format and Time Input Format control how dates and times are entered on forms that require them.

docs.title: Calendar
docs.text: The calendar settings let you enter the day on which the week begins and the month and day on which the fiscal year begins.

docs.title: Date preferences
docs.text:
Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Date Preferences to change the allowed input ranges for specific date fields. By default, the range for Activity Dates runs from 20 years before the current year through 10 years after it.

If your organisation needs to record an activity from 25 years ago, you must extend the range before users can enter that date. A date outside the allowed range produces an error such as: Please enter a date between 01/01/1994 and 12/31/2024.

docs.title: Configure fatal error handling
docs.text:
Use the error-handling settings to specify a custom fatal error screen or override CiviCRM’s built-in error handling.

  1. Go to Administer » System Settings » Debugging and Error Handling.
  2. To define your own fatal error screen, enter the path and filename of a custom Smarty template in Fatal Error Template.
