This integration can let visitors renew memberships, sign up for events, request email updates and donate through your website. You can also share parts of your CRM data, such as event information, with website visitors. Read more in the Website Integration section.

docs.title: Access, languages and licensing
docs.text:
Because CiviCRM is web-based, people in different locations can use it at the same time. It supports translations and multi-language options.

CiviCRM is Free/Open Source software. There are no licence costs or user fees for downloading, installing or using it. You can view and modify its source code and distribute copies of the original source to any person or organisation.

As of 2019, over 11,000 non-profits used CiviCRM. The source also reports that CiviCRM manages over 303,000,000 contacts, 265,000,000 donations and 42,000,000 event registrations; it does not give a date for those totals.

docs.title: Bring an idea to the CiviCRM community
docs.text:
If you have an idea for CiviCRM, start by discussing it with the community. You can then find a way to put it into practice.

  1. Start a conversation on CiviCRM’s Mattermost. It offers live discussion in chat rooms and direct messages. Ask what others think of your idea; someone may have tried something similar before.

  2. Follow up in the place that fits your idea. Other community members may suggest an article on the CiviCRM blog, CiviCRM’s GitLab, a teleconference or a meeting in person.

  3. Make an action plan for the idea. Consider how you will gather resources, fit the work around your day job and meet both your objectives and the community’s needs.

  4. Put the plan into practice and keep the community involved and updated. The community can be supportive, but you will need to drive your project.

You can participate directly even if your organisation works with a consultant. By asking on the forums, you can offer feedback as an end user and receive input from the wider community, not only from your consultant.

docs.title: The CiviCRM community and its history
docs.text:
CiviCRM is shaped by the people who develop, use and document it. This page explains who takes part in the community and how the project has grown.

The community includes the CiviCRM core team; people at non-profit organisations that use CiviCRM; consultants; programmers and developers; power users; volunteers; and community organisers. It is also closely connected to other open source projects. People contribute in different ways, and that diversity helps the software and the community continue to change and improve.

Membership is shaped by how you interact with others. Respectful communication, helping others and recognising that community members give their time and expertise can make participation rewarding. Complaints made without a respectful tone, or treating the community only as a resource, are less likely to receive a response.

docs.title: How CiviCRM developed
docs.text:
Dave Greenberg, Donald Lobo and Michal Mach started CiviCRM in 2004, drawing on their experience with non-profit organisations and tools. Early on, Zack Rosen and Neil Drumm encouraged them to make Drupal a fundamental part of CiviCRM. Using Drupal’s existing functionality let developers focus on CRM features.

The first version was released in 2005 with two core modules: CiviMail and CiviContribute. CiviCRM later added more components, reaching eight core modules alongside third-party components, and broadened its integration with content management systems to include Backdrop, Joomla! and WordPress.

CiviCRM became a leading open source CRM for nonprofits. As of early 2019, it had more than 11,000 installed sites. Its ecosystem includes free software contributors, and organisations using CiviCRM include Amnesty International, Creative Commons, Electronic Frontier Foundation, Free Software Foundation and Wikimedia Foundation.

CiviCRM uses a group-based structure covering areas such as development, maintenance and marketing. A Core Team coordinates the project.

docs.title: Delete a membership entered in error
docs.text:
Delete a membership only when it was entered in error. For example, if you made Jo Smith a member instead of Joe Smith, you would remove Jo Smith’s incorrect membership and any linked contribution record.

Deleting a membership completely removes it and any linked contributions from the database. This action cannot be undone. Give permission to delete memberships only to trusted staff.

To delete a membership from a contact’s record:

  1. Search for the contact.
  2. Open the Membership tab.
  3. Click More next to the membership record.
  4. Click Delete.

To delete membership records from search results:

  1. Go to Memberships > Find Members.
  2. Enter your criteria.
  3. Select the membership records in the Find Members results.
  4. Click Delete.

docs.title: Cancel or manually expire a membership
docs.text:
Change a membership’s status when a contact leaves or does not renew, rather than deleting the record. This keeps the contact’s membership history and any contributions attached to the membership.

  • Choose Cancelled, or another status that is not considered current, when a contact resigns or cancels their membership.
  • Choose Expired when a contact’s membership is in a grace period, you know they will not continue for another period, and they completed their membership period.

You may not need to expire a membership manually. Depending on the rules set up under Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules, memberships can expire automatically based on timeline criteria.

  1. Search for the contact whose membership status you want to change.
  2. Open the Membership tab.
  3. Click Edit next to the membership record.
  4. Check the Status Override box.
  5. Select the appropriate Membership Status, such as Cancelled or Expired.

docs.title: Membership status rules
docs.text:
Use this page to understand the dates and rules that determine a membership's status, including when someone is counted as a member.

The existing rules are listed at Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules.

docs.title: Membership dates
docs.text:
Status rules use a membership's join, start or end date:

  • Join date: The date the contact first signed up for membership with your organisation. It does not change unless someone alters it manually.
  • Start date: The date the current continuous period of membership began.
  • End date: The last day of the current membership.

docs.title: Default statuses
docs.text:
By default, a membership moves through these statuses:

  • Pending: The contact has requested membership but has not paid. You cannot change this status manually to New; the associated contribution record must be updated. For example, if Joe Smith selects the pay later option when signing up, his membership does not change to New until the contribution status of the related payment is changed to Completed.
  • New: The contact has just signed up, or a pending payment has arrived. By default, this status lasts until three months after the membership start date.
  • Current: Follows New and lasts until the membership end date.
  • Grace: Applies after the membership period ends if the contact has not renewed. The contact is still counted as a member during this period.
  • Expired: Applies when the grace period ends. The contact is no longer counted as a member.
  • Cancelled: An administrator has manually cancelled the membership, perhaps because of misbehaviour.
  • Deceased: Keeps a deceased contact's record in CiviCRM but removes the contact from further communications. This status is set automatically from the contact's deceased flag.

docs.title: How CiviCRM selects a status
docs.text:
CiviCRM first checks whether membership override is selected on the membership record. If it is, CiviCRM applies the chosen status. An overridden status remains in place rather than changing according to the status rules.

Without an override, CiviCRM checks the rules from the top of the Membership Status Rules page. It applies the first rule whose start and end dates include today's date.

docs.title: Status rule settings
docs.text:
The form for adding or editing a membership status is shown below. You can add statuses and edit existing ones, except Pending and Deceased.

Each rule specifies when its status starts and stops in relation to a membership event: the join date, start date or end date. For example:

  • One month after the membership start date uses start date and 1 month.
  • Five days before the membership end date uses end date and -5 days.

The Current membership tick box determines whether contacts with that status are considered members or non-members. Its setting appears as Yes or No in the Member column on the status rules summary page.

This setting also affects renewals:

  • For a contact whose status counts them as a member, renewal extends the existing membership end date by the renewal duration.
  • For a contact whose status counts them as a non-member, renewal gives the membership a new start date and an end date based on that start date.

docs.title: Status updates
docs.text:
When a membership is added or renewed, CiviCRM sets its status automatically from the status rules. By default, a newly created membership receives New status.

If statuses are not updating automatically, check that the Update Membership Statuses scheduled job is enabled and runs at least once a day. See Scheduled Jobs for configuration details, and consult your system administrator if appropriate.

docs.title: Membership type settings
docs.text:
Use this page to understand the settings available for a membership type and decide how they fit the memberships your organisation offers.

A membership type is a basic building block for membership management in CiviCRM. One type may be enough for a simple structure; other organisations need a type for each membership they offer. For example, an organisation might offer regular, student and honorary memberships, or use membership types for free and paid subscriptions to different publications.

This page covers common membership type settings. For more complex structures, Membership price sets may provide additional flexibility. If you are having trouble modelling your structure, you can ask on Mattermost or Stack Exchange through Finding the Community Online. Other ways to model your data, or changes to CiviCRM's behaviour, may fit your needs.

The settings appear when you go to Administer > CiviMember > Membership Types and select Add Membership Type.

docs.title: Name and description
docs.text:
• Name: Appears throughout CiviCRM, including on public and backend pages. You can change it later, although changing it may mean updating membership receipts customised using membership names.
  • Description: Optional. You can use it to describe the membership or the contacts it is intended for.

docs.title: Membership organisation
docs.text:
Membership organisation identifies the organisation that the contact becomes a member of. That organisation must already exist as a CiviCRM organisation contact. If you manage memberships for only your own organisation, you can choose the default organisation.

A single CiviCRM instance can manage memberships for more than one organisation. For example, a local sports centre could manage memberships for a tennis club, a football club and a hockey club.

Some contacts may need two memberships of the same organisation at the same time. For example, a parent who is also a health professional might want both a membership that includes a parenting magazine and one that includes a peer-reviewed journal and discounts at training events. CiviCRM's Membership Up-Sell feature expects a contact to have only one active membership with a single organisation at a time. One workaround is to create a separate “dummy” organisation for each possible concurrent membership—for example, an extra organisation for health professionals. A dummy organisation is for administrative purposes and does not have to appear to members on your website.

docs.title: Fees and financial records
docs.text:
• Minimum fee: Enter 0 for a free membership. Otherwise, enter the minimum amount required. Members can be encouraged to pay more than this minimum.
  • Financial type: Defaults to Member Dues, which suits many organisations. Different financial types can support different accounting needs. For finer control, see Membership Price Sets. The financial type can be overridden on specific public membership sign-up pages or when recording a membership in the backend.

For a paid membership, CiviCRM links a membership record to a contribution record. The membership record documents the contact's relationship with the organisation; the contribution record documents the associated financial transaction. CiviCRM stores these under the membership and Contributions tabs respectively, with a link between the records.

docs.title: Auto-renew
docs.text:
Auto-renew can submit a repeat transaction to the payment processor when the current membership expires. You can offer or require it for a membership type, but only when the membership's Duration is one year or less.

Not all payment processors support this functionality. Check that yours is configured for recurring payments before selecting an auto-renew option. See Payment Processors.

Free memberships never auto-renew because auto-renewal depends on a confirmation message from a payment processor. For a similar result, you can set a free membership's Duration to Lifetime and use a scheduled reminder to email those members, for example, annually.

docs.title: Duration and period type
docs.text:
Duration is the number of days, months or years the membership lasts each time someone signs up or renews.

Period type determines when the membership starts:

  • Rolling: Starts on the day the member signs up.
  • Fixed: Starts on a specified calendar date. Additional fields appear according to the Duration.

docs.title: Fixed periods measured in years
docs.text:
When Duration is measured in years, two additional fields appear:

  • Fixed Period Start Date: The calendar date on which all memberships start, such as January 1 or April 15.
  • Fixed Period Rollover Date: Determines the end date when someone signs up partway through the membership year.

For example, with a Duration of one year, a Fixed Period Start Date of January 1 and a Fixed Period Rollover Date of September 1:

  • Someone signing up between 1 January 2018 and 31 August 2018 has an end date of 31 December 2018.
  • Someone signing up on or after 1 September 2018 has an end date of 31 December 2019—up to 15 months of membership for the one-year price.

docs.title: Fixed periods measured in months
docs.text:
When Duration is measured in months, Fixed Period Rollover Date determines whether the duration starts at the beginning of the current or the next calendar month.

For example, for a six-month membership with Fixed Period Rollover Date set to 15:

  • Someone signing up on 1–14 January has an end date of 30 June.
  • Someone signing up on 15–31 January has an end date of 31 July.

If Duration is 12 months, Period type is Fixed and Fixed Period Rollover Date is 1, anyone joining during August 2018 has an expiry date of 31 August 2019.

docs.title: Inherited memberships
docs.text:
Relationship Type lets one contact inherit membership from another. For example, a professional trade organisation could make a company the primary member and allow its employees to receive membership benefits.

The selected relationship type defines how the membership is inherited. The pop-up help screen gives examples of relationship types to select. After selecting one, Max related sets the maximum number of inherited memberships linked to each primary member. In the company example, setting it to 10 would limit membership through employment to ten employees.

The contact holding the membership is the primary member. Contacts who receive it through their relationship with that contact are inherited members.

docs.title: Availability and display order
docs.text:
• Visibility: Public makes the membership type available for inclusion on online membership sign-up forms. Choose Admin for types handled manually by an administrator, such as honorary or lifetime memberships.
  • Order: Determines the type's position in membership type drop-down lists and on membership sign-up pages.
  • Enabled: Unticking this box removes a type that is not yet available or is no longer offered from the user interface. It does not delete membership data, and you can re-enable the type later.

docs.title: Additional member information
docs.text: You can collect more information using one or more custom field sets. A set can apply to all memberships or to specific membership types. If the information differs by type, use more than one set and link each to the relevant type or types. See Creating Custom Fields.

docs.title: Find memberships
docs.text:
Search membership records when you need membership results, or use Advanced Search when you need to combine limited membership information with other contact information.

A contact can have more than one membership. For example, a search might find two memberships belonging to one contact. Decide whether you need a count or list of memberships or contacts before choosing a search.

docs.title: Search with Find Members
docs.text:
1. Go to Memberships > Find Members.
  2. Enter your criteria.
  3. Click Search.

Find members searches membership data and returns membership data.

docs.title: Search with Advanced Search
docs.text:
1. Go to Search > Advanced Search.
  2. In the Display Settings For Results accordion, set Display Results As to Memberships.
  3. Enter your criteria.
  4. Click Search.

Advanced Search can combine limited membership information with other contact information. It returns contacts unless you choose Memberships in Display Results As. See the Searching chapter for more about Advanced Search.

Search results show some membership details. You can use the Actions dropdown to act on all results or a selected subset, including Email - send now or Export members.

docs.title: Send email to selected members
docs.text:
1. Go to Memberships > Find Members and enter your criteria.
  2. On the Find Members results screen, select the records you want to email.
  3. In the -actions- dropdown, select Send Email to Contacts.

You can include data field tokens to personalise the message.

docs.title: View membership records
docs.text: Use the membership dashboard for a snapshot of recent activity, or open a contact record to see that contact’s memberships.

docs.title: View the membership dashboard
docs.text:
1. Go to Memberships > Dashboard.

The dashboard shows a summary of recent memberships by type and date range, alongside recent member activity.

  1. Click a summary number to view the corresponding members.

The linked lists show members who joined or renewed in the last two months or year-to-date, or who are current according to the membership status definitions. From a list, you can take actions such as Delete, Edit, Export, or Send Email to Contacts.

docs.title: View a contact’s memberships
docs.text:
1. Find the contact whose memberships you want to view.
  2. Click the Membership tab.

The tab lists active memberships—those with a current status—before expired or canceled memberships. A pending membership appears when you open the tab, but it is not counted in the number shown on the tab.

You can edit a membership record, renew a membership, or create a new record. If an online credit card payment processor is configured for CiviCRM, creating or renewing offers two options: an offline record, with no real-time transaction, or an online record using a real-time credit card transaction. The online option can also set up auto-renew if the processor supports it. The interfaces are similar, but the credit card option includes payment processing and recording options.

If you view the primary member contact for a membership type with inherited membership, you will also see the contacts who have inherited it.

In the example shown, a maximum of two employees of the primary membership organisation can inherit memberships. Before deleting an inherited membership, check that it is assigned to the wrong employee. Click Delete for that contact to free a place, then select Create to assign the inherited membership appropriately.

docs.title: How members-only websites work
docs.text:
CiviMember can work with your content management system (CMS) to create a members-only section of your website. Each CMS has its own integration module or modules for this purpose.

In a typical setup, a contact creates an account on your site and becomes a member of your organisation through a CiviMember membership sign-up page. When they log in, they can access members-only content.

That content might come from your CMS or from your CRM. Examples include a detailed members directory or a list of private events available only to members.

For information about your CMS, see its section in the Integration chapter of the System Adminstrator Guide. You can also ask questions in the CiviCRM Community.

docs.title: Manual membership entry fields and permissions
docs.text: Use this page to check what the membership form fields do and which permissions staff need. Many fields on the New Membership form are completed automatically if left blank.

docs.title: Access permissions
docs.text:
Permissions are managed at Administer > User & Permissions > Permissions.

User need Permissions Find and view memberships access CiviMember and view contact for the associated record; view contributions if payments are involved. Create or edit memberships edit memberships and edit contact for the associated record; edit contributions if payments are involved.

For more detail, see the default permissions and roles information.

docs.title: Membership details
docs.text:
Field What it does Membership Organization and Type Selects the organisation the contact has a membership with and the membership type. Use this or Choose Price Set. Choose Price Set Selects a Membership Price Set instead of Membership Organization and Type when you have different fee structures for different classes of membership. Number of Terms Sets the number of membership periods or terms. The end date is set for that number of terms. This option is hidden when using membership price sets. Source If left blank, CiviCRM fills in details including whether the transaction was offline or online and who completed the record. Campaign Selects a campaign if the membership is connected with a larger campaign. See the Campaign section for more information. Member Since Defaults to the date the membership record was created. You can override it. Start Date Defaults to the current date for a rolling membership. For a fixed-period membership, CiviCRM determines the date from the membership type configuration. You can override it. End Date Is calculated from the start date and membership type settings. You can override it. Auto-renew Appears only when the selected Membership Type has auto-renew functionality set and you are creating the membership with Submit Credit Card Membership.

Caution: Selecting Status Override? stops the status from updating automatically according to the membership status rules set when defining your memberships. This field lets you set the membership status manually instead.

docs.title: Payment fields
docs.text:
Selecting Record Membership Payment? and completing the transaction fields creates a contribution record as well as the membership record. After recording the membership, you can view its related contribution at the bottom of the membership record.

Field What it does Record Payment from a Different Contact? Records a payment from someone other than the member, often for a gift membership. Financial Type Selects the financial type for the payment. Amount Records the membership payment amount. Received Date and Time Records when the payment was received. Paid By Selects the payment instrument, such as cash or check. The Contributions section has more information about configuring Payment Instruments. Check Number Records the check number when payment was received by check. Transaction ID Stores an auto-generated transaction ID if you have a payment processor. For a manual transaction, you can enter a bank transfer ID or another applicable identifier. Payment Status Selects the status of the membership payment received. The Contributions section has more information about configuring Payment Instruments.

docs.title: Confirmation and receipt fields
docs.text:
Selecting Send Confirmation and Receipt? sends the contact an email confirming their membership.

Field What it does Receipt From Selects the address that sends the confirmation receipt. If the address is not listed, you can add it at Mailings > From Email Addresses. Receipt Message Adds a special message for the member. If left blank, the default confirmation and receipt message is used.

docs.title: Batch entry of membership payments
docs.text:
Use Batch Data Entry in the Memberships menu to enter a batch of membership payments received in the office on paper forms or similar records.

The feature works with new and existing contacts. It verifies the total amount and number of items against the payments recorded on your deposit slip or slips.

The batch entry input grid includes tools for processing many memberships:

  • A copy feature can set all fields to the same value.
  • You can create new contacts without leaving the grid.

Several CiviCRM reserved profiles determine which fields appear in the batch entry grid. To collect information not currently included, you need to alter those profiles to display the fields you want.

For more detail, see Batch Entry of Contributions or Membership Payments.

docs.title: Import memberships
docs.text: Use Importing Memberships to bring in a large set of membership records from outside CiviCRM or to update many existing memberships. The Importing Data page explains the general process and has a section on importing memberships.

docs.title: Prepare the import file
docs.text:
Before importing, check these requirements:

  • Contact records must already exist. For contacts not yet in CiviCRM, import the Contact data first and give it an External ID that you can include in the membership data. For existing contacts, use the Internal Contact ID or the fields from your Unsupervised Duplicate Matching Rule to associate memberships with the correct contacts.
  • The membership data file must contain Membership Type and Start Date. Membership types must exactly match those set up by your CiviCRM Administrator, and start dates must use the date format specified for your CiviCRM installation. Without these fields, you cannot import the file.
  • Use separate imports for different contact types. A file containing more than one contact type will not work. Import new memberships and renewals separately as well.
  • The import file must be a CSV file.

docs.title: Run the import
docs.text:
1. Go to Memberships > Import Memberships.
  2. On the Upload Data screen, select your CSV file.
  3. Select the checkbox if the file contains column headers.
  4. Specify the contact type you are importing.
  5. Indicate the date format used in the file.
  6. Click Continue >>.
  7. On the Match Fields screen, map your data to the appropriate fields under Matching CiviCRM Field. You can choose Save this field mapping to reuse it for future imports.
  8. On the Preview screen, check the table showing Total Rows, rows with errors and valid rows.

Before importing: Rows with errors will be skipped if you continue. You can download a file containing just those records, correct them and import them separately. Alternatively, correct the original CSV file and start the import again.

  1. If there are no errors, or you do not want to correct the errors found, click Import Now>>.

CiviCRM shows the import’s progress. When it finishes, you see a summary of the import activity and its results.

docs.title: Create a membership manually
docs.text:
You can add a membership when your organisation needs to process it rather than have a website contact join through self-service. Self-service can save administrative time, but manual entry is useful when staff need to handle a membership directly.

To create or edit a membership, you need edit memberships and edit contact permission for the associated contact. If you are recording a payment, you also need edit contributions permission. An administrator can manage these permissions at Administer > User & Permissions > Permissions. See the default permissions and roles information for more detail.

docs.title: Add a membership to an existing contact
docs.text:
1. Open the contact’s record.
  2. Select the Memberships tab.
  3. Click Add Membership.
  4. Complete the New Membership form with the membership details.

If a payment processor allows credit card transactions directly on your site, you can instead select Submit Credit Card Membership from the contact’s record to process the membership payment immediately.

docs.title: Add a membership from the Memberships menu
docs.text:
Use this route if you need to create a contact while adding their membership.

  1. Go to Memberships > New Membership.
  2. Select a contact or create a new contact.

  1. Complete the New Member form with the membership and payment information.

This route does not offer credit card submission. You can still record other payment types, such as checks and cash.

docs.title: Record a gift membership
docs.text:
When entering the membership, select Record Membership Payment?, then Record Payment from a Different Contact?. The person paying—the gifter—can be an existing contact or a new contact created during the process.

The payment is recorded on the gifter’s record, with a soft credit for the membership on the recipient’s record. The receipt goes to the gifter. You need to send the recipient a separate email or letter to tell them about their membership.

docs.title: Create an auto-renewing membership
docs.text:
This option is available through a contact’s record when you use Submit Credit Card Membership. It depends on the Membership Type and payment processor settings.

  1. Open the contact’s summary screen.
  2. Select the Memberships tab.
  3. Click Submit Credit Card Membership.
  4. Select a Membership Type set up for recurring payments. The Membership renewed automatically checkbox appears.
  5. Check the auto-renew option if the membership should renew automatically.

Checking the option submits a recurring payment (subscription) request to the selected payment processor. If the request succeeds, the membership renews on the last day of each membership period until the recurring payment is cancelled. Membership payment receipt emails include a link for the member to cancel auto-renewal.

docs.title: Configure a membership price set
docs.text:
You can use a membership price set to let contacts choose multiple membership terms, join more than one organisation, or add non-membership items when they sign up.

The Donwell Swim Club example has five price fields: National Association Fees, Annual Club membership, Club Gear, raffle tickets and donation. It offers two membership types.

Before you create the price set, define its membership types (see Defining Memberships) and all the financial types it will need.

Membership price sets work on online join-up or renewal pages and for new member sign-ups processed manually in the CiviCRM back office. They cannot be used for manually processed renewals. You must renew each membership individually (see the Renewals chapter); you may also need a contribution price set for any non-membership items you offer. You cannot combine memberships that can be auto-renewed with memberships that do not offer auto-renewal or with non-membership items.

docs.title: Create the price set
docs.text:
1. Go to Memberships > New Price Set or Administer > CiviMember > New Price Set.
  2. Enter the price set name. It appears both to the public as part of the price set and to admin staff choosing between price sets, so make it descriptive for both.
  3. Tick Membership.
  4. Set the Default Financial Type. This choice has accounting implications; refer to the Contributions section for more information.
  5. Add pre- or post-form help text if you want to.
  6. Make sure the price set is active.
  7. Select Save.

CiviCRM opens the form for the first price field.

docs.title: Create a price field
docs.text:
1. Enter a Field Label. This label appears to the public.
  2. Choose an Input Field Type:
  3. Text/Numeric Quantity: Shows a text box for a quantity. CiviCRM multiplies the quantity entered by the unit Price to calculate the amount.
  4. Select: Shows a dropdown from which one option can be selected.
  5. Radio: Shows a list from which up to one option can be selected.
  6. Checkbox: Shows a list from which multiple options can be selected.
  7. Check the Financial Type. It starts with the price set’s Default Financial Type, but you can override it.
  8. Set Display Amount?. When ticked, it shows the option’s price next to its label. You can untick it if the label already includes the price; otherwise, leave it ticked.
  9. Set Order, Field Help, Required and Active as needed. These settings are self-explanatory or have help on the form.
  10. Set Active On and Expire On if the field should be visible only from a date, until a date, or between two dates.
  11. Set Visibility to Public for people who can see the membership sign-up page on your website, or Admin for back-office users with appropriate permissions.

For example, you could schedule a price rise at 12:00am on 1 January 2019 by setting the old-price field’s Expire On to 1/12/2019 12:00am and the new-price field’s Active On to 1/12/2019 12:00am. The stated date and the dates entered in this example do not clearly agree, so check the dates before using them.

docs.title: Offer multiple membership terms
docs.text:
Use the National Association Fees field as an example of a Radio field that offers a choice of membership terms.

Select a Membership Type from the dropdown of configured membership types. Number of terms fills with 1, while Label, Amount and Financial Type fill from the membership type’s definition. You can change any of these values.

The National Association Fees membership type lasts 1 year and has a minimum fee of $100. Set Number of terms to 2 to offer 2 years of membership. Give each option a different Label. You can increase Amount to offer concession and standard fees for the same number of terms. Because the labels in this example do not include prices, keep Display Amount? ticked.

This approach needs only one 1-year National Association membership type with a minimum fee of $100, rather than three membership types. Members cannot auto-renew with this multi-term configuration.

docs.title: Offer membership of another organisation
docs.text:
A contact can have only one active membership with a specific organisation. To offer both National Association Fees and swim club membership, link the two memberships to different organisations. See Defining Memberships for more information.

Use a Select field for the swim club membership.

When you select its Membership Type, Number of terms fills with 1 and Label, Amount and Financial Type fill from that type’s definition. You can change any of them. Keep Display Amount? ticked because the option labels in this example do not include prices.

Together, these first two price fields let someone sign up for a minimum of one and a maximum of two memberships.

docs.title: Add non-membership options
docs.text: Price set fields can also offer services, subscriptions and other non-membership options. The Donwell Swim Club example has three such fields: club-branded swimming gear, raffle tickets and a donation.

docs.title: Club gear
docs.text:
Use Checkbox when contacts may choose more than one item from a field.

For products, leave Membership Type and Number of terms empty. Set Label, Amount and Financial Type for each option. Keep Display Amount? ticked if, as in this example, the labels do not include prices.

Radio and Select are interchangeable when you want someone to choose no more than one option. Both can be used for membership or non-membership options. Checkbox can also be used for either, but is needed when someone may select multiple options from one field.

docs.title: Raffle tickets
docs.text:
Text/Numeric Quantity can only be used for non-membership options. Usually, put the unit price in the Field Label or Field Help and leave Display Amount? unticked.

The field appears like this:

Set Active On and Expire On to make the field visible only during the raffle-ticket selling period authorised by the relevant licensing authority.

docs.title: Donation
docs.text:
For an “any amount” donation, set the unit price to

  1. The example includes the currency symbol, but not the unit price, in the field label and leaves Display Amount? unticked.

The completed fields appear together like this:

Price sets can be configured in many ways. Test yours thoroughly before using it on your live site to make sure it fits your situation.

docs.title: Create a membership report
docs.text:
Use a membership report template to create a saved report when the existing reports do not meet your needs.

  1. Go to Reports > Membership Reports.
  2. Click New Member Report.
  3. On the Create New Report Template screen, select a membership report template.
  4. Enter your criteria.

  1. Click Preview Report to check the results.
  2. If the results meet your needs, click Create Report.
  3. Enter the information you want to save with the new membership report.

For more about working with reports, see Reporting.

docs.title: Export membership records
docs.text:
Export the records you need using either the default primary fields or fields you select. You can use the file for further analysis, document mail merges or reports outside CiviCRM.

  1. Go to Memberships > Find Members.
  2. Enter your search criteria to find the membership records you want to export.
  3. On the Find Members search results screen, select the records you want to export.
  4. In the -actions- drop-down, select Export Members.
  5. Select Export PRIMARY fields or Select fields for export, then click Continue.

If you selected Export PRIMARY fields, a file named CiviCRM_Member_Search.csv is created containing membership records based on your search criteria.

If you selected Select fields for export:

  1. Choose the fields you want to export.
  2. If you want to reuse the selection in a future export, select Save this field mapping.
  3. Click Export.

A file named CiviCRM_Member_Search.csv is created containing membership records based on your search criteria and the fields you selected.

docs.title: Membership reporting options
docs.text:
Use this page to identify which report or other view provides the membership information you need.

The membership dashboard gives you a quick summary of current memberships. For each membership type, it shows the current total number of members and totals for last month, this month and the current year to date. You can also search for specific membership details using Advanced Search or Find Memberships.

docs.title: Membership reports
docs.text:
CiviCRM includes these membership reports:

  • Membership Summary groups information about members by a date frequency you specify, such as month, week, quarter or year. For example, you can look at the number of members who joined each month across a date range, membership types or custom data you collect about them.

Selecting a highlighted field opens the corresponding Membership Detail report for that row. For example, selecting May 2015 for the General membership type shows the detail for that group.

  • Membership Detail shows information for each membership record that matches your selected criteria.

  • Lapsed Memberships lists memberships that lapsed or will lapse before the date you specify.

  • Contribution and Membership Details shows information about contributions, including contributions connected to membership records, based on your report criteria.

For more about working with reports, see Reporting.

docs.title: Test an online membership sign-up page
docs.text:
You will use Test-drive to check the sign-up or renewal process and confirm that the information appears as expected in CiviCRM.

  1. Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages.
  2. Click Links next to your membership sign-up/renewal page.
  3. Click Test-drive.

Test-drive shows the same registration pages as a regular visitor, but an online payment is not actually debited from your card. See payment processors for information about dummy processors and card details for test transactions.

  1. Complete the form as someone joining your organisation would.
  2. Repeat the process with different combinations of fields.
  3. Check that the resulting information appears as you expect in CiviCRM.

Memberships submitted in test mode are added as test data. They are not included in membership statistics or ordinary member searches. To find and delete test memberships, select the is test checkbox in Find Memberships.

After making any necessary changes, ask other staff members or people outside your organisation to test the process. Review it periodically: how members fill in the form may show where changes are needed. You can also ask recent members how easy sign-up was and how the form could improve.

docs.title: Add a membership sign-up page to your website
docs.text:
You will make your completed membership sign-up or renewal page visible to visitors. The method depends on whether your website uses Drupal, WordPress or Joomla!.

Membership pages inherit your website theme. You can add images in the page’s HTML text areas. Changes to the page’s wider design are outside the scope of this guide; a website designer familiar with your CMS and CiviCRM can help.

docs.title: Drupal
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages.
  2. Click Links next to your membership sign-up/renewal page.
  3. Click Live Page to view the finished page.
  4. Copy its URL into a content page or assign it to a menu item.

docs.title: WordPress
docs.text:
Choose one of these ways to show the page:

  • Go to Contributions > Manage Contribution Pages, click Links next to your membership sign-up/renewal page, then click Live Page. Copy the URL into an HTML link or menu.
  • Use a plugin such as Page Links To to create a URL “slug”.
  • Click the WordPress shortcode icon to insert the form into a page or post.

docs.title: Joomla!
docs.text:
Create a menu item to expose the membership sign-up/renewal page:

  1. Navigate to a menu and create a new CiviCRM item.
  2. Choose Contributions from the menu options.
  3. In the basic parameters section, select the contribution page from the dropdown menu.
  4. Save the menu item.
  5. View the website to confirm the page works.

docs.title: Create an online membership sign-up page
docs.text:
You will configure a contribution page for membership sign-up and renewal, including membership fees, information collected from members and receipts.

Membership sign-up pages are contribution pages with a membership section. Use a contribution page even if the membership is free. Before you begin, Defining Memberships explains membership types and statuses; the online contributions section explains how to create a contribution page. For more detail about the available tools, see online contribution pages.

docs.title: Check permissions for visitors
docs.text:
The Anonymous and Authenticated roles need these CMS permissions to join or renew online:

  • Profile listings and forms lets you collect core contact information, such as names and addresses.
  • Access all custom data is required to collect custom data.
  • Make online contributions is required unless memberships are free and you do not want to accept donations during sign-up or renewal.

docs.title: Configure the page
docs.text: Create an online contribution page and give it a name. The configuration tabs then appear at the top of the page.

docs.title: Title
docs.text:
Set the page title and basic information, such as the Financial Type recorded for memberships made through the page. You can also add an introductory message, including images and simple HTML.

To offer organisational memberships, select the checkbox that lets people become members on behalf of an organisation. This is the recommended way to offer them. When you enable the option, select a profile to collect organisational information, and choose whether organisational sign-up is optional or required.

docs.title: Amounts
docs.text:
Choose the payment processor for the page. You can select more than one to give people a choice.

Set membership fees on the Memberships tab, not the Amounts tab. If you want to collect membership fees without asking for extra contributions, leave Contribution Amounts section enabled unticked. If you want to ask for contributions in addition to membership fees, tick it and add suggested contribution amounts or configure a contribution price set.

For free memberships, leave Execute real-time monetary transactions unticked and choose a membership type with a zero-value minimum fee.

docs.title: Memberships
docs.text:
Select Membership Section Enabled to use the contribution page for sign-up and renewal. Add the text to display for initial sign-up and for renewals. When a logged-in user with a current or expired membership views the sign-up page, CiviCRM automatically shows a renewal page instead, using the text from the renewals box.

Choose which membership types appear on the form, which type is the default and which types can be auto-renewed.

To offer auto-renewal, you need membership types set up for auto-renewal and a payment processor that supports automatic recurring payments. Visitors will see: “Please renew my membership automatically. (Your initial membership fee will be processed once you complete the confirmation step. You will be able to cancel automatic renewals at any time by logging in to your account or contacting us.)” Membership payment receipt emails include a link for the member to cancel auto-renewal.

You can make membership sign-up optional, for example, on a contribution page that offers membership without requiring it. To do so, select Contribution Amounts section enabled on the Amounts tab. You can choose whether those payments are recorded separately from membership fee payments.

If the Membership Types table cannot provide the options you need, use a Membership price set. For example, price sets can let visitors:

  • Sign up for national and local memberships at the same time.
  • Sign up for multiple membership terms at the same time.
  • Add another option, such as a paid subscription, to membership sign-up.

docs.title: Receipt
docs.text:
Configure the thank-you page that visitors see after sign-up or renewal, and choose whether to generate and send an email receipt. You can customise the message added to the membership receipt and the address it comes from. To further customise the receipt email template, use Mailings > Message templates.

Warning: Before adding staff addresses to CC Receipt To or BCC Receipt To, make sure they are correct and will not bounce or return an error. CiviCRM interprets a returned email as a bounce for the contact who received the receipt, not for the CC or BCC address. This can put the contact’s email address On Hold and prevent future emails from being sent. See the issue report for details.

To receive real-time updates about processed memberships, enter one or more staff email addresses in CC Receipt To or BCC Receipt To, separated by commas.

docs.title: Tell-A-Friend
docs.text: You can add a tell-a-friend feature to the thank-you page. Members can email friends a link and information about your organisation. Friends who receive it are added to CiviCRM if they are not already there; their source field shows that they were added through tell-a-friend.

docs.title: Profiles
docs.text:
A contribution page includes only an email field by default. On the Profiles tab, select an existing profile to collect more information, such as a member’s address or interests. If you have permission, you can also create a profile or edit an existing one. When someone signing up is logged in, available information from CiviCRM populates their profile fields.

Warning: Editing an existing profile changes it everywhere that profile is used.

Do not add a membership profile. CiviCRM collects membership information automatically during online sign-up.

docs.title: Premiums
docs.text:
Premiums are thank-you gifts or incentives. Although they are commonly offered at donation levels—for example, a T-shirt for a $50 donation—you can also use them on membership pages.

Before including premiums, configure them through Contributions > Premiums (Thank-you Gifts). The Premiums tab then controls introductory text, contact information and other premium-related details.

docs.title: Alternative: Contribution Forms
docs.text: Contribution Forms offer another way to take contributions from website visitors. They use FormBuilder, giving site administrators more flexibility to tailor forms, and offer more modern client-side payment integrations. At the time of writing, only a few Payment Processors are supported.

docs.title: Plan membership renewal reminders
docs.text: Choose how to tell members their membership is due for renewal, and account for online renewal and email preferences.

docs.title: Email reminders
docs.text:
You can send one or more automatic renewal emails with Administer > Communications > Schedule Reminders. This is particularly useful for rolling membership types, whose memberships can end at any time of year. Once you have composed your message, follow Schedule Reminders to set up sending.

Write the message for its audience and its timing. For example, a reminder sent three months early to someone who joined on behalf of an organisation may need to allow time for a purchase order and payment through an accounts department. It would differ from a reminder sent one week after an individual’s membership has ended.

If members can renew online, include a checksum token link in every renewal reminder email. The link pre-fills the renewal form with data already in the member’s record.

Before sending reminders: by default, scheduled reminders are sent to people who have opted out of bulk or all emails unless you specifically exclude them. Also exclude members who have chosen automatic renewal if your organisation offers it. Allow time to test reminder templates, especially if you customise messages for different member types or have complex membership structures.

docs.title: Postal reminders
docs.text: You can post letters to all members due to renew, or only to members without an email address and those who have opted out of bulk or all emails. See Postal mail communications for ways to generate the letters.

docs.title: Set a default online membership renewal page
docs.text:
Configure the page used by the Contact Dashboard’s renew link for manually entered memberships.

When someone buys a membership through an online membership signup page, their Contact Dashboard contains a renew link to that page. The link does not appear for a membership entered manually unless you set a Default Online Membership Renewal Page.

  1. If you do not already have one, create a membership page containing all currently available memberships. You may need a Membership price set if fees must be allocated to more than one financial type.
  2. Go to Administer > CiviMember > CiviMember Component Settings.
  3. For Default Online Membership Renewal Page, choose the page containing all your membership types.

A renew link to that page is then displayed on the Contact Dashboard for manually entered memberships.

docs.title: Renew a membership for one contact
docs.text:
Use a contact’s membership record to enter a manual renewal.

  1. Go to the contact’s summary page.
  2. Open the Memberships tab.
  3. Click MORE next to the membership record.
  4. Select Renew to enter a cash, cheque or EFT payment, or Renew-Credit Card to process the renewal through your online payment processor.

docs.title: Update multiple memberships
docs.text:
Use Update multiple memberships, previously called Batch Update Members Via Profile, to change several existing membership records. This is different from Batch Data Entry, which adds new memberships and member payments.

Before you begin, create and configure a Profile containing the membership fields you want to display and update.

  1. Select Memberships > Find Members.
  2. Enter your search criteria and click Search.
  3. On the Find Members results screen, select the membership records.
  4. Select Update multiple memberships from the -actions- dropdown and click Go.
  5. On the Update multiple memberships screen, choose your profile under Select Profile and click Continue >>.
  6. Update the information displayed by that profile. To copy the first record’s value to the other fields in a column, use the “auto-copy” icon at the top of the column.
  7. Click Update Memberships.

The example screen uses a membership profile configured to display Membership Type and Membership Start Date.

docs.title: How membership renewals work
docs.text: Learn what happens when a membership is renewed, including how dates, payments and membership types can change.

docs.title: Renew an existing membership or add a new one?
docs.text:
When someone wants to remain a member as their membership approaches its end date, you will usually want to renew their existing membership through CiviMember rather than create a new one. Renewing keeps the membership history in one record.

A membership has three primary dates:

  • Member Since does not change when the membership is renewed.
  • Start date and End date depend on the membership status when the renewal is processed.

The member column on Administer > CiviMember > Membership Status Rules determines how the dates change:

Membership status has Effect of renewal Yes in the member column Start date stays the same. End date is extended by the duration of the renewal. No in the member column Start date changes to the current date. End date is calculated from the new start date.

If applicable for the membership type, renewal also records a contribution linked to the membership. After several renewals, the contact has one membership record with multiple related financial transactions representing the renewal purchases.

docs.title: Changing membership type during renewal
docs.text:
Membership up-sell lets a contact change membership type as part of renewal. If their membership is linked to an organisation and they renew under another type belonging to the same organisation, CiviCRM changes the existing membership to the new type. It preserves the membership history, including the join date and contributions, and extends the existing end date by the duration of the new membership type.

If you do not want that result, link the membership types to different organisations. One can be a dummy organisation created for this purpose and invisible to the user. See Membership types for more detail.

If you manage memberships for more than one organisation, a contact’s membership type cannot be changed or up-sold to a type from another membership organisation.

docs.title: Automatic renewals
docs.text: For members who chose automatic renewal when they joined, payment is taken from their pre-authorised credit card on the renewal date. Their membership end date is updated, and CiviCRM sends the appropriate thank-you and receipts. For setup details, see Defining memberships, Online memberships sign up and Manual entry of memberships.

docs.title: Online renewals
docs.text:
CiviCRM uses the same page for new memberships and renewals. For a logged-in website visitor with a valid current or expired membership, the renewal version appears at the same URL as the membership join page. Its title and introductory message use the text entered in the renewal fields on the memberships tab when the online membership page was configured.

A current member who is not logged in sees the sign-up page instead. If they submit it and CiviCRM finds their existing contact record from their contact information, their membership is renewed. If CiviCRM does not find the record—for example, because their email address has changed—it creates a new contact and membership. This can cause duplicate records.

To reduce that risk, include a checksum token in renewal reminder emails, and use the new-member introductory message to remind members to log in before renewing.

docs.title: What is CiviMember?
docs.text: CiviMember is the CiviCRM component for managing memberships. This page explains what it can do, how memberships relate to contacts, and how one organisation used it.

docs.title: How memberships work
docs.text:
A member is a contact in CiviCRM with one or more memberships. That contact can be an individual, household, organisation or another contact sub-type.

Memberships can last from a day to a lifetime. They can be free or paid, with simple or complex pricing. They can also be set up to auto-renew if a compatible payment processor is enabled.

CiviMember lets you:

  • Define membership types and pricing schemes.
  • Offer online self-service sign-up and renewal using CiviContribute.
  • Manage memberships manually through the administrative interface.
  • Create and schedule automated messages, such as welcomes for new members and renewal reminders.
  • Track and report on contacts through the membership cycle.
  • Grant members additional website privileges.

You can see a contact’s memberships on their summary screen and on the membership dashboard. You can find memberships through Membership Search or Advanced Search. CiviMember also provides four membership reports, which you can customise to meet your needs.

docs.title: Planning your membership scheme
docs.text:
CiviMember is flexible enough to meet most membership requirements. If you are new to it, reviewing the chapters in this section while you plan your organisation’s membership scheme can help you decide how to model that scheme in CiviCRM.

Adopting CiviCRM will normally change some working practices. Work closely with the people who will manage memberships day to day as you develop your plans.

docs.title: Example: Atlantic Region Public Transit Association
docs.text:
The Atlantic Region Public Transit Association (ARPTA) has four membership categories:

Category Members and benefits Fees Regular Members Public transit systems. Membership is organisation-based, with three tiers based on system size. All employees of a member organisation receive benefits, such as discounted rates at Association events. Tiered by system size. Affiliate Members Businesses providing goods and services to the transit industry. Membership is organisation-based. Up to 10 employees of a member organisation receive benefits, such as discounted rates at Association events. The same for all Affiliate Members. Associate Members Students, government representatives, public interest groups, research institutions and other interested parties. Membership is individual-based. The same for all Associate Members. Honorary Members Retired transit system executives and others who have made a notable contribution to the industry and Association. Membership is individual-based. Free for life.

ARPTA’s membership administrator, Sue, created a separate membership type for each category. ARPTA initially processed new sign-ups and renewals manually while the system bedded in.

Last year, ARPTA’s board decided to improve recruitment and renewal rates to increase membership income, while keeping tight control of—or reducing—the time spent on administration. ARPTA used CiviContribute and CiviMember to create online sign-up and renewal pages for Regular and Affiliate Members. Recruitment campaigns linked potential members to the sign-up pages, while existing members were encouraged to log in to the member section of the ARPTA website to renew.

The online process removed much of the sign-up administration and gave Sue a clear view of new sign-ups, recent renewals and expired members to follow up. Using CiviContribute, she can produce a monthly spreadsheet of membership fees received for the accounts department to import into its accounting software. With less paperwork, she has more time to engage with members and take part in the annual conference, which ARPTA manages using CiviEvent.

ARPTA reported a 30% increase in new members over a year following the move to online sign-up and renewal alongside its marketing campaign. Its analysis also showed a 40% improvement in membership retention. ARPTA attributed this in part to Sue having more time to contact lapsed and expired members, and in part to members finding online renewal convenient and receiving emails Sue set up using the Schedule Reminders feature. Its market research found that members appreciated Sue’s more frequent contact and felt more engaged with ARPTA.

docs.title: Activity attributes and statuses
docs.text: Use this page to check what an Activity records and which statuses are available by default.

docs.title: Activity attributes
docs.text:
Attribute What it records Date and time The point in time when the Activity happens. Duration The time spent on the Activity, which can be collected across a series of Activities. Status Whether the Activity is scheduled, completed, cancelled or in another available status. Added by The person who added the Activity, or the contact if they carried it out themselves via the website. Assigned to The person, usually within your organisation, who will carry out or has carried out the Activity. With contact(s) The contacts in your database who are the subject of the Activity.

To record an Activity between a given contact and multiple other contacts, add those contacts in the With Contact field on the Add Activity form.

docs.title: Default Activity status options
docs.text:
• Scheduled
  • Completed
  • Cancelled
  • Left Message
  • Unreachable
  • Not Required

Administrators can add status options. Any status options they add appear on all Activity Types.

docs.title: Set up a repeating Activity
docs.text:
Set an Activity to repeat at a chosen day and time, with an end point and, if needed, dates to exclude.

  1. Open the Activity Screen.
  2. Under Repeat Activity, set the repetition options you need:
Option Available values or purpose Repetition Start Date and Time When the repetition starts. Repeats Every Hour, Day, Week, Month or Year. Repeats On Sun, Mon, Tue, Wed, Thr, Fri or Sat. Ends After a specific number of occurrences or on a specific date. Exclude Dates Multiple dates can be selected.

  1. Save the Activity. A confirmation screen displays all the dates for which an Activity will be created. A new Activity is created for each repetition; you can edit or delete each one individually.

Before editing a repetition: Changes to its date or time are not applied to other repeating Activities. When you edit one repetition, you can apply other changes to that Activity only, to that Activity and all future Activities in the series, or to every Activity in the series.

docs.title: Configure Activities for your organisation
docs.text: Administrators can create additional Activity Types and create additional status options. You can also set up custom fields to collect data for Activities.

docs.title: Create an Activity Type
docs.text:
Several Activity Types are included by default. Create another type when you need to record a specific kind of work your organisation does.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Activity Types.
  2. On the Activity Type Options page, click Add Activity Type.

  1. Assign the new Activity Type to Contact if it should be available from the Actions button when viewing a contact record. Assign it to CiviCase if its Activities are only for use inside a case.

For example, you might create Activity Types called Training and Interview. For more on creating custom fields, refer to the Custom Fields chapter. For details on producing reports, see the Reporting section.

docs.title: Set up custom fields for Activities
docs.text:
When setting up a custom data set, specify Activity as what the data will be used for. You can also specify a particular Activity Type. The custom fields will then be available when recording the relevant Activities.

For example, a custom field set associated with Activities could include funder and project. You could then produce reports of Activities undertaken for a particular funder or project. You could also make a custom field specific to one Activity Type—for example, to classify meetings as a staff meeting, client meeting or other organisation's meeting.

docs.title: Add an Activity status
docs.text:
Before adding statuses: Every status option appears on every Activity Type. Consider which options your organisation needs before adding more.

To add status options, go to Administer > System Settings > Option Groups.

docs.title: Understanding Activities
docs.text:
Learn what Activities record and when they are useful for your organisation.

Activities provide one place to record and view the history of interactions between your organisation and your constituents, clients and partners. You can use them to track meetings, phone calls and other interactions. CiviCRM components also use Activities to record actions such as contributions, event attendance and petition signatures.

An Activity happens at a specific point in time and involves at least one contact. It can involve several contacts. If you need to know who at your organisation carried out a task, record it as an Activity. You can assign an Activity to a staff member or volunteer; an email is automatically sent to the assignee.

docs.title: Activities and groups
docs.text:
Sometimes you could use either an Activity or a group to record something. For example, you could record that a membership packet was sent as an Activity, or add the contact to a group called “received membership packet”.

An Activity is usually more useful for this example because you can record when the packet was sent, who sent it and any notes about what the person requested. You can also schedule the work by setting a future date and time and setting the status to Scheduled.

docs.title: Activities and events
docs.text: An event is something a contact attends, such as a meet-up, training, dinner or fundraising event. An Activity records an interaction with your organisation. That interaction could be a meeting, a phone call or a donation.

docs.title: Add a contact
docs.text:
Use the contact creation form to add an Individual, Organisation, Household or available contact subtype.

An Individual requires a first name and last name or an email address. An Organisation or Household requires its Organisation/Household name. You can enter other information now and edit the record later.

  1. From the navigation menu on a non-public page, choose Contacts > New Individual to add an Individual. The Contacts menu also lets you create other contact types and subtypes.

  1. Enter the contact’s information. Creation forms place basic details, such as name and email, at the top. More specific fields, including addresses, communication preferences and any custom fields for the contact type, are grouped in accordions below.

  2. Select Check for Matching Contacts after entering the information you have in that section. This helps you avoid creating a duplicate.

  3. Choose a save option:

  4. Save saves the record and opens the contact screen.
  5. Save and New saves the record and clears the form so you can add another contact.
  6. Cancel discards what you entered and returns to the CiviCRM dashboard.

docs.title: Address options on the form
docs.text:
You can enter multiple addresses, such as home, work and a separate billing address. The address-sharing checkbox lets you use an existing contact’s address or create a new contact to share it with. If you choose a new contact, select its contact type; a pop-up form then lets you add its record.

For an Individual’s work address, Share Address With offers a quick search to select an existing employer. Alternatively, select New Organisation from the create new contact drop-down to create the employer’s record. When a person uses another contact’s address, the address can be edited only from the “master contact’s” record; shared address changes are synchronised between the contacts.

The countries offered in the drop-down depend on Available Countries at Administer > Localization > Languages, Currency, Locations. Available address fields can be changed at Administer > Localization > Address settings. The Address Name field, which can label an address “Summer Home”, is hidden by default but can be enabled there.

docs.title: Tags and groups on the form
docs.text: You can add the new contact to existing groups and apply existing tags. To create groups or tags, see Groups and Tags.

docs.title: Edit a contact
docs.text:
Choose an editing method based on how much of the contact record you need to change.

  • To change one block on the Summary tab, hover over its upper-right corner and select Edit Info. You can edit that information directly on the summary screen.
  • To change a lot of information, select the edit button above the contact’s tabs to open the full editing form.

If two admin users both open the editing form and then save the same contact, the second is notified of the first user’s edit and given a chance to manually “merge” the edits.

docs.title: Delete contacts
docs.text:
Delete a contact from its record or search results, or use advanced search to delete multiple contacts.

By default, deleted contacts move to the “trash” rather than disappearing completely. They can be restored later using advanced search’s search in trash feature. See “searching” in the “working with your data” chapter for more information.

docs.title: Delete one contact
docs.text:
Choose either method:

  • Open the contact record and select the Delete contact button at the top right.
  • Search for the contact. At the end of its row in the results, select More > Delete Contact.

docs.title: Delete multiple contacts
docs.text:
Delete Permanently is an option for multiple contacts, distinct from sending them to the trash. Check which option you select before confirming.

  1. Run an advanced search.
  2. Check each record to delete, or use the checkbox in the results header to select all.
  3. From the actions drop-down, choose Delete Contacts to send them to the trash, if enabled, or Delete Permanently.
  4. On the warning page, select Delete to continue or Cancel to return to the previous screen.

docs.title: Contact subtypes
docs.text:
Contact subtypes let your organisation distinguish kinds of contacts within CiviCRM’s core contact types and collect different information about them.

Each subtype is based on an Individual, Organisation or Household. For example, Student could be based on Individual. Farm could be based on Organisation or Household, depending on how your organisation uses it.

Subtypes are useful when only some contacts need a particular set of custom data. If you need subject areas and qualifications for teachers but not other Individuals, you could create a Teacher subtype based on Individual, then create a custom data set that extends only Individuals of that subtype. See custom fields for more information.

Core contact types are mutually exclusive: a contact cannot be both an Organisation and an Individual. A contact can, however, have more than one user-defined subtype—for example, both Teacher and Parent.

You can create subtypes and edit contact types at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Contact Types. You cannot delete the built-in contact types, but you can change their names and associated images.

docs.title: Customise the contact display
docs.text:
Use display preferences and address settings to change which contact sections, tabs and address fields your organisation sees.

Use an account with Administer CiviCRM privileges.

docs.title: Hide a section
docs.text:
For example, if your organisation does not need to store demographics information:

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences.
  2. Clear the Demographics box under Editing Contacts.
  3. Select Save.

You can also use Display Preferences to rearrange the order in which information appears. See Customizing the user interface for more detail.

docs.title: Change postal address fields
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Localization > Address Settings.
  2. Check or uncheck fields under Address Editing.
  3. Select Save.

docs.title: Change which tabs appear
docs.text: You can enable or disable specific tabs at Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Display Preferences. Some tabs also depend on enabled components: for example, the Contributions tab is hidden if CiviContribute is disabled.

docs.title: Contact records and tabs
docs.text:
Use this page to look up the information stored on contacts and the purpose of each contact tab.

Contacts are the basic building block of CiviCRM. Relationships, activities, groups and contributions all connect to contacts.

docs.title: Contact types and fields
docs.text:
CiviCRM comes with three contact types:

  • Individuals: People.
  • Organisations: For example, companies or other non-profit organisations.
  • Households: Typically families that share a physical location.

Each contact record has core fields for names, greetings and addressees, contact methods such as email addresses and phone numbers, physical addresses, and communication preferences. You can add custom fields for all contacts or for particular contact types or subtypes. For more about subtypes, see Contact subtypes.

docs.title: Contact screen
docs.text:
A contact record is organised into tabs. The first is the Summary tab; the others show different aspects of the contact. Tabs can appear or disappear depending on enabled components and your permissions. For example, you see the Memberships tab only if CiviMember is turned on and you have permission to see memberships. Extra tabs can also display custom data collected about contacts.

Above the tabs, the Actions button provides shortcuts for actions involving the contact, such as adding a note or recording a contribution, meeting or other activity.

docs.title: Summary tab
docs.text: The Summary tab shows names, addresses, contact details and contact methods. Some fields, such as first name and nickname, apply to Individuals; others, such as organisation name, apply to Organisations.

docs.title: Individual names
docs.text: An Individual’s name can have a prefix, first name, middle name, last name, suffix and nickname. You do not have to use every part. Prefixes and suffixes come from drop-down lists; options can be added at Administer CiviCRM > Customize Data and Screens > Dropdown Options > Individual Prefixes (Ms., Mr...).

docs.title: Addresses
docs.text:
A contact can have more than one address, but each must have a different location type, such as work or home. One address can be marked as primary for postal mailings. You can choose it explicitly or let it default to the first address entered.

Contacts can share an address. For example, an Individual can share a work address with their employer’s Organisation record. Shared addresses are synchronised in both directions: when one changes, the other is automatically updated.

The Billing Address used for a person’s credit card payments is stored in the contact’s Billing location. If a mapping provider is enabled, you can use the map icon beside an address to see the contact’s location on a map.

docs.title: Phone numbers and email addresses
docs.text:
A contact can have multiple phone numbers, each with a location, such as work or home, and a type, such as landline, fax or mobile. Numbers entered as type mobile are available for sending SMS.

A contact can also have multiple email addresses. One can be explicitly marked to receive bulk mailings, such as CiviMail e-newsletters and announcements. When sending email through CiviMail, bouncing email addresses are automatically marked as on hold. See Email for more information.

docs.title: Communication preferences and privacy
docs.text:
You can record preferred communication methods and privacy options. Privacy options are respected by certain functions: for example, mailing labels are not printed for contacts marked Do not mail, and emails are not sent to contacts marked Do not email.

Privacy option Meaning Do not phone The contact has chosen not to be contacted by telephone. Do not email The contact has chosen not to be contacted by email. Do not mail The contact has chosen not to be contacted by post. Do not SMS The contact has chosen not to receive text messages on their mobile device. Do no trade The contact has chosen not to have their information shared or sold to other organisations. NO BULK EMAILS (User Opt Out) Set when a contact selects the Opt Out action in a CiviMail email.

docs.title: Greetings and addressees
docs.text:
By default, greeting and addressee fields are calculated from the contact’s name. For example, the default postal greeting for an Individual named Jenny Soper is “Dear Jenny”.

Global defaults can be configured at Administer CiviCRM > Communications > Email Greeting Formats, Postal Greeting Formats or Addressee Formats. You can also select a different format or customise it for an individual contact.

docs.title: Demographics and closed contacts
docs.text: For Individuals, you can record birth date, gender, whether they are deceased and when they died. For Organisations or Households that no longer exist, you can record that they are “closed” by editing the block containing Nickname and Legal Name.

docs.title: Relationships tab
docs.text:
A relationship is a named connection between contact records. A contact can have many relationships. The tab lists Current Relationships and Inactive relationships.

For more about when to use them, see the relationships chapter of Organising your data.

docs.title: Activities tab
docs.text:
The Activities tab lists interactions with a contact, including built-in activities such as event attendance, contributions and phone calls, as well as custom activities. You can record an activity using the icons at the top of the tab, such as Send an Email, Meeting or Phone call.

See Activities for more information.

docs.title: Mailings tab
docs.text: The Mailings tab is visible only if Enable CiviMail to create activites on delivery is unselected at Administer > CiviMail > CiviMail Component Settings. In that case, each bulk email is recorded on the Mailings tab rather than the Activities tab. This improves how quickly the Activities tab loads if your organisation sends bulk email to large mailing lists.

docs.title: Contributions tab
docs.text:
