Update a smart group's saved search when you need it to include different contacts. For example, you might expand a group of current members to include new members.

  1. Click Manage Groups.
  2. Click Settings next to the smart group whose criteria you want to change.

  1. On the group settings screen, click Edit Smart Group Criteria at the bottom left.

  1. On the screen showing the search results, click the bar at the top to display the group's criteria.
  2. Update the criteria.
  3. When you are happy with the results, select all records.
  4. From the Actions list, choose Update Smart Group.

The smart group is now based on the new criteria.

docs.title: Override smart group membership
docs.text: Manually add or remove a contact when you need an exception to a smart group's criteria. By default, those criteria determine membership, but a manual addition or removal overrides them even if the contact's eligibility later changes.

docs.title: Add a contact
docs.text: Use the same workflow you would use to add a contact to a standard group.

docs.title: Remove a contact
docs.text:
The Groups tab on a contact record does not offer the Remove button for a smart group in the way it does for a standard group. To remove the contact manually:

  1. Go to Contacts > Manage Groups.
  2. Select Contacts in the right-hand column of the smart group to view its current contacts.
  3. Check the box next to the contact you want to remove.
  4. From Actions, select Group - remove contacts.
  5. Confirm the removal.

The group record then appears under Past Groups on that contact's record.

docs.title: Return a removed contact to criteria-based membership
docs.text: Once a contact has been removed, their smart group record has a Delete option under the Groups tab on their contact record. Delete that record if you want the contact to be included in the smart group again according to its criteria.

docs.title: How smart groups work
docs.text:
Learn how CiviCRM uses saved search criteria to maintain groups of contacts, and how those groups can be used.

A smart group is a saved search. For example, you could create one for all members based in Europe. When you ask to see the contacts in the group, CiviCRM shows contacts who meet the criteria you specified.

docs.title: A membership directory
docs.text:
You can use a smart group with a profile to display a directory of members on your website. The smart group identifies members of your organisation, while the profile specifies which fields appear in the directory. Configure the profile to show only contacts in that smart group.

When a contact becomes a member—for example, by completing a membership form and paying online—they are automatically added to the smart group and published in the directory.

docs.title: An events newsletter
docs.text:
You can create a smart group of people who have registered for or attended an event and designate it as a mailing list. The group is then available in CiviMail for sending an events newsletter. As people register or are marked as having attended, they are automatically added to the group and subscribed to the newsletter.

Smart groups respect subscription preferences. If someone unsubscribes from the newsletter, they are removed from the smart group.

docs.title: Smart group caching
docs.text:
For performance reasons, CiviCRM often caches smart groups: it saves the contacts who meet the criteria for a period of time rather than running the search every time the group is used. The speed improvement may be small for a simple search involving few contacts, but significant or necessary for a complex search involving many contacts.

Caching means a change may take up to 5 minutes to appear in a smart group. In newer versions of CiviCRM, the default smart group query cache timeout is 5 minutes. You can adjust the timeout in Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences.

When a group is accessed, CiviCRM checks whether its cached results are older than the timeout allows. If they are, CiviCRM rebuilds the group and resets the expiry to now + cache timeout setting. Setting the timeout to 0 turns off the cache.

docs.title: Review petition signatures and results
docs.text: You can see who has signed a petition, work with those contacts and review petition results in an Activity Report.

docs.title: View signatures
docs.text:
1. Go to Campaign > Dashboard > Petitions.
  2. Click More > Signatures next to your petition’s name.
  3. View an individual’s petition activity, or select contacts to send them an email or perform a batch update via profile.

docs.title: Review results with an Activity Report
docs.text:
Use an Activity Report to review all or some of a petition’s results.

  1. Go to Reports > Create Reports from Templates > Activity Report.
  2. In Display Column, select the fields you want to see, such as Target Contact Email.
  3. Expand Petition Questions and select the criteria you want to see, such as specific responses to a petition question.
  4. Click Preview Report to view the results.

You can also export the survey report information to a CSV file for more detailed reporting.

docs.title: Share a petition for signing
docs.text:
Use your petition’s signing URL to invite existing contacts or visitors to your website to sign it.

  1. Go to Campaigns > Dashboard > Petitions to view, manage or edit your petitions.

  1. Click More > Sign next to your petition’s name. Your petition opens.
  2. Copy the URL. You can email the link to your existing contacts or add it to your website.

People who follow the link can complete the form, answer its questions and submit a response.

After they click Sign the Petition, they see a message prompting them to check their email and verify their email address.

docs.title: Review petition signatures and results
docs.text: You can see who signed a petition and use an Activity Report to review all or some of its results.

docs.title: View signatories
docs.text:
1. Click Campaign > Dashboard > Petitions.
  2. Click More > Signatures next to the name of your petition.

docs.title: Review results with an Activity Report
docs.text:
1. Go to Reports > Create Reports from Templates > Activity Report.
  2. In the Display Column area, select the fields you want to view, such as Target Contact Email.
  3. Expand the Petition Questions area and select the criteria you want to see, such as specific responses to a petition question.
  4. Click Preview Report to view the results.

You can also export the survey report information to a CSV file for more detailed reporting of the results.

docs.title: Set up a petition
docs.text:
Set the permissions for signers, create profiles to collect their information and responses, then create your petition.

Before you begin, enable the CiviCampaign component. You cannot use Petition without it. See Campaign.

docs.title: Set CMS permissions
docs.text:
Set permissions for the roles that need to sign the petition. For a public petition, grant them to anonymous and authenticated users (“Guest” in Joomla! or “Subscriber” in WordPress).

  1. Open your Drupal, Joomla!, or WordPress Access Control page from Administer > Users and Permissions > Permissions (Access Control).
  2. Grant Sign CiviCRM Petition, Profile Create, and Access all Custom Data to the required roles.

docs.title: Create two custom profiles
docs.text:
You need one profile to collect each signer's contact information and another to collect responses to petition questions. Responses are recorded in an activity record of type Petition for each person who signs.

The contact profile must collect at least an email address. Petition sends signers an email prompting them to verify their address, and only verified email addresses can be counted.

  1. At Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles, create a contact profile with the fields you want to collect, such as First Name, Last Name, and Email. You may want to require some fields so you have enough information to communicate with signers later.
  2. At Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Custom Fields, create a set of custom fields for responses to the petition questions. Select Activities from Used For and Petition Signature for Activity Type.
  3. At Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles, create a profile for the petition responses. Select Activity from the Field Name drop-down menu, then select the custom fields you created.

If you choose Allow Duplicate Contact to be Created, you will need to periodically dedupe records. For both profiles, you may want to use these Advanced Setting options:

  • Drupal user account registration option?: Select No account create option if you do not want a Drupal account created for every petition signer.
  • What to do upon duplicate match: Select Allow Duplicate Contact to be Created if you do not want anonymous users to update an existing contact record's information.

For more on custom field sets, see Creating Custom Fields in Organising Your Data. For more on profiles, see Profiles.

docs.title: Create the petition
docs.text:
Once both profiles are ready:

  1. Go to Campaigns > New Petition.
  2. Enter the petition details:
  3. Petition Title (required): The name of your petition.
  4. Introduction: Text explaining the petition to potential signers and encouraging them to sign.
  5. Campaign: If the petition is a strategy or activity within a campaign, select that campaign.
  6. Contact Profile (required): The profile that collects signers' contact information.
  7. Activity Profile: The profile that collects petition responses.
  8. Is Active?: Check this box to make the petition active.
  9. Is Default?: Check this box to make the petition default.
  10. Click Save to save the petition information.

docs.title: What is CiviPetition?
docs.text:
CiviPetition is a CiviCampaign function for creating online petitions that publicly gather responses and information. A petition can collect signatures for a cause, gather answers to questions, or do both.

Petitions are often used to show support for a cause to an elected official or to educate people about an issue. They can also work as online surveys when you do not know who will respond—for example, when anyone can submit a response through a petition on your organisation’s website. Analysing those responses can help your organisation build support for its cause.

docs.title: Example: a City Council petition
docs.text:
Townsville Organisation for Tenants (TOFT) wanted to show Townsville City Council how satisfied or dissatisfied the public was with its work to provide safe public housing. TOFT created a petition that gathered answers to questions alongside signatures, then presented the results to the City Council.

A staff member created the petition in CiviCampaign and emailed it to TOFT’s existing contacts. She also linked it from the organisation’s website so the community could respond online. Working with the Communications Director, she used communication strategies to encourage people to visit the website and complete the petition.

Respondents could choose whether to receive email updates about the campaign’s progress throughout the year. After the petition drive, the staff member compiled the electronic signatures and responses and created reports to analyse the results. TOFT communicated the results to the City Council and used them to shape its messages, tell its story and build interest in the campaign.

docs.title: How petitions work
docs.text: This page explains how petitions use campaigns, profiles and permissions, and what to consider when planning one.

docs.title: Petitions and campaigns
docs.text:
Petitions are a feature of CiviCampaign. They are essentially online surveys: when someone responds to a petition, CiviCRM creates a Petition activity record containing their answers to the petition questions.

A petition does not have to be connected to a campaign. For example, if the Toft Organisation For Tenants (TOFT) used a petition to assess members’ satisfaction with TOFT’s website, it probably would not need to connect it to a campaign.

The petition described in the previous chapter is part of TOFT’s Demand for Better Housing campaign, which also includes a survey and other activities. Connecting that petition to the campaign enabled staff to analyse its responses alongside the campaign’s other strategies and activities.

docs.title: Profiles and custom fields
docs.text:
When a site visitor signs a petition, CiviCRM saves a contact and creates an activity. Profiles display the fields for each:

  • The contact profile collects information about the signer. It is required and must include an email address field. Email addresses are needed to validate and accurately verify submissions and count signatures, particularly so that multiple submissions from one person are not counted.
  • The activity profile can collect information specific to the petition signature.

To ask questions on a petition, you first need custom fields to store the answers. You then create the profiles and select them when you create the petition. For more information, see Creating Custom Fields and Profiles in Organising Your Data.

docs.title: CMS permissions
docs.text: You need to set permissions that allow specific roles to Sign CiviCRM Petitions. See Set-up for the permissions you need to allow.

docs.title: Questions to consider
docs.text:
Before creating a petition, consider how people will find it and what your organisation will do after they sign:

  • Do you plan to send the petition by email?
  • Will you link to it on your website?
  • Will you use social media or offline strategies to bring people to your website to sign?
  • How will you frame your message so that people want to sign?
  • What will you do with the petition results?
  • What follow-up activities will help you continue communicating and build relationships with signers?

docs.title: Enter pledge payments in a batch
docs.text: Use Batch Data Entry when you have many pledge payments to record. Its grid lets you enter payments, use the ‘autocopy’ icons at the top of columns to fill in values, and check the total amount and item count against your deposit slip(s).

docs.title: Create the batch
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Batch Data Entry.
  2. Select New Data Entry Batch.
  1. Enter the batch details:
Field What to enter Batch Name CiviCRM supplies a default of “Batch N” plus the open date. You can edit it. Required. Type Select Payment Type Pledge Payment to show the appropriate reserved profile in the batch entry grid. Not required. Description A description of the batch. Not required. Number of Items The total number of payment items in the batch. Required. Total Amount The total amount of all payment items in the batch. Required.

After saving the batch information, the batch data entry screen opens.

To Edit or Delete batch information, return to the Bulk Data Entry screen and click Edit or Delete next to the batch.

docs.title: Enter payments
docs.text:
The grid supports pledge payments made by check, cash, EFT and other payment instruments. Enter a payment on each line.

Field What to enter or expect Contact Start typing an existing contact’s name and select it from the suggested names. Alternatively, use the “-create new contact-“ drop-down to select New Individual, New Organization, or New Household, then enter the contact’s details in the window that opens. Open Pledges Click the down arrow to see the contact’s open pledges. Assign the payment to any open (pending) pledge. Type The Financial Type; it pre-fills when you select an open pledge. Amount Pre-fills when you select an open pledge. With the appropriate permissions, you can change the amount or schedule by clicking adjust payment amount next to Amount. (Payment) Status Defaults to Completed. Received – Date and Time Pre-fills with the current date and can be edited. Source Enter text describing the source of the payment. Paid by Enter the payment instrument, such as cash, check or EFT. Required. Check Number Fill in if the payment was made by check. Send Receipt Check the box if you want to send an email receipt. Invoice ID Soft Credit Soft Credit Type

If the grid profile includes contact information such as a phone number or email address, those values are populated for an existing contact and can be updated.

docs.title: Save or process the batch
docs.text:
You can enter all transactions in one session or save the batch and finish later. To continue later:

  1. Click Save & Continue Later.
  2. When you return, go to Contributions > Batch Data Entry.
  3. Click Enter Records next to the batch.
  4. Continue entering or editing its transactions.

Once you have finished entering payments, click Validate & Process the Batch. The batch status becomes Closed, and the batch is available for searches and reporting.

If the item count or total amount differs from the values entered when the batch was created, CiviCRM alerts you when closing it. Choose one of these options:

  • Continue entering or editing payments, then click Validate & Process the Batch again.
  • Click Ignore Mismatch & Process the Batch? to update the batch values to match its transactions and set its status to Closed.

docs.title: Cancel a pledge
docs.text:
Cancel a pledge when it will not be fulfilled.

  1. Find the pledge through its contact record or the Find Pledges search tool.
  2. Click more to the right of the pledge.
  3. Click Cancel.

docs.title: Record an offline pledge payment
docs.text:
Record a payment manually when a donor pays a pledge by an offline method, such as cash or cheque.

  1. Find the donor’s contact record using Search >> Find Contacts.
  2. Open the Pledges tab.
  3. Click the small view payments arrow at the far left of the pledge table to show the scheduled pledge payments.
  4. Find the next scheduled Pledge Payment and record it as Completed.

You can also Edit a Scheduled Payment to change its due date or amount.

docs.title: Pledge reports and templates
docs.text:
Use this page to identify the available reports for analysing pledges and the templates you can use to create your own.

Report or template What it provides Pledge Detail Report Per-contact information, including amount pledged, pledge status, next payment date, balance due and total amount paid. This report is based on the Pledge Report template. Pledged But not Paid report Pledges that are not completed and have a due date in the past. This report is based on the Pledged But not Paid template. Pledge Summary Report template Can be used to create a report summarising total pledge amounts by, for example, city or month of initial pledge.

The two reports are configured to display particular information. You can create a new report from the relevant template to suit your needs. See Reporting Set-up for details.

docs.title: Enable pledges on an online contribution page
docs.text:
You can let donors pledge future donations through a CiviContribute form, choose how often they will donate, and receive reminders of their commitment.

Some payment processors do not support automated pledge payments, and payments may arrive by non-electronic methods such as cheques. You can still record future income against a current source, such as an event or email campaign. When a payment arrives, you can manually change its status from Pending to Complete if the payment method does not support this automatically.

docs.title: Enable the pledge option
docs.text:
Before you begin, create a contribution page if you do not already have one.

  1. Open the contribution page’s settings.
  2. Go to the Amounts tab.
  3. Tick Pledges. The pledge options appear.

docs.title: Choose pledge options
docs.text:
Set the options you want to offer on the form:

  • Supported pledge frequencies: Choose whether donors can pledge daily, weekly, monthly or annual donations.
  • Allow frequency intervals: Let donors specify a gap between payments, such as once every 5 days, 5 weeks, 5 months or 5 years.
  • Send payment reminder: Enter how many days before a scheduled payment the donor should receive a reminder, for example by email.
  • Send up to: Set the maximum number of reminders a donor can receive for one scheduled payment.
  • Send additional reminders: Set the number of days between reminders.
  • Allow other amounts: Let donors choose their own pledge amount. You can also set minimum and maximum payment amounts.
  • Fixed Contribution Options: Enter up to ten fixed contribution amounts in the table. The form displays them as radio button options, showing both the label and dollar amount.

When you have finished, choose Save, Save and Done, Save and Next or Cancel. Once pledges are enabled, the option to make a pledge appears on the online form.

To check and monitor current pledges, use the available reports or go to Contributions > Pledges > Dashboard. For more about pledges, including creating them internally on behalf of constituents rather than through an online form, see the Pledges chapter.

docs.title: What is CiviPledge?
docs.text:
CiviPledge helps your organisation keep track of a donor’s promise to give and the payments made towards it.

A pledge is a promise to give a donation at a pre-arranged time in the future. The donor may give the full amount at once or pay at regular intervals until they reach the total. For example, Sally pledges $3000 over five years, with monthly payments of $50.

Donors can make a pledge through an online Contribution Form (see Contributions), or an internal user can make one on their behalf. The pledge links the individual contributions together, but payments are handled separately: either manually, such as by cheque, or automatically through a Payment Processor.

If a donor misses a payment, the pledge status can be updated accordingly. Email reminders can also be set to go out automatically at specified intervals before payments are due.

docs.title: Find and review pledges
docs.text: Use the pledge search to locate individual records, or open the dashboard to see recent pledges and summary figures.

docs.title: Find a pledge
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Pledges > Find Pledges.
  2. Search by Pledger Name, Email Address or a pledge detail such as Payment Start Date, Pledge Status or Honoree information.

The results show a summary of matching pledges. Each row has View, Edit and Delete options. If a pledge’s Status is “in progress” or “Pending”, it also has a Cancel option.

docs.title: View the dashboard
docs.text: Go to Contributions > Pledges > Dashboard to see recent pledges and a summary table of pledges recorded over the current month and past year.

docs.title: Create a pledge
docs.text: Use New Pledge to record a constituent’s promise to donate, choose a payment schedule and, if needed, set up reminders or online payments.

docs.title: Enable CiviPledge
docs.text:
Before using CiviPledge, you must enable it for your installation if it is not already enabled.

  1. Go to Administer > System Settings > Enable CiviCRM Components.
  2. Select the CiviPledge checkbox.
  3. Click Save.

docs.title: Enter the pledge
docs.text:
1. Go to Contributions > Pledges > New Pledge.
  2. Enter the pledge details using the fields below.
Field What to enter Pledge by Select contact Type the name of an existing contact, or create a new contact before setting up the pledge. A new window opens when you create a contact. Total Pledge Amount The total amount to be donated. To be paid in The number of instalments and the payment period, if there is more than one instalment. Payments are due on the The day a payment is due in each instalment cycle, such as the second day of the week, month or year. Pledge Made The date the pledge was promised. Payments Start The date scheduled payments will start. Send Acknowledgment? Select this to send a notification email if outgoing mail is configured and the contact has an email address. Acknowledgement Date The date the individual was notified that the pledge was created. This is populated automatically if an email was sent. Financial Type The Financial Type of the contribution, such as Donation or Event Fee, to indicate what the pledged money is for. Campaign If available, the Campaign that the pledged money is intended to support. Self-service Payments Page An online Contribution Form through which the donor can make a payment. Honoree information Details of someone the individual has chosen to dedicate the pledge to. You can also set payment reminders.

An individual can also make a pledge through an online contribution form. See the Contributions section.

docs.title: Set up payment reminders
docs.text:
One or more reminders can be emailed to the donor before a scheduled payment date. Before setting a reminder schedule, check these requirements:

  • The Process Pledges (process_pledge) scheduled job must be enabled to update pledge payment statuses and send reminders. Alternatively, a cron job can be scheduled to run this task separately from other scheduled jobs. See the Scheduled Jobs chapter for more information.
  • The donor must have a valid email address and must not have the “Do Not Email” flag checked.

When creating the New Pledge, choose the reminder schedule using these settings:

Setting What it controls Send Initial Reminder The number of days before the payment date to send the first reminder. Send up to The maximum number of reminders the individual will receive for one scheduled payment. Send additional reminders The number of days between reminders, such as 5 days before the next reminder is sent.

docs.title: Offer online payments
docs.text: A donor can make a scheduled payment online if a Contribution Page with a Payment Processor has been created. When creating the New Pledge, select that page from Self-service Payments Page. If reminders are enabled for the pledge, their emails will include a link to the page.

docs.title: Use configured reports
docs.text: Use reports that have been configured for you to view results, export data, and work with the contacts they return. This page assumes CiviReport is already configured.

docs.title: View a report
docs.text:
1. Go to Reports.
  2. Select the relevant report type.
  3. Click View Results to use the preset criteria, or click the report name to open its criteria settings.

A report opens as a table. Some reports also offer a dropdown menu for viewing results as a bar or pie chart.

Reports can also be configured for direct access from navigation menus. For example, an event report can appear in the Events menu.

You can create a PDF version of a table or graph for printing or emailing.

To use report data in a spreadsheet for further calculations, click Export to CSV. This outputs the data as a comma-separated variable (CSV) file.

If you have the appropriate permissions, you can adjust a report’s criteria and settings while viewing it. See Set-up for details about configuring reports.

docs.title: Put a report on your dashboard
docs.text:
Your dashboard is the first page you see when you log in to CiviCRM. You can configure it yourself, but not all reports may be available to add.

  1. From your dashboard, click Configure Your Dashboard.
  2. Select a report from the list of available reports.
  3. Drag the report onto your dashboard.

docs.title: Add report contacts to a group
docs.text: This option is not available in every report. When a report offers it, choose the group you want to add the returned contacts to from the dropdown menu.

docs.title: External reporting
docs.text:
External reporting can help you work with CiviCRM data in ways that reporting within CiviCRM does not cover.

Reporting within CiviCRM assumes that you want real-time data from your “production” CiviCRM database and that you only want to report on data held in CiviCRM. External tools may be useful if you want to combine CiviCRM data with data from other applications, or create reports, overviews, dashboards or data transformations outside CiviCRM.

Examples of external tools include Metabase, Tableau, Power BI, RapidMiner and Pentaho. These kinds of tools can access CiviCRM data through a direct connection to the MySQL or MariaDB database, or potentially through the CiviCRM API.

How to set up external reporting is outside the scope of this page. If your organisation does not have the necessary skills, contact your CiviCRM experts or whoever supports you with CiviCRM or reporting.

docs.title: CiviReport criteria, settings and permissions
docs.text: Use this reference to check what the available report options do. A report template is a general report that you can customise into a specific report instance and make available to users; the options shown depend on the template.

docs.title: Report criteria
docs.text: Tab Availability What it controls Columns All reports The data displayed for each record. Grouping Summary reports How data is summarised or compared. Sorting Detail reports The order of results. Filters All reports Which records the report includes.

docs.title: Columns
docs.text: Column checkboxes select the data displayed for each record. Most reports require at least one display column that you cannot unselect. In the membership detail report, Contact Name and Membership Type are required.

docs.title: Grouping
docs.text:
Grouping can summarise data instead of displaying every individual row, or compare types of data. For example, you can compare donations per year.

You can select more than one grouping criterion. Results are then nested by both groupings, although not every combination will make sense for your data. You may need to experiment with Group By Columns. Some Groups By Columns cannot be selected at the same time as certain Display Columns; CiviCRM warns you if you make an invalid selection.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text: Sorting is available in some detail reports.

docs.title: Filters and date ranges
docs.text:
Filters determine which records appear. Without filters, the Membership Detail report shows all membership records. You could instead filter it to show members of a particular membership type who joined last year.

Most reports have a date range filter. You can use an absolute range, such as “1st Jan 2010” to “31 July 2010”, or a relative range, such as “Previous Year”.

Relative ranges are useful for reports you run repeatedly:

  • This year includes records from the start of the current year.
  • Previous quarter includes records from the previous quarter.
  • Last 12 months includes records from one year before today through today.

The “Last ...” ranges can be combined with Group By Columns. Combining Ending Year with Group By Month gives a monthly summary for the previous 12 months. The example below shows total contributions received over the past 12 months and each month’s total.

docs.title: Report access and permissions
docs.text:
The Access tab can control who views or edits an individual report. A Reserved Report can be altered only by someone with the Administer Reserved Reports permission. Report access can also be limited to particular ACL roles; see Permissions and Access Control in the Initial Set Up chapter.

Four permissions are specifically associated with reports:

Permission What it allows CiviReport: access CiviReport View the CiviReport menu, but only view reports set with the access CiviReport permission. CiviReport: access Report Criteria Change report search criteria. CiviReport: administer reserved reports Edit all reserved reports. CiviReport: administer reports Manage report templates.

docs.title: Create and manage a CiviReport report
docs.text:
Use a supplied report template to create a report that you can run again and make available to other users. This guide assumes you know why you need the report and that a supplied template can produce it.

If the template you need does not exist, you or your developer can consult creating custom reports in the Developer Guide.

docs.title: Create a report from a template
docs.text:
1. Open Administer > CiviReport > Create new report from templates. Templates are grouped by component, with a brief description of each intended use. If a template already has report instances, you will see an Existing Reports link.

  1. Select a report template by clicking its name. The configuration screen opens.

  2. Choose the report criteria on the available tabs. Columns and Filters are available in all reports; summary reports may offer Grouping, and detail reports may offer Sorting. The choices depend on the template. See CiviReport criteria, settings and permissions for what these options do.

  3. Click Preview Report. Check the results and adjust the criteria if needed. You may need to preview and revise the report several times. The report settings tabs appear only after you preview the report.

docs.title: Set up and save the report
docs.text:
1. On Title and Format, enter a title and description that help others understand the report, such as “Student members joined so far this year”.

Each report includes a standard HTML header and footer, shown at the beginning and end of PDF or downloaded versions. To display the actual report title, replace “CiviCRM Report” between < title> and < /title>. You can add a logo with an < img> tag or change the printed report’s appearance with a custom CSS file instead of print.css.

  1. If you want regular email delivery, use Email Delivery to fill in Subject, To and CC. Separate multiple addresses in To or CC with commas.

Email delivery requires a scheduled task: enable Mail Reports (mail_report) to send report emails. Alternatively, you can schedule a cron job to run this task separately from other scheduled jobs. The scheduled job configuration specifies the report instance and, optionally, the format. See Scheduled Jobs.

  1. On Access, choose whether to place another link to the report in the navigation menu. All reports are included in Report > Report listing. If you check Include Report in Navigation Menu?, the Parent Menu field appears so you can choose where the additional link goes.

Choose View Results to open the results page—for example, for a report using a relative date filter such as “Number of new contributors last calendar month”. Choose Show Criteria to let someone change the criteria before running the report.

  1. On Access, set who can view or edit the report if needed. Report-by-report permissions can simplify the interface for junior users or restrict sensitive reports. For example, you might select “access CiviContribute” for a contribution report so that only people who can see contribution data can access it. Alternatively, you can limit access to particular ACL roles. See Permissions and Access Control in the Initial Set Up chapter.

  2. If appropriate, check Available for Dashboard?. Users with the right permissions can then add the report by clicking Configure Your Dashboard on their dashboard.

  3. Click Create Report when the criteria and settings are correct. The report appears in Reports > All Reports and in any navigation menu you selected on Access.

docs.title: Change or copy a report
docs.text:
To permanently change an existing report’s criteria, open the report, make your changes, then click Update Report.

To keep the existing report and create another with different filters, open it, change the filters, then click Save a Copy.... Enter a new title and description when prompted. For example, you might keep an Event Income Summary report covering all events for an events manager and make a copy showing only Fundraiser events for a fundraising manager.

docs.title: What is CiviReport?
docs.text:
CiviReport helps your organisation use information about contacts and their interactions to evaluate its impact, meet reporting requirements and make decisions. Reports can be useful to funders and other stakeholders as well as to your own staff.

A report queries the CiviCRM database using the criteria and fields available in a report template. You can create, run and schedule reports. Results can appear on the page when you run a report, in a dashlet on the dashboard, or in a scheduled email that can include a CSV file or PDF.

docs.title: Following up with previous donors
docs.text:
1two3, a support organisation for street workers, launched a capital campaign for a new shelter. Anne, its development director, wanted to contact people who had made a large donation last year but had not given money this year.

Anne created an instance of the LYBUNT report (“Last year but unfortunately not this”) and filtered it to show people who gave more than €500 last year. She ran the report, then used Add to Group to put those donors in a new group so she could email them about the campaign.

She also added the report to her CiviCRM Dashboard to review progress. Donors who give this year automatically drop off the list because they no longer meet its criteria. Anne can use the remaining list for follow-up phone calls or other personalised contact.

docs.title: Receiving regular financial reports
docs.text:
WAM is an academic membership organisation with about 1,500 members. Members renew online and pay either online by card or offline by direct debit. Mark, its finance officer, needs regular reports to track incoming money; automating them was a key reason WAM implemented CiviCRM.

Mark receives the reports by email with CSV attachments, which he can import into accounting software or an online banking interface. WAM’s requirements were fairly complex, so some reports needed custom report templates alongside the standard ones.

Every Monday morning, Mark receives a report of completed online payments from the previous week for import into Sage. It includes each payment’s amount, time, purpose (membership or event) and reference ID, so he can trace it back to the CiviCRM record.

At the end of each month, he receives a list of members who pay by direct debit and whose memberships are due to expire the following month. He imports part of that list into WAM’s online banking interface to set up direct debit payments for the renewals. These emailed reports save Mark several hours a month, leaving more time for issues that contribute to the effective management of WAM’s financial resources.

docs.title: Seeing contributions across a household
docs.text:
A non-profit organisation in Ohio keeps individual records organised by household. For example, a husband might attend several paid events while his wife registers for other events and makes separate donations.

Staff need to see the total contributions from everyone in a household when someone calls about a family member’s donation or event payment. They can run the Donation Summary Report (Household) as needed, using the household name to find the contributions and other relevant information for the caller.

docs.title: Planning your use of CiviReport
docs.text: This page explains the ideas to consider before configuring CiviReport for daily use. It is intended for system administrators and anyone who wants to understand the thinking behind CiviReport. If you only need to view reports your administrator has already configured, you can skip it.

docs.title: What CiviReport is for
docs.text:
CiviReport can support organisational planning and the analysis of membership or donor development. Reports can have tabular or graphical output, and you can schedule them to be emailed to specific people.

An organisation can ask many different questions about its data. CiviCRM aims to cover 90% of reporting scenarios while allowing administrators and developers to extend it for the remaining 10%.

docs.title: Report templates and reports
docs.text:
A report template is the starting point for any number of reports. CiviCRM includes predefined templates designed to meet basic reporting needs. For example, the Membership Report(Detail) template could be used for one report showing student members who joined in the past quarter and another showing memberships cancelled this year.

Future versions of CiviCRM are likely to include more templates. An organisation can also create a template for its own requirements and contribute it to the CiviCRM community. Writing a new report template requires PHP and SQL skills; see the Developer Guide for details.

docs.title: Reports and searches
docs.text:
CiviCRM’s built-in search covers most scenarios. CiviReport is useful when you need to display complex information in an accessible way, particularly when you will ask the same question—or similar questions—repeatedly.

The current report interface does not support most common batch actions, including Update via Batch Profile and Smart Group creation. If you need to act on a result set, use a search rather than a report.

Reports and searches have different strengths. Reports can be more flexible in some cases: you can change the columns displayed and, in summary reports, order by whichever displayed results you choose.

docs.title: Ways to use a report
docs.text:
• Run it once: Use Print Report to view it in a browser, generate a PDF, or Export to CSV. Each option runs the report when you select it.
  • Show it on a dashboard: If you make a report Available for Dashboard, users with appropriate permissions can add it to their dashboard. The report runs each time the dashboard loads. This can be useful for regular updates, such as new members or donations this month.
  • Email it on a schedule: For example, a finance office could receive a monthly report of event fees received, or a membership administrator could receive a weekly report of overdue renewals.

docs.title: Detail and summary reports
docs.text: Reports often come in pairs: one shows a summary and the other shows the detail. The reports can be linked so that someone can see information at a glance and then drill down for more detail.

docs.title: Questions to consider
docs.text:
Before configuring reports, consider:

  • Would a report serve this task better than a search?
  • Which reports are available? The list is growing. For the complete list in your version, and an explanation of how the reports can be used, see Create reports from templates in the Reports dropdown menu.
  • What do you need to learn from your data—for example, how many new members joined during a period or how much money a fundraising campaign collected?
  • Which fields do you need?
  • Does the report offer enough options, or will you need to analyse the results further in a spreadsheet?
  • Is this a one-off question or one you will ask regularly? Could a report template streamline future reports?
  • Who needs to see the report? Does it contain sensitive information that should be limited to privileged users, or useful daily updates for everyone?

The relevant component sections in the rest of this book describe available report templates and compare them with searches.

docs.title: Additional filter patterns
docs.text: The code supports adding more filters for some patterns through the API or at civicrm/admin/options/relative_date_filters. Adding other patterns is generally “patch-welcome”; the hardest part is defining what a new pattern means and how it relates to the others.

docs.title: ending
docs.text:
The ending prefix counts backwards from now. If you use it in the middle of a month, the filter starts partway through the relevant month. For example, the source describes a filter used on the 15th as starting on the 16th of the relevant month.

docs.text:

docs.title: Search result actions
docs.text:
Use this page to check what you can do with selected search results. The Action options vary by the type of record you searched for: a Contact search and a Contribution search, for example, offer different options.

For contact searches, select one or more results before you choose an Action. This applies whether you used Quick Search, Advanced Search, SearchKit, or Find Contacts.

docs.title: Contact Search actions
docs.text:
These Action options appear for Contact entity searches.

  • Add activity — Add an Activity to the selected contact records.
  • Communication preferences - alter — Add or remove communication preferences. For example, selecting No bulk emails (User Opt Out) automatically excludes a contact from future email communications sent from CiviCRM. Learn more about Communication Preferences.

  • Dedupe - Merge 2 Contacts — Merge contact data, such as addresses, phone numbers and email addresses. You can also choose to move all or some related records, such as groups, contributions and memberships. This option is unavailable if you select more than two contacts. Learn more about Deduping and Merging Contacts.
  • Delete Contacts — Delete contacts without permanently removing them from CiviCRM. If you delete contacts by mistake, you can find them in the trash through Advanced Search and restore them. Learn more about deleting and restoring contacts.
  • Download Spreadsheet — Choose a file format and download the columns enabled in your search.

  • Email - schedule/send via CiviMail — Compose and send a mass mailing to two or more selected contacts. In the next step, you can add or exclude other groups of contacts. Learn more about CiviMail.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) — Send email to selected contacts. Contacts with Do Not Email set, or without a valid email address on file, will not receive it.
  • Email - unhold addresses — Remove Hold from email addresses in bulk. While an address is on Hold, no further email is sent to it unless someone fixes the address and removes the hold.
  • Export Contacts — Export a predefined set of fields (an export mapping), or create a mapping that you can save for reuse. The export is a CSV file that you can open in standard spreadsheet software or use directly for mail merges. Learn more about Exporting Contacts.
  • Group - add contacts — Add contacts to an existing group or create a new group. Learn more about Groups.
  • Group - remove contacts — Choose an existing group from which to remove contacts in bulk.
  • Mailing labels - print — Choose a label format from the dropdown list to generate labels for bulk postal communication. Learn more about postal mailings in CiviCRM.
  • Print/merge document — Create merge letters using tokens for database fields. You can save a letter as a template and output it as PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt). Learn more about Print/Merge Documents.
  • Profile Update — Update multiple contacts of the same basic type, such as all Individuals or all Organizations.
  • Tag - Add/Remove Tags — Add or remove existing tags. You cannot create a new tag from this action. Learn more about Tags.
  • Update Contacts — Choose the data fields to update. Changes apply to every selected contact.

docs.title: Contribution Search actions
docs.text:
These Action options appear for Contribution entity searches.

  • Delete contributions — Permanently delete the selected contributions and all associated transactions and activity. This cannot be undone.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) — Send email to fewer than 50 recipients. If you do not need to track opens or link clicks, this is quicker and easier than a CiviMail mass mailing. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export contributions — Export a predefined set of fields (an export mapping), or create a mapping that you can save for reuse. The export is a CSV file that you can open in standard spreadsheet software or use directly for mail merges.
  • Printing selected rows — Print the selected search results. You must have a printer connected to your device.
  • Receipts - print or email — Email receipts to contributors, or click Process Receipt(s) to download a PDF with one receipt per page.

  • Record payments for contributions — Record payments only for contributions with Pending status. Selecting contributions with another status produces an error message in the upper-right of the screen.

  • Thank-you letters - print or email — Email thank-you letters from CiviCRM or create PDF merge letters for the selected contacts. Learn more about Print/Merge Documents.
  • Update multiple contributions — Edit Contribution fields using a Profile that you have created first. To configure one, go to Administer CiviCRM > Customize Data and Screens > CiviCRM Profile. Learn more about using Profiles for updating information.

docs.title: Participant Search actions
docs.text:
These Action options appear for Participant entity searches.

  • Cancel registration — Set a participant’s status to Canceled.
  • Delete participants from event — Permanently delete the selected participations and all associated transactions and activity. This cannot be undone, but it does not delete the participants’ contact records.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) — Send email to fewer than 50 recipients. If you do not need to track opens or link clicks, this is quicker and easier than a CiviMail mass mailing. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export participants — Export a predefined set of fields (an export mapping), or create a mapping that you can save for reuse. The export is a CSV file that you can open in standard spreadsheet software or use directly for mail merges.
  • Group - add contacts — Add contacts to an existing group or create a new group. Learn more about Groups.
  • Group - create smart group — Save search criteria as a smart group. CiviCRM reruns the search using those criteria each time you open the group, which is useful for complex searches you revisit regularly. The group includes all contacts that meet the criteria, even if you selected only a few search results. Learn more about Smart Groups.
  • Name badges print — Choose a badge type to generate a printable PDF with the selected participants’ names. Learn more about Event Badges.
  • PDF letter - print for participants — Create merge letters using tokens for database fields. You can save a letter as a template and output it as PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt). Learn more about Print/Merge documents.
  • Participant status - change — Change participant statuses. Emails are sent when a status changes from the pending class, such as Pending (pay later) or Pending from approval, to Registered or Attended in the positive class. Emails are also sent when a status changes to Expired or Canceled.
  • Print selected rows — Print what is shown on screen for the selected rows.
  • Update multiple participants — Edit multiple fields for multiple participants in a table grid. You must create the Profile you want to use before choosing this action. Learn more about using Profiles for updating information.

docs.title: Activities Search actions
docs.text:
These Action options appear for Activity entity searches.

  • Delete activities — Permanently delete the selected activities. This cannot be undone.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) — Send email to fewer than 50 recipients. If you do not need to track opens or link clicks, this is quicker and easier than a CiviMail mass mailing. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export activities — Export a predefined set of fields (an export mapping), or create a mapping that you can save for reuse. The export is a CSV file that you can open in standard spreadsheet software or use directly for mail merges.
  • Print selected rows — Print what is shown on screen for the selected rows.
  • Print/merge Document — Create merge letters using tokens for database fields. You can save a letter as a template and output it as PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt). Learn more about Print/Merge documents.
  • Tag - add to activities — Add one or more tags to Activity records.
  • Tag - remove from activities — Remove one or more tags from Activity records.
  • Update multiple activities — Edit Activity fields using a Profile that you have created first. Learn more about using Profiles to update multiple activity records.

docs.title: Member Search actions
docs.text:
These Action options appear for Member entity searches.

  • Delete Memberships — Permanently delete the selected memberships and all associated transactions and activity. This cannot be undone.
  • Email - send now (to 50 or less) — Send email to fewer than 50 recipients. If you do not need to track opens or link clicks, this is quicker and easier than a CiviMail mass mailing. Learn more about small group emails.
  • Export members — Export a predefined set of fields (an export mapping), or create a mapping that you can save for reuse. The export is a CSV file that you can open in standard spreadsheet software or use directly for mail merges.
  • Group - create smart group — Save a search that you can use for mailings or as a filter in later searches or reports. The group includes all contacts that meet the search criteria, even if you selected only a few search results. Learn more about Smart Groups.
  • Mailing labels - print — Choose a label format from the dropdown list to generate labels for bulk postal communication. Learn more about postal mailings in CiviCRM.
  • Print selected rows — Print what is shown on screen for the selected rows.
  • Print/merge document for memberships — Create merge letters using tokens for database fields. You can save a letter as a template and output it as PDF, HTML, Word (.docx), or Open Document (.odt). Learn more about Print/Merge documents.
  • Update multiple memberships — Edit Membership fields using a Profile that you have created first. Learn more about using Profiles to update membership information.

docs.title: Find contacts and use search results
docs.text: Use Quick search when you have a contact in mind. Use Advanced Search when you need contacts who meet particular criteria, such as members of a group in a specified country.

docs.title: Find a contact with Quick search
docs.text:
The Quick search box is at the top left of the navigation menu.

  1. Click the Quick search box and type to use the default Name/Email search. To choose another criterion, click the box again and select one from the dropdown list.
  2. Review the matching contacts in the dropdown below the box.
  3. If the contact is not shown, type more characters to refine the search, or press Return to turn it into an Advanced Search.

You often need only the first few letters of a name. If automatic wildcard is enabled in Search Preferences, a Name/Email search for peter can find a person whose first or last name is Peter, a name such as MaryPeterson, an email address such as bluepeter@gmail.com, or an organisation such as Alpeter Community Centre.

Note

For a phone search, enter digits without formatting. The search uses a field from which all non-numeric characters have been removed.

Tip

To search by first and last name, enter Lastname, Firstname—for example, Peterson, Mary, not Mary Peterson.

CiviCRM can store nicknames for contacts: Joe for Joseph, or IBM for International Business Machines. On a new installation, searching for Joe finds Joseph, and searching for IBM finds International Business Machines. The Include Nickname setting in Search Preferences controls this behaviour.

Quick search shows up to 10 results by default. An administrator can change the Autocomplete Results setting under Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences. That page also allows Quick search criteria to be changed, including hiding basic contact fields not normally used in Quick search and adding custom field options.

docs.title: Find contacts with Advanced Search
docs.text:
Advanced Search can search across the information you hold about contacts. Search criteria appear in expandable blue bars, sometimes called “accordions”, for types of data such as addresses, notes, Contributions and Events.

  1. Go to Search > Advanced Search.
  2. Open the section containing the criterion you need. For example, open Demographics to specify a birth date range for people aged 16 to 18.
  3. Enter your criteria and run the search.

By default, using criteria from two categories finds contacts who match both. For example, criteria for advisory group membership and country can find advisory group members in Venezuela.

docs.title: Choose the type of result
docs.text: Advanced Search returns Contact records by default. To return another record type, select it from Display Results As. For example, you could search for people with a Membership renewal activity last week and display the results as Memberships, so you can export names, addresses and Membership expiration dates to create and post membership cards.

docs.title: Work with the results
docs.text:
An Actions box appears above search results. Select all records or specific records, then choose an action. The available actions are described in Search Result Actions.

To see more information about a contact in the results, hover over the contact icon in the left column. The contact summary pop-up displays fields from the Summary Overlay profile, which can be changed under Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Profiles.

docs.title: Search settings and behaviour
docs.text: Use this page to check how CiviCRM interprets criteria and displays results when you work with Advanced Search and other searches.

docs.title: Combining criteria
docs.text:
Search Operator in Search Settings determines whether criteria from different categories are combined with AND or OR. AND is the default. For example, AND finds people in the Volunteers group who also have a Volunteer Training activity; OR finds people who meet either condition.

The way values combine also depends on the control:

  • Multiple checked values within a criterion group are combined with AND. For example, you can search for contacts whose Preferred Communication Method is both Email and SMS.
  • Multiple values selected from a dropdown are always combined with OR. For example, you can find contacts in Alaska or Arizona.

With the default AND operator, selecting the major donor tag and Mexico returns major donors in Mexico, not people who meet only one of those criteria.

A cross at the right end of an expanded section’s header indicates that it has selections in use. Closing the section does not remove its criteria; click the cross to stop using them.

docs.title: Date range filters
docs.text:
Most component searches have a date range filter. You can use:

  • An absolute range, such as 1st Jan 2010 to 31 July 2010.
  • A relative range, such as Previous week.

Relative ranges can find contacts who contributed in the last 7 days (From 1 Week ago), this financial year’s registered Event Participants (This Year), or contacts of a certain age. They are especially useful when saving a search as a Smart Group: an automatically populated group of contacts sharing specified characteristics or activities. See Groups and tags.

Relative date filters based on a “week” assume Sunday is the first day. That differs from the Monday start used in Europe and many countries in the Asia/Pacific region. The first day of the week can be set under Administer > Localization > Date Format.

docs.title: Result views and deleted contacts
docs.text:
The default Advanced Search result columns are Name, Street Address, City, State, Postal Code, Country, Email and Phone. To show a different set—for example, Gender and Date of Birth instead of Country—use a Profile with the Search Views option selected. Its fields must have Expose Publicly and for Listings visibility and be marked as Results Columns. A profile for that example could include birth date, gender and address fields. See Profiles for more about creating profiles.

You can combine a Search View with the Batch Update via Profile action to view and update selected fields across a batch of contact records.

Search in Trash searches contacts that have been deleted but not permanently deleted. Deleting a contact moves the contact and all related data to trash. Only users with the relevant permission can search in trash and restore a contact.

docs.title: Wildcards and capitalisation
docs.text:
The wildcard % represents any characters, including letters, numerals and punctuation. It can appear before, after or within a word. A search for Mich% can find Michael, Michelle, Michał and the misspelling Micheal. A search for Mich%el excludes Michał and Micheal, while still finding Michelle and Michael.

A single % can also return records whose field value is empty, rather than NULL. To find records where a field contains at least one character, use %_%; this excludes empty and NULL values.

Text searches are not case-sensitive. For example, brooklyn can find Brooklyn or BROOKLYN, and mi%el can find a name beginning with an uppercase M.

docs.title: Number of rows
docs.text: Advanced Searches and CiviCRM reports previously displayed 50 rows by default. As of CiviCRM 5.39, System Administrators can change the number shown under Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Search Preferences. A higher number makes the screen slower to load, so avoid setting it too high.

docs.title: Advanced Search limitation
docs.text: Advanced Search cannot correctly filter Activities by Case Type when a contact is the client in more than one Case and has the same Activity Type in each Case. The source describes a future resolution but does not specify a version.

docs.title: URL filters for searches
docs.text:
Some Advanced Search and component search URLs, such as Find Contributions, can be bookmarked with parameters to reopen a search. This page lists parameters described for those searches. URL filtering for SearchKit is covered on the SearchKit interface page and the FormBuilder form page.

A parameterised URL needs reset=1&force=1 after the question mark, followed by supported parameters. The following example works on Drupal with Clean URL support. It searches for contributions from a person with a name like Bob, a contribution source like dad, and a contribution date on or before 01 Jan 2018:

civicrm/contribute/search?reset=1&reset=1&force=1&sort_name=bob&receive_date_high=20180101&contribution_source=dad

The example contains reset=1 twice, as it does in the source.

Date/Time Parameters

Omit the time entirely, as in 20200101, or provide all six time digits, as in 20200101235959.

docs.title: Supported parameters
docs.text:
The following parameters are described as working in a standardised way for contribution searches. Examples and comments retain the source’s parameter spelling where it differs from the field name.

Field Example Comments Min version (where known) sort_name sort_name=bob Sort name is like bob% or %bob%, depending on site configuration.* contribution_source contribution_source=dad Contribution source is like %dad% or dad%.* cancel_reason cancel_reason=dunno Described in the source as “Contribution source like %dunno% or dunno%”.* invoice_number invoice_number_reason=xyz Invoice Number is like %xyz% or xyz%.* The example’s parameter name differs from the field name in the source. contribution_page_id contribution_page_id=1 5.21 PR receive_date_high receive_date_high=20180101132323 Contribution received on or before 01 Jan 2018, 1.23 pm. receive_date_low receive_date_low=20161001 Contribution received on or after 01 Oct

  1. | | | receive_date_relative | receive_date_relative=this.year | Contribution received this year. | | | contribution_cancel_date_high | contribution_cancel_date_high=20180101132323 | Contribution cancelled on or before 01 Jan 2018, 1.23 pm. | | | contribution_cancel_date_low | contribution_cancel_date_low=20161001 | Contribution cancelled on or after 01 Oct

  2. | | | contribution_cancel_date_relative | contribution_cancel_date_relative=this.year | Contribution cancelled this year. | | | event_high | event_high=20190101000000 | Event end date on or before 1 January

  3. | 5.21 PR | | event_low | event_low=20190101000000 | Event Start date on or after 1 January

  4. | 5.21 PR | | event_relative | event_relative=this.year | Event Start Date on or after the start of this year and event end date on or before the end of the year. | 5.21 PR | | participant_registration_date_high | participant_registration_date_high=20190101000000 | Participant Registration Date on or before 1 January

  5. | 5.21 PR | | participant_registration_date_low | participant_registration_date_low=20190101000000 | Participant Registration date on or after 1 January

  6. | 5.21 PR | | participant_registration_date_relative | participant_registration__date_relative=this.year | Participant Registration Date on or after the start of this year and event end date on or before the end of the year. The example has a double underscore, as in the source. | 5.21 PR | | participant_status_id | participant_status_id=1,2 | Participant Status in Registered and Pending Pay Later. | 5.21 PR | | participant_role_id | participant_role_id=1,2 | Participant Role IN (Attendee, Host). | 5.21 PR | | case_start_date_high | case_start_date_high=20190101000000 | Case Start Date on or before 1 January

  7. | 5.21 PR | | case_start_date_low | case_start_date_low=20190101000000 | Case Start Date on or after 1 January

  8. | 5.21 PR | | case_start_date_relative | case_start_date_relative=this.year | Case Start Date on or after the start of this year and on or before the end of the calendar year. | 5.21 PR | | case_end_date_high | case_end_date_high=20190101000000 | Case End Date on or before 1 January

  9. | 5.21 PR | | case_end_date_low | case_end_date_low=20190101000000 | Case End Date on or after 1 January

  10. | 5.21 PR | | case_end_date_relative | case_end_date_relative=this.year | Case End Date on or after the start of this year and on or before the end of the calendar year. | 5.21 PR | | case_type_id | case_type_id=1,2 | Case Type is one of Housing Support or Adult Care Support. | 5.21 PR | | case_status_id | case_status_id=1 | Case Status is Opened. | 5.21 PR | | case_subject | case_subject=test | Case subject is like %test%. | 5.21 PR | | case_deleted | case_deleted=1 | Case is deleted. | 5.21 PR | | case_id | case_id=1 | Case id =

Turning it off can significantly improve performance on large sites, but searching for dad will then find daddy, not grandad.

docs.title: Date formats
docs.text:
• _high and _low fields take an 8- or 14-digit number representing year, month and day, optionally followed by hour, minute and second. For example, 20180921235959 means 21 September 2018 at 23:59:59. Omitting 235959 makes the time midnight.
  • Relative date fields use relative date values. See the list of relative date formats.

docs.title: Choosing a search method
docs.text: CiviCRM offers several ways to find stored information. The right method depends on whether you need a particular contact, records that meet criteria, or information for a report.

docs.title: Why search?
docs.text:
You might search to:

  • Find a specific contact. Quick search can find contacts by name, email address or other characteristics.
  • Find contacts to act on. For example, you might invite an advisory group to a meeting, send renewal reminders to people whose memberships recently expired, or email contacts under 25 in a particular location about a nearby event.
  • Answer an ad-hoc reporting question.

Search results can help with ad-hoc reporting, but searches cannot group results by particular criteria, summarise them or easily produce graphs. For more advanced reporting, see CiviReport.

docs.title: Available search methods
docs.text:
• Quick search helps you find a contact from the box in the navigation menu.
  • Advanced Search offers criteria across contact information and components. It can return contacts or another record type.
  • Full-text Search searches text values across the database’s fields. It can help when you remember words from an activity description but not the contact’s name.
  • Component searches, such as Find Members, Find Participants and Find Contributions, search a component’s data. They work similarly to Advanced Search but return memberships, event registrations and contributions respectively, rather than contacts. Each has its own Action list; see the relevant Component chapter for details. You can also use Advanced Search with Display Results As to find component records using Advanced Search criteria—for example, event attendances by contacts who are also members.
  • Custom searches may be supplied by CiviCRM core or by your organisation’s extensions.
  • SearchKit is more powerful than Advanced Search but requires more technical knowledge. It is intended for site builders and power users. See the SearchKit section for more information about its functionality and reports.

If you are new to CiviCRM, start with Quick search, Advanced Search and component searches.

docs.title: Select results for Search Kit actions
docs.text: After you build a search, select the results you want to act on. The available Action options depend on the entity you searched: for example, Contacts and Contributions have different options.

docs.title: Select results
docs.text:
If you select no results, only Download Spreadsheet appears under Action.

Select one or more results using any of these methods:

  • Select individual results.
  • Click the dark gray box to select all results.
  • Click the dropdown arrow at the upper-left of the results list to select all results, all results on the page, or no results.

Once you select results, more Action options become available. See Search Result Actions for descriptions of the primary actions available for each entity.

docs.title: Link to a filtered Search Form
docs.text: You can configure a Search Form page to take filter values from its URL. This lets you link to a filtered view, including from another search form using tokens in the Link URL field.

docs.title: Add a URL filter
docs.text:
1. Edit the form with its search display tab selected.
  2. In the left-side panel, find Filters and select a field, such as Hair color.
  3. Select URL.
  4. Enter a codename, such as haircolor.

If the field you want is missing, add it to the Search first. You can get the exact field name needed by adding the filter in the form setup.

Append the codename and value to the form page URL. For example:

https://your.example.org/civicrm/path/to/your/searchformpage/#?haircolor=brown

For multiple URL filters, add subsequent values like this:

#?haircolor=brown&hairlength=short

If the Search already filters a field—for example, to receive dates before this week—a URL filter narrows the results further rather than replacing the existing filter.

docs.title: Use a pseudoconstant field
docs.text:
A : in a field name indicates a pseudoconstant: an underlying database value, generally a number, maps to a name and label. For example, payment_instrument_id is a number. If you know the number, you can use payment_instrument_id=1 in the URL; you can also use payment_instrument_id:name=Cash.

The name variant is more readable and discoverable. It is also useful when you work with multiple sites: ID numbers are likely to differ between sites, while the name is fixed.

docs.title: Use a date value
docs.text:
These date filter formats are accepted:

  • receive_date=2021-09-23
  • receive_date=20210923
  • receive_date=20210923234040 (time: 23:40:40)
  • receive_date=this.month (see the list of relative date formats)

docs.title: Filter multiple fields with one value
docs.text:
You can use one URL value to filter a set of fields. Add a hidden field to the form, use Combine multiple fields to add the other fields, then copy the resulting field name from the Markup tab into your URL.

For example, add the first name field as a hidden field and use Combine multiple fields to add the last name field. You can then filter both fields at once by appending #/?first_name,last_name=foo to the form URL.

docs.title: Create a Search Form for a SearchKit display
docs.text:
You can use FormBuilder to make a SearchKit display available to users. Start from SearchKit or from an existing saved search in FormBuilder.

A Search Form requires a SearchKit saved search. If you are starting in SearchKit, you can create a SearchKit entity table or reuse an existing one.

docs.title: Start from SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Create or open a SearchKit entity table.
  2. Enter an appropriate name for the search and click Save.

After a successful save, Forms and View Results appear on the right.

  1. Click Forms. You will see existing FormBuilder forms and a button to create a new form using the saved search.
  2. Click the button to create a new form. The FormBuilder editor opens.

docs.title: Start from FormBuilder
docs.text:
Use this route if the SearchKit entity table already exists.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > FormBuilder.
  2. Open the Search Forms tab. It lists existing Search Forms and provides an option to create one.
  3. Click New Search. A dropdown of existing SearchKit saved searches appears.
  4. Select the search you want. The FormBuilder editor opens.

docs.title: Configure the form
docs.text:
The editor has a configuration pane on the left and a layout pane on the right.

In the configuration pane, set the form options that you need:

  • Title is required and visible on the form.
  • Description is highly recommended for clarity.
  • Permission determines who can access the form.
  • URL is where the form will be found. It must start with civicrm/.
  • A checkbox controls whether the form is accessible from the website front end.
  • A checkbox adds the form to the navigation menu.
  • Placement can make the form available in the Contact Layout editor, the dashlets interface, a Contact summary tab or block, or through tokens.

The layout pane contains a placeholder for the SearchKit display, fields you can expose as form filters, and options for hidden filters.

docs.title: Find contacts with multiple relationships of the same type
docs.text: Use SearchKit to list contacts with more than one, or another chosen number of, relationships of the same type. For example, a children’s summer camp could find contacts with more than one child and use the results as a mailing list for enrollment discounts to multi-child families.

docs.title: Set up the search
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Search > SearchKit.
  2. Click New Search.
  3. Ensure Contacts is selected as the primary entity to search for.
  4. Add a new entity by selecting With (required) and Contact Related Contacts.
  5. Click +Group By.
  6. Group by both Contact ID and Relationship Type.

docs.title: Count the relationships
docs.text:
1. Below the search criteria, click +Add and select Contact Related Contacts: Relationship.
  2. To show the relationship type in the results, optionally add Contact Related Contacts: Relationship from contact. This can be helpful if your search includes more than one relationship type.
  1. Open Field Transformations, just below the Having drop-down list.
  2. Select Count as the transformation for Relationship.

docs.title: Filter and save the results
docs.text:
1. Under Having, select (Count) Contact Related Contact: Relationship from the Select field* drop-down list.
  2. Select greater than (>).
  3. Enter 1 in the field to the right of the symbol.
  4. Click Search to view contacts with more than one relationship of the same type.
  5. Name your search and save it.

docs.title: Show employees’ event attendance on an Organization contact record
docs.text: Use SearchKit and FormBuilder to add a tab showing events attended by an Organization’s employees.

docs.title: Create the saved search
docs.text:
1. Go to Search > SearchKit.
  2. On the Submission Forms tab, click New Search.
  3. Enter Events Attended By Employees as the search title.

docs.title: Configure the search
docs.text:
1. On the Search For tab, click + Entity and choose Contact Related Contacts.
  2. Change the entity to With (required).
  3. Set Relationship to Contact to Employee of.
  4. Click + Entity and choose Contact Related Contacts - Contact Participants.
  5. Change that entity to With (required).

  6. Click + Entity and choose **Contact Related Contacts

  7. Contact Participants

  8. Participant Event**.
  9. Change that entity to With (required).
  10. On the Select Fields tab, use the x symbol to remove Contact ID, Sort Name, Contact Type and Contact Subtype. Leave Event Title selected.
  11. Use + Add Field to add these fields:
  12. Contact related contacts
  13. Contact Participants
  14. Participant Event
  15. Start Date
  16. Contact related contacts
  17. First Name
  18. Contact related contacts
  19. Last Name
  20. Contact related contacts
  21. Primary Email

docs.title: Add the table display
docs.text:
1. Click + Add at the lower left of the screen and choose Table.
  2. Give the table a name. This name appears as the tab title on the contact record.

  3. Click Sorting and choose Contact related contacts

  4. Contact Participants

  5. Participant Event
  6. Start Date.
  7. Change the sort order to Descending.
  8. Click Columns > Use Custom Columns.
  9. Use the down arrow on Event Title to change its Header text to Event Name.
  10. Use the down arrow on Start Date to change its Header text to Event Date.
  11. Click Save at the top of the screen.

docs.title: Create the form
docs.text:
1. Click Forms at the top right of the page.
  2. Choose Create form for Events Attended By Employees. FormBuilder opens in a new browser tab.
  3. In the configuration pane on the left, set Title to Events Attended By Employees.
  4. Set Placement to Contact Summary Tab.
  5. Set Contact Type to Organization.
  6. Click Save at the top of the screen.

On an Organization contact record with employees who have attended an event, their attendance appears in a new tab. The tab title is the name you gave the table display; in this example, Events Attended By Employees.

docs.title: Build a donor-member invitation list
docs.text: You will create a search for current members who have donated at least a chosen amount and have no participant record, then download the results as a CSV file.

docs.title: Start with current members
docs.text:
You can start with Contacts and link Memberships, or start with Memberships and link Contacts. Because the result needs to be a list of contacts, this example starts with Contacts. Search for cannot be changed after you save the search.

  1. On the SearchKit page, click New Search.
  2. Select Contacts from Search for.

  1. Change With (optional) to With (required).
  2. Select Memberships from +Entity.
  3. Under Where, set Status to is one of New and Current.
  4. Enter a name for the search.
  5. Click Save.

The search now includes contacts with memberships in the selected statuses. You can click Search to preview the results.

docs.title: Exclude contacts with participant records
docs.text:
To find members who have never attended an event in this example, exclude contacts with a participant record.

  1. Change a second With (optional) field to Without.
  2. Select Contact Participants.

The search now excludes contacts with participant records.

docs.title: Include donors
docs.text:
1. Change a third With (optional) field to With (required).
  2. Select Contact Contributions as the entity.
  3. Under Where, set Financial Type = Donation.

A contact may have multiple donations. To list each contact only once, select Contact ID from Group By.

Group By enables Field Transformations such as combine, count and sum. To show each contact’s total contribution amount:

  1. Click +Add to add a column to the search results.
  2. Select Total Amount.
