  3. Under Field Transformation, select Sum next to the Total Amount field.

docs.title: Set the major-donor threshold
docs.text:
A condition on a summed amount belongs under Having, rather than Where, because it uses a Field Transformation.

  1. Under Having, set (Sum) Contact Contibution to greater than or equal to your chosen amount.

The results now include only donors who meet that amount.

docs.title: Add contact details
docs.text:
Not every contact has an email address or phone number in the database. Use With (optional) when adding these entities so the search can include contacts without those details.

  1. Add the contact’s primary email as an entity.
  2. Add the contact’s primary phone number as an entity.

The configured results will likely look something like this:

docs.title: Download the invitation list
docs.text:
Before using the contact details: A contact may have specified that they do not want to be phoned or emailed. Check this on their Contact Summary and take it into account.

  1. Click Actions above the search results.
  2. Select the available action to download the data as a spreadsheet (CSV file).

docs.title: Create a public membership logo grid
docs.text: In this lesson, you will create a grid of member logos that links to members’ websites and can be filtered by membership type. The grid uses live CiviCRM data and will be available to visitors who are not logged in.

docs.title: Create the search
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Search > SearchKit and click New Search.
  2. Enter a search title, such as “Our Members”, in the box labelled “Untitled Search”.
  3. Select Memberships from the Search for list.
  4. Add a With for Membership Contact. This gives the search access to contact data, such as the display name you will use in a tooltip.
  5. Add a second With for Contact Websites. This gives the search access to members’ website links.
  1. Click Search to check the results. In this example, the search returns six memberships. SearchKit also adds some columns automatically when you add Membership Contact and Contact Websites.

docs.title: Add the logo URL
docs.text:
The search columns determine which data is returned. This example uses the standard contact image as the logo; using a custom field for a different image requires another data source.

  1. Click +Add at the top right of the results table.
  2. Choose Membership Contact: Image URL.
  3. Click Search to refresh the results. The results now include the image URL.

  1. Click Save.

docs.title: Configure the grid
docs.text:
1. Click +Add beneath the search title and add a Grid display. The Grid display arranges the results in tiles.
  1. Give the display a title, such as “Our Members”. SearchKit initially adds all the search’s columns to the display. You can drag items to change their order.
  1. Click Preview. At this stage, the results appear in a 3×3 grid below the button, but they are not yet displayed as logos.
  2. Remove the items you do not need by clicking the remove symbol in each item’s section. For this example, leave only Membership Contact: Image URL.
  3. Check Image to display the URL as an image.
  4. Optionally, set size attributes to make the logos a consistent size—for example, set the height to 200px.
  5. Check Link, select Other... from the dropdown menu, then select Membership Contact - Contact Websites: Website from the token dropdown.

Before using the link token, remove its civicrm/ prefix. The prefix would prevent the link from reaching the member’s external website. Change:

civicrm/[Membership_Contact_contact_id_01_Contact_Website_contact_id_01.url]

to:

[Membership_Contact_contact_id_01_Contact_Website_contact_id_01.url]

  1. Check Tooltip and make sure the label that appears to its right is a token for the Display Name.
  2. Click Refresh to preview the logos.

This configuration shows only members whose records have logos. To include members without logos, check Alternative image.

docs.title: Create a form for the grid
docs.text:
1. Return to the SearchKit dashboard and click Forms > + Create Form for Our Members Grid.
  1. Give the Form a name and a description.
  2. Enter the URL for the page that will display the results, such as civicrm/members.
  1. Click Save. A View Page link appears; it shows the formatted grid.
  2. Switch from Form Settings to the Our Members Grid tab.
  3. Drag Membership Type into the Form Layout tab to add a filter.
  1. Change the filter preset to show the membership types you want.
  2. Change any layout details you need, such as the title of a container element.

While you are logged in to CiviCRM, the URL you specified—for example, your.civicrm.tdl/civicrm/members/—displays the configured Form.

docs.title: Make the form public
docs.text:
The grid is not yet accessible to anonymous visitors. The following settings allow all users, including people who are not logged in, to view and filter it.

  1. Return to the search’s display configuration and click Enforce Permissions to unlock it. The button now reads Bypass Permissions.

  1. Click Save before returning to the Form configuration.
  2. In the Form configuration, select Generic: Allow all users (including anonymous) from the restrictions dropdown list.
  3. Check Accessible on front-end of website.

Visitors can now view and filter the form whether or not they are logged in.

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
You will build a SearchKit overview that shows upcoming events, their speakers and hosts, and participant counts. You can then add links, a filtering form and a navigation menu item.

The default Manage Events overview is available from Event > Manage Events:

The overview you will build can look like this:

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Create a search

  2. Go to Administer > Search > SearchKit and click New Search.

  1. Name the search, for example, Upcoming Events.
  2. Select Events from Search for.
  3. In Where, select Event Start Date, >= and Now. You can instead use Pick a Date or tailor the search with other options.

  1. Save your work.
  2. Click Search to view the results.

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Add the event start date

The search shows the event ID and title by default. Select the event start date column from the list on the right-hand side to show it too.

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Add speakers and hosts

Speaker and host information comes from participants.

  1. Add the participant entity as shown:

  1. In Where, filter the participant role to Speaker or Host, using Contains as shown. A participant can have multiple roles stored in the participant role field.

  1. Add Participant Contact so the search can show speakers’ and hosts’ names. The search now looks like this:

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Show one row per event

An event with more than one speaker or host otherwise appears multiple times. Group the search by event ID:

Use the List field transformation to show speakers and hosts as a comma-separated list:

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Count participants

Applying Count to the Participant ID already in the search would count only hosts and speakers because of the Where filter. Add separate Event Participants entities for the other counts.

  1. Add Event Participants again for the registered/attended count:

  1. Add another Event Participants entity for the cancellations/no-shows count:

  1. Click Add at the upper right of the search results display to add the Participant ID (2 and 3) columns.
  2. Under Field Transformations, select Count and check Distinct next to the Participant ID (2 and 3) labels.

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Name and sort the columns

  2. Under Compose Search, click Add... and select Table. A table display lets you change the column names.

  1. Name the display and add a Sort By value.

  1. Scroll down and give the columns meaningful names in their Header fields. The preview might now look like this:

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Add links to the counts and title

Add a Link to each participant count so readers can open the list of participants with that status:

  • Registered/attended count: civicrm/event/search?reset=1&force=1&event=[id]&status=true
  • Cancellations/no-shows count: civicrm/event/search?reset=1&force=1&event=[id]&status=false

You can also add a Link to the event title using civicrm/event/manage/settings?reset=1&action=update&id=[id]. It opens the event’s Info and Settings page.

The overview now looks like this:

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Add an optional filtering form

  2. Click the form button at the upper right of the search.

  1. In FormBuilder, give the form a name and a page link.

  1. Click the Upcoming Events Table tab.
  2. Drag form elements into the form layout pane.

You can add a Container first to lay out the other form elements:

docs.title: Create an upcoming events overview with SearchKit
docs.text:
1. Add the overview to the navigation menu

If you used civicrm/upcoming-events as the form’s page link, you can create a navigation menu item for it.

  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Navigation Menu.
  2. Create a menu item using the page link.

Users can then open the overview from the navigation menu:

The menu item leads to the completed search form:

docs.title: Saved search expiration dates
docs.text: An expiration date keeps a saved search that is useful only for a defined period from appearing in the list indefinitely.

docs.title: What happens when a search expires
docs.text: After the expiration date, the search is hidden from the display, not deleted. To restore it to the display, you must delete the expiration date via the API explorer or an SQL statement.

docs.title: How an expiration date appears
docs.text:
The expiration date is set on the search:

The search is then shown with an expiration date:

docs.title: Export and import saved SearchKit searches
docs.text: You can share a saved search with someone else or bring a shared search into your CiviCRM site. You can do both through the graphical interface: you do not need to create code, though you will need to copy and paste it.

docs.title: Export a saved search
docs.text:
You must save your SearchKit query before you can export it.

  1. On the main SearchKit page, open the additional actions menu (☰) beside your saved search.
  2. Choose “Export”.

The export window shows the coded version of your search and provides a button to copy it. You can also include any associated displays, groups or forms in the export.

If you want to include the saved search in a custom extension, use “API Explorer Export” instead. Its link is at the top of the export window.

  1. Copy the SearchKit query to your clipboard.

You can save the copied query in a file for future reference, import it into another site, or send it to someone else to use and modify on their system.

docs.title: Import a saved search
docs.text:
1. On the default SearchKit page, click “Import” below the “New Search” button in the top right corner.
  1. Paste the exported search into the empty box.
  2. Submit it.

You return to the main screen, where you can see the newly imported search.

docs.title: Field transformations
docs.text: Field transformations are formulas you apply to fields in a result set. You can use them to display another field when a value is missing, round a number, count occurrences or sum values.

docs.title: Transformation categories
docs.text:
Search Kit organises transformations into four categories:

  • Comparison
  • Text
  • Math
  • Aggregate — available only when you use Group By

docs.title: MySQL documentation
docs.text:
For more information about the functions, see the MySQL documentation:

  • Built-in functions
  • Aggregate functions

Not all MySQL functionality has been implemented in Search Kit.

docs.title: How Group By changes search results
docs.text:
Use “Group By” to understand patterns in your search results. It organises data around one or more common elements of the selected entity, showing one row per value of the selected “Group By” fields.

For Contacts, you can group by Created Date, Contact Subtype or Location information, among other options. For Contributions, options include Contribution Date, Amount and Payment Method.

docs.title: What grouping shows
docs.text:
Grouping can help you count, total or average numeric information, or concatenate data in other fields. For example, you can group contacts by Country to see a count of contacts per Country.

You can select more than one “Group By” option. If you group by Country and Address (primary) State/Province, clicking “Search” displays additional rows: one for each State/Province of data in the system.

You can drag search result columns left or right to change their display order. If you change the column order, click “Search” again to display the results.

docs.title: Having conditions
docs.text: Use Having conditions to filter the results displayed in a SearchKit table, including aggregate data or transformed field values.

docs.title: Where and Having
docs.text:
Your result set starts with an initial Entity selection and may include additional Entity selections made with With/Without. Where and Having provide further ways to filter it. Both are in the Filter Conditions tab on the left.

Where filters data before it is returned from the database and can use any field in the CiviCRM database. Having filters the results displayed in the table and can use only fields included in those results.

A Having condition uses a result field, an operator and a comparison value.

docs.title: Operators
docs.text:
In general, Having operators work like similarly named SQL operators.

Operator Behaviour Matches Pattern Matches a regular expression pattern. Is Like Matches a complete field. To find part of a field, you usually need wildcards, such as %search term%. Contains Searches serialized fields, which store multiple values together. For example, Contact Subtype could contain Parent, Volunteer or Staff. Contains matches a full value such as Parent, not part of a value.

Negated operators such as Not Like, ≠ and Doesn't Contain do not match NULL fields with no value. They match only fields that have a value that does not meet the condition. To include NULL fields as well, you can search for ≠searchterm or Is Empty.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
This condition displays only results whose phone number matches a regular expression describing a particular format.

Reversing the condition displays results that do not match the pattern, helping you find records where a phone number may need fixing.

Glob-matching with % or * can be useful, but regular expressions are more flexible and powerful for filtering results. Many regular expression tutorials are available online.

You can also compare one field with another instead of comparing a field with a value you provide. This example displays rows where the display name and email address are the same.

docs.title: SearchKit and FormBuilder permissions
docs.text:
Use this page to understand the permission settings that affect who can view SearchKit displays and FormBuilder forms.

Access can depend on settings in SearchKit and FormBuilder, CMS user roles (CiviCRM functionalities), and ACL roles (fine-grained permissions). For background, see Permissions and Access Control.

docs.title: SearchKit display permissions
docs.text:
Every display you create in a search, including a table or grid, has an Enforce permissions/Bypass permissions toggle at the top. The displayed text indicates its current state:

Setting Effect Enforce permissions Respects existing CiviCRM permissions. Access can be controlled through CMS roles and CiviCRM’s more detailed ACL controls. Bypass permissions Anyone who can view the display can see all its results, regardless of their permission level. Be careful what you expose.

docs.title: FormBuilder form permissions
docs.text:
Both Search forms and Submission forms have a permission on the form settings tab. This permission controls who can view the form.

You can combine multiple permissions with “and” to require all of them, or “or” to require only one. The available permissions include CMS role permissions, such as WordPress : delete_pages, and CiviCRM permissions, such as CiviContribute: Access CiviContribute. You can use either type or both.

For examples, see who can use a form. For permissions that control whether a form autofills with data from the database, see additional permissions.

docs.title: Query Info
docs.text: Query Info shows the underlying code for your SearchKit search in API and SQL format. You can copy that code for use outside SearchKit. This optional feature is recommended for people who are comfortable using API and SQL commands directly.

docs.title: Search displays
docs.text: Use this page to look up how Search Displays present SearchKit results, which display types are available, and how to format results.

docs.title: Displays and the default table
docs.text:
A saved search can have zero, one or multiple displays, so you can present the same data in different ways. To create one, click Add... on the left when editing your saved search, then choose a type from the dropdown list.

You can also show any search as a table without creating a display. This default Search results table is what you see when you click Search. You can view it as a standalone page or embed it in a form. Creating your own display gives you configuration options that the default table does not provide.

docs.title: Display types
docs.text: Type What it provides Table Results in rows and columns, with an optional pager and selectable actions. Row and column styling is highly configurable. List Results on one or more lines. Each field can have different styling or a custom CSS class. Grid Side-by-side content, such as image gallery thumbnails. Tree Hierarchical data in a nested tree structure. Data Entry A spreadsheet-like input form for batch data entry, rather than a display that outputs data. Autocomplete Search results as a user types, with control over how each result appears in the dropdown. Once created, the display can be selected in FormBuilder, or you can select Make Default Autocomplte to affect forms site-wide. DB Entity A database table or view accessible through SearchKit, the API or SQL-based tools.

docs.title: Displays and features from extensions
docs.text:
More search displays are available through the Extensions Directory:

  • ChartKit: Enable this extension, which is already bundled with CiviCRM core, to show data as plots, charts and graphs.
  • SearchKit Calendar: Download this extension for a time-based display of events, activities and other data.
  • SearchKit Maps: Download this extension to show locations of contacts, events and other data on a map.
  • SearchKit Tokens: Download this extension to create SearchKit tokens for use in mailings.
  • SearchKit Column Display: Download this extension for a display that stacks fields into columns.
  • Other extensions: Check the Extensions Directory for the latest additions.

docs.title: Configuration options
docs.text:
Depending on the display, you can configure:

  • Field selection and ordering
  • Column headers and labels
  • Sorting preferences
  • Link configurations
  • Inline editing capabilities
  • Access permissions
  • Display-specific styling
  • Pagination settings
  • Formatting and rewriting results

docs.title: Rewriting results
docs.text: Field rewrites change how Search Display results appear to users. Rewritten fields are display-only; they do not change the underlying stored data.

docs.title: Combining fields
docs.text:
Put field names in square brackets to replace them with their values:

[first_name] [last_name]
[street_address], [city] [postal_code]

These rewrites can produce values such as Jane Smith and 123 Main St, Springfield 12345.

docs.title: Smarty syntax
docs.text:
For more complex formatting, use Smarty template syntax with curly brackets. You can combine Smarty syntax and square-bracket field names in the same rewrite.

Conditional display:

{if $nick_name}[nick_name]{else}[first_name]{/if} [last_name]

Math operation:

{$total_amount - $fee_amount}

Value transformation:

{if $age_years >= 18}Adult{else}Minor{/if}

Square-bracket field names, such as [display_name], are replaced with their values automatically. In Smarty code, use {$field_name} to access a raw field value—for example, 125 instead of $125.00. Smarty modifiers such as |date_format and |crmMoney help with common formatting needs.

docs.title: Search button
docs.text:
Use the Search button to preview or refresh your search results.

You must click the Search button whenever you want to see results. Changing the search settings clears the displayed results, so click the button again to see the updated results.

docs.title: Search For options
docs.text: Use Search For to choose the primary entity—such as a contact, activity or contribution—for a SearchKit query.

docs.title: Primary entities
docs.text:
• Activity — Past or future actions concerning one or more contacts.
  • Contacts — Individuals, organizations, households and other contacts.
  • Contributions — Financial records consisting of transactions, line items and other details.
  • Events — Scheduled in-person or online events that contacts can register for and attend.
  • Grants — Funds applied for and given out by your organisation.
  • Individuals — Contacts of type Individual.
  • Memberships — Records of contacts belonging to an organisation’s membership program.
  • Organizations — Contacts of type Organization.
  • Participants — Records of contacts’ attendance and roles in events.
  • Pledges — Promises to contribute to an organisation at a future time, either in full or at regular intervals until a total goal is reached.
  • More — A long list of less commonly searched entities. See that list for descriptions of each entity.

docs.title: Modifier entities and grouping
docs.text:
After you select a Search For entity, you can optionally select modifier entities. The available modifiers depend on the primary entity, and each has a description to help you choose.

You can also optionally group the results. The grouping options depend on the primary entity, and each has a description to help you choose.

docs.title: Create a Soft Credit search and table
docs.text:
You will build a search that combines Soft Credit, contribution and contact information, then show the results in a table.

A Soft Credit lets you recognise someone other than the donor for a contribution. For example, if you ask people to donate for your birthday and John Doe contributes 25 euro, you can receive recognition through a Soft Credit. For more information, see Soft Credits.

The finished search will bring together the contact with the Soft Credit, the contact who made the contribution and the contribution itself. It can help you see who your best contribution solicitors are.

docs.title: Start a search
docs.text:
1. Open SearchKit from the Search menu. The Saved Searches page lists existing searches; the Soft Credit example may already appear there.
  1. Click New Search. An empty search form opens.
  1. Replace Untitled Search with a name, such as “Soft Credit Example Search”.

You can also add a tag to categorise the search, such as a tag for Fundraising searches. Leave the Add selection box for now; you will use it to add a display later.

docs.title: Choose entities and conditions
docs.text:
The entity selection initially shows Contacts.

  1. Select the Contribution Soft Credits entity. It provides the contact with the Soft Credit, the ID of the linked contribution, the Soft Credit amount and the Soft Credit type. The Soft Credit amount can differ from the contribution amount.
  2. Use +Entity next to With (optional) to add Contribution and Contact. SearchKit links the Soft Credit to the contribution by contribution ID, and links the contribution to its contact by contact ID.
  3. Add a condition limiting contributions to the financial type Donation. This excludes payments for Memberships or Events.
  4. In Where, set the contribution date range to 1 Jan 2021 through 30 April 2022.

Your selected entities and conditions should look like this:

You will not use Group By in this example. It can group results by a field such as Contact Display Name.

docs.title: Select result fields
docs.text:
At the bottom of the form, the initial fields typically include an ID and sometimes a name.

  1. Click Search above the field names to run the search and see its initial results.

  1. Remove Soft Credit ID and keep the name of the Soft Credit contact.
  2. Use Add on the right to include these fields from the selected entities:
  3. Soft Credit amount
  4. Soft Credit type
  5. Name of the contributing contact
  6. Contribution total amount
  7. Contribution date
  8. Contribution source
  9. Contribution status
  10. Contribution payment method

  1. Click Search again. The results now show the selected fields.

The Action box beside Search offers several actions. Its default action downloads results as a CSV file; that standard action can be switched off.

docs.title: Transform two fields
docs.text:
1. Expand Field Transformations below the entities section. It lists the selected fields and the transformations available for them.
  1. Select Uppercase beside the Contribution Contact Name label to make that name stand out.
  2. Select Date Only beside the Contribution Receive Date label to omit the timestamp.
  1. Click Search to see the transformed results.

docs.title: Save and view the search
docs.text:
1. Click Save in the upper right. Saving makes a View Results button available beneath Save.
  2. Click View Results to see the saved search results. You can return to the search to customise it further.

Save regularly while building the search and table so you do not lose your progress.

docs.title: Optional: inspect Query Info
docs.text:
Query Info, below Field Transformations, shows the technical translation of the selected entities and fields. It is useful for developers, but you can skip it to complete this lesson. For this example, it displays:

{
  "version": 4,
  "select": [
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_Contribution_Contact_contact_id_01.display_name",
    "amount",
    "soft_credit_type_id:label",
    "UPPER(ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.contact_id.display_name) AS UPPER_ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_contact_id_display_name",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.total_amount",
    "DATE(ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.receive_date) AS DATE_ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_receive_date",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.source",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.contribution_status_id:label",
    "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.payment_instrument_id:label"
  ],
  "orderBy": [],
  "where": [
    [
      "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.receive_date",
      "BETWEEN",
      [
        "2021-01-01 11:09:00",
        "2022-04-30"
      ]
    ]
  ],
  "groupBy": [],
  "join": [
    [
      "Contribution AS ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01",
      "LEFT",
      [
        "contribution_id",
        "=",
        "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.id"
      ],
      [
        "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.financial_type_id:name",
        "=",
        "\"Donation\""
      ]
    ],
    [
      "Contact AS ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_Contribution_Contact_contact_id_01",
      "LEFT",
      [
        "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01.contact_id",
        "=",
        "ContributionSoft_Contribution_contribution_id_01_Contribution_Contact_contact_id_01.id"
      ]
    ]
  ],
  "having": []
}

docs.title: Add a table display
docs.text:
1. Click Add... on the left side of the search form.
  1. Select Table. The available display types are Smart Group (a smart group of search results), Table (a table overview), List (a vertical list) and Grid (an unformatted grid). This example uses Table.
  1. Name the table.
  2. Click Save in the upper right.
  3. Use Sort by to choose the fields that sort the table. You can sort them in ascending or descending order.

The next section lets you Enable Actions, set Page Size (the number of results per page), choose a table style, set the text shown when there are no results, and choose whether the search runs automatically. In this example, only the no-results text is changed; the other settings keep their default values.

docs.title: Arrange the table columns
docs.text:
The table settings list the fields in your search.

  • To change a column’s position, click and hold its handle, then move it.

  • To remove a column, click its remove icon.

  • You can change each column’s heading and alignment, and enable inline editing.
  • To show another field already defined in the search, use Add at the top of the column list. The same button can add a link, button, menu or custom code.

For this example, add a menu for viewing the Soft Credit contact, the contributing contact and the contribution:

  1. Click Add at the top of the column list.
  2. Select Menu. A new menu column appears at the bottom of the list.

  1. Edit the menu column to include the three viewing options. Add... within the menu section offers suggestions based on your selected entities.

  1. Save the table, then click View Results. The table displays the search results with the menu.

docs.title: Add the table to the navigation menu
docs.text:
1. Copy the URL from your browser while viewing the table.
  1. Go to Administer > Customize Data and Screens > Navigation Menu.
  2. Click Add Menu Item.
  1. Enter the menu item options and paste the copied URL, starting with civicrm/ onwards.

docs.title: Tag a SearchKit saved search
docs.text:
Add a tag when you create a search, edit an existing search, or work from the Saved Searches main screen. You can then use tags to filter the saved-search list.

Tags categorise data in CiviCRM and can categorise SearchKit searches by Department or Initiative. A tag can be enabled for one or more of these types: Contact, Activity, Case, File, and SavedSearch.

docs.title: Add a tag while creating or editing a search
docs.text:
1. Click Configure Settings in the left sidebar to show the Tags box.
  1. Click the Tags box to select an existing tag or add a new one.

docs.title: Add a tag from the Saved Searches screen
docs.text:
You can also update an existing search from the Saved Searches main screen. Creating a tag here adds it to CiviCRM enabled for SavedSearch, so it can be used elsewhere in the system, such as from Advanced Search.

  1. Click the tag icon with the down arrow beside the saved search.

  1. Begin typing in the Add tag… field. Matching tags appear, or you can choose Create Tag.

docs.title: Filter saved searches by tag
docs.text:
On the SearchKit landing page, use Filter by tags… at the upper right of the saved-search list to select one or more tags.

Learn more about working with tags.

docs.title: SearchKit search controls
docs.text: Use this page to look up where SearchKit controls appear and what their options do.

docs.title: Access SearchKit
docs.text:
Open Search > SearchKit.

On older versions of CiviCRM, the SearchKit extension might not be enabled by default. You or your site admin may need to go to Administer > System Settings > Extensions, select Install beside SearchKit, then select the Install button.

docs.title: Select an entity and result fields
docs.text:
Start a search by selecting the entity you want to find, such as a Contact or Contribution. You can select more than one entity.

Some fields appear by default when you click Search. To display more, click +Add on the right of the field list in the selected results and select the fields you need.

To remove a field from the results, click the x beside its name in the header row.

docs.title: Set criteria in Where
docs.text:
The Where section defines criteria for the entity. Its operators generally work like the similarly named SQL operators.

Operator Behaviour Matches Pattern Matches a regular expression pattern. Is Like Matches a complete field. Use wildcards to find part of a field, for example %search term%. Contains Searches serialized fields that store multiple values together, such as a Contact Subtype containing Parent,Volunteer,Staff. It matches a full value such as Parent, not part of a value. Not Like, ≠, Doesn't Contain Match fields that have a value which does not meet the criterion. They do not match NULL fields with no value.

To include NULL fields when excluding a value, you can search for ≠ searchterm OR Is Empty. This matters particularly for custom fields: when a custom field has no value, its custom field group row might not exist in the database. For a Yes or No field, use Is Empty to find all entities that are not Yes. It finds both NULL values and No (FALSE/0) values; ≠ Yes does not.

docs.title: Choose a join option
docs.text:
When you include another entity, SearchKit offers these join options:

Option Results With (required) Includes only contacts that have the specified additional information, such as an address. With (optional) Includes all contacts and shows the additional information where available. Without Includes only contacts that do not have the specified additional information.

The option you choose affects both which contacts appear and what additional information the results show.

docs.title: Sort results
docs.text: Click a column header to sort by that column. To sort by multiple columns, hold down Shift while clicking additional column headers.

docs.title: Forms
docs.text: Use Forms to configure SearchKits for display as dashlets or in the menu. This is also where you configure filters.

docs.title: Understanding SearchKit and its results
docs.text:
SearchKit lets you build searches and choose how to display their results. This page explains who it is for and how the information you include affects the rows you see.

SearchKit is a search query builder with extensive options for displaying results. It is suited to site builders, power users and developers. Non-technical staff are likely to need training or significant time to learn its interface. Alternatively, an experienced user or developer can create Search Displays and make them available through the menu system or as a dashlet on the main CiviCRM screen.

Saved SearchKit searches can be intended for different roles of staff users or for unauthenticated end users.

docs.title: Entities and joins
docs.text:
An entity is a type of thing you search for, such as a Contact or Contribution. When a search includes more than one type of information, SearchKit uses a join. The interface presents joins as “with” or “without” options.

Adding an entity can change the number of rows in your results. For example, a search for Contacts with (optional) Addresses can return a separate row for each address associated with a contact.

Display Name Location Type Street Address Is Primary Timmy Home Sesame Street Yes Timmy's Mum Home Sesame Street Yes Timmy's Mum Work Downing Street No Timmy's Dad

With optional addresses, Timmy appears once because he has one known address. Timmy's Mum appears twice, once for each address. Timmy's Dad appears without address details.

If you want one row per contact rather than one per address, you can use Group By to group the rows.

docs.title: Primary contact details and joined details
docs.text:
A contact normally has one primary address, one primary email and one primary phone. You can include these useful fields without joining an address table.

If you also add an address join, the results can contain both fields from the Contact entity and fields from the joined addresses. Match the field you choose to the Entity name shown in the box next to Required. In this example, Contact Addresses are the joined non-primary addresses, while Address (primary) Country comes from the primary address.

docs.title: How SearchKit relates to other searches
docs.text:
SearchKit fully replaces the older, more limited Search Builder. It is more powerful than Advanced Search and covers some additional parts of CiviCRM. Many users may still prefer Advanced Search or searches such as Search > Find Contacts and Events > Find Participants. New features are no longer being added to those searches, but they are expected to remain part of CiviCRM for the foreseeable future.

The Quick Search in the upper left is still more convenient when you want to retrieve records quickly using part of an email address, a name or another single term.

docs.title: Where filters
docs.text: Use Where to filter data in the database before it is returned to SearchKit. To filter data after it is returned from the database, use Having.

docs.title: Filter components
docs.text:
A Where filter has four main components:

  • The element you want to compare.
  • The operator.
  • The value or field to compare against.
  • Whether to compare with a value or a field.

In general, the operators work like their similarly named arithmetic or SQL operators.

docs.title: Operator behaviour
docs.text:
• Matches Pattern matches a regular expression pattern.
  • Is Like matches a complete field. To find part of a field, you usually need wildcards, such as %search term%.
  • Contains is useful for searching serialized fields, which store multiple values together. For example, Contact Subtype could contain Parent, Volunteer and Staff. Contains matches a full value such as Parent, not part of a value.
  • Negated operators such as Not Like, ≠ and Doesn't Contain do not match NULL fields with no value. They match only fields that have a value that does not meet the criterion. To include NULL fields, search for ≠ searchterm OR Is Empty.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text:
This filter includes only contacts whose email address contains ‘.gov’:

This filter includes contacts whose primary address is not the same as their billing address:

docs.title: With (optional), With (required), and Without
docs.text:
Use this reference to understand how each option affects your search results when you add an entity in Search Kit.

When you create a search, you first choose a starting entity. You can then add zero or more entities to include their fields as columns or change which rows the search returns. For example, you might start with Contacts and add Contact Addresses.

Each additional entity is joined to the starting entity and any entities you have already added. The join option determines which combinations appear in the results:

Option Rows returned With (optional) Rows from the earlier entities remain in the results even when there is no matching row in the new entity. For example, Contacts With (optional) Contact Addresses returns a row for a Contact with no addresses; that row’s Contact Addresses fields are empty/NULL. With (required) Only rows with a match in the new entity are returned. For example, Contacts With (required) Contact Addresses excludes Contacts with no addresses and returns a row for every combination of a Contact and one of its addresses. Without Only rows from the earlier entities that have no match in the new entity are returned. For example, Contacts Without Contact Addresses returns a row for each Contact with no Contact Address.

You can also add an entity to restrict the rows returned, even if you do not need its fields as columns. For example, you could search for Contacts who have bought tickets for the Annual General Meeting, or those who have not yet bought tickets.

docs.title: Send an SMS to many contacts
docs.text:
Choose recipients for a one-time message or a recurring mailing list, then compose and send or schedule a bulk SMS.

Before you begin, an SMS provider must be configured in CiviCRM. If you have not set up an SMS gateway, read the Set-up section in this chapter first.

docs.title: Choose recipients
docs.text:
For a one-time message, run an advanced search using the criteria your recipients must meet. Select some or all contacts in the results, then choose “Send SMS to Contacts” from the Actions drop-down menu. This method creates activities of type “Text Message (SMS)”.

If you regularly send bulk texts to the same group of contacts, use a mailing list. For help creating one, see Set-up in the Email chapter.

docs.title: Create a bulk SMS
docs.text:
1. Go to Mailings > New SMS.
  2. Name the SMS. The name appears as an SMS activity on every recipient’s contact profile, so use a subject that will help you identify its content later.
  3. Select recipients by moving the mailing lists you want from the Include Group(s) box on the left to the right with Add.
  4. If needed, specify groups to exclude. Contacts in both an included and an excluded group will not receive the message—for example, contacts who have already received a similar SMS.
  5. Click Next.

Before writing your message, bear in mind that both methods of adding content have a 160-character limit—the length of one text message.

  1. Select an available SMS Provider.
  2. If you want to use an existing mailing template, select one. For more information about templates, see Set-up in the Email chapter.
  3. Write the message in Compose On-Screen, or upload it from a text file. You can insert tokens to personalise the SMS with information about each contact.
  4. If you want to reuse the message, tick Save as New Template before moving to the next screen.

On Schedule or Send, you can send the SMS immediately or schedule it for a future date and time. If you are not ready to do either, click Continue Later to save your progress. To return to it, go to Mailings > Draft and Unschedule Mailings, tick Is SMS, click Search, then click Continue beside the message in the list of unsent texts.

Before sending, you can click the “Preview SMS” banner at the bottom to check the content. Click “Submit Mass SMS” to send the message.

docs.title: Send an SMS to a few contacts
docs.text:
Send a text message to an existing contact, add other recipients if needed, and check the recorded SMS activity.

Before you begin, an SMS provider must be configured in CiviCRM. If you have not set up an SMS gateway, read the Set-up section in this chapter first.

  1. Open the contact’s profile.
  2. Click Actions.
  3. Select Send SMS.

You can also create an SMS from the contact’s Activity tab using the -new activity- drop-down menu.

The message page has these fields and options:

  • From: Choose the SMS provider you want to send the message from.
  • To: The mobile number of the contact you selected is filled in automatically. To add recipients, type a name after the first number and select a contact from the suggestions. Contacts without a phone number of type “Mobile” will not appear.
  • Name the SMS: Give the message a subject you can recognise later, such as “Change of email address request”. This name appears in the SMS activity on recipients’ profiles.
  • Use Template: Insert an existing SMS template to save time. For more information, see Set-up in the Email chapter.
  • Plain-Text Format: Enter up to 160 characters of message text. You can insert tokens to include information about the contact.
  • Save as New Template: Save the message text as a template if you want to reuse it.

Once the SMS has been sent, a confirmation message appears and an SMS activity is added to each recipient’s contact profile. To find it, open a recipient’s profile, select the Activity tab and look for an activity of type “Text Message (SMS)”. Click View in the last column to see details, including the message content and campaign.

docs.title: Report on SMS activity
docs.text:
Use the Activities report to find SMS activity recorded in CiviCRM and narrow the results to the messages you need.

  1. Open the Activities report under Reports > Contact Reports.

  1. Filter by the SMS activity type you need: Inbound SMS, Mass SMS or SMS delivery.

  1. Add any other filters you need:
  2. Message status, such as completed or scheduled
  3. Date and time
  4. The recipient’s group or tag

  5. Recipient characteristics, such as name and location

  6. Click Preview Report at the bottom of the Filters window to update the results.

docs.title: Set up a Twilio SMS gateway
docs.text:
Use this guide to connect Twilio to CiviCRM, send a test message and receive replies. Contacts must have a mobile number recorded with Phone Type set to Mobile; contacts without one will not receive an SMS. Users need the CiviCRM: send SMS permission to see SMS menu items and send messages.

Twilio offers communications and telephony services in most countries. CiviSMS uses its Programmable SMS feature. A free trial account lets you test the service.

docs.title: Register and get a number
docs.text:
A trial account includes a free rented Twilio mobile phone number for sending SMS. A free account must verify a mobile phone number before that number can receive SMS. This guide uses the phone number verified during registration as the test recipient.

  1. Register for a Twilio trial account.
  2. Verify your account phone number by SMS or call. You will then reach the Console.
  3. On the Console homepage, select Programmable SMS.
  4. Select Get Started.
  5. Select Get a number near the top of the page. Twilio will suggest a number.
  6. If the suggested number's country is not correct, select Search for a different number.
  7. Note the number you want, then select Choose this number.
  8. Select Done.

You now have a rented number that can send and receive SMS messages.

docs.title: Send replies to CiviCRM
docs.text:
1. In Twilio, select the All Products & Services icon in the far-left navigation bar. Alternatively, go to Develop > Super Network > Phone Numbers.
  2. Select Phone Numbers.
  3. Select your new number from the list.
  4. Under Messaging, change A message comes in webhook to the appropriate URL below, replacing example.com with your CiviCRM installation:
  5. Drupal: https://example.com/civicrm/sms/callback?provider=org.civicrm.sms.twilio
  6. WordPress: https://example.com/civicrm?civiwp=CiviCRM&q=civicrm%2Fsms%2Fcallback&provider=org.civicrm.sms.twilio

This sends replies to your messages back to CiviCRM.

  1. Select Save.

docs.title: Add Twilio in CiviCRM
docs.text:
1. Return to the Twilio Console homepage.
  2. Copy your Account SID.
  3. Reveal and copy your Auth Token.
  4. Install the Twilio extension.
  5. In CiviCRM, go to Administer > System Settings > SMS Providers.
  6. Select Add New Provider.
  1. Complete the provider settings:
  2. Name: Select Twilio.
  3. Title: Enter a title users will see, such as “Twilio SMS”.
  4. Username: Enter your Account SID.
  5. Password: Enter your Auth Token.
  6. API type: Leave as http.
  7. API URL: Leave as https://api.twilio.com/.
  8. API Parameters: Enter From= followed by your Twilio mobile phone number in international format with no spaces. On a second line, enter mo=1.

Sending limit: Twilio allows around 200 messages per day from each long number. If you need to send more and cannot afford a short code, you can get additional long numbers from Twilio. List them after From=, separated by | (the “pipe” character), for example, From=12345051212|19875052323|15675052345. When you include multiple long numbers, one is chosen at random each time an SMS is sent.

  1. Select Save to create the provider.

docs.title: Test and upgrade
docs.text:
You can now use CiviSMS to send an SMS to a mobile phone number you have access to. See Everyday Tasks for ways to send messages. If you reply to an SMS, the reply is created as an activity on your CiviCRM record.

To use Twilio fully as an SMS gateway, upgrade to a paid account by selecting Upgrade in the top-right corner of the Twilio Console. After upgrading, your rented mobile phone number is available for full use and is charged against your Twilio credit. You can then send SMS to any mobile phone number.

docs.title: Set up a Clickatell SMS gateway
docs.text: Use this guide to connect a Clickatell account to CiviCRM so you can send single and mass text messages. Contacts must have a mobile number recorded with Phone Type set to Mobile; contacts without one will not receive an SMS. Users need the CiviCRM: send SMS permission to see SMS menu items and send messages.

docs.title: Create a Clickatell connection
docs.text:
Clickatell is an online SMS gateway. For this setup, use its Developer's Central product, which provides the APIs needed to connect to CiviCRM. The CiviCRM developer guide has more information about APIs. Registration is free and includes 10 complimentary credits to try the service.

  1. Register at Clickatell for a Developer's Central account.
  2. Sign in, selecting Central API as the product and entering your Client ID.
  3. In the Central Home dashboard, select Create a new Connection under Connection Status. The newer label is Get another API, and the page may look different.

  1. Select HTTP/S as the connection type. The newer label is HTTP API.
  2. Review the four optional settings:
  3. Description: Change the connection name, for example, “CiviCRM HTTP”.
  4. Replace leading zero: Enable this if your contacts' mobile numbers begin with 0. If it is not enabled, all numbers must begin with the country code for delivery to succeed. This option no longer exists in the newer interface.
  5. Enable IP Address Restriction: If you know your CiviCRM server's IP address, enter it to prevent messages being sent through your account from elsewhere, even by someone with your username and password. The newer wording is Protect your account from fraud by restricting IP addresses.
  6. Enable your app to receive message delivery notifications: The source identifies this as a possible new option. Enter the URL for your site. Examples:
    • Drupal: http://www.example.com/civicrm/sms/callback?provider=org.civicrm.sms.clickatell
    • WordPress: https://www.example.org/?page=CiviCRM&q=civicrm%2Fsms%2Fcallback&provider=org.civicrm.sms.clickatell
  7. Select Submit and Get API ID.
  8. Make a note of the API ID shown on the next page.

docs.title: Add Clickatell in CiviCRM
docs.text:
1. Install the Clickatell extension.
  2. Go to Administer > System Settings > SMS Providers.
  3. Select Add New Provider.
  1. Complete the settings:
  2. Name: Select Clickatell.
  3. Title: Enter a title users will see, such as “Clickatell SMS”.
  4. Username: Enter your Clickatell username.
  5. Password: Enter your Clickatell password.
  6. API type: Select http.
  7. API URL: Enter https://api.clickatell.com.
  8. API Parameters: Enter your API ID in the format api_id=8473658.
  9. Is this provider active?: Tick this to enable the SMS gateway.
  10. Is this a default provider?: Tick this if you want Clickatell to be the default when multiple SMS providers are available.

CiviCRM is now configured to send text messages to contacts with mobile numbers.

docs.title: Test the gateway
docs.text:
Use the methods in Everyday tasks to test sending. Before you purchase credits, Clickatell replaces the content of messages sent using the 10 complimentary credits with thank-you text like this:

Thanks for testing Clickatell's gateway coverage. You will be able to change the content of your message after your initial purchase of message credits.

docs.title: Update settings after upgrading to a paid account
docs.text:
After upgrading your Clickatell account, change the provider parameters and reply callback settings to get them working again.

  1. In CiviCRM, go to Administer > System Settings > SMS Providers.
  2. Select Edit on your Clickatell provider.
  3. In API Parameters, add from= and mo=1 beneath the api_id line. The from= number is the mobile phone number associated with the api_id in your Clickatell account. For example:
api_id=8473658
from=15551234567
mo=1
  1. In Clickatell Developer's Central, select the America's 2 Way SMS tab.
  2. Select Manage beside the mobile phone number you are using.
  3. For Primary Callback: Reply Path, select HTTP Get.
  4. Enter the same callback address used before:
  5. Drupal: http://www.example.com/civicrm/sms/callback?provider=org.civicrm.sms.clickatell
  6. WordPress: https://www.example.org/?page=CiviCRM&q=civicrm%2Fsms%2Fcallback&provider=org.civicrm.sms.clickatell

docs.title: What is SMS?
docs.text:
SMS stands for Short Message, or Short Messaging Service. It refers to the text messages that mobile phones send and receive.

CiviCRM can send and receive SMS messages within the system. This gives your organisation another way to communicate with constituents and track those communications alongside email.

You might use SMS to:

  • Share information in areas where mobile or landline internet access is unavailable or unstable.
  • Collect information or responses from remote areas.
  • Run an SMS marketing campaign.
  • Send alerts and reminders.
  • Tell event participants about a last-minute change to a meeting’s location or time.

docs.title: Record survey responses
docs.text:
Find respondents to interview and record their answers in CiviCRM.

  1. Go to Campaign > Interview Respondents.
  2. On the Find Respondents to Interview screen, select the survey name in Survey. This field is required.
  3. Select the group of contacts to interview in Group(s).
  4. Click Search.
  5. Select the individuals whose responses you want to record. To select every contact found, choose All n records, where n is the number of contacts in the search results.
  6. Click Go. The Record Survey Responses screen appears.
  7. Record each individual's responses to the survey questions.
  8. In the Result column, select a response status, such as Completed or No Answer.
  9. Click Record Response.

Then choose the action that fits what you need to do next:

  • Click Done if you have finished recording responses. You return to the Find Respondents to Interview screen.
  • Click Release Respondents if you decide not to record responses for the contacts. On the Release Respondents screen, click Release Respondents again. The contacts will no longer be reserved, so another volunteer can reserve them for interviewing.
  • Click Reserve More Respondents to find more contacts to interview.

At the end of the canvass, a program lead can review the survey results. See Reports and Analysis to learn how to view the report.

docs.title: Prepare a survey WalkList
docs.text:
Print a list of addresses for a survey of type Walklist, then use the completed sheets to enter canvass responses in CiviCRM.

Door-knocking may be part of a larger campaign, so you may want to set up a Campaign if you have not already done so.

docs.title: Print the WalkList report
docs.text:
1. Go to Reports > Create Templates from Reports > Survey Report (Detail).
  2. In Display Columns, check Street Number, Street Name, Street Unit and Survey Responses.
  3. In Group By Columns, check Street Name and Odd/Even Street Number.
  4. In Set Filters, select your survey name in Survey.
  5. For Respondent Status, select Is Equal to and Reserved from the dropdown menus.
  6. Click Preview Report.
  7. Click Print Preview.
  8. Print the report.

The printout includes a cover sheet with the survey questions, showing both label and value. The report is sorted by street name and odd and even street numbers. See Set up for more information.

docs.title: Collect and enter responses
docs.text:
Organisers and volunteers can use the WalkList report sheets to collect responses while door-knocking. At the end of each day or evening of canvassing, they can enter those responses in CiviCRM.

  1. Go to Campaigns > Interview Respondents.
  2. Enter the name of your survey and the name of the target group you surveyed.
  3. If you want to work with a smaller group of contacts, enter the street name.
  4. On the Find Respondents to Interview screen, select the contacts whose responses you want to record.
  5. Click Go.
  6. Enter the responses and results from your WalkList sheets.
  7. Click Record Response.

docs.title: Reserve survey respondents
docs.text:
Reserve a group of contacts before interviewing them. You can reserve a smaller subset if that is more manageable within the time available.

To view or edit existing surveys, go to Campaign > Dashboard > Surveys. This page shows a summary of your surveys. Use the links at the right to manage a survey, or click Add Survey to create one.

If you need to create a group first, see Groups and Tags.

Note

CiviCRM parses a street address into Street Name, Street Unit and Street Number only if Street Address Parsing is enabled. To enable it, go to Administer > Administration Console > Configuration Checklist > Address Settings and check Street Address Parsing in the Address Editing area. This is useful for a large door-to-door canvass.

  1. Go to Campaigns > Reserve Respondents.
  2. Select the survey name from the Survey dropdown menu. This field is required.
  3. Select the group of contacts to interview from the Group(s) dropdown menu.
  4. If needed, enter criteria to limit the search to a geographic area, such as Street Address, Street Name, Street Unit, Street Number, City or Zip/Postal Code.
  5. Click Search. The Find Respondents to Reserve results appear.

  1. Select the contacts to reserve. To select every contact found, choose All n records, where n is the number of contacts in the search results.
  2. Click Go. The Reserve Respondents screen appears.

  1. Click Reserve.

docs.title: Review survey results in a report
docs.text:
Use Survey Report (Detail) to view responses to a survey. You can filter the results, export them to a CSV file, or view a formatted print preview.

  1. Go to Administer > CiviReport > Create New Report from Template.
  2. Under Campaign Report Templates, select Survey Report (Detail). Alternatively, click a survey name on the survey dashboard.
  3. On the Columns tab, check Survey Responses and any other columns you want to see, such as Street Number and Street Name.
  4. On the Filters tab, select your survey under Survey.

  5. Under Respondent Status, select Interviewed.

  6. If you want to limit the results by an answer, use the drop-down area named after your custom data set of questions. For example, you can show all the “yes” responses to one question.

  7. Click Preview Report.

The Survey Report (Detail) - Template screen shows the results. You can also export the report information to a CSV file for more detailed reporting.

To see a formatted report with the cover sheet of questions and responses, click Print Preview. The report shows street names in ascending order if you indicated that in the survey responses area criteria.

docs.title: Set up a survey
docs.text: Create the fields for your questions, then add them to a survey through a profile. If the survey belongs to a specific campaign, review the Campaigns section as well.

docs.title: Plan your questions
docs.text:
A survey uses custom data sets to capture questions and responses, and a profile to arrange the questions as they appear on the survey.

  • If you expect to run many short surveys—for example, 20–30 surveys a year with 3–4 questions each—consider creating one custom data set containing all their questions. Create a separate custom profile for each survey that includes only its questions.
  • If you expect to run a few surveys—for example, 3–4 a year with no more than 10 questions each—consider creating different custom data sets for each group of survey questions. Use custom profiles to include the questions for each survey.

docs.title: Set up survey types if needed
docs.text:
Survey responses are recorded in an activity record for an individual. The default CiviCRM survey types are Survey, Canvass, PhoneBank, WalkList, and Petition. You can create a survey type to describe another type of activity you conduct.

To create or edit survey types:

  1. Go to Administer > CiviCampaign > Survey Types.

  2. Click Add Survey Type to create a type, then complete the form.

docs.title: Create the survey fields
docs.text:
1. Go to Administer > Customize > Custom Data.
  2. Click Add a Set of Custom Fields. For more on creating field sets, including fields with multiple answers, see Creating Custom Fields.
  3. Set the custom data set to be used for Activities, with the relevant Activity type: Canvas, PhoneBank, Survey, or Walklist.
  4. Add your questions and any help text to the field set.
  5. Click Save to create the field set for the responses.

For a PhoneBank survey where you enter responses directly into CiviCRM, you may want to add the phone number to the profile and set it to view only. Interviewers can then see the number while speaking to respondents.

For a Walklist survey, you may want to use full field labels but shorter values. The values appear in the printed list of Walklist addresses used by survey collectors and may make responses easier to record. For example, use Wrong address as the label and WA as the value. See Everyday Tasks for more information.

You can create a profile for the questions from the main profile screen now, or create it when you add the survey.

docs.title: Create the survey
docs.text:
1. Go to Campaigns > New Survey.
  2. Enter a Title for the survey.
  3. If the survey is part of a campaign, select the campaign from the dropdown menu.
  4. Choose the type of Activity, such as Canvas, PhoneBank, Survey, or Walklist.
  5. In Instructions for Interviews, enter information that will help volunteers conduct the survey.
  6. In Maximum Reserved at one time, enter the maximum number of contacts that can be reserved for interview at one time. This lets you divide contacts among volunteers.
  7. In Total reserved per interview, enter the total number of contacts that any interviewer can reserve.
  8. In Release frequency, enter the number of days after which reserved respondents are released if they have not been surveyed.
  9. Click Save and Next to add questions, or Save to save the survey.

When adding questions, you can add two profiles: one to collect contact information and one for survey questions. For either profile, you can select an existing profile, edit or copy one, or create a new one. Creating a profile within the survey opens a drag-and-drop profile builder. There you can add individual or activity standard or custom fields, rename fields, change their order and other settings, and name the profile.

Survey Results record and track the status of each completed survey, such as Completed, No Answer, or Call. If an earlier survey has a survey Result Set you want to reuse, select it. Otherwise, click Create a new result set and enter the status results you want to track, such as Completed, Not Home, Moved, Wrong Address, and Deceased.

docs.title: What is CiviSurvey?
docs.text:
CiviSurvey is a CiviCampaign feature for recording offline survey responses in a standardised way and generating reports from the data. It records each individual’s responses in an activity record of the type Survey.

CiviSurvey records responses from your existing contacts. If you want to gather responses from people who may not be in your database, use CiviCampaign’s Petition feature instead. See Petition.

docs.title: Example: A public housing survey
docs.text:
Toft Organisation For Tenants (TOFT) protects tenants’ rights and lobbies for affordable housing. To understand the scale of housing problems in one neighbourhood and identify the most pressing issues, TOFT decided to survey residents about housing conditions and complaints about landlords. A focus group determined the questions and whom to ask.

A TOFT staff member created a survey in CiviCRM and built a list of respondents from existing contacts. She generated and printed a walk list report for the volunteers carrying out the survey.

Over one week, volunteers visited selected public housing buildings, interviewed respondents and recorded their answers on the walk list. At the end of each day, they entered each individual’s responses into CiviCRM. Some did this from home; others used computers at TOFT’s office.

After the survey, the programme leader searched activities in CiviCRM for the group of people surveyed and generated reports to analyse their responses. TOFT used the findings to plan its next campaign strategy and shape messages about issues affecting the neighbourhood.

docs.title: Track contacts who voted at the polls
docs.text:
Use CiviCampaign’s “Get Out the Vote” GOTV (Voter Tracking) feature to mark contacts you have surveyed or plan to survey who have voted at the polls.

Before you begin, enable the CiviCampaign component. You also need to have created a survey, created a group of contacts you plan to interview, and reserved respondents for that survey. See CiviCampaign and What is CiviSurvey for more information.

  1. Click Campaigns > GOTV (Voter Tracking.
  2. On the GOTV (Voter Tracking) search screen, select the Survey you are using. This field is required.
  3. In Group(s), select the group of contacts whose voting you want to track.
  4. Click Search.
  5. On the GOTV (Voter Tracking) screen, check Voted? next to each individual you know has voted at the polls.

You can float your cursor over the “individual contact” icon next to a person’s name to see more information about that individual.

docs.title: Planning a CiviCampaign survey
docs.text:
This page explains how surveys use profiles and respondent groups, and the decisions to make before creating a survey.

Surveys are part of CiviCampaign, so CiviCampaign must be enabled to use them. A survey does not have to be connected to a campaign. For example, your organisation could conduct a membership satisfaction survey to assess its own service without associating it with a campaign.

docs.title: Questions and responses
docs.text:
CiviCampaign surveys use profiles to capture participants’ responses. Custom fields hold the questions and responses; if you collect multiple-choice responses, those fields need option values. A profile displays the survey questions. You can create a profile from the main profile screen or while creating a survey.

For instructions, see Creating Custom Fields and Profiles.

docs.title: Respondents
docs.text:
Before you capture responses, you need a group of the contacts you want to survey. You can use an existing group or create one for the survey. The survey process calls this reserving respondents. After a contact completes the survey and their data is recorded, they are released from the group.

For more about creating groups, see Groups and Tags in Organising Your Data. Surveys are designed for existing contacts. If you want responses from the wider public, use the Petition tool; see the Petitions section.

docs.title: Drupal permissions
docs.text: If you use Drupal, specific roles need the Reserve Campaign Contacts and Release Campaign Contacts permissions to conduct surveys. See the Drupal permissions documentation.

docs.title: Decisions to make
docs.text:
• Campaign connection: A general survey can serve any programme without being connected to a campaign. If the survey is a strategy within a campaign, connecting it lets you analyse it alongside that campaign’s other strategies and activities.
  • Response types: Decide whether standard responses, such as Yes, No, Undecided and Declined, will make results easier to analyse, or whether an open-ended question would let people provide a narrative.
  • Number of questions: If you need more than one question, you will need custom fields. If you need more than three, consider using Petition instead of Survey.
  • Survey process: Decide who will conduct the survey and how they will enter the data into CiviCRM.
  • Audience: Decide which group of your constituents you want to survey.

docs.title: Ask for help in CiviCRM chat
docs.text:
Use these steps to prepare a question, post it in a suitable channel and keep the discussion easy to follow.

  1. Search for an existing answer. Search the web, especially https://docs.civicrm.org and https://civicrm.stackexchange.com, to see whether others have asked your question.

  2. Describe the problem in detail. A specific question is easier to answer than a vague one. For example, instead of “I can't install CiviCRM”, say “When I try to install CiviCRM, I see error XYZ on screen.”

  3. Include your configuration. Give your CiviCRM version, your CMS and its version, and other relevant details. Say whether you use a caching system such as Memcache or Redis.

  4. Explain what you have tried. For example: “I read the docs at https://docs.civicrm.org and it says to do X, Y, Z, but when I do Y I don't see the expected screen.” If you have already discussed the issue on https://civicrm.stackexchange.com, link to that conversation so people do not need to ask the same questions again.

  5. Choose one channel for your question. Avoid posting the same question in multiple channels:

  6. ~user-support for using CiviCRM
  7. ~dev-newcomers for new developer support

  8. ~town square if you are unsure

  9. Ask one question at a time. Keep support discussions public rather than sending someone a direct message without checking with them first. Public discussions help others too.

  10. Keep replies in one thread. Use MatterMost's reply feature so people can follow the issue and join in. Shift+Up Arrow is a shortcut to reply.

  11. Give people time to respond. Community members lead busy lives. If no one answers, check back later or try posting on https://civicrm.stackexchange.com.

docs.title: Report a CiviCRM bug
docs.text: Use this guide to check a problem you have found, share enough detail for others to investigate it, and report it as a bug if appropriate.

docs.title: Check the problem first
docs.text:
1. Search Stack Exchange for a similar problem. Follow any relevant advice you find there.

  2. Check the documentation carefully, including documentation for related parts of CiviCRM. What looks like a bug may come from a misunderstanding of how those parts work together.

  3. Check whether your server setup could be affecting CiviCRM. Server settings vary and can change how CiviCRM operates.

  4. Check the versions of CiviCRM, PHP and MySQL you use. Older or unsupported versions can cause unpredictable errors. If a bug has been fixed in the latest CiviCRM release, the community may advise you to upgrade, even though upgrading can put a burden on your organisation. Supporting multiple versions at once is difficult.

  5. Check whether your CiviCRM source code has been customised. Changes can have unintended effects. Your in-house developers, consultant or service provider may be able to identify a relevant change. Community members may also help, but you may need to share source code, try suggestions and allow time to investigate.

  6. Review any newly installed or enabled modules or components that were not included in the usual installation package. Check that you have a stable version compatible with your version of CiviCRM.

docs.title: Try the demo site
docs.text:
Issues involving email output or payment processing cannot be recreated on the demo sites. For other issues, select a demo site that matches your CiviCRM version and try to reproduce the problem there.

If the problem also occurs on the demo site, it is likely to be in CiviCRM’s source code. Record exactly what you did and the demo site URLs for each step; this will help others find and fix it.

If you cannot reproduce the problem there, it may still be a CiviCRM bug. Your server setup or customisations may be triggering it.

docs.title: Ask the community
docs.text:
Remove confidential details before sharing a URL or configuration file. In particular, do not share your database log-in.

If the problem remains, post a question on Stack Exchange. Explain what you are trying to do and how you are doing it. Include the URL you used, with confidential details removed, if it might help others see whether you are configuring the wrong page.

Give enough background for someone unfamiliar with your organisation’s use of CiviCRM to understand the problem. Include:

  • What you did, what you expected to happen and what actually happened.
  • Your CiviCRM version, CMS platform and CMS version, and browser and browser version. Include all of these.
  • Your PHP and MySQL versions.
  • Screenshots of the error or issue.
  • The history of the problem.
  • How consistently it happens—for example, whether it always happens, has been reported by others but cannot be reproduced consistently, or happens in one browser but not another.
  • If you reproduced it on a demo site, the exact steps and demo site URLs.
  • If you did not reproduce it on a demo site, as much information about your server setup as you can feasibly share. Configuration files from the web server, CMS and CiviCRM can be valuable once sensitive information has been removed.

Specific questions are more likely to get useful replies. If the community suggests that you have found a CiviCRM bug, report it to the CiviCRM issue tracker.

docs.title: Getting a fix
docs.text:
The time needed to fix a bug depends on its severity and complexity. A fix might be ready the same day or take much longer.

The easiest way to get bug fixes is to download and install the latest revision of CiviCRM. It is also possible to apply a fix between releases, known as patching, to your existing software. If you have the technical skills, refer to the CiviCRM Developer’s Guide for instructions on applying a patch. Otherwise, seek technical assistance to provide tests and a patch for the issue.

docs.title: Contribute to the CiviCRM User Guide
docs.text: You can edit a page directly or use a fork to submit several related changes. Choose the approach that fits the work you want to do.

docs.title: Before you edit
docs.text:
Follow the Documentation style guide. Commit edits based on the current version of CiviCRM against the master branch. The Developer guide has more information about versions.

  1. Sign up for a civicrm.org account if you do not already have one.
  2. Log in at lab.civicrm.org.

docs.title: Edit one page
docs.text:
1. Find the page you want to edit, such as Menu, Dashboard and Dashlets.
  2. Click the pencil icon next to the page title.

The GitLab editing screen opens at lab.civicrm.org.

  1. Make your changes.
  2. Describe them in a descriptive commit message.
  3. Select commit changes.

This creates a merge request. Someone on the documentation team will review your changes before they are published.

docs.title: Submit several related changes
docs.text:
1. Select the Fork button at the top right of the page.
  1. Use a git client to clone the CiviCRM User Guide repository to your computer.
  2. Locate the Markdown file (.md) you want to edit in your file system. Match it to the page you want to change. For example, the source identifies <your_file_system>/docs/getting-prepared/is-civicrm-for-you.md for the page “What is CiviCRM?”.
  3. Make one or more related changes.
  4. Commit the changes in your git client.
  5. Push the changes from your git client to your fork.
  6. In GitLab, click merge request to create a new merge request.
  1. Click merge request.
  2. Leave a descriptive message.
  3. Click Create merge request.

Someone on the documentation team will review your PR. Your changes will be published once they are approved.

For more advanced contributing guidance and resources on CiviCRM documentation and Markdown, see the CiviCRM developer guide and its documentation resources.

docs.title: Map French to Canadian French
docs.text:
You can change the language mapping when you need a more specific regional translation. For example, Canadian French can differ substantially from French from France.

To use fr_CA instead of the default fr_FR for France French, add this code to your civicrm.settings.php file:

  define('CIVICRM_LANGUAGE_MAPPING_FR', 'fr_CA');

See CRM-9558 for more information.

docs.title: Contribute CiviCRM translations
docs.text:
You can help translate CiviCRM into a new language or improve an existing translation. The steps below assume a bit of technical background.

The translation workflow is still a work in progress. Refer to the translation team instructions for the most current guidance.

docs.title: Join a language team
docs.text:
1. Create an account on Transifex.
  2. Find your language in the CiviCRM teams and join its team.
  3. Start translating using the online or offline approach below.

If you need to request a new language, ask in the translation chat.

Translation is team-based. An existing team may have a glossary and a translation set, and can review your work and offer constructive criticism. If there is no team for your language, you can create one. Teams can use Transifex forums and messaging to coordinate their work.

docs.title: Translate online
docs.text:
Online translation needs no software installation. Transifex has fewer features than an offline tool such as PoEdit, but it is the easiest way to contribute translations or make an occasional quick correction. Every translator should have a Transifex account.

  1. Select a component. You will see its language teams.
  2. Click the icon in the Options column next to your language. You will see the component’s files.
  3. Click the “pencil and paper” icon. The online translation screen lists the translatable strings in that file.
  4. Enter a translation for each string you want to translate.
  5. When you finish, click Send for review at the end of the page.

docs.title: Translate offline
docs.text:
If you do not have a reliable Internet connection, you can download files and translate them on your computer. Offline software offers more features than the online system. PoEdit is a common editor; it is free software with a large community of users.

The exact steps depend on your tool, but the process is:

  1. Download the files you want to translate from transifex.net.
  2. Open the files in your translation tool and translate them.
  3. Send the files back to the site when you finish.

docs.title: Keep terminology consistent
docs.text:
Teams are encouraged to build a glossary and use peer review. The CiviCRM glossary for translations can help you identify frequently seen strings and maintain consistent terms. Translate the common terms for your language and reach a team consensus on them. You can also use this glossary of common terms.

PoEdit and other translation software can build a translation memory, which translation tools can use automatically. Building one from glossary terms can help your team stay consistent; the PoEdit help system explains how to build the database, and most other translation software should provide similar help.

A translation memory can contain only CiviCRM translations or include other projects. Including other projects might automatically translate more strings and help start a new translation, but it can reduce consistency, and most strings will be marked as fuzzy.
